## Preserved Previous Revision

Date: 2026-08-27
Status: Revised after latest proposal-readiness review; awaiting re-review

## Summary

Chainworks agents currently receive provider instructions, one resolved skill
fragment, task and artifact paths, materialized input artifacts, output
contracts, and runtime identifiers. They do not receive one compact,
control-plane-owned statement of the run mission, the purpose of the current
stage, their role in that mission, or the consumer of their result.

At the same time, most production skills in `examples/agents/agents.yaml` are
one-line `inline_skill` descriptions while detailed procedures and role rules
live in large per-agent prompts. Existing external skill bundles are split
between example and plugin trees, and their eval scenarios are declarative
documents rather than an executable quality system.

This design replaces that arrangement with three separate contracts:

1. a frozen base mission plus a Rust-owned durable authority overlay and
   per-invocation assignment context;
2. Agent Skills-compatible procedural bundles with one canonical source;
3. deterministic and live evaluation lanes that compare candidate behavior
   with a frozen baseline.

The new production path is mandatory for every newly compiled run. It has no
feature flag, disable switch, cohort, or legacy single-path fallback. Existing
context-absent frozen runs remain available for historical readback, but cannot
resume live provider or side-effect execution after V2 cutover.

## Problem Evidence

The current implementation has several structural failure modes.

- A normal task sees the Idea only when the task explicitly declares an Idea
  input. Later implementation and review agents usually infer the global goal
  from large proposal and review artifacts.
- Workflow states have labels and owners, and tasks have names, but neither has
  a typed purpose or completion outcome.
- Agent role, reusable procedure, runtime restrictions, output-shape advice,
  and historical corrections are mixed inside long catalog prompts.
- `external_skill` resolution reads the complete `SKILL.md` as raw prompt text,
  including frontmatter, and does not expose bundle resources through a
  versioned run-local manifest.
- Production agents primarily use `inline_skill`, so the skill layer has little
  practical effect on behavior.
- Existing skill scenarios are not executed against a baseline, repeated
  across production providers, or scored by retained assertions.

The retained P095 history provides a concrete authority failure. An older run
brief required a default-off canary while a later explicit operator directive
required mandatory activation with no feature flag. Reviewers continued to
reason from the stale brief. The model did not have a typed authority chain
that made the supersession visible and enforceable.

## Current Skill Inventory

The production catalog currently declares twelve skill IDs. Eleven are
`inline_skill` entries and one, `docs_quality_guardian`, is a hardcoded
`builtin_agent`. None of the Agent Skills-style bundles under `examples/skills`
or `plugins/proposal-lifecycle-review/skills` is used as an external production
bundle by the current catalog.

The migration inventory is:

| Current skill ID | Canonical disposition | V2 execution mode | Effect owner | Partial-failure rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `proposal_review_triad` | retire for new catalogs; historical snapshot compatibility only | `historical_only` | none | V2 compile rejects any reference |
| `proposal_review_router_skill` | `proposal-review-router` | `proposal_review` | read-only reviewer fan-out | signed missing result completes its ordinal and forces aggregate `not_ready` |
| `proposal_implementation_audit` | `proposal-implementation-audit` | `implementation_audit` | read-only evidence inspection | incomplete evidence yields typed not-ready, never inferred pass |
| `docs_quality_guardian` | `docs-quality-guardian` | `docs_review`, `docs_closeout` | declared run-artifact/docs permission | partial write is non-current until output-contract settlement |
| `orchestrator_core` | `lead-orchestration` | `lead_orchestration` | idempotent control-plane commands | committed command receipt is reconciled; no blind retry |
| `proposal_writer_core` | `proposal-authoring` | `proposal_authoring` | declared proposal-artifact write | partial generation cannot become current |
| `code_writer_core` | `code-implementation` | `implementation` | workspace source/test writes | ambiguous write enters typed reconciliation |
| `security_checker_core` | `security-review` | `security_review` | read-only evidence inspection | missing scan/result blocks settlement |
| `prepush_review_core` | `prepush-review` | `prepush_review` | read-only evidence inspection | missing required proof blocks settlement |
| `github_commit_push` | `github-delivery` | `delivery` | existing Git/external side-effect authority | post-dispatch ambiguity reconciles by durable effect identity, never retry |
| `connect_publisher` | `connect-publishing` | `publishing` | existing network publication authority | post-dispatch ambiguity reconciles by durable effect identity, never retry |
| `steward_core` | `forge-steward` | `post_run_tuning` | recommendation artifacts only | cannot mutate or promote production inputs |

The example and plugin copies of proposal review and implementation audit have
different digests today. The canonical registry becomes the authoring source;
plugin packaging is generated from it under an explicit host-routing contract.
Exact parity is enforced for host-neutral bundle bytes and separately for
copies generated under the same host contract; different host adapters are
versioned and are not falsely required to be byte-identical.

## Goals

- Make the global run mission visible and authoritative in every provider
  invocation.
- Tell every agent why the current task exists, what the agent owns, what it
  must not own, and what valid completion means.
- Separate role identity from reusable procedures and from runtime policy.
- Adopt Agent Skills bundle structure and validation for production skills.
- Freeze the base context, role, skill, resource, and eval provenance with the
  run, then pin the exact durable authority-overlay head used by each
  invocation.
- Turn historical Chainworks failures into executable regression cases.
- Measure whether skill, context, workflow, model, or budget changes improve
  behavior relative to a frozen baseline.
- Let Steward detect and propose tuning work without allowing autonomous
  mutation of canonical production skills.

## Non-Goals

- Add new agent IDs or reviewer disciplines.
- Add a runtime feature-management system.
- Let a provider choose its own role, authority order, permissions, or required
  outputs.
- Make untrusted artifacts part of system instructions.
- Automatically merge Steward-generated prompt, skill, model, or catalog
  changes.
- Run live provider benchmarks in every ordinary pull-request gate.
- Rewrite active frozen runs to use the new context format.

## Stabilization-Freeze Alignment

The roadmap freeze prohibits speculative context experiments and new agent
roles. This design is a correctness migration for existing production agents,
not a new role family or an optional experiment.

- Existing agent IDs and workflow ownership remain unchanged.
- The catalog gains typed role charters for those existing IDs.
- The compiler and executor gain one mandatory context contract.
- Candidate tuning is evaluated outside production before promotion.
- No runtime switch can select the old path for a newly compiled production
  run.

## Core Model

### AuthorityChainV1

The immutable `RunPlanSnapshot` contains only the compile-time base authority
events and `base_authority_chain_head`. Post-start authority does not mutate or
replace that snapshot. Accepted mid-run directives and approval-derived
authority events live only in the separately protected release-authority
SQLite store. Candidate/control-plane SQLite contains signed readback
projections and pending cross-store operation references, never authority
events, heads, approval bindings, principal admissions, or fences that can
authorize execution.

Every base or overlay entry is an `AuthorityEventV1` containing:

- `schema_version = authority_event_v1` and `authority_event_id`;
- `run_id` and previous chain head;
- `source_kind`, limited to `operator_idea`, `operator_directive`,
  `approval_decision`, or `approved_proposal`;
- one closed `AuthorityDirectiveV1` value and its semantic digest;
- durable source record identifier, optional bounded anchor within that record,
  source ordinal, exact source digest, and revision identifier;
- sorted unique `supersedes` authority event IDs;
- creation and acceptance timestamps;
- authenticated principal ID, principal class, capability, and live principal
  table revision used for admission;
- `event_sha256`, which binds the canonical event bytes and previous head and is
  itself the resulting authority-chain head.

Review reports, implementation artifacts, tool output, provider prose, and
workspace files are evidence, not authority events. They cannot silently
supersede operator intent or an accepted approval decision.

The overlay uses two authoritative **release-authority-store** tables:

- `authority_run_events`, an append-only event ledger whose first overlay event
  points to the frozen `base_authority_chain_head`;
- `authority_run_heads`, one current head and monotonic `context_revision` per
  run.

Every append is one `ReleaseAuthorityOperationV1` with
`control_plane_effect = none`. The live gateway first derives principal class,
caller class, capability, token ID and PrincipalTable revision from the
reloadable auth boundary, then the authority coordinator purpose-signs an
`AuthorityOverlayAppendAdmissionV1` over that authorization fact, source
manifest, prior head/revision and proposed event. Finalize appends the event and
head, anchor receipt and same-store projection outbox in one predecessor-CAS
authority transition. A revoked, disabled or re-scoped principal cannot reach
prepare, and a control-plane row claiming another principal or table revision
is not an input to this operation.

The candidate database receives only `run_authority_event_projections`,
`run_authority_head_projections`, approval-binding projections and fence
projections, each carrying the finalized authority sequence, signed object and
outbox receipt. GraphQL, reports, Swift and filesystem artifacts are readback
only. Execution admission, approval settlement, prompt commit, broker effect
admission and retry read finalized signed authority objects directly or require
an `AuthorityReadbackWatermarkV1` proving the exact projection is current; none
accepts a projection as authority. Direct SQL insertion or mutation of an
event, head, principal, approval binding or fence therefore produces zero work
claim, provider launch, prompt, approval settlement or effect admission and is
covered by retained forgery fixtures.

#### Genesis and BaseAuthorityLedgerV1

The chain does not start from an empty string or an implementation-defined
constant. The compiler constructs one `AuthorityGenesisV1`:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "authority_genesis_v1",
  "installation_id": "...",
  "installation_root_public_key_sha256": "sha256:...",
  "authority_key_custody_profile_sha256": "sha256:...",
  "run_id": "...",
  "idea_id": "...",
  "workflow_snapshot_sha256": "sha256:...",
  "catalog_snapshot_sha256": "sha256:...",
  "authority_source_mapping_policy_sha256": "sha256:...",
  "authority_source_manifest_sha256s": ["sha256:..."],
  "run_context_binding_sha256": "sha256:...",
  "genesis_sha256": "sha256:..."
}
```

`genesis_sha256` is the domain-separated canonical digest of those fields
without itself. It is the previous head for the first base event. It does not
include the complete `RunPlanSnapshot` or `RunMissionV1`, so neither digest is
circular.

The frozen snapshot contains one `BaseAuthorityLedgerV1` with
`schema_version`, the complete `AuthorityGenesisV1`, an ordered `events` array,
`base_authority_chain_head`, and `base_ledger_sha256`. The base event order is
normative: `operator_idea` precedes `approved_proposal`; within each source,
events preserve the source adapter's zero-based `source_ordinal`; ties are
invalid rather than sorted heuristically. Every event's `previous_chain_head`
equals genesis or the immediately preceding event hash. The base head is the
last event hash, or genesis when the array is empty.

Base source adapters are versioned and deterministic. They emit a closed
mapping receipt from each source span to directive, conflict key, and ordinal.
The compiler system identity, `RunPlanCompile` capability, source record,
digest, revision, and adapter version are persisted on each base event. Rust
and Swift readers verify genesis, event order, every link, and the ledger
digest before exposing effective authority.

`runs.start` uses the generic cross-store authority operation; it never inserts
an authoritative head in control-plane SQLite. After preallocating the run ID
and frozen generation binding, the gateway computes the immutable
`CanonicalCommandOutcomeCoreV1` before allocating either writer. Authority
prepare binds that core, reserves the run ID and immutable genesis/base-ledger/
head tuple, creates the prepared run-admission transition and records expected `current_head =
base_authority_chain_head`, `context_revision = 0` and base-ledger digest. The
control-plane transaction inserts the Run, frozen base ledger, provisional
signed head projection, a projection/reference to the precomputed command-
outcome core and projection intent as
`pending_authority_finalize`. Authority finalize opens the committed database
through the trusted descriptor, byte-compares that tuple, inserts exactly one
canonical `authority_run_heads` row at revision zero, activates the immutable
run admission, appends the authority event/anchor and publishes the outbox.
Before finalize the Run may exist only as an unclaimable provisional row: it
cannot append an overlay, create owner/work truth, launch or return success.
Crash recovery resumes or aborts that same operation and cannot create a second
Run/head. A finalized run cannot exist without the canonical authority head,
and a direct control-plane head row remains nonauthoritative.

#### AuthoritySourceManifestV2

Production compilation never derives authority by interpreting Idea or
proposal prose. Each admitted source is normalized into one closed
`AuthoritySourceManifestV2` before `runs.start`. Its exact fields are
`schema_version = authority_source_manifest_v2`, source kind
`operator_idea | approved_proposal`, source ID, canonical source revision,
exact source-content digest, adapter ID/version, an ordered non-empty
`directive_mappings` array, and `authority_source_manifest_sha256`. Each
mapping contains a zero-based source ordinal, a stable source locator, one
complete `AuthorityDirectiveV1`, its conflict key, and a closed disposition
`active | superseded_in_source`. A locator is evidence only; the complete
directive bytes are the compiled truth.

The Idea adapter consumes one durable `idea_authority_source_v2` object stored
with the exact Idea revision and selected by `runs.start`, not arbitrary Idea
text. It has separate bounded fields for objective, ordered scope
includes/excludes, success criteria, execution constraints and priority; the
adapter maps each element to a documented conflict-key namespace and ordinal.
The proposal adapter consumes one checked-in
`proposal_authority_source_v2` sidecar whose approved revision digest equals
the separately stored proposal artifact selected by the approval. The sidecar
is not embedded in the bytes whose digest it names, so there is no digest
fixed point. Prose headings, Markdown list order and LLM extraction are never
fallback inputs. Missing sidecars, duplicate locators/ordinals/conflict keys,
unknown fields, or source-content digest drift fail before genesis or Run
insertion.

`AuthoritySourceMappingPolicyV2` is release-owned, carried in
`chainworks_signed_contract_v1`, pinned by the active evaluation trust policy
and candidate manifest, and pins both adapter builds, the exact Idea/proposal
source schemas, conflict-key derivation rules and the closed directive
enforcement registry. The ordered source-manifest digests and this policy
digest are bound by both `AuthorityGenesisV1` and
`RunContextGenerationBindingV2`; changing either requires a new compilation
and cannot reinterpret an existing base ledger. Every `hard` directive must
resolve to exactly one executable adapter and enforcement point:

- `objective` uses `prompt_objective_pin_v2` and fails prompt admission when
  the protected objective section is absent or digest-mismatched;
- `scope` uses `permission_scope_v2` and compiles deny/allow root, tool and
  effect capabilities checked before claim, launch and effect prepare;
- `success_criterion` uses `output_transition_assertion_v2` and gates terminal
  output/transition settlement;
- `execution_constraint` uses `runtime_constraint_v2` at the operation points
  declared by `RuntimeConstraintPolicyV2`;
- `priority` uses `scheduler_priority_v2` at claim ordering only.

`hard` is invalid when an adapter is absent, advisory-only, accepts a different
value shape, or lacks all declared enforcement hooks. Provider compliance is
never an enforcement adapter. Rust and Swift compile the same source manifests
through generated schema types and shared mapping fixtures; byte-identical
genesis, directives, conflict keys, base event order and normalized plan bytes
are required.

#### AuthorityDirectiveV1

Authority is not an arbitrary JSON document. `AuthorityDirectiveV1` is a
closed, unknown-field-denying tagged object:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "authority_directive_v1",
  "directive_kind": "execution_constraint",
  "conflict_key": "constraint.feature.p095.activation",
  "enforcement": "hard",
  "value": {
    "value_type": "boolean",
    "boolean_value": true
  },
  "directive_sha256": "sha256:..."
}
```

`directive_kind` is exactly one of `objective`, `scope`, `success_criterion`,
`execution_constraint`, or `priority`. `enforcement` is `hard` or `advisory`.
`conflict_key` is 1-128 lowercase ASCII characters matching
`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._:-]*` and identifies the single logical authority slot that
the directive writes. Include/exclude forms for the same scope subject use the
same key, so they cannot coexist accidentally.

`value` is tagged by `value_type` and contains exactly one of:

- `boolean_value`, a JSON Boolean;
- `integer_value`, an interoperable JSON integer;
- `string_value`, 1-4096 UTF-8 bytes after decoding;
- `string_list_value`, 1-64 strings of at most 512 UTF-8 bytes each, with
  duplicates rejected and order always preserved;
- `scope_value`, a closed `{ "disposition": "include" | "exclude",
  "subject": string }` object whose subject is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes.

The complete canonical directive is capped at 8 KiB. Nulls, unknown fields,
unknown enums, non-integer numbers, empty values, duplicate keys, and fields for
a different `value_type` are invalid. `directive_sha256` uses the canonical
digest contract below over only `schema_version`, `directive_kind`,
`conflict_key`, `enforcement`, and `value`; provenance belongs to the enclosing
event. It is therefore a stable semantic digest distinct from the event hash
and authority-chain head.

The value-kind matrix is closed:

| `directive_kind` | Allowed `value_type` | Required conflict-key prefix |
|---|---|---|
| `objective` | `string` | `objective.` |
| `scope` | `scope` | `scope.` |
| `success_criterion` | `string` or `boolean` | `success.` |
| `execution_constraint` | `boolean`, `integer`, `string`, or `string_list` | `constraint.` |
| `priority` | `integer` | `priority.` |

There are no implicit cross-key conflicts in V1. Source adapters must map one
logical subject to one stable key under the required prefix; normative source
mapping fixtures cover Idea, proposal, operator-directive, and approval inputs.
Different active values for one key are the complete V1 definition of a
contradiction. This avoids locale-, provider-, or prose-dependent conflict
inference.

For each `conflict_key`, zero or one event may be active. A first write requires
an empty `supersedes` list. Replacing a value requires `supersedes` to contain
exactly the currently active event for that key. An event cannot supersede an
inactive event or an event with another key. The closed directive-kind invariant
table validates value type and key prefix. Free-text semantic conflict judgement
is never delegated to a provider.

#### EffectiveAuthorityProjectionV1 and RuntimeConstraintPolicyV2

Authority becomes executable through two normative contracts, not through
prompt interpretation. `EffectiveAuthorityProjectionV1` binds the run, base
ledger, overlay head and decimal-string context revision; ordered active event
IDs/directive digests; effective mission digest; sorted hard and advisory
directive rows; resolved scheduler priority; runtime-policy digest; and
`effective_authority_sha256`. Every directive row retains conflict key, kind,
enforcement, value digest, source event, and the resolved policy-entry ID. The
projection contains no unbounded source prose.

`RuntimeConstraintPolicyV2` is a release-owned, versioned registry carried in
`chainworks_signed_contract_v1` and selected by the active evaluation trust
policy. The candidate records only that resolved digest and can neither author
nor choose the policy. Each
entry names one exact conflict key or bounded key family, directive kind and
value schema, allowed bounds, affected operation kinds, evaluation function,
enforcement points, and one closed supersession action:

- `next_claim_only` for scheduler priority;
- `reprepare_before_prompt` for constraints whose new value must be compiled
  into provider context;
- `cancel_before_prompt` for a newly prohibited provider invocation;
- `cancel_and_quarantine_after_prompt` when an already-sent prompt must not
  create further trusted output or effects;
- `deny_new_effects_allow_settlement` when existing observation may settle but
  no skill script, control-plane command, workspace write, Git, publish, or
  external side effect may begin.

A hard directive is invalid unless the source-mapping policy and exactly one
runtime-policy entry accept its kind, key, value and complete enforcement-point
set. Advisory directives may be displayed and included in the mission but never
grant permission or bypass a hard entry.
One policy contains at most 256 entries and one run at most 256 active conflict
keys; exceeding either cap fails the append before mutation. Historical events
remain append-only but active projection/readback is therefore bounded.
The Rust `RuntimeConstraintEvaluator` is the only production evaluator. It is
called by the unified execution-admission service for claim, spawn,
`provider_bound`, prompt commit, broker call, side-effect prepare/start,
settlement and retry. Provider output cannot reinterpret or waive its result.

Every authority-head append recomputes the complete projection in its
release-authority-store transaction. When any active hard row or its resolved policy effect changes,
the append also CAS-updates one run-level `AuthorityRecheckFenceV1` containing
old/new head, revision, projection digests, affected operation classes and
one bounded epoch/token per runtime operation class plus
`authority_fence_sha256`. Only classes selected by the changed policy entries
increment. This is O(1) durable fencing rather than an unbounded scan of active
attempts. Advisory-only changes increment no runtime class;
`next_claim_only` increments only the scheduler-claim class and atomically
updates queued priority, so neither cancels prepared work.

#### Authority append command

The only external mutation is operator-only MCP `runs.authority.append`. It is
not exposed as a GraphQL mutation. The command requires:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "run_authority_append_request_v1",
  "idempotency_key": "lowercase UUIDv7",
  "run_id": "...",
  "caller_request_id": "lowercase UUIDv4",
  "expected_authority_chain_head": "sha256:...",
  "directive": {
    "schema_version": "authority_directive_v1",
    "directive_kind": "execution_constraint",
    "conflict_key": "constraint.feature.p095.activation",
    "enforcement": "hard",
    "value": { "value_type": "boolean", "boolean_value": true },
    "directive_sha256": "sha256:..."
  },
  "supersedes": []
}
```

The MCP adapter stamps `source_kind = operator_directive` and the durable
authority exact-request source record; neither is accepted from request JSON. Both
external directives and approval-derived events enter one Rust
`AuthorityAdmissionService`; repositories expose no lower-level public append.
The service reads the live principal table and applies this closed authorization
matrix before revealing run or head existence:

| Source | Required caller | Required capability | Additional provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operator_directive` | authenticated `PrincipalClass::Operator` | `RunsAuthorityAppend` | MCP tool must be `runs.authority.append` and caller class is boundary-derived |
| `approval_decision` | authenticated `PrincipalClass::Operator` that settled the approval | `ApprovalsResolve` | non-forgeable authority-store approval settlement ID/digest and finalized operation |
| `operator_idea` or `approved_proposal` base event | run compiler system identity | `RunPlanCompile` | frozen source digest and signed compile admission |

`approval_decision` is not a second write path. Approval settlement calls the
same authority admission service with a purpose-signed operation capability
bound to the authenticated approval command, principal, run, approval, and
decision. The authority append, approval-binding transition, canonical
approval settlement, command outcome, audit rows and projection outbox commit
in one release-authority-store pending-anchor transaction. A caller-supplied source kind,
principal ID, capability, approval ID, or system identity is ignored or rejected
rather than trusted.

#### ApprovalAuthorityBindingV1

An authority-bearing approval freezes one `ApprovalAuthorityTemplateV1` and its
first `ApprovalAuthorityBindingV1` in the same authority operation that creates
the canonical approval; candidate SQLite receives only their signed
projections. The template binds approval ID, run ID, approval schema, presentation
payload digest, and a closed decision map independent of an authority head.
Every allowed decision maps either to one complete canonical
`AuthorityDirectiveV1` plus its conflict key, or to the explicit value
`no_authority_effect`. The template is immutable and has
`approval_authority_template_sha256`; approval prose is never reparsed during
binding or settlement.

Each binding is a durable generation that adds canonical decimal-string
`binding_generation`, the authority head observed at presentation, the exact
active event each authority-bearing decision would supersede, lifecycle state,
predecessor binding digest, presentation revision, and
`approval_authority_binding_sha256`. The decision map, heads, predecessor and
presentation revision never change after insertion. Lifecycle state is exactly
`presented`, `rebound`, `settlement_reserved`, `stale`, `superseded`, or
`settled` and changes only by
CAS; each state transition retains the prior binding digest in an append-only
lifecycle event before storing the digest for the new state. Only the current
generation in `presented | rebound` is actionable.

A run may have at most 128 pending authority-bound approvals. Approval creation
that would exceed the cap fails before presentation. The indexed set processed
by an authority append is therefore bounded, and the append transaction must
visit exactly the recorded pending count before it can commit.

Every authority-head append transaction processes all still-pending bound
approvals for that run before it commits. For each approval it marks the prior
current generation `stale` and inserts exactly one successor under a unique
`(approval_id, authority_chain_head)` constraint:

- when all conflict keys referenced by the decision map retained the same
  active event, the successor is `rebound`, keeps the template, binds the new
  head, and remains actionable;
- when any referenced active event changed, the successor is `superseded`,
  contains no actionable decision bindings, sets the approval to
  `reissue_required`, and cannot settle or admit work.

The approval being settled is not part of that rebind set. Settlement has one
closed order inside the pending-anchor authority transaction: validate the
selected current binding at head `H`; CAS it to `settlement_reserved` and
remove it from the pending-approval index; apply the selected decision and,
only when authority-bearing, derive `H -> H2`; visit exactly the remaining
recorded pending count and rebind/supersede those approvals to `H2`; then append
the selected binding's terminal `settled` event, canonical approval outcome and
the complete projection outbox set. The selected generation retains `H` as its
presented head and records `H2` as settlement head; it is never made stale or
rebound to the head created by its own decision. A `no_authority_effect`
decision keeps `H2 = H` and performs no unrelated rebind. Crash or conflict at
any point exposes none of these rows as finalized, and recovery resumes the
same reserved settlement rather than re-presenting the approval.

Operator-only `approvals.reissue` is the sole transition from the current
`superseded` generation. It requires the expected generation/digest and current
authority head, rereads the immutable template, resolves every decision against
the current active set, and inserts one next `rebound` generation with an
incremented presentation revision. Reissue does not approve, reject, append
authority, or enqueue work; it only republishes the now-current consequences for
operator review. A concurrent head change or duplicate reissue allows one CAS
winner. The loser receives replay or a stale-binding error and never creates a
second current generation.

`approvals.resolve_authority` for a bound approval requires the lowercase UUIDv4 caller
request ID, approval ID, decision, `binding_generation`,
`approval_authority_binding_sha256`, and `expected_authority_chain_head`. The
generation must be current and `presented | rebound`; its head must equal both
current release-authority-store truth and the head required by the selected mapping. The
internal transaction capability carries the authenticated principal and live
principal table revision from the boundary. In one transaction the service
validates the binding and prepares one authority-only
`ReleaseAuthorityOperationV1`. Finalize performs the ordered target-settle,
authority-head and remaining-binding CAS defined above,
appends the derived event when the mapping is authority-bearing, marks the
authority binding `settled`, stores the canonical approval settlement and
command outcome, and emits one signed complete projection outbox set in the
same pending-anchor transition. That outbox may contain an immutable
owner-materialization request, but it never contains a child work admission.
The request is consumed only by the owner-materialization chain below:
`owner prepare -> candidate rows -> snapshot receipt -> authority finalize`.
Only that finalize may sign and publish the initial child work admissions.
Candidate SQLite may later project the settlement and owner-materialization
request; it does not settle the approval, derive work, or make any child row
claimable. Any failure changes none of those authority rows. An unbound, stale,
superseded, or
`no_authority_effect` decision cannot append an event.

MCP `approvals.authority.get` and the GraphQL `Approval.authorityBinding` field
return the same `ApprovalAuthorityReadbackV1`: approval/template IDs and
digests, current binding generation/digest/state, presented and current heads,
presentation revision, sorted allowed decisions, `reissue_required`,
projection health and the complete current signed
`AuthorityReadbackWatermarkV1` envelope/digest. MCP returns those exact signed
bytes, GraphQL exposes the same `signedContractBase64url` and typed projection,
and Swift verifies and retains the byte-identical envelope. They expose no
directive value or inactive binding history.
Both surfaces are Operator-only; existing non-Operator approval/report
redaction remains unchanged. The ordinary approval list includes only bounded
current-binding summary fields so the UI can submit resolve or reissue without
guessing a head or digest.

The semantic intent hash binds `run_id`, expected head, the adapter-derived
source kind, `directive_sha256`, and the sorted `supersedes` set; it excludes
both transport and caller request IDs.
`caller_request_id` uses the existing `command_idempotency` and
`command_request_aliases` contract. The closed precedence is:

1. the same principal/request ID and same intent returns the stored response;
2. the same principal/request ID with different intent fails with
   `command_idempotency_conflict`;
3. a different request ID for the same principal, command, and complete intent
   replays the committed outcome and records a request alias;
4. absent a replay, a stale expected head fails with
   public `stale_precondition` and internal reason `authority_head_conflict`;
5. at the current head, a directive digest that is already active and does not
   perform the required replacement fails with public `semantic_duplicate` and
   internal reason `authority_duplicate_event`;
6. concurrent appends against one head allow exactly one complete transaction
   to commit; the loser observes replay, head conflict, or in-flight status
   according to the preceding rows.

Thus repeating the original request with its original expected head is an
alias replay, while submitting the same directive again against the new current
head is a semantic duplicate. Append event, head CAS, command outcome, audit,
and projection outbox commit in one release-authority-store transaction before
anchor finalization.

An append that violates the per-key supersession rule or produces two active
values for one conflict key fails with public `stale_precondition` and internal
reason `agent_context_authority_conflict`. Rust and Swift reconstruct the active set by
verifying the hash chain, applying events in chain order, and replacing only the
declared conflict key. Shared vectors make the resulting ordered active-event
IDs and effective authority bytes normative.

#### Owner occurrence and work-admission linearization

Before any child work exists, the `execution_reducer_controller` derives one
immutable `ExecutionOwnerOccurrenceV1` from a closed origin union. The
`workflow_state` origin binds the frozen normalized plan, workflow state,
state-occurrence ordinal, loop generation and finalized parent transition. The
`terminal_run_hook` origin binds the finalized terminal Run event, frozen
Steward policy/configuration digest and fixed hook ordinal one and forbids every
workflow-state/loop/parent-transition field. The `steward_command` origin binds
the finalized `steward.run_analysis` command journal, frozen reason `manual` or
an explicitly commanded `config_change`, active Steward configuration revision
and server-resolved artifact/cohort scope and forbids every workflow-state,
loop and terminal-Run-hook field. The distinct `steward_config_change` origin
binds the approved-HEAD automatic path's pending previous/current Steward
configuration and catalog hashes, exact work-item/enqueue identity and daemon
observation revision; it forbids a command-journal field and every workflow or
terminal-hook field. Its tagged owner reference is
exactly one of
`stage_execution { stage_occurrence_id, stage_execution_id }` or
`lead_conflict_mediation { mediation_id }` or
`steward_analysis { steward_analysis_id }`. Stage and mediation require the
`workflow_state` origin. Steward reason `post_run_hook` requires
`terminal_run_hook`; `manual` and command-triggered `config_change` require
`steward_command`; automatic `config_change` requires
`steward_config_change`. Every arm also binds a closed scope of exact `run` or
`installation_steward`, owner reducer/version, one required
`system_steward` child semantic key, one conditional `steward_auditor` child
semantic key and child cardinality range zero through two. The conditional key
can become eligible only from the signed terminal health-report artifact of the
required child. The authority-store unique key is
`(owner_scope_kind, owner_scope_id, owner_origin_kind, owner_origin_key,
owner_kind, owner_id)`, where the origin key is the state occurrence, terminal
Run event, canonical Steward command digest or automatic config-change tuple
digest. An append-only
`ExecutionOwnerOccurrenceTransitionV1` carries predecessor revision/digest and
state `available | materialization_pending | active | settled | canceled |
revoked`.

Owner materialization and child issuance use one predecessor-linked
`ReleaseAuthorityOperationV1`. Authority prepare reserves the owner key and all
derived child semantic keys; one candidate control-plane transaction may then
insert the matching StageExecution or mediation projection and child work rows
as `pending_authority_finalize`. For `steward_analysis`, the same transaction
instead inserts the matching `steward_analyses` owner projection and its one
analysis work row from the finalized terminal Run event, frozen Steward command
or automatic config-change origin; it never fabricates a
StageExecution, mediation or AgentExecution ID. The controller obtains the one-use
`ControlPlaneSqliteSnapshotReceiptV1` for that committed transaction and
verifies every ID/cardinality/owner binding from its immutable snapshot,
then authority finalize advances the owner transition to `active`, issues the
immutable child work admissions and publishes the signed outbox. Until that
finalize, no row is claimable. Recovery continues or aborts the same operation;
it never derives a second stage occurrence from row absence or timestamps.
This is the only legal initial-work issuance path. Approval settlement and the
generic admission controller can request owner materialization, but neither may
sign, publish, or project an initial child admission independently. Exact replay
returns the same owner occurrence, operation, snapshot receipt, admission set
and outbox-set digests; a competing materializer either joins that operation or
receives `stale_precondition` with zero rows made claimable.

Approved HEAD's independent `WorkItemKind::StewardAnalysis` producer and public
reasons `manual`, `post_run_hook`, and `config_change` are explicit seal-time
migration sources, not grandfathered launch paths. A generated
`StewardOwnerSchemaMigrationManifestV1` inventories and rebuilds every
owner-kind/keyed table, CHECK/foreign-key/unique constraint, index, repository
query and projection at approved HEAD, including `agent_executions`,
`agent_retry_budget_ledger`, `artifact_source_generation_claims`, Steward work
items/analyses/run links/recommendations and their joins. The rebuild admits
`steward_analysis`, preserves every stage/mediation row byte-for-byte, makes
stage-only fields conditionally null, and is exact-set checked against the live
SQLite schema before seal; an omitted owner-keyed surface holds migration.

Before `legacy_execution_sealed`, the mapping inventory covers every queued,
claimed, running and terminal Steward work item plus its `steward_analyses` row,
trigger reason, command/config or terminal-Run origin, provider-session/call,
output and recommendation artifacts. `post_run_hook` maps only to its uniquely
linked finalized terminal Run event. `manual` and command-triggered
`config_change` map to their unique committed command journal and frozen
config/artifact scope. Approved-HEAD automatic `config_change` rows instead map
from their exact pending previous/current config and catalog hashes, work-item/
enqueue identity and daemon observation; migration never invents a command or
command journal. A coherent zero-call analysis maps to one owner plus its
orchestration/admission record and no `AgentExecution`. A one-call analysis maps
the stored `system_steward` call to one child `AgentExecution` with attempt
generation one. A coherent two-call analysis maps the first stored call to a
`system_steward` child generation-one attempt and the second to a distinct
`steward_auditor` child generation-one attempt whose admission is linked to the
first child's signed terminal health-report artifact. The two calls are never
attempt generations of one execution, and migration never relaunches either
recorded call. Missing reason/origin, more than two calls, wrong agent order,
two calls without the health-report dependency, duplicate, orphaned or
synthetic-ID-requiring combinations hold the seal. Already-terminal
rows map directly to terminal settlements without relaunch. Crash before or
after every schema-rebuild/owner/admission/attempt/finalize boundary resumes the
same migration/mapping receipts. After seal, the old work-item dispatcher cannot
claim Steward work; new post-run analyses use `terminal_run_hook`, manual and
command-triggered config-change analyses use `steward_command`, and automatic
config-change analyses use `steward_config_change`, all through the
`steward_analysis_v1` reducer. The automatic path preserves its pending hashes
and enqueue identity and never fabricates `steward.run_analysis` history.

The sole authority linearization point for an attempt generation is finalizing
the matching `ExecutableWorkAdmissionTransitionV1` from `claim_pending` to
`claimed` against its predecessor reducer checkpoint. Candidate dispatch
materialization, queue claim and prompt preparation are later projections of
that decision and are not independent authority linearization points.

#### Per-invocation pinning

One logical `AgentExecution` may own multiple attempts. The immutable identity
is `AgentExecutionAttemptV1 { agent_execution_id, attempt_generation }`; every
dispatch, grant, prompt, receipt, projection entity and artifact path uses both
components. `attempt_generation` starts at one and increments by CAS. No retry
overwrites or reuses bytes from an earlier attempt.

The authority-store `ExecutionReducerCheckpointV2` is canonical attempt-
selection and owner-reduction truth. The control-plane `AgentExecution` row is
an operational projection that stores the signed checkpoint digest,
`current_attempt_generation`, `attempt_state_revision`, optional
`settled_attempt_generation`, and optional
`canonical_execution_outcome_sha256`; candidate code cannot make that row
authoritative by updating it directly. Creating an attempt uses the generic
cross-store authority operation: an immutable signed work-admission transition
first reserves the next generation, the control-plane transaction inserts the
matching unique `(agent_execution_id, attempt_generation)` row and dispatch
intent as `pending_authority_finalize`, and authority finalize CASes the
predecessor checkpoint plus `claim_pending -> claimed` before that pointer
becomes claimable. Concurrent prepare or retry callers therefore finalize
exactly one next generation. An
older generation may append bounded terminal, late-output, process-reap, or
quarantine evidence, but cannot launch, commit a prompt or effect, settle the
parent, or update an owner reduction after the signed checkpoint advances.

Only a signed terminal settlement of the current generation may advance the
canonical checkpoint to an outcome and project `settled_attempt_generation`.
`StageExecution` and Run status reduce from signed child and owner settlements,
never by scanning candidate rows for the newest-looking attempt. Retry after a
lost provider or broker response first reconciles the prior generation's
process and authority-owned logical-effect registries; only then may one
successor admission be issued. Recovery uses the same authority operation and
cannot infer a current attempt from timestamps, paths, or provider session
state.

Every terminal attempt is represented by one immutable purpose-signed
`AgentExecutionAttemptSettlementV1`. It binds the attempt, work-admission and
latest admission-transition digests, prior reducer checkpoint/revision, exact
dispatch/process/provider state, the immutable `ProviderPromptSeriesV2`
identity plus terminal `ProviderPromptSeriesStateV2` head, one terminal
`AgentOutputSettlementV2`, complete
process-clearance, the immutable `EffectSlotAttemptTerminalSetV2`, slot-owned
effect-terminal receipts and terminal auxiliary-occurrence transitions,
terminal reason/outcome, and controller component/build/key epoch. It never
contains an `AttemptSuccessorEligibilityV1` digest or any field derived from
that later object. One signed
`AgentExecutionOwnerSettlementV1` binds owner kind/ID/reducer version, the exact
sorted child settlement digests, prior owner checkpoint/revision and resulting
owner state/outcome. Candidate rows, timestamps, provider prose and unsigned
receipts cannot substitute for either settlement.

`AgentOutputSettlementV2` is the closed authority truth for output handling. It
binds the attempt and complete prompt series; terminal provider response and
request-turn correlation; the required output-contract and artifact inventory;
the exact materialization/projection receipts; and exactly one source
`original_turn`, `same_session_repair`, `bounded_transcript_recovery`,
`provider_envelope_recovery`, `resurrection_output_only`, or `none`. Its terminal
outcome is exactly `valid_completed`, `valid_failed`, `valid_repair`,
`missing_required`, `invalid_required`, `late_output_quarantined`, or
`no_output_expected`. Repair and recovery arms bind their P079 repair lease,
permission decision, transcript/provider-envelope attribution and recovery flag.
The resurrection arm binds its P086 attach receipt, prompt marker, provider
session/request-turn identity and pre/post source-edit proof. The late-output arm
binds cancellation epoch and quarantine receipt and can never carry accepted
artifact bytes. The current `AgentOutputSettlement` enum maps exhaustively into
these arms during migration; a missing, unknown, contradictory or uncorrelated
legacy combination holds rather than becoming `none`. Attempt settlement cannot
finalize until this object and every output projection are terminal.

Effect-slot completeness is explicit even when the provider never asks to use
an optional slot. Claim finalization creates an active
`EffectSlotAttemptClaimSetV2` containing every assignment-owned slot for that
attempt. Its only nonterminal row states are `available`, `claimed`, and
`joined_existing`; it cannot be created while a prior slot claim or effect
attempt is nonterminal or ambiguous. Claiming a slot is one authority CAS that
both creates or joins the unique `(agent_execution_id, effect_slot_id)`
occurrence/registry row and advances the current-attempt claim row.

An external-effect logical identity is stable across execution retries, but
each permitted effect retry is a new immutable
`SkillScriptEffectAttemptV1`. The first claim creates revision one. Only a
signed terminal `failed_no_effect`, or `failed_reconciled` whose reconciliation
receipt proves no external effect, may authorize a successor transition under
the same logical effect and immutable intent. That transition allocates a new
lowercase UUIDv7 `effect_attempt_id`, sets `effect_attempt_revision = prior +
1`, binds the predecessor attempt and terminal receipt, and rechecks the frozen
retry policy, admitted failure code and remaining budget before it consumes the
predecessor's `eligible_retry_no_effect` successor row and creates the
successor attempt's `claimed` active row. A committed/completed effect, an
ambiguous or reconciliation-required effect, a policy-denied effect and an
exhausted effect are irreversible and always become `reused_terminal`; no new
effect attempt can follow them. Exact request replay always returns the
original terminal effect-attempt result and never performs the retry transition.

Attempt settlement atomically fences that attempt generation and derives one
immutable `EffectSlotAttemptTerminalSetV2`. Every row is irreversible and is
exactly `not_requested_terminal`, `completed_terminal`,
`failed_no_effect_terminal`, `failed_reconciled_no_effect_terminal`,
`reused_completed_terminal`, or `retired_without_effect_terminal`; no row named
`available`, `retry_available`, `carried_forward_available`, `claimed`, or
`joined_existing` is legal in a terminal set. Every claimed/joined row binds one
terminal effect-attempt receipt. A concurrent late claim and settlement have one
CAS winner: after the settlement fence, the old attempt can never claim a slot.

Only after that terminal set is finalized may the reducer derive a separate
`AttemptSuccessorEligibilityV1`. It binds the terminal attempt/settlement,
retry policy and budget and contains one `EffectSlotSuccessorEligibilitySetV1`
whose rows are exactly `eligible_unclaimed`, `eligible_retry_no_effect`, or
`reuse_irreversible_terminal`. This object is consumed by at most one successor
work-admission finalize and never mutates or re-labels the predecessor's
terminal set. A missing or ineligible object means no successor. When the owner
becomes terminal, the same owner-settlement transaction fences every globally
unclaimed slot as never requestable, so no later attempt or delayed provider call
can create an effect. Zero-use, partial-use, all-use, retry carry-forward,
terminal-reuse and claim-versus-settlement races are retained fixtures.
The signed dependency order is strictly
`EffectSlotAttemptTerminalSetV2 -> AgentExecutionAttemptSettlementV1 ->
AttemptSuccessorEligibilityV1 -> successor executable-work admission`.
No digest edge points backward, and generated dependency-graph plus crash
vectors reject a settlement containing eligibility, eligibility without its
terminal settlement, or a successor admission that consumes anything other
than the one post-settlement eligibility object.

The parent state machine is closed:

```text
pending --create attempt 1--> active
active --signed retryable attempt settlement--> retry_admitted
retry_admitted --claim finalized successor admission--> active(new generation)
active --current attempt canonical success--> settled_success
active --current attempt exhausted/terminal failure--> settled_failure
pending|active --owner cancellation--> canceled
active --unresolved process/effect/identity invariant--> quarantined
quarantined --typed clearance plus signed attempt settlement--> retry_admitted | settled_failure
```

`settled_success`, `settled_failure`, and `canceled` are terminal parent states.
`quarantined` is a durable no-attempt hold and can be cleared only by the
separately named process/effect reconciliation command. Clearance never returns
the same attempt to `active`: one authority finalize transaction consumes the
hold/clearance, writes the terminal attempt settlement, advances the predecessor
checkpoint and either creates exactly one successor work admission in
`retry_admitted` or settles the parent failure. The successor is unclaimable
until that transaction is anchored. An attempt itself follows
`prepared -> launching -> provider_bound -> prompt_committed -> settling ->
completed | failed_no_effect | failed_reconciled | canceled | quarantined`.
Successor creation is permitted only from current `failed_no_effect`,
`failed_reconciled`, or pre-prompt `canceled` after all process/effect truth is
terminal. A prompt-committed, superseded, noncurrent or quarantined attempt
cannot create a successor or settle the parent. Parent-state revision,
generation, predecessor attempt/admission-transition digests, attempt settlement
and reconciliation-set digest are one authority CAS.

Every `AgentExecution` has closed `owner_kind = stage_execution |
lead_conflict_mediation | steward_analysis`, immutable `owner_id`,
`owner_occurrence_sha256`, tagged owner-origin kind/key, conditional workflow
state-occurrence or Steward-command fields and an owner-reducer version.
`stage_execution_v2` reduces the canonical outcomes of exactly the child
executions registered to that stage. `lead_conflict_mediation_v2` reduces the
designated lead execution into the owning `lead_conflict_mediations` record and
its settlement/confirmation state; it never writes a nullable or unrelated
StageExecution. `steward_analysis_v1` reduces exactly one Steward agent
execution into the preallocated `steward_analyses` owner row and recommendation/
experiment artifact set; it is triggered only by its bound terminal Run event
or finalized manual/config-change Steward command, cannot reopen or mutate a
Run, cannot promote production inputs and never
falls back to a stage or mediation reducer. Owner settlement, attempt settlement and successor-or-terminal
checkpoint commit in one authority transaction, after which the signed
projection outbox updates control-plane owner/readback rows. Adding another
owner kind requires a new reducer, migration,
recovery matrix and nonzero gate; unknown owners quarantine instead of falling
back to stage reduction.

#### Auxiliary execution occurrences

Existing externally visible operations do not remain a parallel candidate-owned
truth after V2 cutover. The authority-store
`ExecutionAuxiliaryOccurrenceV2` is one immutable tagged union whose
`occurrence_kind` is exactly `external_effect`, `provider_continuation`, or
`lead_mediation_confirmation`. Every arm binds run, owner occurrence,
conditional agent execution/current attempt, frozen authority/generation and a
stable logical key. Its predecessor-linked
`ExecutionAuxiliaryOccurrenceTransitionV2` is purpose-signed by
`execution_admission_controller`; candidate side-effect, continuation and
mediation tables are projections only. Attempt and owner settlement include
the exact sorted terminal auxiliary-transition digests, and cannot finalize
while an occurrence is nonterminal or omitted.

The `external_effect` arm replaces the authoritative role of the existing
generic side-effect ledger for `github_commit_push` and `connect_publisher`.
It requires an `agent_execution_id` and the assignment's matching
`EffectSlotDeclarationV2.external_effect` arm. The occurrence copies and
verifies its closed effect kind, operation class and release-owned target-
resolver-policy digest before any target is resolved; candidate/provider input
cannot supply or override a target. Its sole authority unique claim is exactly
`(agent_execution_id, effect_slot_id)`, and its stable logical key is derived
only from those immutable assignment-owned identities. The first claim stores
one immutable effect intent containing operation class, normalized target set,
resolver/precondition and payload digests. A later request for the slot must
byte-match that intent; changed target, operation or payload is zero-dispatch
`external_effect_intent_conflict` and cannot allocate another occurrence. Attempt,
request, process and provider session are audit fields only. Its closed lifecycle is
`available -> prepared -> dispatched -> observing -> settled`, with
`prepared -> failed_no_effect` only after verified no dispatch and
`dispatched | observing -> reconciliation_hold -> settled | failed_reconciled`.
The first external-boundary receipt is committed before dispatch; recovery
queries the existing remote-effect identity and never sends a second commit,
push or publication. A new attempt reuses the same occurrence and terminal
receipt rather than allocating another effect. Exact request replay returns the
original occurrence/receipt even when the current attempt changed.

The `provider_continuation` arm is the V2 owner of every P086
`agents.continue_work` mode, including live-handle continuation,
provider-session resurrection and output-only recovery. It binds the existing
continuation ID, parent execution/current attempt, adapter-declared capability,
requested and observed provider-session lineage, prompt marker/fingerprint,
continuation instruction digest, worktree evidence scope and one stable
`continuation_prompt_effect_id`. Its transitions use the closed V2 vocabulary
and legacy mapping below; only authority-signed transitions are admission
truth. `prompt_sent` is produced only by the authority-owned prompt gateway
using a `ProviderPromptTurnReservationV2` additionally bound to this
continuation occurrence and its predecessor prompt turn; crash/replay
reconciles that same stable turn effect and cannot send a second copy.
Attach/resurrection receipts, terminal provider correlation and
output-only source evidence are required settlement inputs. Only one current
continuation occurrence may exist for one parent execution/attempt and logical
instruction; a successor is possible only after the predecessor is terminal
and the parent reducer remains current.

The `lead_mediation_confirmation` arm binds mediation and confirmation IDs,
the immutable allowed-decision set, presentation digest and current mediation
owner transition. Its lifecycle is `presented -> settlement_reserved ->
settled | superseded`. `ResolveLeadMediationConfirmation` is an authority-only
operation: it exact-replays by principal/request and semantic decision, appends
the confirmation transition and matching mediation owner settlement in one
pending-anchor transaction, and can neither settle a StageExecution nor create
a second confirmation. Mediation owner reduction cannot complete from the old
control-plane confirmation row alone.

The V2 continuation transition vocabulary is closed rather than inherited by
prose: `available`, `queued`, `starting`, `preflight_passed`,
`running_pre_prompt`, `prompt_send_reserved`, `prompt_send_started`,
`prompt_sent`, `observing`, `worktree_observed`, `reconciliation_hold`,
`finalizing`, `cancelling_pre_prompt`, `cancelling_after_prompt`, `succeeded`,
`no_progress`, `failed_no_prompt`, `failed_after_prompt`,
`cancelled_no_prompt`, `cancelled_after_prompt`, or `failed_reconciled`.
Migration first reduces the complete legacy side-effect ledger, then maps the
legacy continuation status with this exhaustive table:

| Legacy continuation status | Required legacy provider-send evidence | V2 transition |
|---|---|---|
| `accepted` | no `started`/`committed` provider send | `available` |
| `queued` | no `started`/`committed` provider send | `queued` |
| `starting` | no started external boundary; otherwise apply the ledger override below | `starting` |
| `running` | no `started`/`committed` provider send; otherwise apply the ledger override | `running_pre_prompt` |
| `preflight_passed` | no `started`/`committed` provider send | `preflight_passed` |
| `prompt_sent` | exactly one matching `provider_send = committed` | `prompt_sent` with consumed stable prompt effect |
| `observing` | exactly one matching `provider_send = committed` | `observing` |
| `worktree_observed` | exactly one matching `provider_send = committed` | `worktree_observed` |
| `needs_continuation_reconciliation` | any bounded ledger shape, preserved in full | `reconciliation_hold` |
| `finalizing` | committed send or signed terminal no-prompt branch | `finalizing` |
| `cancelling` | no send started/committed, or exactly one committed send | `cancelling_pre_prompt` or `cancelling_after_prompt` respectively |
| `succeeded` | exactly one committed send plus terminal provider/worktree evidence | `succeeded` |
| `no_progress` | signed zero-send terminal evidence or one committed send plus terminal no-progress evidence | `no_progress` with explicit `prompt_effect_consumed` Boolean |
| `failed` | signed zero-send failure or one committed send plus terminal/quarantine evidence | `failed_no_prompt` or `failed_after_prompt` |
| `cancelled` | signed zero-send cancellation or one committed send plus cancellation/late-output settlement | `cancelled_no_prompt` or `cancelled_after_prompt` |

For every legacy ledger row, `planned` proves no boundary call only when no
matching worker/process observation exists; `started` without a conclusive
remote observation maps to `reconciliation_hold`; `committed` preserves the
original request/response fingerprints and consumed effect; `released` binds
its release receipt; and `failed` maps to a no-effect terminal only with signed
zero-effect evidence, otherwise to `reconciliation_hold`. A committed
`provider_session_attach` must bind the migrated attach receipt; a started
attach without that receipt holds. Runtime/worktree lease rows preserve owner,
epoch and release evidence; an unreleased or PID-ambiguous lease holds.
`provider_cancel` planned/started/committed rows map respectively to cancellation
pending, reconciliation hold, or observed cancellation. Any duplicate sequence,
unknown kind/state, impossible status/ledger combination, mismatched fingerprint
or committed send without a prompt marker blocks seal.

The migration inventory is exhaustive for every P086-owned row family, not only
the continuation status and generic side-effect ledger. For each continuation it
must contain exactly one source disposition for: the continuation row and full
status history; the closed `ResurrectionPhase`; admission and observation
deadlines with durable clock-baseline correlation; supervised provider process
registration, PID-birth identity, process state and cancellation epoch; runtime
and worktree leases; the terminal continuation ledger; provider-send rows;
provider-session attach/resurrection receipts including the raw attach receipt
and its sanitized projection; prompt marker, request fingerprint and request-
turn correlation; output-only source evidence; and terminal provider/worktree
settlement evidence. The signed `LegacyContinuationMappingReceiptV1` binds
the complete sorted source-row digest inventory, every resulting auxiliary-
occurrence transition and every preserved receipt/projection digest.

The migration consumes that complete inventory in one cross-store operation.
A legacy committed send can only materialize a consumed `prompt_sent` effect;
it can never create an available prompt reservation. Missing, duplicate,
unknown, cross-continuation or impossible combinations, including a raw attach
receipt without its sanitized projection or a resurrection phase without its
process/deadline truth, enter a typed migration hold and block
`legacy_execution_sealed`. Crash/restart fixtures cover all fifteen legacy
statuses, all five ledger states for every ledger kind, every resurrection
phase, each deadline/process/receipt family and every pre/post candidate-commit
and authority-finalize boundary. They prove byte-stable mapping replay and
exactly one consumed continuation prompt.

Before `legacy_execution_sealed`, the migration inventory must classify every
nonterminal generic side-effect row, P086 continuation/provider-send row and
lead-mediation confirmation. A row is either converted once into a signed
auxiliary occurrence preserving its original IDs, ledger/receipt/history and
remote-effect identity, or terminally rejected/settled with signed evidence.
Unknown, duplicate or ambiguous rows hold cutover. After seal, repository
writers for all three legacy lifecycles require an authority occurrence
transition and cannot advance a candidate row directly. Fault matrices crash
before/after every dispatch, prompt and confirmation boundary and prove one
effect, one continuation prompt and one confirmation settlement.

Every attempt owns one durable `InvocationDispatchIntentV2`. Its `prepared` row
pins these fields before any provider process can exist:

- run ID, stage/task ID, agent execution ID, attempt generation, and logical
  invocation idempotency key;
- immutable run snapshot hash, run context generation, candidate manifest and
  promotion receipt digests, and base authority head;
- overlay `authority_chain_head` and `context_revision`;
- effective mission, effective-authority projection, runtime-constraint policy,
  authority-fence digest, and every policy-selected operation-class fence token;
- role, assignment, ordered aggregate skill, prompt-envelope manifest, and exact
  spooled prompt-byte digests;
- provider profile, adapter, model, effort, permission profile, and session
  binding fingerprint;
- dispatch state, lease owner/epoch/deadline, and bounded process/session
  identity fields.

#### Authority-owned prompt delivery linearization

Candidate code never writes provider prompt bytes directly. Each attempt owns
one immutable `ProviderPromptSeriesV2` identity with the exact active
`ProviderPromptTurnBudgetPolicyV1`, per-purpose and independently configured
aggregate ceilings, closed permitted purposes `initial`, `continuation`,
`same_session_repair`, or `resurrection_output_only`, and revision-zero
`ProviderPromptSeriesStateV2`. The identity never changes. Every ordinal,
consumed counter and reservation head lives in an immutable predecessor-linked
series-state snapshot. For every turn the release-authority
`provider_prompt_gateway` creates at most one
immutable `ProviderPromptTurnReservationV2` under both unique
`(agent_execution_id, attempt_generation, prompt_turn_ordinal)` and unique
`prompt_effect_id`. Turn one has purpose `initial` and no predecessor. Every
later turn binds the immediately preceding reservation/terminal transition,
provider request-turn identity and the purpose-specific P079/P086 occurrence;
skipped ordinals, two current turns and a repair/continuation without a terminal
predecessor are invalid. The reservation also binds the finalized work
admission, reducer checkpoint, provider process/session and binding receipt,
exact spooled prompt bytes/digest/length, current authority head/revision,
prompt operation-class fence token, issue/deadline and gateway identity. Its
predecessor-linked transition lifecycle is exactly:

The release-owned turn policy is frozen into the Run/attempt admission before
turn one. It declares exactly one initial-turn slot, a positive bounded
continuation ceiling derived from the frozen workflow/assignment within the
release maximum, and independent P079 same-session-repair and P086
resurrection-output-only ceilings derived from those frozen policy revisions.
The aggregate ceiling is an independent release-owned positive value no greater
than the checked sum of the four purpose ceilings; this allows a mixed-purpose
sequence to exhaust aggregate budget while each purpose still has capacity. A
candidate, provider response or retry command cannot raise or transfer either
budget. The gateway CASes the exact current series-state revision and creates
the turn reservation plus its immutable successor state atomically. CAS loss,
crash or replay returns or completes that same revision; it never increments a
counter twice. Zero-policy, exact-purpose, purpose-plus-one, exact-aggregate,
aggregate-plus-one-with-purpose-capacity, lost-response replay and concurrent-
next-turn vectors are byte-identical in Rust and Swift and issue no extra
provider bytes.

```text
available -> send_prepared -> send_started -> sent
available|send_prepared -> failed_no_bytes
send_started -> failed_no_bytes | ambiguous_send_hold | sent
ambiguous_send_hold -> failed_no_bytes | sent
```

Only the gateway owns the registered provider input descriptor. For the one
current turn it first
commits `send_started`, then performs one bounded write of exactly the reserved
bytes. The finalized full-byte `sent` transition is the sole prompt-delivery
linearization point and records the observed byte count/provider-turn
correlation or `failed_no_bytes` with OS evidence that zero bytes were accepted.
Candidate transport receives only the terminal signed transition and projects
`prompt_committed` from `sent`; it has no independent prompt CAS or writable
descriptor. An exact request joins/replays the same reservation. Another
request, turn, attempt or process cannot consume it, and no next-turn
reservation is possible after `send_started` until that transition is
reconciled. Final attempt settlement binds the complete ordinal-sorted series,
every terminal transition and the last provider request-turn correlation; a
candidate status or provider transcript cannot omit or synthesize a turn.

Every authority append that changes the prompt operation-class fence reads the
run's prompt-reservation index in its authority transaction. It may finalize
only when each earlier reservation is terminal: `failed_no_bytes` is ordered
before the append and permanently disables that old reservation, while `sent`
is ordered before the append and proves exactly one complete prompt was written
under the old head. `send_started` or uncertain/partial OS write blocks the
append in nonterminal `ambiguous_send_hold`; the prompt reconciler must prove one of the two
terminal branches before either append or retry proceeds. Thus no database lock
is held over provider I/O, but the authority sequence has one linear order:
either zero prompt bytes before the new fence or exactly one complete prompt
before the append. Crash fixtures cover reservation, transition fsync, every
write boundary, provider acknowledgement and append competition.

Preparation is the invocation's local control-plane materialization point, not
an authority or attempt-creation linearization point. It is reachable only
after the signed `claimed` work transition is finalized. In one candidate
SQLite transaction the worker claims the projected work item, reads the current authority head,
verifies the run-generation binding, materializes all context references, and
inserts the immutable execution pin plus `prepared` dispatch intent. If the head
or generation CAS loses, no pin is written and preparation restarts from current
truth. An authority append committed after `prepared` does not rewrite the pin:
it advances the run fence and makes every stale pre-prompt transition fail its
fence check. A queued work item has no pin and therefore observes the latest
head when preparation begins.

The dispatch state machine is:

```text
pending_authority_finalize -> prepared
prepared -> launching -> provider_bound -> prompt_delivery_pending
prompt_delivery_pending -> prompt_committed -> observing -> settled
pending_authority_finalize -> cancelled_projection_only
prepared|launching|provider_bound|prompt_delivery_pending -> authority_recheck_required
authority_recheck_required -> cancelled|failed_closed|identity_ambiguous_hold
prepared|launching|provider_bound|prompt_delivery_pending -> cancelled|failed_closed|identity_ambiguous_hold
prompt_committed|observing -> settled|reconciliation_required
reconciliation_required -> settled|failed_closed
identity_ambiguous_hold -> reconciliation_required|failed_closed
```

`pending_authority_finalize` can advance only after the authority gateway
returns the exact finalized `claimed` transition and matching outbox receipt.
It has no launcher, prompt, broker or effect route. Abort before authority
finalize deletes or terminally marks only that provisional projection;
`cancelled_projection_only` is not an attempt settlement and cannot create a
successor.

Each local projection transition is a compare-and-swap over execution ID, attempt generation,
current state, lease epoch, and every policy-selected operation-class fence
token pinned for that transition. The overall fence digest remains readback and
reconstruction evidence but is not an over-broad cancellation token. The
supervisor rechecks current authority before spawn registration and before
`provider_bound`; the authority prompt gateway performs the final reservation
and fence check before `send_started`, while broker and side-effect admission
recheck it again. If a relevant hard operation-class
token changed before prompt, the attempt enters `authority_recheck_required`,
any verified process is
terminated/reaped, and a new attempt generation prepares from current truth.
If append races with `provider_bound`, the authority prompt-reservation index
and append ordering above make either `failed_no_bytes -> append` or
`sent -> append` win; a control-plane SQLite commit cannot decide that race.
After signed prompt commit the evaluator applies the entry's declared post-prompt
action; it never resends the prompt or trusts late output from a cancelled
attempt. `identity_ambiguous_hold` is a nonterminal blocking state for the
attempt: it blocks work-item reclaim, retry, provider resurrection, skill-script
execution, side-effect preparation and terminal attempt reduction until
verified clearance derives `reconciliation_required` or a signed failed
settlement derives `failed_closed`. It cannot expire on a timer and is never
counted as terminal evidence.

Entering that state atomically writes `InvocationIdentityHoldV1` with run,
execution and attempt, provider-session ID and cancellation epoch, daemon and
supervisor instance IDs, last verified process fingerprint, bounded ambiguity
reason, required clearance action, created revision/time, state `held`, and
`dispatch_hold_sha256`. The object contains no launch credential or raw process
environment. It is immutable; clearance writes a linked settlement row rather
than editing the held evidence.

Before a worker can claim production work, the release supervisor starts the
candidate suspended from work claim and asks the OS-isolated
`runtime_identity_attestor` to produce one purpose-signed
`RuntimeSelfAdmissionReceiptV1` for that daemon instance. The attestor measures
the launchd/audit-token identity, executable vnode and code signature, binary
and sealed-resource digests, PID/UID/process-birth fingerprint and sandbox
profile directly. It sends a nonce over a read-only self-description channel
and treats returned compiler/renderer/schema/tool-policy values only as claims
to compare with independently opened sealed resources and the promoted
manifest. Candidate bytes cannot write the receipt, choose the measured path,
call the attestation key or obtain a control-plane writer/work-claim endpoint
before the signed receipt is finalized in the authority store. The receipt
binds every observed/claimed pair, attestor component/build/key epoch and the
candidate manifest selected by the cutover generation. A forged self-report,
measurement mismatch or attestor failure enters the generation's durable
`emergency_hold_v2`; that daemon instance cannot claim or dispatch production
work. The execution-admission predicate rechecks the purpose signature and
admitted daemon-instance ID in every prepare and dispatch transaction.

Provider-launchable work has a second, independent authority boundary. The
candidate may propose a work transition, but candidate-owned control-plane rows
are never sufficient claim or launch truth. The OS-isolated
`execution_admission_controller` is the sole signer of
`ExecutableWorkAdmissionV1` and its predecessor-linked
`ExecutionReducerCheckpointV2`, both canonical in the authority store. The
same controller is the sole semantic writer of owner-occurrence transitions,
work issue/claim/settle/revoke transitions, attempt and owner settlements and
successor reducer checkpoints; launch and broker helpers can submit observed
receipts but cannot advance this lifecycle. The
checkpoint reduces only finalized signed run/proof admission, frozen
`workflow_v2` and `agent_catalog_v2` plans, prior work admissions, terminal
attempt/effect receipts and authority-head fences. It never reconstructs state
from mutable timestamps, queue order or unsigned candidate rows.

One work admission binds run and admission scope, workflow/state/task IDs,
state-occurrence and loop-generation ordinals, the exact
`execution_owner_occurrence_sha256`, tagged owner kind/ID and conditional stage
occurrence/StageExecution or mediation identity, zero-based task and fan-out
ordinals, parent transition/checkpoint, immutable agent identity and assignment
template, exact effect-slot inventory, canonical `agent_execution_id`, current
attempt generation, retry/reducer reason, candidate daemon self-admission and
generation/authority heads. It is immutable;
one append-only purpose-signed `ExecutableWorkAdmissionTransitionV1` carries
admission ID, monotonic revision, predecessor transition digest, operation and
state `available | claim_pending | claimed | settled | revoked`, plus the
conditional control-plane claim transaction, attempt settlement or revocation
receipt. Its unique semantic key is
`(run_id, owner_origin_kind, owner_origin_key, owner_kind, owner_id, task_ordinal,
fanout_ordinal, work_generation)`. Cardinality
and the next legal transition are derived from the frozen normalized plan;
neither an ID nor an ordinal is accepted from the candidate unless it equals
that derivation.

Initial issuance is the owner-materialization authority-only prepare/finalize
operation defined above. The generic admission controller does not issue a
parallel initial admission: it verifies and consumes the finalized owner's
immutable admission set. For retry or successor issuance, the controller CASes
the predecessor checkpoint and consumes the complete prior attempt/effect
settlement in one authority-only prepare/finalize operation, then signs exactly
one successor checkpoint, immutable work admission and revision-one
`available` transition. Only after finalize may the signed outbox project those
objects into control-plane SQLite. Candidate work claim first reserves that transition as
`claim_pending`; its control-plane transaction must byte-match the reservation
while creating the parent execution/current-attempt pointer and dispatch intent
as `pending_authority_finalize`. A one-use coherent control-plane snapshot
receipt lets the controller verify the resulting transaction before one authority finalize CASes
`claim_pending -> claimed`. Until finalization, the candidate row is
unclaimable and unable to reach the launcher. Retry or successor work is
admitted only in the authority transaction that consumes the previous signed
attempt/effect settlement and advances the reducer checkpoint. Recovery
continues or aborts that same transition revision and never issues a sibling
admission for one semantic key.

`attempt_admission_issuer` therefore validates a finalized immutable
`ExecutableWorkAdmissionV1` plus its latest signed `claimed` transition first,
then treats parent/work/dispatch rows in the
candidate database only as a projection that must byte-match it. Direct SQL
insert/update, duplicate task identity, skipped/repeated fan-out ordinal,
forged parent settlement, unsigned retry, or a control-plane database copied
from another run has no signed work admission and receives zero spawn/effect
authorization. This remains true even when every promoted digest in the forged
row is otherwise internally consistent.

The release-owned provider launcher allocates a logical provider-session row and
cancellation epoch before spawning. It generates a random 256-bit launch
credential from the OS CSPRNG, stores only its domain-separated hash with
execution ID, attempt generation, daemon instance, and a ten-second expiry, and
passes the plaintext once through an anonymous inherited pipe. It never appears
in argv, environment, files, logs, receipts, crash reports, or provider input.
Its sealed wrapper consumes and closes the pipe before provider `exec`, then
atomically spends the credential while registering PID, process group, UID,
process-birth fingerprint, wrapper binary digest, and launch token hash against
the `launching` row. Reuse, wrong binding, or expiry fails registration and the
wrapper exits without executing the provider.
