After provider initialization, the release-owned launcher observes the adapter
transport and writes a signed
`ObservedProviderBindingReceiptV1`. It binds the dispatch pin and actual daemon
instance, wrapper and provider executable digests/versions, adapter build,
provider session ID, request transport, model, effort, permission profile,
MCP/tool inventory digest, runtime-home digest, handshake transcript digest and
launcher component/build/key epoch. Candidate adapter claims are inputs to
comparison, not receipt authority.
The receipt contains bounded identities, not credentials or raw transcript.
`provider_bound` commits only when the receipt exactly matches both the
candidate manifest and dispatch pin. An adapter that cannot prove an actual
required identity is unsupported for V2. Mismatch requires verified process
group termination; ambiguous cleanup enters `identity_ambiguous_hold`.
Provider prompt transport cannot start before `provider_bound` commits.

The engine never commits `prompt_committed` before I/O. The authority-owned
gateway alone advances the reservation to `send_started`, performs the bounded
write, and makes the full-byte `sent` transition the sole prompt-delivery
linearization point. Only after finalized `sent` may the candidate projection
materialize `prompt_committed` with request-turn ID, prompt marker and provider-
session binding. A crash in `send_started` is an ambiguous hold, not a sent
prompt and not resend authority. The prompt reconciler uses the pinned
descriptor byte count plus provider/session/turn observation to derive only
`failed_no_bytes`, `sent`, or a continuing hold; recovery attaches after `sent`
when supported and otherwise settles `reconciliation_required`. Late output
from a cancelled or superseded generation is quarantined under the existing
execution-truth rules.

Crash outcomes are normative:

| Durable observation after restart | Recovery action |
|---|---|
| no dispatch row | no provider launch occurred through the V2 path; normal work-item reclaim may prepare once |
| `prepared` with broker grant `prepared` and no spawn journal/proxy-admission receipt | reacquire the lease and create exactly one proxy admission plus `spawn_pending` journal for the same immutable attempt pin |
| broker grant `proxy_admission_prepared` with no accepted-server receipt and verified no provider/proxy process | CAS that epoch to `abandoned`, revoke the unused XPC admission and finalize the signed attempt settlement; the authority reducer alone decides whether one successor admission is allowed |
| broker grant `activation_pending` with an accepted-server receipt and verified provider/proxy absence | CAS that epoch to `revoked`, preserve the accept receipt, finalize signed `failed_no_effect` attempt settlement and let the authority reducer issue at most one successor admission |
| broker grant `proxy_admission_prepared` or `activation_pending` with a registered/ambiguous process | reconcile the existing XPC-admission/process/accept receipts; install that same epoch, terminate/reap and settle, or enter `identity_ambiguous_hold`; never create a second admission or process |
| broker grant `installed` with the attested live session/proxy XPC connection | reattach to that exact session/connection; session loss revokes it and settles through the parent attempt policy |
| `launching` without a registered wrapper | inspect the supervisor spawn receipt; verified absence or verified reap settles `failed_closed`, while any ownership ambiguity enters `identity_ambiguous_hold` |
| `launching` or `provider_bound` with verified process and no prompt reservation beyond `available` or `send_prepared` | terminate/reap it, settle the reservation `failed_no_bytes`, then let the reducer decide whether a new attempt generation is allowed |
| prompt reservation `send_started` without terminal byte-count evidence | enter or retain `ambiguous_send_hold`; only `provider_prompt_reconciler` may derive zero-byte failure or full `sent`; never resend |
| finalized prompt reservation `sent`, whether or not `prompt_committed` projection exists | project `prompt_committed`, then attach/reconcile by pinned turn identity; never send the prompt again |
| `identity_ambiguous_hold` or cleanup unverified | no retry or launch; require verified process-absence clearance |

Every launch attempt already has a provider-session ID and cancellation epoch.
Before migration seal, every existing session receives one immutable,
server-derived `ProviderSessionContractPartitionV1`: sessions created under the
approved-HEAD contract are `legacy_v1`; sessions bound to a finalized V2 run/
work admission and dispatch-hold family are `authority_v2`. Unknown, mixed,
cross-generation or evidence-incomplete rows hold the seal. The release-owned
`provider_session_partition_controller` is the sole partition writer in the
authority store. Its migration operation inventories the exact approved-HEAD
provider-session set before seal, writes exactly one immutable partition per
row and emits one signed
`ProviderSessionContractPartitionMigrationReceiptV1`; no control-plane row or
API handler may assign or repair a partition. After seal, authority-v2 session
creation and its partition are one authority-store transaction bound to the
finalized run/work admission, while legacy partition creation is permanently
closed. For every GraphQL or MCP V1 operation and MCP V2 clearance, the shared
command boundary authenticates and authorizes the caller, resolves the
partition from authority truth, and enforces the compatible operation family
before resource lookup, exact-request or alias replay lookup, command-journal/
authority-operation allocation, or mutation. The partition is never accepted
from the caller and a wrong, unknown or held partition is a non-enumerating
zero-write denial.

V2 clearance does not change the existing Operator-only
`provider_session.mark_process_absent` P083 wire contract. Those legacy GraphQL
and MCP operations retain their current request/result families and may mutate
only a server-resolved `legacy_v1` session. A V1 request naming an
`authority_v2`, unknown or held session returns the frozen non-enumerating
denial with zero replay disclosure, journal, process or attempt mutation. The
additive
`provider_session.mark_process_absent_v2` operation must reference the held
`authority_v2` session/epoch and current dispatch
hold digest. Its authority operation records the Operator and evidence digest,
marks process fate `absent_verified`, and writes one individually signed
`ProviderProcessClearanceReceiptV1`, but the
old attempt remains unclaimable until authority finalize also verifies every
effect slot terminal and atomically writes its
`AgentExecutionAttemptSettlementV1`, `settled` work-admission transition and
successor-or-terminal reducer checkpoint. Only that same finalize may create
one next-generation `available` work admission. The control-plane projection
then moves the held dispatch to `failed_closed` and the attempt from
`quarantined` to its signed terminal outcome; it never resumes or reuses the
ambiguous process. Exact replay returns the same settlement/admission digests;
a different or stale hold cannot clear the attempt or issue a sibling successor.
Concurrent V1/V2 requests resolve the same immutable partition and dispatch-
hold CAS; only the compatible arm can commit. V1-on-V2, V2-on-V1, stale/cross-
generation and concurrent vectors all prove zero mutation by the wrong arm.
The additive V2 mutation remains MCP-only as
`provider_session.mark_process_absent_v2` over HTTP and stdio for an
Operator/`AgentOperator` caller. Its result is authority-only: it returns the
clearance receipt, attempt settlement, work-admission transition and reducer-
checkpoint digests, finalized authority operation ID/sequence,
`authority_projection_status = pending` and the complete immutable
`AuthorityProjectionOutboxSetV1`; it contains no control-plane `journal_id`,
transaction ID or `MutationProjectionReceiptV1`. GraphQL exposes bounded
readback of the resulting attempt, process fate, dispatch and authority
projection operation/sequence/status/outbox-set watermark; its mutation-
projection-receipt fields are null for this authority-only result. It exposes no
process-absence mutation. A GraphQL document that attempts
`p083MarkProviderSessionProcessAbsentV2` fails schema validation before
authorization or resolver execution and performs zero mutation. The existing
V1 GraphQL mutation and MCP tool remain qualified against their unchanged V1
result/journal contract.

The authority head is part of the provider-session binding fingerprint. A head
change prevents reuse or resurrection of a session that was primed with an
older mission. Historical readback and deterministic reconstruction use the
head stored on the execution, never the run's current head.

Operator MCP attempt readback and the GraphQL dispatch connection expose, for
every attempt generation, its pinned authority head/revision, effective mission
and effective-authority digests, runtime-policy, pinned/current overall fence
digests, sorted bounded relevant operation-class token relations and hard-
constraint summaries, current fence relation
`current | recheck_required | post_prompt_restricted`, and the resulting
allowed next actions. Non-Operator report policy continues to redact these
operator diagnostics. No UI infers constraints from prompt or artifact text.

### RunMissionV1

`RunMissionV1` is the immutable compile-time base mission stored in the frozen
`RunPlanSnapshot`. `EffectiveRunMissionV1` is the per-invocation projection of
that base plus the pinned durable overlay head. The base object is never
rewritten when an overlay event is accepted.

Required fields:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "run_mission_v1",
  "run_id": "...",
  "objective": "...",
  "authoritative_directives": [],
  "in_scope": [],
  "non_goals": [],
  "success_criteria": [],
  "base_authority_chain_head": "...",
  "source_refs": [],
  "content_sha256": "sha256:..."
}
```

The effective object adds `authority_chain_head`, `context_revision`, and
`base_mission_sha256`. Its digest and the exact overlay event IDs used to build
it are stored on the execution.

The original operator Idea title and body remain available verbatim as a
frozen source. A normalized mission may improve readability, but it is never
allowed to erase or weaken the verbatim operator directives. Coverage checks
bind every normalized hard constraint to a source anchor.

### RunContextGenerationBindingV2

Every new V2 production or proof run stores one immutable
`RunContextGenerationBindingV2` inside its `RunPlanSnapshot`. It contains the
cutover generation, `AgentContextCandidateManifestV1` digest, promotion receipt
digest, workflow and catalog snapshot digests, the signed authority-source
mapping-policy digest and ordered run-specific source-manifest digests,
skill-registry, complete pair-disposition-set and ordered resolved-skill
digests, neighbor-graph, trigger-harness and terminal pair-proof-set digests,
proof-matrix and client-capability support-policy
digests, context compiler and prompt builder identities, and all required
wire-version discriminators. The binding additionally stores the active
`release_generation_admission_scope` and digest. The frozen snapshot stores one
closed `RunContextAdmissionRefV1` sibling: a production Run contains the same
production generation-admission digest plus its finalized
`release_run_admission_sha256`; a proof Run contains the `probe_only` generation
admission, proof run/epoch/fixture namespace and matrix/cell-set digests and
forbids a production run receipt. The binding and run ID are computed first.
For production, the immutable canonical command-outcome core is computed next,
before either writer allocation. The release-authority operation core then
binds that outcome-core digest, and the run-admission receipt signs the
operation core plus binding and outcome-core digest; the prepared operation
revision references all three. The final snapshot/run row stores the closed
union afterward. The outcome core contains no admission or operation identity,
and no admission or operation core contains the final snapshot/Run/outcome
digest, so the order is acyclic. Neither arm is derivable from a mutable
generation cache, and mixed-arm fields are schema-invalid.

`runs.start` remains an MCP-only Operator boundary. V2 requires an
`AgentContextStartSelectionV2` with the actual MCP caller's expected cutover
generation and every promoted digest, plus a release-gateway-minted
signed token carrying `RunStartNegotiationReceiptV1` from the same authenticated
MCP logical session. At V2 this token is minted by the release-authority MCP
gateway, not the candidate daemon. Before
the database transaction, the Rust compiler reads workflow/catalog bytes from
opened descriptors, publishes referenced skill snapshots, and computes the
candidate binding without trusting path names after open. The gateway allocates
the run ID, computes `CanonicalCommandOutcomeCoreV1` from that ID, binding,
selection, authenticated session and semantic intent, then computes the
immutable release-authority operation core that binds the outcome-core digest.
It signs one `ReleaseRunAdmissionReceiptV1` that references the operation core,
binding and outcome core, and only then writes the prepared
`ReleaseAuthorityOperationV1` revision referencing all three; the control-plane
transaction then:

1. verifies the live marker is `open_v2`, its generation equals the expected
   generation, all supplied digests equal the promoted candidate, and the
   run-start negotiation token is canonical, bound to the same MCP logical-
   session/principal/client identity and selection digest, and names request/
   result/error schema versions admitted by exactly one current passing MCP
   start capability profile in the open proof matrix; a new command additionally
   requires the token to be fresh and unconsumed, while a committed exact replay
   follows the consumed/expiry exception below only after all session, signature,
   restart, profile and stored-receipt checks succeed;
2. verifies the compiled workflow, catalog, assignment templates, and skills
   are exact members of that candidate manifest; run-specific mission, input,
   blocker, and artifact generations are then bound separately in the frozen
   snapshot and invocation pins;
3. verifies the prepared run admission against the active production generation
   admission, same logical session/request, registered workspace, complete
   binding and precomputed outcome core, then inserts the Run, frozen snapshot,
   generation binding, run-admission union, immutable outcome-core projection/
   reference and run-start audit row atomically;
4. reports the committed row to the gateway, which anchor-finalizes the run
   admission and finalized exact-request result in the authority store before
   returning success or permitting work claim.

No run row exists before step 3 commits. A lost generation/digest CAS leaves
only unreferenced content-addressed files eligible for bounded cleanup. Exact
request replay returns the original run; a new request cannot reinterpret old
bytes under a newer generation. Promotion and `runs.start` serialize on the
same cutover row, so one commits first and the other either observes that exact
generation or fails without creating a mixed snapshot. A crash after step 3
leaves the Run unclaimable until the same authority operation finalizes; it
cannot create a second Run or a second admission.

### AgentRoleV1

Each existing production agent receives a role charter in the catalog:

```yaml
role:
  mission: Implement the approved code-owned scope and leave verifiable evidence.
  owns:
    - production source changes
    - code-owned tests
    - implementation progress and self-assessment
  does_not_own:
    - proposal approval
    - documentation closeout
    - commit, push, publish, or release decisions
  success_criteria:
    - required code-owned scope is implemented
    - focused verification is reported truthfully
    - remaining work is classified by the correct owner
```

Role data is not a skill. It describes durable organizational responsibility,
not a procedure for completing a particular class of task. The compiled wire
object adds `schema_version = agent_role_v1`, `agent_id`, and `role_sha256` to
the five YAML fields shown above.

### TaskAssignmentV1

Each invocation receives a compiled assignment derived from the frozen
workflow state, task declaration, role charter, active artifact generations,
and output contracts.

Required fields:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "task_assignment_v1",
  "state_id": "state_7_implementation_started",
  "state_purpose": "Implement the human-approved proposal revision.",
  "task_name": "implement_approved_proposal",
  "task_purpose": "Close current code-owned work without broadening scope.",
  "done_when": [],
  "upstream_inputs": [],
  "downstream_consumers": [],
  "active_blockers": [],
  "required_outputs": [],
  "permission_profile_id": "CODE_WRITE",
  "ordered_skill_ids": ["code-implementation"],
  "effect_slots": [
    {
      "schema_version": "effect_slot_declaration_v2",
      "effect_slot_id": "workspace_patch",
      "kind": "skill_script",
      "skill_script": {
        "script_uri": "skill://sha256/0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef/scripts/apply",
        "operation_class": "workspace_write"
      },
      "operation_class": "workspace_write",
      "cardinality": "at_most_once",
      "effect_slot_declaration_sha256": "sha256:..."
    }
  ],
  "assignment_sha256": "sha256:..."
}
```

Every referenced input and blocker includes its active generation and digest.
Superseded or stale artifacts can be shown as history but cannot appear as
active assignment truth. `effect_slot_id` is a unique lowercase identifier
minted by the compiler from the frozen task declaration. Every row is one
closed `EffectSlotDeclarationV2` tagged union with common
`effect_slot_id`, `operation_class`, `cardinality = at_most_once`, and digest.
Its `kind` is exactly:

- `skill_script`, with a non-null `skill_script { script_uri,
  operation_class }` arm and absent `external_effect`; or
- `external_effect`, with a non-null `external_effect { effect_kind,
  operation_class, target_resolver_policy_sha256 }` arm, where `effect_kind` is
  exactly `git_commit_push` or `connect_publish`, and absent `skill_script`.

The repeated arm/common operation class must be byte-equal. Unknown kinds,
both/neither arms, an operation mismatch, a caller-selected target, or a script
URI on an external effect fail compilation. A write script or external effect
is not callable unless the assignment declares its slot; two intentionally
distinct logical effects require two distinct immutable slots. The unique
authority claim remains exactly `(agent_execution_id, effect_slot_id)` across
attempt, session, grant and request replacement.

### Workflow DSL Additions

Workflow states gain required production metadata:

```yaml
state_7_implementation_started:
  label: Implementation
  purpose: Implement the approved proposal revision in the dedicated worktree.
  outcome: Code-owned scope is implemented and verification evidence is current.
  owner: lead_orchestrator
```

Agent tasks gain:

```yaml
- agent: code_writer
  task: implement_approved_proposal
  purpose: Close current code-owned implementation and test blockers only.
  done_when:
    - implementation outputs satisfy their declared contracts
    - code-owned blockers are either closed or reported with evidence
  effect_slots:
    - id: workspace_patch
      kind: skill_script
      script: skill://sha256/0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef/scripts/apply
      operation_class: workspace_write
```

The Rust and Swift workflow definitions, validators, compilers, inspectors, and
snapshot serializers must remain schema-compatible. `effect_slots` is required
when a task can invoke a write script and forbidden for undeclared scripts;
duplicate IDs or a slot/script/operation mismatch fail compilation.
Tasks that own `github_commit_push` or `connect_publisher` instead declare
`kind: external_effect`, the corresponding closed `effect_kind`, operation
class and release-owned target-resolver-policy digest; no script field or
caller target is legal on that arm.

These additions are a breaking DSL revision rather than optional fields on the
existing format. A V2 production workflow has top-level
`schema_version: workflow_v2`; a V2 production catalog has top-level
`schema_version: agent_catalog_v2`. Their generated Rust and Swift enums are
closed and do not accept integer `1`, omitted discriminators, aliases or
unknown future versions. `workflow_v2` requires state purpose/outcome,
assignment purpose/done-when, authority-source binding, effect-slot declarations
and the normalized-plan digest inputs above. `agent_catalog_v2` requires role,
permission, provider-profile, model/effort, skill-composition and sandbox-policy
bindings. Existing V1 documents remain readable only for frozen historical
runs while `legacy_bridge` is retained; they cannot compile a new V2 production
Run, proof Run or candidate. Generated normalization fixtures prove V1
rejection before Run insertion and byte-identical V2 normalized plans across
Rust and Swift.

### PromptEnvelopeV2

The engine serializes one provider-neutral envelope in this order:

1. runtime and security invariants;
2. active authority chain and global mission;
3. role charter;
4. task assignment;
5. active skill bodies and brokered logical resource manifest;
6. input artifacts clearly fenced as untrusted data;
7. required outputs and validation contracts;
8. runtime invocation identifiers and freshness rules.

Mission, role, and assignment are protected sections. Artifact materialization
cannot displace or truncate them. Large artifacts are referenced by canonical
path and digest instead of being copied wholesale into the initial prompt.

Prompt diagnostics persist section byte counts, total byte count, context
version, and section digests. Raw sensitive content is not copied into metrics
or ordinary operator logs. `PromptEnvelopeManifestV2` is out-of-band evidence:
it references the rendered prompt bytes but is not embedded in those bytes, so
its exact-prompt digest is not circular.

Budget admission applies to every exact provider-bound request, not only skill
bodies or the first prompt. For the resolved provider/model profile the initial
manifest records tokens for every protected section, artifact reference,
injected skill body, required-output contract, adapter prefix/suffix and framing
token, tool schema and MCP server description. `PromptTokenBudgetPolicyV1`
supplies that profile's `context_window_tokens`,
`max_initial_request_tokens`, `max_accumulated_context_tokens`, exact per-turn
framing rules, a release-pinned provider-default maximum-completion-token value
and `completion_reserve_tokens`; no budget value has an ambient default. For
each send, `effective_max_completion_tokens` is exactly the explicit maximum in
the authority-owned provider request when present, otherwise the release-pinned
provider/model default. A missing or unknown default, provider-selected value,
explicit value above policy, or adapter that cannot prove the sent maximum is a
pre-send denial. The policy requires
`completion_reserve_tokens >= effective_max_completion_tokens`; equality is
valid, and no prompt, tool or continuation lane may borrow from that reserve.
Initial admission requires both
`actual_initial_request_tokens <= max_initial_request_tokens` and
`actual_initial_request_tokens + completion_reserve_tokens <=
context_window_tokens`.

Turn cardinality is a separate release-owned admission dimension.
`ProviderPromptTurnBudgetPolicyV1` binds the exact frozen workflow/assignment,
P079 and P086 policy revisions and supplies the four purpose ceilings and their
independently configured positive aggregate ceiling for the resolved profile.
The aggregate must be no greater than the checked sum of the four purpose
ceilings but need not equal that sum, so an aggregate-only exhaustion case is
reachable while each purpose retains capacity. `PromptTokenBudgetPolicyV1` cannot
override it, and a token-valid request still fails before reservation when its
purpose or aggregate turn counter is exhausted. The series, every reservation,
dispatch readback and Swift projection carry the same turn-policy digest and
remaining counters.

Before **every** later provider send, including a continuation after any broker
tool, the release-owned prompt gateway constructs one predecessor-linked
`ProviderContextBudgetStateV1`. It tokenizes the complete provider-visible
context exactly as the selected adapter will serialize it and recomputes the
effective maximum and reserve relation: the initial request,
all retained system/user/assistant messages, model output, tool-call frames,
bounded tool results from skill resources, skill scripts and Git evidence,
provider/MCP framing, the pending next message or tool result, and the nonzero
completion reserve. It records every ordered component digest and token count,
the tokenizer/profile/policy identities, provider session, request-turn ordinal
and prior budget-state digest. Neither a candidate-reported token counter nor a
provider usage summary is admission truth.

The send is admitted only when the completion maximum/default proof is current,
`completion_reserve_tokens >= effective_max_completion_tokens`,
`accumulated_context_tokens <= max_accumulated_context_tokens` and
`accumulated_context_tokens + completion_reserve_tokens <=
context_window_tokens`. The resulting admitted state digest is mandatory in the
one-use prompt reservation and `ProviderSendIntentV1`; the credential proxy
rejects a send whose pending body or turn does not match it. Unknown framing or
tokenizer identity, integer overflow, missing predecessor, omitted tool output,
or a request exactly one token above either bound fails before any provider or
upstream byte with `provider_context_budget_exceeded`. There is no hidden
truncation, provider-specific best effort or borrowing from the completion
reserve. Context compaction would require a separately versioned, reviewed
policy and proof contract; V2 fails closed instead.

Retained vectors cover explicit maximum, pinned-default maximum, unknown or
changed default, reserve equal to maximum and reserve one token below maximum,
plus exact-limit and limit-plus-one for the initial request and after each
supported tool-result class, ordinary model turn and continuation turn for every
production provider/model profile. They compare the tokenized bytes and actual
maximum-completion field with the adapter's serialized request and prove that a
denied state writes no prompt-send reservation, provider-send intent or upstream
bytes.

## Version Discrimination and Wire Contract

The context-envelope version is independent of the existing
`run_plan_snapshot_format_version`. The latter continues to describe P066
catalog/toolchain-cache compatibility and is not renamed or overloaded.
`RunPlanSnapshot` gains the optional string field
`agent_context_envelope_schema` with this exact mapping:

| Existing `run_plan_snapshot_format_version` | `agent_context_envelope_schema` | Reader behavior |
|---|---|---|
| absent | absent | legacy pre-P066 snapshot; historical readback only after cutover |
| `1` | absent | P066 snapshot with no typed context; historical readback only after cutover |
| absent or `1` | `agent_context_envelope_v2` | typed V2 context reader and execution admission |
| any supported value | unknown non-null string | preserve bounded raw metadata but reject provider execution with `agent_context_version_incompatible` |
| unsupported non-null plan format | any | retain the existing unsupported-plan-format rejection |

A new production snapshot after cutover must contain
`agent_context_envelope_schema = agent_context_envelope_v2`. Absence never
defaults to V2. No numeric value, field presence heuristic, catalog field, or
prompt content may select a context reader.

### Normative Schemas

The implementation adds machine-readable JSON Schemas under
`docs/reference/agent-context/schemas/` and shared canonical-byte vectors under
`docs/reference/agent-context/vectors/`. These files, versioned with the daemon,
are the normative wire source for hand-written Rust and Swift types. Every
new agent-context/V2 schema sets `additionalProperties: false`, lists every
required field, and uses an exact `const` discriminator. The three frozen V1
`runs.start` compatibility schemas are the sole exception: they preserve the
pre-cutover no-discriminator decoder and permissive unknown-field behavior, and
their separate `tools/list` golden preserves the exact historical advertised
descriptor. The parity gate verifies that both runtimes accept and reject the
same vector set; neither runtime-generated schema is the source of truth.

Wire rules are uniform:

- Chainworks-owned field names are lowercase `snake_case` and case-sensitive;
  schemas that deliberately mirror an existing external/domain protocol preserve
  its exact declared casing, including ACP `extensionId`, and list every such
  exception in that schema rather than normalizing it;
- all fields are required unless the normative schema marks them optional;
- an optional absent value is omitted and JSON `null` is forbidden; V1 preserves
  only behavior represented by its advertised pre-cutover schema, not accidental
  decoder permissiveness outside that schema;
- the sole readback compatibility exception is the nested current
  `operator_readback_v1` producer payload inside
  `agent_context_rollout_projection_v1`. That version explicitly requires the
  producer's nullable fields `waiver_expires_at`, `waiver`,
  `enforcement_mode_reason`, `disabled_reason_code`,
  `p083_rollback_ttl_expires_at`, `p083_last_preflight_hash`, and
  `cutover_policy_revision`, plus their declared compatibility aliases and
  GraphQL renderings `waiverExpiresAt`, `waiver`, `enforcementModeReason`,
  `disabledReasonCode`, `cutoverPolicyRevision`, and
  `rolloutContractCutoverPolicyRevision`. The producer's nested rollback
  discriminator remains exactly `schema_version` even inside the GraphQL
  `rollbackDisposition` object; it is intentionally not recursively camelized.
  The two P083 producer fields are separate GraphQL compatibility exceptions:
  they remain exactly `p083_rollback_ttl_expires_at` and
  `p083_last_preflight_hash` in the nested GraphQL object. Their camel-case
  spellings, omission, or simultaneous snake/camel forms are invalid.
  No other V2
  schema inherits this exception, and a future null removal requires a new
  mapping version and fixture;
- required empty arrays remain present; no decoder synthesizes a default;
- enum strings are closed lowercase ASCII values and unknown values fail;
- IDs use their existing canonical wire form; command request IDs retain their
  existing per-command UUID version;
- hashed objects require their self-digest field on the wire but omit only that
  named field while computing it;
- timestamps, integers, ordering, duplicate-key rejection, and Unicode follow
  `chainworks_canonical_digest_v1` below.

All arrays in that table preserve declared order except these schema-declared
sets, which sort by raw canonical key: authority `supersedes` by event ID,
mission source refs by `(source_kind, source_id, revision)`, role ownership and
criteria strings by UTF-8 bytes, skill manifest files by portable path, skill
registry entries by `skill_id`, neighbor-graph nodes by `skill_id` and edges by
`(left_skill_id, right_skill_id, edge_kind)`, legacy
source nodes by source-node ID, migration fragments by `fragment_id`, process
clearances by `(provider_session_id, cancellation_epoch)`, and projection
intents by `(projection_kind, entity_id)`, active authority rows by
`(conflict_key, event_id)`, proof cells by their canonical dimension tuple,
evaluation pairs by pair identity, reviewer results by selected-reviewer
ordinal, reviewer barrier rows by selected-reviewer ordinal, unresolved
incidents by `(signal_id, incident_id)`, pair-proof-set rows by
`pair_disposition_sha256`, rollout-signal migration rows by old signal ID,
authority-generation handoff actions by canonical step ordinal, executable
build inputs by `(input_kind, stable_input_id)`, native-fixture production-deny
rows by `(resource_kind, canonical_identity)`, and sandbox roots by normalized
capability kind/path bytes. Typed
assignment inputs, blockers, outputs, skill composition, write-journal entries
and connection edges remain ordered because prompt, effect and keyset order are
semantic.

### Northbound Mutation and Discovery Contract

All request and result schemas below live in the normative schema directory,
set `additionalProperties: false`, reject null, and cap the complete request at
64 KiB unless an existing lower cap applies. MCP state-changing tools retain
the existing boundary `idempotency_key` as a lowercase UUIDv7. Every new
context mutation, `approvals.reissue`, and the extended process-absence command
also require a lowercase UUIDv4 `caller_request_id` for
the durable semantic command contract. The two IDs are not aliases:

- `idempotency_key` caches one exact MCP tool request, including
  `caller_request_id`;
- `caller_request_id` identifies one durable command lease and participates in
  exact-request/conflict lookup, but is excluded from the semantic intent hash;
  a different caller request ID may therefore enter `command_request_aliases`
  when every command-specific semantic field is equal;
- V1 `runs.start` retains only its existing UUIDv7 `idempotency_key`, which is
  also stored as its command-journal request ID, and retains its exact current
  result/error/journal projection;
- pre-existing GraphQL `approveApproval`, `rejectApproval` and
  `approvalsResolve`, GraphQL `p083MarkProviderSessionProcessAbsent`, MCP
  `approvals.resolve`, and MCP V1 `provider_session.mark_process_absent` remain
  distinct frozen compatibility operations with their current request, result,
  error, replay and transport-specific journal behavior. They
  do not gain a V2 semantic-alias row, authority watermark, authority outbox or
  projection receipt. Authority-bound settlement, mediation and extended
  process clearance use the separately named `approvals.resolve_authority`,
  `lead_mediation.resolve_authority`, and
  `provider_session.mark_process_absent_v2` operations with both IDs.

The rules in this section for semantic aliasing, V2 validation precedence and
authority/control-plane projection receipts apply only to newly versioned V2
operations. A frozen compatibility adapter dispatches to the exact HEAD command
path and serializes the exact HEAD result/error shape; generated goldens compare
those bytes and journal side effects before and after the migration. It cannot
be upgraded in place by attaching V2 fields or by routing through the generic
V2 alias/error adapter.

After Phase -2, one protected-base declarative source,
`docs/reference/agent-context/operations.yaml`, is the sole exhaustive production
owner of every callable GraphQL query, mutation and subscription, MCP HTTP/stdio
tool, provider-visible broker tool and private-XPC operation. Its first
generation must import the signed `AgentContextBootstrapOperationManifestV1`
rows, triplets, authorization and replay bytes unchanged under disposition
`frozen_bootstrap_compatibility`; the bootstrap manifest is the sole owner only
before this import and cannot acquire another operation. `operations.yaml` owns
each remaining public or private name, request/result/error triplet, call-level
authorization tuple, writer, replay class and projection adapter. The separate
`docs/reference/agent-context/read-surfaces.yaml` source may only narrow
field-level visibility, redaction and error rendering after the referenced
operation has been admitted; it cannot define an endpoint, capability,
principal class, resource resolver or second schema triplet. Before any API
edit, a pinned discovery generator records
`AgentContextExistingPublicSurfaceInventoryV1` from GraphQL SDL/introspection,
GraphQL resolver and checked-in operation-document inventories, MCP HTTP/stdio
`tools/list`, canonical MCP capability/router/alias inventory and provider-
broker descriptors at the approved HEAD. The approved-HEAD baseline is exactly
42 GraphQL query fields, 11 mutation fields, 8 subscription fields and 55 MCP
capability IDs; those cardinalities are assertions over complete sorted names,
source symbols and wire digests, not substitutes for that exact set.
The following approved-HEAD name inventories are normative generator inputs,
not examples:

- GraphQL queries (42): `ideas`, `idea`, `runs`, `run`,
  `p083IdentityHoldSessions`, `approvalInbox`, `artifacts`, `artifact`, `stages`,
  `runStageTopology`, `activeAgentExecutions`, `timelineRawDetail`,
  `runQueueSummary`, `stageQueueSummary`, `stage`, `agentExecutions`,
  `runEscalationReadback`, `stewardAnalyses`, `stewardAnalysis`,
  `stewardAnalysisRunLinks`, `stewardRecommendations`, `daemonStatus`,
  `boundaryRuntime`, `operatorAlerts`, `storageHealth`,
  `startupRecoverySummary`, `toolchainCacheHousekeepingSummary`,
  `unresolvedSideEffects`, `sessionLineages`, `sessionLineage`,
  `sessionGenerations`, `sessionEvents`, `sessionKpiSummary`, `sessionHealth`,
  `sessionObservabilityAvailable`, `continuationStatus`,
  `continuationCandidates`, `continuations`, `continuationMetricsSummary`,
  `providerSessionAttachReceipt`, `p080Diagnostics`, `tempArtifactInventory`;
- GraphQL mutations (11): `approveApproval`, `rejectApproval`,
  `approvalsResolve`, `runsCancel`, `providerSessionShutdown`,
  `p083RollbackExecution`, `p083SetEnforcementMode`, `runsRetry`, `stagesRetry`,
  `sideEffectsForceReconcile`, `p083MarkProviderSessionProcessAbsent`;
- GraphQL subscriptions (8): `runStatusChanged`, `stageStatusChanged`,
  `approvalRequested`, `approvalResolved`, `runtimeStatusChanged`,
  `daemonStatusChanged`, `sessionStatusChanged`, `p080DiagnosticsUpdates`;
- MCP capability IDs (55): `IdeasCreate`, `IdeasList`, `RunsStart`, `RunsList`,
  `RunsGet`, `RunsMainSyncRequest`, `RunsMainSyncRetry`,
  `RunsMainSyncSetOverride`, `RunsMainSyncRepairState`,
  `RunsMainSyncRecordRecoveryDecision`, `RunsKnowledgeCapsuleIgnore`,
  `RunsRetrofitCatalogSnapshot`, `RunsCancel`, `ApprovalsList`,
  `ApprovalsResolve`, `StagesRetry`, `StagesConsumeProviderQuotaHold`,
  `WorkflowConflictsResolve`, `WorkflowLoopBudgetExtend`,
  `LegacyDiscoveryOverrideCreate`, `ReportsGet`, `ArtifactsOverrideContract`,
  `StewardRunAnalysis`, `StewardListAnalyses`, `StewardGetAnalysis`,
  `RuntimeHealth`, `OperatorAlertsList`, `StorageHealth`, `StorageWritePressure`,
  `StorageEvidenceSpoolSummary`, `StorageReconcileEvidenceOrphans`,
  `ProposalGateSettle`, `EffectsList`, `EffectsInspect`, `EffectsReconcile`,
  `EffectsMarkConflict`, `EffectsMarkUnrecoverable`,
  `EffectsClearAfterManualVerification`, `StorageMaintenanceRepairSlot`,
  `StorageProjectionsClearBacklog`, `StorageProjectionsClearPoison`,
  `AgentsContinuationStatus`, `AgentsContinuationCandidates`,
  `AgentsContinueWork`, `AutomationAutoRetryLatest`, `P080DiagnosticsGet`,
  `P080ReconcileRequest`, `P080ClearPermanentHold`, `ProviderSessionShutdown`,
  `P083RollbackExecution`, `P083SetEnforcementMode`, `RetryRun`,
  `SideEffectsForceReconcile`, `ProviderSessionMarkProcessAbsent`,
  `TempArtifactsInventoryPreview`.

The generator derives canonical public tool names, `boundary.runtime.get` and
Codex underscore aliases from those capability rows and requires every alias to
retain its own descriptor/router/source-symbol observation. An omitted/reordered
name, alias that is counted as another capability, duplicate or extra current-
HEAD symbol is drift, even if all four cardinalities still match.
Its exact-set key is `(transport, public_name, current_wire_generation)` and its
rows bind the observed request/result/error shape, authorization, replay,
journal/receipt behavior and source symbol. The protected
`operations.yaml` must account for every discovered query, mutation,
subscription, read-only or mutating MCP tool, broker tool and private-XPC call
with exactly one logical operation. Every operation row has disposition
`frozen_compatibility`, `migrate_in_phase`, or `retire_before_phase`; a future
row names the phase in which its endpoint is introduced. The generated
operation schema set requires exactly one request/result/error triplet per
logical operation, including subscription payload/error closure. The generated
read-surface schema set references that triplet and contains only field
projection/redaction/error-arm schemas; it cannot repeat or replace it.
Missing/extra endpoints, handwritten
routers, aliases without canonical rows or a changed discovery digest fail
generation before serve.

The approved-HEAD GraphQL compatibility set explicitly includes
`approveApproval`, `rejectApproval`, `approvalsResolve`, `runsCancel`,
`providerSessionShutdown`, `p083RollbackExecution`,
`p083SetEnforcementMode`, `runsRetry`, `stagesRetry`,
`sideEffectsForceReconcile` and GraphQL V1
`p083MarkProviderSessionProcessAbsent`; the baseline separately includes MCP V1
`provider_session.mark_process_absent`. Each GraphQL row and each MCP row
receives its own exact frozen request/result/error triplet, authorization row,
current replay and observed journal/receipt class until an explicit later
migration or retirement row becomes eligible. The GraphQL V1 success preserves
its marked-absent/provider-session/cancellation/journal/request payload. The MCP
V1 **descriptor** preserves approved HEAD's optional `journal_id` property, but
the separately captured approved-HEAD success/denial payload goldens preserve
only schema/status/optional-request/denial and omit it. Compatibility generation
therefore neither removes the optional descriptor field nor synthesizes it into
an observed payload. Listing selected V2 tools in the prose cannot remove or
merge any of these baseline rows.

A pinned release generator emits the signed
`AgentContextOperationManifestV1`, signed
`AgentContextOperationSchemaSetV1`, every request/result/error JSON Schema,
MCP descriptor metadata, GraphQL operation/union/error adapters, Rust and Swift
discriminators, and the operation rows rendered later in this proposal. Every
manifest row contains exactly one logical operation ID; boundary class
`northbound`, `provider_broker`, or `private_internal`; conditional MCP,
GraphQL, provider-broker or private-XPC operation names; one
request, result and error schema version/digest triplet; mutability and replay
class; either the northbound principal/caller/capability tuple, the broker
grant/session/permission tuple, or the private peer component/build/audit-token/
designated-requirement/purpose tuple;
validation-precedence ID; authority/control-plane writer; and exact logical-
result projection adapter plus closed `result_receipt_class`. A logical operation ID is version-qualified when
one public transport name has incompatible wire generations. Thus
`runs_start_legacy_operation` and `runs_start_context_operation` are distinct
manifest rows with distinct
triplets that both map to public MCP name `runs.start`; their capability
profiles and cutover phases are mutually exclusive, and no other duplicate
public name is allowed. An operation cannot be handwritten into a router,
SDL, client document or descriptor without a manifest row, and a manifest row
cannot omit its three schemas even when the operation is transport-specific.

The same protected `operations.yaml` also generates
`AgentContextOperationAuthorizationInventoryV1`. One logical operation expands
to exactly one authorization row for every transport/public-name pair that the
manifest declares: MCP HTTP and stdio share one public-name row only when their
policy tuple is identical, GraphQL has its own row, provider-broker stdio has
its grant/session tuple, and `private_internal` has no public-name field and
exactly one registered local-XPC operation plus peer/component tuple. A
northbound row binds principal class, derived caller class, capability and
server-side resource-scope resolver; a private row instead binds audit token,
process-birth identity, designated requirement, component/build, purpose and
resource resolver. Every row binds a validation-precedence entry and positive/
negative fixture IDs. A transport or private endpoint without one row, two rows
for one endpoint, a row without an endpoint, a private row carrying a public
name, or policy drift between descriptor/SDL/XPC router and inventory fails
generation before serve.

Northbound state-changing rows are Operator-only unless their generated row is
the single explicit `self_authenticated_principal` exception for
`runtime.principals.rotate_self`. That exception derives principal, token,
session and target from live authentication, admits no caller-selected target
and still requires its current resource scope. It cannot be copied to another
operation. Provider-broker tools never inherit a northbound caller class: they
require the exact active grant/session/generation/composition tuple. Generated
fixtures execute every admitted tuple plus missing principal, wrong principal
class, wrong derived caller class, missing/revoked capability, wrong resource
scope and exception-confusion denials on every declared transport. The summary
table below is rendered documentation; only exact equality with the generated
inventory is accepted.

Read fields are not granted independent call authority. A second protected source,
`docs/reference/agent-context/read-surfaces.yaml`, generates the signed
`AgentContextReadAuthorizationInventoryV1`. Its exact-set key is
`(surface_kind, transport, public_parent, public_field_or_method)`. It covers
every V2 GraphQL root/field (including `Run.agentContext`, its connections,
`Approval.authorityBinding` and incident/cutover/attempt readback), MCP read
tool, report/Steward projection, Swift private-XPC fetch and authority helper
read. Each row references exactly one admitted operation-manifest and call-
authorization row, inherits its principal/caller/capability/resource resolver,
and may declare only an equal-or-narrower visibility arm `operator`, `redacted`,
or `non_enumerating_denial`, an error-union/code, live-auth checkpoint and
positive/negative fixture IDs. A field or private method without exactly one
row, an orphan row, a duplicate request/result/error triplet, any call-level
authorization declaration or parent/child policy widening fails generation and
failed-serve.

GraphQL HTTP authenticates and resolves the latest `PrincipalTable` on every
request before resource lookup. GraphQL WebSocket authenticates `connection_init`
into a bounded logical session but re-resolves the live table/session fences at
every subscribe operation and immediately before every emitted payload; revoke,
disable or re-scope terminates the affected subscription without one stale
frame. Field resolvers receive only the inventory-derived authorization context
and cannot reuse a parent object's existence as authority. Private XPC rows use
the closed tagged `PrivateBoundaryPeerAuthorizationV1`, whose mutually exclusive
arms are `release_component { component_id, build_sha256, designated_requirement,
audit_token_binding, purpose }` and `preprovisioned_automation_principal {
principal_id, capability, resource_scope_sha256, logical_session_sha256 }`.
Caller-supplied component/principal tags are rejected; an untagged internal
boolean or free-form component name is not authorization.

Generated live-transport fixtures cover GraphQL HTTP and WebSocket independently,
including connection-init-before-revocation, subscribe-after-revocation and
revocation between two payloads, plus every private-XPC arm and wrong audit
token/designated requirement. They prove Agent/Observer/ReadOnlyOperator receive
only the explicitly declared redacted branch, unauthorized or out-of-scope
resources remain non-enumerating, and no adjacent child field recovers
Operator-only authority, rollout, output-repair or artifact payload detail.

`docs/reference/agent-context/errors.yaml` is the single source for the signed
`AgentContextErrorRegistryV1`. Each closed error row owns canonical code,
classification, retryability, recovery mode, allowed safe-detail fields,
precedence and the exact JSON-RPC data/GraphQL extension projections. Request
schemas reference only registry codes; no per-tool schema may redefine code,
retryability or safe fields. The schema set contains exactly three rows per
manifest operation and no other operation schema. Generation fails on an unreferenced error, missing
or orphan request/result/error schema, duplicate logical operation/code or a
duplicate public name outside the declared mutually exclusive `runs.start`
variant group, schema
triplet reused under incompatible semantics, hand-authored SDL branch, or a
router/client symbol absent from the manifest. The candidate manifest and
evaluation trust policy pin source, generator, operation-manifest, operation-
schema-set and error-registry digests before candidate registration.

Retained black-box vectors enumerate every manifest row through real MCP HTTP,
northbound MCP stdio, provider-broker MCP stdio and conditional GraphQL HTTP/WS
transports. They validate advertised
request/result/error digests, success rendering, every reachable error class,
authorization and validation precedence, exact replay semantics and zero-write
denials. The gate compares generated Rust/Swift symbol inventories and actual
SDL/introspection/tool descriptors to the manifest, rather than grepping names
or accepting a synthesized logical object.

The read-only MCP tool `runtime.agent_context.start_selection.get` takes
`agent_context_start_selection_request_v2` with exactly its discriminator and
required `workflow_id`. Candidate registration stores the complete canonical
`AgentContextCandidateCoreV1`, `AgentQualityTargetDeclarationV1` and
`AgentContextCandidateManifestV1` payloads plus the core's workflow/assignment
index in the authority store, not only their digests; the lineage controller
verifies the acyclic bindings and signs those immutable bytes before the
candidate row can advance. In one
**authority-store** SQLite read transaction the gateway reads the finalized
production generation/admission, candidate manifest and indexed workflow, and
constructs
`AgentContextStartSelectionV2` with exactly these fields:

- `schema_version = agent_context_start_selection_v2`, `workflow_id`,
  `cutover_state = open_v2`, canonical decimal-string `cutover_generation` and
  `cutover_revision`;
- `context_schema_version`, `prompt_envelope_schema_version`,
  `role_schema_version`, `assignment_schema_version`,
  `skill_snapshot_schema_version`, `digest_contract_version`, and
  `promotion_policy_version`;
- `candidate_id`, `candidate_sha256`, `promotion_receipt_sha256`,
  `proof_matrix_sha256`, `client_capability_support_policy_sha256`,
  `catalog_snapshot_sha256`, `authority_source_mapping_policy_sha256`,
  `skill_registry_sha256`,
  `skill_pair_disposition_set_sha256`, `skill_neighbor_graph_sha256`,
  `skill_trigger_harness_sha256`, and `skill_pair_proof_set_sha256`;
- `workflow_source_sha256`, `workflow_normalized_plan_sha256`, and ordered
  `assignment_templates`, whose closed entries contain `state_id`, `task_name`,
  and `assignment_template_sha256`;
- sorted unique `required_capability_versions` and `selection_sha256`.

`selection_sha256` covers that complete object without itself. No digest
required by `runs.start` is sourced from another health read or a mutable client
file, control-plane projection or cross-store join. A missing/mismatched
manifest payload is failed-serve, not a fallback to the candidate cache. The
tool returns a selection only while the authority marker is `open_v2`; other
cutover states return the authorized `-32009` admission envelope.
`runtime.health` advertises this tool and its schema version but is not itself
selection truth.

Initialize creates one `McpLogicalSessionIdentityV1`. For Streamable HTTP it
binds the server-issued `Mcp-Session-Id`, authenticated `token_id`, initialize
generation and restart nonce; TCP connection reuse or replacement is irrelevant.
For stdio it binds the daemon-owned stdio transport process identity, random
session nonce, authenticated `token_id` and initialize generation. Both forms
also bind normalized MCP `clientInfo`, negotiated protocol version and the exact
ordered tool name/request/result/error schema-digest inventory returned to that
session. A reinitialize, daemon restart, token rotation or transport replacement
creates a different session identity.

The selection is then signed into an ASCII compact
`run_start_negotiation_token` with exactly
`base64url_no_pad(JCS(RunStartNegotiationReceiptV1)) + "." +
`base64url_no_pad(P256_raw64_low_s_signature)`. The signature algorithm is
exactly `ecdsa_p256_sha256_raw64_low_s_v1` from the active
`AuthorityKeyCustodyProfileV1`; the signature input is
`chainworks.run-start-negotiation.v1\0` followed by the canonical payload bytes.
The payload contains its schema version, receipt ID and self-digest, logical
session digest, principal ID and non-sensitive `token_id`, client/protocol/tool
inventory digest, selection digest, cutover generation/revision,
`McpStartCapabilityProfileV1` digest, required `runs.start` request/result/error
schema digests, issue/expiry timestamps, gateway restart nonce, signing-key ID,
key epoch and custody-profile digest.
It contains no raw bearer, caller-supplied app claim or transport endpoint and
has a 60-second TTL.

Only after both objects exist does the tool construct
`AgentContextStartSelectionResultV2` with exactly `schema_version =
agent_context_start_selection_result_v2`, nested `context_selection`,
`run_start_negotiation_token`, and `start_selection_result_sha256`. The result
digest covers the complete nested selection and exact compact token bytes while
omitting only itself. The dependency graph is strictly
`context_selection -> negotiation receipt/token -> start-selection result`.
Neither the token nor the selection contains the result digest, so there is no
reverse reference or fixed-point serialization.

The release-gateway negotiation signing key is the purpose-scoped Secure
Enclave P-256 key selected by the active authority key-custody profile.
Rotation records a
monotonic key epoch; the current and immediately previous public keys verify for
at least 60 seconds plus clock skew, while only the current key signs. Gateway
restart changes the restart nonce and invalidates every prior token even if its
signature key remains valid. The start transaction decodes one canonical token,
rejects non-canonical base64/JCS or extra segments, recomputes its digest,
verifies signature/key epoch/restart nonce/expiry and matches the complete
logical session and capability profile. Token use is canonical only in the
authority store. Authority prepare inserts one predecessor-linked
`RunStartNegotiationConsumptionV1` under the unique key
`(run_start_negotiation_receipt_sha256, token_id)` with preallocated run ID,
principal/logical-session/profile, complete semantic request digest,
idempotency key, operation ID and state `reserved`. No candidate Run row can
reserve or consume it. The only transitions are
`reserved -> finalized` in the same pending-anchor authority transition that
activates the Run admission, or `reserved -> aborted` before any Run can become
claimable. An aborted row is terminal and the token cannot be reserved again;
the caller must obtain a new selection. Candidate-row deletion, projection
rollback or another idempotency key therefore cannot make the token unused.

For a new command, freshness and absence of any consumption row are required.
For a committed exact replay, the gateway first revalidates signature, key
epoch, restart nonce, logical session, principal, profile and stored receipt
digest, then reads the authority exact-request and finalized consumption rows;
only wall-clock expiry and terminal consumed state are accepted because the
original commit proved freshness and consumption. The replay lookup is scoped
to that same logical session and returns only the original Run ID and logical
result. Same token with another request digest/idempotency key or Run ID is a
non-enumerating terminal conflict. A new key cannot consume the token again,
and a new initialize/restart/session cannot replay a cached success; it must
obtain current readback or a new selection. Copied,
wrong-HTTP-session, wrong-stdio-session, wrong-transport, schema-incomplete or
malformed tokens always fail. Expired or already-consumed tokens fail unless
they satisfy the matching committed exact-replay branch above. Every denial
avoids revealing another client's support state. The token is compatibility/freshness evidence,
never a replacement for principal/caller/capability authorization.

Swift operator-shell compatibility is separate from run-start admission. Each
supported app release still supplies a release-signed
`ClientCapabilityManifestV1` to the checked-in contract harness, and its
qualifying proof-matrix row is required before `open_v2`. The live app remains a
GraphQL read/approval client and does not mint or forward the MCP run-start
token. If a future app owns `runs.start`, that is a separately versioned
northbound boundary and cannot reuse this MCP-session token.

The implementation checks in six generated compatibility schemas under
`docs/reference/mcp/agent-context/`: `run_start_request_v1.schema.json`,
`run_start_result_v1.schema.json`, `run_start_error_v1.schema.json`, and their
V2 counterparts. V1 freezes the current pre-cutover surface: no discriminator;
exactly these eight required fields: `idea_id`, `workflow_id`,
`workflow_title`, `workspace_root`, `artifact_root`, `workflow_yaml_path`,
`agent_catalog_yaml_path`, and UUIDv7 `idempotency_key`; the three current
optional configuration JSON strings;
present optional values must be strings and `null` is invalid; current
permissive unknown-field behavior from the descriptor's omitted
`additionalProperties`; and either the complete current Run
projection with `journal_id`, the existing delivery-preflight blocked result, or
the current structured JSON-RPC error. V2 is the closed
`additionalProperties: false` request/result/error triplet in the table below.
The capability inventory records six distinct schema digests. For each phase,
the advertised request descriptor must match its corresponding request schema;
observed result and error bytes must validate against their own distinct schema
digests. Rust validators and retained wire fixtures consume those same files;
prose is not the compatibility source and no contract claims that request,
result and error schemas have one shared digest.

The bridge/V1 `tools/list` object remains byte-compatible with the current
serializer: `runs.start` has `name`, `description` and `inputSchema` only. V2
extends `McpTool` and the serializer once, before `schema_prepared`, so every V2
agent-context tool descriptor contains exactly `name`, `description`,
`inputSchema`, `outputSchema`, and:

```json
{
  "_meta": {
    "chainworks/schemaContract": {
      "schemaVersion": "mcp_tool_schema_contract_v1",
      "requestSchemaVersion": "run_start_request_v2",
      "requestSchemaSha256": "sha256:...",
      "resultSchemaVersion": "run_start_result_v2",
      "resultSchemaSha256": "sha256:...",
      "errorSchemaVersion": "run_start_error_v2",
      "errorSchemaSha256": "sha256:..."
    }
  }
}
```

`inputSchema` and `outputSchema` are the fully materialized checked-in request
and result schema objects whose canonical digests equal the metadata fields; an
error schema is metadata because MCP has no standard `errorSchema` member. The
metadata object is closed, uses the exact namespaced key above, and appears for
all V2 agent-context tools with their own three schema versions/digests. The
session tool-inventory digest covers the complete ordered descriptors including
description, schemas and `_meta`; a missing `outputSchema`, missing error digest,
unknown metadata field or mismatch is `run_start_client_incompatible`. No V1
descriptor gains these fields, and the maintenance restart is the only
advertisement switch.

For a successful V2 `tools/call`, `outputSchema` validates the value of the MCP
`structuredContent` member, not the outer `CallToolResult`. The outer result is
exactly `{ content: [{ type: "text", text: <compact-jcs> }],
structuredContent: <logical-result>, isError: false }`, with no additional
content blocks or outer members. `<logical-result>` is the result object named
by `resultSchemaVersion`; `<compact-jcs>` is its RFC 8785 canonical UTF-8 JSON
with no newline, byte-for-byte. A mismatch between text and structured content
is `mcp_result_projection_invariant_failed` and no success is cached. JSON-RPC,
authorization and typed command errors remain JSON-RPC errors and never return
a schema-shaped successful `structuredContent`. Checked-in goldens cover the
complete bridge/V1 descriptor and result plus every V2 phase descriptor and
actual HTTP/stdio success/error frame, rather than validating a synthesized
logical object alone.

Byte ownership is explicit. `AuthorityExactRequestRecordV1` stores only the
canonical logical-result schema, canonical logical-result bytes/digest and
finalized operation identity. It never stores a JSON-RPC request ID, an outer
`CallToolResult`, HTTP headers/body framing, or stdio newline. The gateway
deterministically projects those logical bytes into
`mcp_call_tool_result_v2`, verifies `structuredContent` plus the compact-JCS text
mirror, and finally wraps that object in `mcp_jsonrpc_success_envelope_v2` with
the **current** request ID. Thus exact replay preserves logical-result and
`CallToolResult` bytes while rewrapping transport/JSON-RPC framing; HTTP and
stdio are not claimed byte-identical to one another. Errors are newly wrapped
from their canonical error contract with the current request ID and safe
correlation fields.

Same-logical-session transport loss continues through exact `runs.start`
replay. A gateway restart or stdio process loss creates a new logical session
and never accepts the old negotiation token as replay authority. Instead the
Operator-only read-only tool `runtime.agent_context.run_start_outcome.get`
accepts the original UUIDv7 idempotency key and
`run_start_recovery_fingerprint_sha256`, the canonical digest of every original
run-start semantic field and nested selection while excluding the negotiation
token, logical-session identity and idempotency key. The gateway requires the
same live principal ID as the original record plus
`RunsStartOutcomeRead`; bearer rotation or a new attested stdio session is
allowed only when that principal remains enabled and capable. It returns a
finalized logical `run_start_result_v2` from the authority exact-request record,
or returns typed `reconciliation_required` with the existing operation ID when
the record is `control_plane_committed | anchor_pending`. It performs no
reconciliation itself and changes zero rows, reservations, leases, timestamps,
attempt counters or projection state. It cannot create a Run, consume a token,
append an event or reinterpret request bytes. Missing,
different-principal/fingerprint, aborted-before-commit and unresolved records
return non-enumerating typed outcomes; an aborted caller must obtain a new
selection and new idempotency key. This distinct recovery readback preserves
one committed Run without permitting cross-session replay of the old command.

One daemon process advertises one `runs.start` generation. The maintenance
restart is the only switch point:

| Migration/cutover state | `tools/list` advertisement |
|---|---|
| `not_started / legacy_bridge` bridge daemon | V1 `runs.start`; no V2 start-selection tool |
| `schema_prepared` through `emergency_hold_v2` V2 daemon | V2 `runs.start` plus start-selection/cutover tools; ordinary start remains state-denied |
| `open_v2` | the same V2 descriptors; starts require a passing profile and same-session token |

There is no V1/V2 `oneOf`, per-request descriptor change or feature flag.
`McpLogicalSessionIdentityV1` binds the exact `tools/list` inventory digest, so a
token minted before any descriptor or phase restart cannot cross it. Black-box
HTTP and stdio fixtures retain V1 success/error bytes, V2 success/error bytes,
all phase-specific inventories, wrong-transport/session/key/expiry/replay
denials and zero-write assertions.

The compact incident-repair token has one wire grammar:
`base64url_no_pad(JCS(IncidentRepairAuthorizationTokenClaimsV1)) + "." +
base64url_no_pad(P256_raw64_low_s_signature)`. It uses the active authority
key-custody profile and exact algorithm
`ecdsa_p256_sha256_raw64_low_s_v1`. Its signature input is
`chainworks.incident-repair-token.v1\0 || canonical_claims_bytes`; claims bind
the signed repair-authorization digest, issuing principal, exact action-slot-set
digest, authority sequence, issue/expiry, key purpose/ID/epoch and random
one-use nonce plus custody-profile digest. Execute first performs ordinary live authorization and closed
request-shape validation, then canonical decode, digest/signature/current-key,
principal, authority-sequence, TTL and unconsumed-slot checks. Noncanonical
base64/JCS, extra segments, another principal, copied action set, expired epoch
or replay under a different slot is `release_incident_repair_denied` with zero
target disclosure. Exact replay of a finalized execute returns the same logical
outcome but never makes the slot available again.

Authority-operation pagination uses only
`AgentContextAuthorityOperationCursorV1`. The gateway snapshots one finalized
authority sequence/head, normalizes the closed state filter, sorts rows by raw
`(authority_sequence, operation_id)` ascending bytes, and MACs scope, live
principal ID, snapshot, filter, five-minute expiry, last tuple and gateway key
ID/epoch. The next page reads that same historical authority snapshot; it never
mixes newly finalized operations. Filter/scope/principal mismatch or malformed
MAC is non-retryable `cursor_invalid`; expired key/snapshot is retryable
`cursor_snapshot_unavailable` requiring pagination restart. A cursor call is zero-write and
does not refresh TTL, reconcile an operation or allocate an exact-request row.

The exact generated operation schemas are below. Rows with provider-broker tool
names are served only over the attested broker-proxy MCP stdio boundary and use
grant/session authorization rather than a northbound principal:

Each row binds the one request/result/error triplet with the matching request
and result names in the schema inventory; the result column does not repeat the
error name unless the error family needs additional clarification. For each
revision the generated gate derives the required operation count from
`AgentContextExistingPublicSurfaceInventoryV1` plus phase-eligible future rows and
requires exactly that many manifest rows and exactly three matching schema
rows per operation. The count is never a hand-maintained constant. Any missing,
extra or many-to-one mapping is an orphan or duplicate and fails before schema
publication.

| Tool | Request schema and required fields | Result schema and required fields |
|---|---|---|
| `runtime.agent_context.start_selection.get` | `agent_context_start_selection_request_v2`: `schema_version`, `workflow_id`; no caller path/client fields and no idempotency field because selection is read-only | `agent_context_start_selection_operation_result_v2`: one complete `agent_context_start_selection_result_v2` containing nested `context_selection`, compact ASCII `run_start_negotiation_token` minted for this authenticated MCP logical session, and aggregate result digest |
| `runtime.agent_context.run_start_outcome.get` | `run_start_outcome_recovery_request_v1`: `schema_version`, original UUIDv7 `idempotency_key`, `run_start_recovery_fingerprint_sha256`; read-only and accepts no old token/session/path | `run_start_outcome_recovery_result_v1`: `status = finalized` with the original logical `run_start_result_v2` and authority exact-request digest, `status = not_committed` with `new_selection_required`, or `status = reconciliation_required` with bounded existing operation ID/revision/digest; every branch is zero-write and never creates/finalizes a Run |
| `runtime.agent_context.cutover.get` | `agent_context_cutover_get_request_v2`: only `schema_version`; read-only | `agent_context_cutover_get_result_v2` containing one `agent_context_cutover_readback_v2`: cutover/migration state, head and revision; generation/candidate/repair state; replacement-admission ID/state/digest/expiry; inventory freshness/blockers; generic migration owner identity, epoch/deadline and absence status/receipt; self-admission and zero-unsafe digests; proof admission/matrix/epoch/run/latest receipt; current Swift/MCP capability qualification rows; provider-process clearance status/digest; active rollout-signal policy and notification-watchdog alert; separate promote/open release-evidence bundle, CI-selection, branch-protection, policy, alert-snapshot and unresolved-incident-set digests plus authority-evidence revisions; active release-generation admission scope/digest and transition-core digest; authority readback watermark, allowed next actions, required versions and current projection health |
