`legacy_journal_only` is a closed compatibility-only receipt class. It is legal
only when the approved-HEAD operation inventory proves the endpoint already
returns that exact journal shape and the manifest disposition is
`frozen_compatibility`; no new or V2 operation may select it. The gate compares
the frozen request/result/error and journal bytes against the baseline before
and after every phase. Migration or retirement requires a separately reviewed
manifest row and cannot silently reinterpret a legacy journal as a projection
receipt.

The generated manifest's `canonical_writer` field is decisive. Every V2 row
whose writer is `release_authority` or one of its purpose controllers, including
authority directives/approvals, principal/key epochs, registry publication,
incidents/repair authorization, release evidence, rollout policy, upgrade,
promotion/probe/open, owner absence, migration lease and replacement, declares
only `result_receipt_class = authority_projection`. Its logical result contains
the finalized authority operation ID/sequence and complete immutable outbox-
intent set and cannot contain `journal_id`, control-plane transaction ID or
`mutation_projection_receipt_v1`. Every row whose canonical writer is the
control-plane transaction layer declares only `control_plane_projection`.
Generation rejects a dual-class result, an authority row with a journal field,
a control-plane row with an authority outbox presented as its commit receipt, or
a projection payload written before authority finalize.

Every **northbound or private-internal V2 domain mutation** whose generated manifest row declares
`result_receipt_class = control_plane_projection | authority_projection`
requires the corresponding tagged projection receipt. A control-plane mutation uses `projection_status = pending`
and one complete immutable `mutation_projection_receipt_v1`. An authority-only
mutation uses `authority_projection_status = pending` and the finalized
operation's signed `AuthorityProjectionOutboxSetV1`; it never fabricates a
control-plane transaction/journal ID. The set contains every sorted non-empty
individual `AuthorityProjectionOutboxV1` row required by that logical result,
including all approval rebind/supersede, settlement and work-admission entries;
returning one representative row is schema-invalid. Both projection receipt
arms contain canonical source revision/head and `status_at_commit = pending`.
This is commit-time truth, not a live status field:
replay returns the original canonical domain outcome even when projection
workers have since applied or degraded an intent. MCP exact replay returns its
deterministically regenerated `CallToolResult` from stored logical-result bytes
and wraps it with the current JSON-RPC request ID; no stored JSON-RPC envelope,
HTTP body/header or stdio frame is replayed. GraphQL resolves that same outcome through the
caller's selection set; the same operation/variables/selection canonicalizes to
the same data object, while a different selection set may render a different
transport object without changing semantic outcome. Current status is read only
through SQLite-backed readback surfaces.

Provider-broker calls and non-authority internal helper actions instead declare
`result_receipt_class = broker_effect | broker_read | internal_action`. They do
not receive a generic projection receipt: `skills.script.run` returns its
authority-owned script/effect/apply receipt, Git capture returns its immutable
snapshot/capture receipt, resource/Git reads return bounded object/chunk
digests, and internal actions return their purpose-specific action journal. The
generator rejects a stateful broker result lacking its specific receipt, a
broker result carrying a control-plane/authority projection receipt, or a
northbound mutation with `result_receipt_class = none`. This scopes the rule
without weakening exactly-once broker authority. A `private_internal` operation
that mutates canonical authority truth follows the canonical-writer rule above
and therefore uses `authority_projection`, never `internal_action`.

The non-MCP heartbeat triplet is equally closed.
`runtime_owner_lease_renew_internal_request_v1` contains exactly schema version,
closed resource kind/ID/scope digest, lease ID/epoch/digest, owner identity
digest, expected resource phase/head/revision, authority component
identity/digest, monotonic clock-baseline ID and remaining budget, plus a
purpose-bound authority signature. Its
`runtime_owner_lease_renew_internal_result_v1` contains exactly `status =
active`, unchanged resource/lease ID/epoch/owner/phase/head, previous/new lease
digests, heartbeat/deadline, authority event digest, finalized authority
operation ID/sequence, `authority_projection_status = pending` and the complete
immutable `AuthorityProjectionOutboxSetV1`. Its manifest row is
`boundary_class = private_internal`, `canonical_writer = release_authority` and
`result_receipt_class = authority_projection`; it has no public name, journal or
mutation-projection receipt. Its
`runtime_owner_lease_renew_internal_error_v1` contains no success fields and one
of `unauthorized_component`, `audit_token_mismatch`,
`owner_identity_mismatch`, `resource_scope_mismatch`, `stale_lease`,
`reserved_takeover`, `phase_head_drift`, `lease_expired`,
`clock_baseline_mismatch`, or `signature_invalid`; every arm is pre-mutation.
The triplet is accepted only on the local release-authority XPC maintenance
channel after audit-token and observed process-identity verification and is
never exposed by GraphQL or MCP.

The additive V2 result schemas never use `replayed` as an action status. Frozen
compatibility schemas may retain an approved-HEAD `replayed` field or value only
when their captured bytes require it; the V2 adapter does not copy that value
into `CanonicalCommandOutcomeV1`. V2 replay provenance exists only in command
and audit readback.

`CanonicalCommandOutcomeCoreV1` is constructed after any server-side resource
ID and immutable generation binding/selection are preallocated but before
either control-plane transaction or release-authority operation allocation. It
binds the logical operation, preallocated resource identity, frozen binding/
selection where applicable, live authenticated principal and token ID,
canonical request and semantic-intent identities, canonical writer, receipt
class and tagged logical-result schema. It explicitly excludes every release-
run admission, future transaction, journal, authority operation, projection and
finalized-result identity. A release-authority operation core may bind the
outcome-core digest; the reverse edge is schema-invalid. After exactly one
writer commits, `CanonicalCommandOutcomeV1` binds that core to exactly one
finalized control-plane journal/transaction or authority operation/sequence,
the committed source heads, original action status, stored logical-result bytes
and the operation's sole projection receipt or authority outbox set. Reverse
edges and a result that names both writer families are invalid.

The first committed `CanonicalCommandOutcomeV1` is the only V2 domain success
representation. MCP exact and semantic-alias replay use its stored logical
result to regenerate one schema-validated `CallToolResult`, then wrap the
current JSON-RPC request ID and current HTTP/stdio framing. GraphQL exact and
semantic-alias replay deterministically render that same canonical logical
outcome for the current selection set and compare after GraphQL response
canonicalization, never by reusing MCP bytes or bytes from another selection
set. Lost response, cross-transport retry and crash-after-commit fixtures prove
that lookup returns the original outcome and never allocates a second journal,
authority operation, mutation, projection intent or external effect.

For `agent_context_reprobe_request_v2`, `reprobe_reason =
infrastructure_inconclusive` requires `prior_probe_receipt_sha256` and forbids
`process_clearance_set_sha256`; it is valid only from `probe_v2 /
probe_inconclusive` with candidate state `probe_active`.
`process_hold_cleared` requires the complete `process_clearance_set_sha256` from
cutover readback, forbids the prior probe receipt, and is valid only from
`emergency_hold_v2 / emergency_hold` when every unresolved invariant belongs to
that process-only clearance set. The candidate may be `promoted` after a prior
open or already `probe_active` when the hold interrupted a proof epoch. The
service mints and consumes a proof admission inside the same transaction that
creates the proof run. No caller can mint, reuse, or separately consume a
reprobe admission.

The semantic intent hashes are closed. Exact caller-request lookup retains the
existing global unique scope `(principal_id, caller_request_id)` across all
commands. Reusing one caller request ID for another command is always
`command_idempotency_conflict`, even if that command's semantic fields happen
to hash equally. Semantic-alias lookup is separately scoped by authenticated
principal ID plus canonical command name and the command's replay policy; every
listed field uses canonical wire bytes.
Neither request ID, transport metadata, projection status, journal ID, response
field or server-generated timestamp is included. Command-declared expected
lease identity/epoch/digest, resource head and baseline fields are semantic
inputs exactly where the table lists them; no server-generated renewal output
is added implicitly:

| Command | Complete semantic intent fields |
|---|---|
| `runs.authority.append` | `run_id`, `expected_authority_chain_head`, adapter-derived `source_kind`, `directive_sha256`, sorted `supersedes` |
| `approvals.reissue` | `approval_id`, `expected_binding_generation`, `expected_binding_sha256`, `expected_authority_chain_head` |
| existing GraphQL `approveApproval` | `approval_id`, fixed `resolution = approve` and canonical digest of present/absent bounded comment |
| existing GraphQL `rejectApproval` | `approval_id`, fixed `resolution = reject` and canonical bounded-reason digest |
| existing GraphQL `approvalsResolve` | current approval ID, resolution and present/absent comment semantics exactly as implemented; no V2 alias is generated |
| existing MCP `approvals.resolve` | exact current stage-approval semantics for the qualified arm; the advertised mediation arm is a frozen incompatible legacy profile and is never a V2 semantic-alias or qualification input |
| `approvals.resolve_authority` | `approval_id`, `resolution`, canonical digest of present/absent bounded comment, `binding_generation`, `approval_authority_binding_sha256`, `expected_authority_chain_head` |
| `lead_mediation.resolve_authority` | confirmation/mediation/run IDs, conflict fingerprint, resolution, canonical bounded-comment digest, binding generation/digest and expected authority head |
| `runtime.agent_context.skill_registry.publish` | `skill_registry_source_sha256`, `expected_registry_revision`, `expected_skill_registry_sha256` |
| `runtime.agent_context.release_evidence.issue` | `release_evidence_selection_sha256` from the submitted complete nested selection, including its authority-minted `issuance_generation` and issuance state |
| `runtime.agent_context.release_evidence.expiry.reconcile` | transition/candidate semantic key, exact available issuance generation/revision/digest, expiry-lease ID/epoch/revision/digest, correlated baseline/deadline observation and conditional owner-absence receipt ID/digest |
| `runtime.agent_context.rollout_policy.activate` | signed new `rollout_signal_policy_sha256` and `rollout_signal_migration_plan_sha256`, expected predecessor policy digest/activation sequence, current unresolved-incident-set digest and expected authority revision |
| `runtime.agent_context.rollout_signal.retirement_settle` | retired-hold incident/revision/digest, predecessor/current policy and migration-plan digests, computed retirement-settlement evidence digest |
| `runtime.agent_context.authority_upgrade.begin` | successor release-bundle/helper-matrix/protocol/store-schema identities, expected current authority generation/head/anchor/writer-lease digest, compatibility-proof digest, complete authority-generation-drain-inventory digest, every family head and zero-active aggregate digest |
| `runtime.agent_context.key_epoch.transition` | action, purpose, conditional exact affected epoch, expected authority/key-registry/custody-profile heads; overlap/account/key bytes are never caller input |

| `runtime.agent_context.promote` | `candidate_id`, `candidate_sha256`, `promotion_receipt_sha256`, `proof_matrix_sha256`, decoded `release_evidence_bundle_sha256`, `expected_candidate_state`, `expected_cutover_generation`, `expected_cutover_revision` |
| `runtime.agent_context.probe_start` | `expected_cutover_generation`, `expected_cutover_revision`, `candidate_sha256`, `proof_admission_id`, `proof_matrix_sha256`, `probe_workflow_sha256` |
| `runtime.agent_context.reprobe` | `expected_cutover_generation`, `expected_cutover_revision`, `candidate_id`, `candidate_sha256`, `expected_candidate_state`, `reprobe_reason`, `expected_probe_epoch`, the one conditionally required evidence digest, `proof_matrix_sha256`, `probe_workflow_sha256` |
| `runtime.agent_context.open` | `expected_cutover_generation`, `expected_cutover_revision`, `expected_probe_epoch`, `candidate_sha256`, `proof_matrix_sha256`, `proof_run_id`, `probe_receipt_sha256`, `rollout_soak_receipt_sha256`, decoded `release_evidence_bundle_sha256` |
| `runtime.agent_context.incidents.acknowledge` | `incident_id`, `expected_incident_revision`, `expected_release_incident_sha256`, `expected_alert_snapshot_sha256`, canonical digest of present/absent bounded comment |
| `runtime.agent_context.incidents.resolve` | `incident_id`, `expected_incident_revision`, `expected_release_incident_sha256`, `expected_alert_snapshot_sha256`, `clearing_sample_pair_sha256`, computed `resolution_evidence_sha256` |
| `runtime.agent_context.incidents.repair_authorize` | tagged scope plus exact incident/revision/alert snapshot, incident-independent alert-health/sampler/source identity, notification/watchdog alert identity, or incident-independent watchdog-health/lease/inventory identity, and canonical sorted requested-action/target digest |

| `runtime.agent_context.authority_operations.reconcile` | operation ID, expected operation revision/digest/phase and exact recorded observation set to be reconciled |
| `runtime.principals.issue` | new principal/class/capability/scope fields, expected table/policy digests and complete target-owned enrollment-proof/successor-key digests |
| `runtime.principals.rotate_self` | server-derived authenticated principal/token/logical-session/current credential generation, expected table revision and complete successor-key enrollment-proof digest |
| `runtime.principals.reset_credential` | target principal/current credential and key-binding generations, expected table/principal/policy revisions, canonical bounded-reason digest and current-signing-key enrollment-proof/successor-key-binding digests; no old bearer or caller key |
| `runtime.principals.rescope` | principal, complete new class/capability/scope set and expected table/principal/policy revisions/digests |

| `runtime.principals.revoke` | principal, conditional exact credential generation, expected table/principal revisions and canonical bounded-reason digest |
| `runtime.principals.verifier_epoch.transition` | action, conditional exact affected epoch and expected verifier-registry/table/authority heads; account/key/overlap bytes are never caller input |
| `runtime.agent_context.skill_broker.reconcile` | grant/install epoch/revision/digest, attempt/reducer checkpoint and complete observation-set digest |
| `runtime.agent_context.skill_effects.reconcile` | request/effect/intent/apply-journal revisions/digests and complete pre/post observation-set digest |
| `runtime.agent_context.authority_upgrade.reconcile` | handoff ID and exact handoff/action-journal/recovery revisions/digests; no caller-selected action |
| `runtime.owner_absence.verify` | resource kind/ID, owner kind/instance, runtime-owner identity digest, complete expected lease ID/epoch/digest, resource head/revision and clock-baseline ID |
| `runtime.agent_context.migration_lease.acquire` | expected migration phase/head and cutover revision, expected prior lease state and conditional prior lease ID/epoch/digest |
| `runtime.agent_context.migration_lease.takeover` | expected migration phase/head and cutover revision, expired lease ID/epoch/digest, owner-absence receipt ID/digest |
| `runtime.agent_context.replacement_admission.issue` | expected migration phase/head and cutover generation/revision, old/new candidate and passing receipt digests, proof-matrix/schema-compatibility digests, lease epoch/digest, conditional owner-absence receipt, inventory and zero-unsafe digests |
| `runtime.agent_context.replace_candidate` | replacement admission ID/digest, expected migration phase/head, expected cutover generation/revision, old candidate digest, new candidate ID/digest, passing promotion receipt, proof-matrix digest, migration-lease epoch/digest, inventory digest and zero-unsafe digest |
| existing `provider_session.mark_process_absent` | `provider_session_id`, integer `cancellation_epoch` |
| `provider_session.mark_process_absent_v2` | `provider_session_id`, integer `cancellation_epoch`, `dispatch_hold_sha256` |

Semantic alias is command-declared rather than universal:

| Command class | Different request ID, same semantic intent |
|---|---|
| ordinary durable mutation with a terminal reusable outcome | joins in-flight or aliases the finalized logical result |
| one-use issuance while the same issuance generation is `available` | joins/aliases that one issuance only |
| one-use issuance after `consumed`, `expired`, or `revoked` | stale precondition; caller must obtain the next authority-minted selection/generation |
| one-use consume/execute command | may alias only the already finalized consume/execute outcome; it never makes the admission/token available again |
| read-only GET/list | no command lease, exact-request row or semantic alias; each call reads one authorized snapshot |

This policy applies to release-evidence bundles, proof/replacement/run/work/
attempt admissions, repair authorizations and any future one-use capability.
Exact replay under the original globally unique caller request ID remains a
historical replay of the original logical result; terminal current state is
reported separately and no exact replay refreshes expiry or consumption.

`runs.start` intentionally has no second semantic-alias layer: its existing
UUIDv7 key and canonical MCP request hash are the command identity, and the
single-active-run invariant remains separate. The MCP canonical request hash
excludes only `idempotency_key`; it includes tool name, canonical request
arguments, principal ID, derived non-sensitive `token_id`, caller class and
matched boundary row exactly as the current P081 contract requires. For V2
`runs.start`, normalization replaces the compact token bytes with the verified
`run_start_negotiation_receipt_sha256` and additionally includes
`mcp_logical_session_sha256`; therefore transport loss inside one HTTP session
can replay while an identical key/request in a different initialized session
cannot. Raw bearer
bytes are never hashed, persisted or returned. Other commands' semantic hashes
exclude both request IDs, which is what makes a different-ID alias replay
possible without weakening the MCP same-key conflict check.

All northbound command errors use a closed `agent_context_command_error_v1`
payload with `classification`, Boolean `retryable`, `retry_mode`, safe request
IDs and the bounded expected/current fields allowed below. Rust and Swift share
these exact outcomes:

Validation precedence is identical for HTTP and stdio: JSON-RPC framing and
tool-name dispatch; live principal/class/capability; initialized logical
session/advertised inventory; closed request-schema shape/required
fields/types/bounds; then token/signature/session/freshness and resource
preconditions. Therefore for an authorized initialized caller an omitted V2
negotiation-token field is
`-32602 / invalid_request`; a present but malformed, stale, wrong-session or
unsupported token is the non-enumerating `-32009 /
run_start_client_incompatible`. No adapter may validate token bytes before the
closed request shape or return both codes for one input.

| Condition | MCP JSON-RPC / `data.code` | GraphQL `extensions.code` | Classification | `retryable` / `retry_mode` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| live principal/class/capability denial | `-32004 / authorization_denied` | `authorization_denied` | `authorization_denied` | `false / terminal` |
| schema, bounds or conditional-field failure | `-32602 / invalid_request` | `invalid_request` | `invalid_request` | `false / correct_payload` |
| same boundary or command identity committed | success, original logical result reprojected with current request ID | success, original logical fields rendered for current selection | `exact_replay` | not applicable |
| different caller request ID and same semantic intent committed | success, original logical result reprojected; alias row recorded separately | success, original logical fields rendered for current selection | `alias_replay` | not applicable |
| same MCP key and same hash pending | `-32603 / idempotency_in_flight` | not applicable | `mcp_request_in_flight` | `true / exact_retry_after` |
| same MCP key and different hash | `-32603 / idempotency_conflict` | not applicable | `mcp_request_conflict` | `false / new_key_for_new_intent` |
| same caller request ID and different command/intent | `-32009 / command_idempotency_conflict` | `command_idempotency_conflict` | `command_request_conflict` | `false / new_request_for_new_intent` |
| same semantic lease still pending | `-32009 / command_in_flight` | `command_in_flight` | `command_in_flight` | `true / exact_retry_after` |
| stale head/generation/revision/binding or approval no longer actionable | `-32009 / stale_precondition` | `stale_precondition` | `stale_precondition` | `true / refresh_then_new_request` |
| current-head semantic duplicate | `-32009 / semantic_duplicate` | `semantic_duplicate` | `semantic_duplicate` | `false / terminal` |
| authorized resource is absent | `-32002 / resource_missing` | `resource_missing` | `resource_missing` | `false / correct_identifier` |
| pending authority-bound approval cap reached | `-32009 / pending_approval_cap_exceeded` | `pending_approval_cap_exceeded` | `resource_limit` | `true / settle_existing_then_new_request` |
| attempt fenced by newer hard authority | `-32009 / authority_recheck_required` | `authority_recheck_required` | `policy_denial` | `true / prepare_new_attempt` |
| provider sandbox missing, mismatched or escaped | `-32009 / provider_sandbox_unavailable` | `provider_sandbox_unavailable` | `policy_denial` | `false / replace_candidate_or_host` |
| active key-custody profile, Secure Enclave or canonical signature ABI is unavailable/mismatched | `-32009 / authority_key_custody_unsupported` | `authority_key_custody_unsupported` | `policy_denial` | `false / use_supported_host_or_release` |
| authority-generation handoff external state is partial, live-both or not equal to a journal pre/post image | `-32009 / authority_handoff_identity_hold` | `authority_handoff_identity_hold` | `reconciliation_required` | `true / inspect_and_reconcile_same_handoff` |
| evidence lease/signature/identity invalid | `-32009 / agent_quality_evidence_admission_invalid` | `agent_quality_evidence_admission_invalid` | `evidence_incomplete` | `false / issue_new_lease` |
| proof matrix incomplete or cell mismatched | `-32009 / agent_context_proof_matrix_incomplete` | `agent_context_proof_matrix_incomplete` | `evidence_incomplete` | `true / complete_same_matrix` |
| present run-start negotiation token malformed/stale/wrong-session/unsupported | `-32009 / run_start_client_incompatible` | not applicable | `compatibility_denial` | `false / renegotiate_same_mcp_session` |
| migration lease acquire conflicts with a live or unreleased owner | `-32009 / agent_context_migration_lease_conflict` | `agent_context_migration_lease_conflict` | `ownership_conflict` | `true / refresh_or_wait_for_release` |
| owner absence is live, ambiguous, PID-reused, scope-mismatched or unverifiable | `-32009 / runtime_owner_absence_inconclusive` | `runtime_owner_absence_inconclusive` | `ownership_conflict` | `true / obtain_fresh_owner_evidence` |
| migration writer has stale lease epoch | `-32009 / agent_context_migration_lease_fenced` | `agent_context_migration_lease_fenced` | `ownership_conflict` | `true / refresh_lease_readback` |
| forward replacement has unsafe or stale evidence | `-32009 / agent_context_candidate_replacement_blocked` | `agent_context_candidate_replacement_blocked` | `reconciliation_required` | `true / settle_blockers_then_new_request` |
| protected skill source/signature/predecessor is invalid or stale | `-32009 / skill_registry_publication_blocked` | not exposed | `evidence_incomplete` | `true / refresh_source_then_new_request` |
| release-evidence signature, scope, head, ruleset, candidate or transition is invalid | `-32009 / release_evidence_invalid` | `release_evidence_invalid` | `evidence_incomplete` | `false / issue_correct_evidence_bundle` |
| release-evidence bundle or one selected receipt/snapshot is expired or revision-stale | `-32009 / release_evidence_stale` | `release_evidence_stale` | `evidence_incomplete` | `true / ingest_then_issue_new_evidence_bundle` |
| rollout-policy predecessor is stale or an unresolved changed/removed signal lacks one valid signed migration-plan row | `-32009 / rollout_policy_incident_migration_blocked` | `rollout_policy_incident_migration_blocked` | `stale_precondition` | `true / refresh_or_submit_signed_signal_migration_plan` |
| alert snapshot is unknown/firing or unresolved incident set is nonempty | `-32009 / release_alert_gate_blocked` | `release_alert_gate_blocked` | `policy_denial` | `true / resolve_alert_then_issue_new_evidence_bundle` |
| incident acknowledge/resolve revision, state, owner or clearing evidence is stale/invalid | `-32009 / release_incident_precondition_failed` | not exposed | `stale_precondition` | `true / refresh_incident_then_new_request` |
| incident repair authorization/action is broad, stale, expired, consumed or target-mismatched | `-32009 / release_incident_repair_denied` | not exposed | `policy_denial` | `true / refresh_incident_then_new_request` |
| notification is not delivery-exhausted or requeue CAS is stale | `-32009 / incident_notification_requeue_conflict` | not exposed | `stale_precondition` | `true / refresh_notification_then_new_request` |
| selected authority evidence key/revision is held by another operation | `-32009 / authority_evidence_fenced` | `authority_evidence_fenced` | `ownership_conflict` | `true / reconcile_or_wait_then_refresh_selection` |
| control-plane writer lease is absent/stale/draining/fenced | `-32009 / control_plane_writer_fenced` | `control_plane_writer_fenced` | `ownership_conflict` | `true / complete_writer_handoff` |
| authority projection worker lease is stale, absent or fenced | `-32009 / projection_worker_fenced` | `projection_worker_fenced` | `ownership_conflict` | `true / refresh_or_take_over_projection_lease` |
| authority operation has an unreconciled prepare/conditional-control-plane-commit/anchor/finalize state | `-32009 / release_authority_reconciliation_required` | `release_authority_reconciliation_required` | `reconciliation_required` | `true / reconcile_same_operation` |
| generation/run/work/attempt launch admission is forged, stale, wrong-scope or consumed | `-32009 / provider_attempt_launch_admission_invalid` | not exposed | `policy_denial` | `false / prepare_authorized_work_and_attempt` |
| authority projection has not reached the required authority sequence | `-32009 / authority_projection_pending` | `authority_projection_pending` | `evidence_incomplete` | `true / wait_or_reconcile_projection` |
| authority projection bytes/head disagree at the required sequence | `-32009 / authority_projection_degraded` | `authority_projection_degraded` | `durable_truth_corrupt` | `false / operator_repair_projection` |
| successful MCP structured/text projection disagrees with the result schema | `-32603 / mcp_result_projection_invariant_failed` | not applicable | `durable_truth_corrupt` | `false / operator_repair` |
| malformed or wrong-scope connection cursor | `-32009 / cursor_invalid`, reason `malformed` or `filter_changed` | `cursor_invalid` | `cursor_invalid` | `false / correct_cursor_or_restart_pagination` |
| expired or unavailable cursor snapshot | `-32009 / cursor_snapshot_unavailable`, reason `expired` or `snapshot_unavailable` | `cursor_snapshot_unavailable` | `cursor_snapshot_unavailable` | `true / restart_pagination` |
| required projection-intent write rolls back | `-32603 / projection_intent_commit_failed` | `projection_intent_commit_failed` | `storage_not_committed` | `true / exact_retry` |
| committed outcome or alias row is corrupt | `-32603 / idempotency_replay_corrupt` | `idempotency_replay_corrupt` | `durable_truth_corrupt` | `false / operator_repair` |

Concurrent same-intent losers observe in-flight or alias replay according to
whether the winner committed; different-intent CAS losers observe
`stale_precondition`. No race-dependent generic `INTERNAL` outcome is allowed.

Known domain denials never collapse to `internal`. The complete generated
`errors.yaml` inventory, not a second prose list, decides whether a canonical
public row projects through MCP `-32009`, another declared JSON-RPC number, or a
GraphQL extension. Where both transports exist they use that row's byte-equal
lowercase code, classification, retryability/mode and safe fields. Internal
reasons first pass through the exhaustive normalization table in the Runtime
Failure Contract; an alias can never escape as a second public spelling.
Evaluation and sandbox failures likewise use their one generated registry row
with classification `evidence_incomplete`, `policy_denial`, or
`reconciliation_required` as declared there.

GraphQL errors implement `agent_context_graphql_error_v1`: exact `code`,
`classification`, `retryable`, `retryMode`, authorized `requestId`, and only the
same bounded expected/current detail allowed in MCP. MCP and GraphQL fixture
generation reads one checked-in error registry; adding a domain failure without
both mappings fails schema generation and the gate. Only an unclassified defect
may return `internal`, and that path emits no domain or resource detail.

The operation manifest assigns every GraphQL-reachable error code to exactly one
delivery channel. Parse/coercion/schema failures, missing authentication,
capability/caller-class denial, non-enumerating resource denial, transport
failure and system/storage/invariant defects are GraphQL `errors` only and
return no mutation-union data. An authenticated, authorized, structurally valid
request for a visible resource may return a generated `DenialPayload` union arm
only for the operation's closed expected domain/precondition denial set. No code
may appear in both sets, and a resolver cannot choose the channel dynamically.
`operations.yaml` records the partition per GraphQL operation; generated SDL,
resolver adapters and fixtures fail when an arm is missing, duplicated or
reachable through the wrong channel. Frozen legacy mutations retain their exact
HEAD payload/error partition and are not rewritten by this V2 rule.

All UUID/ID strings are canonical lowercase ASCII and at most 200 bytes unless
their existing domain type is stricter; digests are exactly `sha256:` plus 64
lowercase hex characters. Revisions/generations that can exceed GraphQL/JSON
safe integers use canonical unsigned decimal strings with no sign or leading
zero. Paths retain the existing run-start canonicalization and 4096-byte cap.
Each optional configuration JSON string retains its current 64 KiB decoded cap.
`comment` is at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Error `path` is a JSON Pointer of at most
256 ASCII bytes and `reason` is exactly `missing_required`, `unknown_field`,
`wrong_type`, `invalid_format`, `out_of_bounds`, or
`conditional_field_missing`, not arbitrary parser text.

`context_selection` is exactly the nested selection object in the discovery
result, including `selection_sha256`; it never includes the token or aggregate
result digest. The server recomputes and compares it under
the run-start transaction; the client does not edit or omit fields. A successful
`run_start_context_admission_v2` contains exactly `schema_version`, `run_id`,
canonical decimal-string `cutover_generation` and `cutover_revision`,
`candidate_sha256`, `promotion_receipt_sha256`, `workflow_source_sha256`,
`workflow_normalized_plan_sha256`, `catalog_snapshot_sha256`,
`authority_source_mapping_policy_sha256`, ordered
`authority_source_manifest_sha256s`,
`skill_registry_sha256`, `skill_pair_disposition_set_sha256`,
`skill_neighbor_graph_sha256`,
`skill_trigger_harness_sha256`, `skill_pair_proof_set_sha256`,
`proof_matrix_sha256`,
`run_start_negotiation_receipt_sha256`, normalized MCP client identity and
negotiated tool-schema inventory digest,
`release_generation_admission_sha256`, `release_run_admission_sha256`,
`binding_sha256`, `context_schema_version`, and `base_authority_chain_head`.

The boundary authorization matrix is closed:

| Surface/tool | Required `PrincipalClass` | Required derived `CallerClass` | Required capability |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCP start-selection readback | `Operator` | `AgentOperator` | `RuntimeAgentContextStartSelectionGet` |

These checks are conjunctive. An `Agent` principal also derives
`AgentOperator` on MCP, but fails the required principal class even if its
principal entry was mistakenly granted one of these capabilities. Automation,
Observer, ReadOnlyOperator, DeveloperBreakGlass, caller-class overrides, and
caller-supplied provenance cannot perform these production mutations. The only
Automation exceptions are the three lease/barrier-bound internal rows above;
they have no candidate, promotion, cutover, run, incident or effect authority.
GraphQL exposes no
run-start, append, promote, probe, reprobe, open or candidate-replacement
mutation.

Validation precedence is normative and shared by HTTP MCP and stdio MCP:

1. bounded JSON-RPC envelope parsing returns only standard parse/request errors;
2. live bearer principal resolution, principal enabled/revoked state, exact
   principal class, derived caller class, tool provenance, and capability are
   checked before tool-specific schema, run, candidate, or generation lookup;
3. the initialized `McpLogicalSessionIdentityV1`, restart nonce and advertised
   descriptor inventory are verified before any replay lookup;
4. the complete request schema and ID versions are validated; a missing
   `context_selection` is only `-32602`, never a version/state error;
5. path and identifier normalization completes without mutation;
6. for `runs.start`, negotiation signature/session/profile/restart binding is
   verified as described above before the MCP UUIDv7 exact-request lookup; the
   lookup key and stored canonical request hash include
   `mcp_logical_session_sha256` and
   `run_start_negotiation_receipt_sha256`; other tools proceed directly to the
   applicable exact-request lookup. A cross-store authority record returns only
   `finalized_success`, `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT`,
   `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`, or the typed same-operation reconciliation path; its
   provisional control-plane outcome is never a cached success. Ordinary
   control-plane commands retain the existing finalized cache behavior and
   `-32603` structured envelope;
7. the durable UUIDv4 command lease applies exact-request and same-intent alias
   precedence before semantic state checks;
8. authorized semantic existence, expected-state, head, generation, receipt,
   and admission CAS checks execute in one command transaction.

Authorization denial uses the existing non-enumerating `-32004` policy
envelope. All post-authorization failures use the common command payload and
classification table above. Schema errors use `-32602` and add bounded
`agent_context_request_error_v1 { path, reason }` detail. Version, generation,
digest, binding, or cutover-state failures use `-32009`, message `context
admission denied`, and add `agent_context_admission_error_v1` detail with only
safe expected/current generation, revision, state, and schema fields.
Authorized missing resources use existing `-32002` plus classification
`resource_missing`. Optional details are absent rather than null. No error
includes raw paths, bearer material, launch credentials, prompts, directive
values, or evidence bytes.

The same vectors cover every malformed field, unauthorized principal/caller
combination, revoked or re-scoped principal, exact replay, alias replay,
in-flight lease, idempotency conflict, stale CAS, semantic duplicate, and
concurrent loser. Given a valid bounded JSON-RPC envelope, an old authorized app
omitting `context_selection` receives exactly `-32602` after cutover; an
unauthorized caller receives `-32004` regardless of whether its tool payload is
malformed.

2. Normalize fields that are semantic sets by sorting them according to the
   schema's declared key before serialization. Arrays that express workflow or
   instruction order retain their declared order.
3. Serialize as RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme bytes. Duplicate object
   keys are invalid. Floating-point numbers are prohibited in these contracts;
   JSON numeric fields are integers in the interoperable range
   `-9007199254740991...9007199254740991`. Larger signed or unsigned values use
   schema-declared canonical decimal strings. Timestamps are canonical UTC
   RFC3339 strings with exactly millisecond precision.
4. Preserve the input Unicode scalar sequence exactly. Do not apply NFC, NFD,
   case folding, or locale-sensitive transformation. Canonically equivalent but
   byte-distinct Unicode strings therefore have different digests by design.
5. Hash `domain || 0x00 || canonical_json`, where `domain` is the ASCII schema
   name and version, for example `chainworks:task_assignment_v1`.
6. Encode SHA-256 as lowercase hexadecimal with the `sha256:` prefix.

A purpose-signed structured object never places signature bytes inside that
payload. It is stored or transported as
`chainworks_signed_contract_v1 { payload_schema, payload, payload_sha256,
key_purpose, key_id, key_epoch, authority_key_custody_profile_sha256,
algorithm = ecdsa_p256_sha256_raw64_low_s_v1, signature_base64url }`.
`payload_sha256` must equal the payload's self-digest above. The exact signature
input is `chainworks:signed-contract:v1\0 || utf8(payload_schema) || 0x00 ||
utf8(key_purpose) || 0x00 || utf8(key_id) || 0x00 ||
canonical_decimal(key_epoch) || 0x00 ||
decoded_digest_32(authority_key_custody_profile_sha256) || 0x00 ||
utf8(algorithm) || 0x00 ||
decoded_digest_32(payload_sha256)`. Base64url is unpadded and canonical. The
decoded signature is exactly the canonical 64-byte P-256 `r || low_s` value
defined by the custody profile. The outer envelope has no self-digest, and its closed schema uses the payload
discriminator to select the exact referenced payload schema. A changed
algorithm, custody profile, key ID, key epoch, purpose, payload digest or non-canonical envelope
therefore invalidates the signature before any state lookup or mutation.
Duplicate-key, high-`s`, DER, wrong-length, wrong-purpose and cross-epoch
fixtures are mandatory. Compact
run-start and release-
evidence tokens use their separately specified framing and signature domains;
they are not this envelope.

File-content digests hash exact file bytes with the domain
`chainworks:skill_resource_v1`. The skill bundle digest hashes the canonical
manifest, not a directory walk or host metadata. Authority event hashes also
bind the previous head digest, giving the overlay a verifiable hash chain.

Normative Rust and Swift fixtures include:

- shuffled object insertion order;
- ordered and set-valued arrays;
- composed and decomposed Unicode examples;
- quotes, control characters, slashes, and non-ASCII text;
- minimum and maximum interoperable JSON integers plus decimal-string 64-bit
  extrema;
- every excluded self-digest field;
- every existing legacy snapshot representation retained as opaque bytes.

Neither Foundation `JSONEncoder.sortedKeys` nor ordinary `serde_json`
serialization alone is considered the normative implementation. Both runtimes
must pass the shared canonical-byte fixtures.

## Legacy Snapshot to Context V2 Transition

Snapshots with an absent `agent_context_envelope_schema` remain byte-for-byte
legacy records under the existing plan-format reader selected by the mapping
above. They are never recompiled, normalized, or converted during readback.

| Surface | Legacy context-absent behavior | `agent_context_envelope_v2` behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Run mission | Idea appears only for selected tasks | frozen `RunMissionV1` base plus pinned `EffectiveRunMissionV1` overlay projection |
| Agent `prompt` | arbitrary injected catalog prompt | prohibited in production catalogs; content moves to role, skill, runtime policy, or output contract |
| `skill_ref` | one legacy skill identifier | replaced by catalog `allowed_skills` and task `skills` |
| `skill_role` | optional injected specialization | prohibited |
| `roles/*.md` | may append protected role text | not loaded as role authority; retained only as ordinary reference data when explicitly needed |
| hardcoded role maps | `proposalReviewModeMap` and Rust equivalent may inject role blocks | prohibited and removed from V2 resolution |
| `resolved_skill.injected_content` | precomposed prompt fragment | replaced by `SkillBundleSnapshotRef` plus parsed `SKILL.md` body |
| inline/builtin skills | accepted | rejected for a new production run |
| Role authority | prompt, skill role, and generic specialization may compete | exactly one `AgentRoleV1` protected section |

Migration is an explicit source rewrite of the canonical catalog and workflow.
Each current `skill_role` is translated into an explicit existing-agent role
charter and, where needed, a typed task mode. V2 compilation fails if any legacy
role or prompt field remains. It does not perform a heuristic runtime migration.

## Agent Skills Registry

### Standards Baseline

Bundles follow the Agent Skills specification and guidance as published from
the official [`agentskills/agentskills`](https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/tree/69ef37e9424c0a7ea9dd2293b559e43ec8176379)
repository at immutable commit
`69ef37e9424c0a7ea9dd2293b559e43ec8176379`, observed on 2026-08-28. The
repository stores `docs/reference/agent-skills-upstream-lock.json` with that
commit, the exact specification, best-practice, description-optimization and
evaluation source paths, every vendored file SHA-256, the `skills-ref` source
tree digest and its validation-corpus digest. A dependency update is a reviewed
candidate-manifest change; a branch, tag, website response or host-installed
package is never an implicit production input.

A Rust `SkillBundleAdmissionV1` implementation is the production admission
authority on every host. A host-installed `skills-ref` executable is never used
to decide whether a run can start. Gates compare the Rust result with the
lockfile-built `skills-ref` binary and vendored corpus; a missing, mismatched or
network-fetched installation fails the gate and cannot change admission truth.

Progressive disclosure is mechanical. Checked-in
`PromptTokenBudgetPolicyV1` pins `chainworks_prompt_tokenizer_v1`, its merge
table/corpus digest and the complete production provider/model tokenizer
compatibility table. Admission requires each `SKILL.md` body to contain at most
500 lines and at most 5,000 policy tokens under every compatible production
profile. A task composition may inject at most 12,000 policy tokens across at
most four bodies, in addition to the byte limits below. Every compatibility row
also pins the provider framing/tool-schema tokenizer, context window, exact
initial-request ceiling and completion reserve used by the full-envelope rule
above. Unknown tokenizer identity, token-count overflow or a provider profile
without a complete pinned compatibility row fails candidate admission. Longer
schemas, rubrics, examples and templates must be referenced bundle resources
and are not injected into the initial prompt.

### Canonical Layout

The repository-owned source is:

```text
.agents/skills/<skill-name>/
|-- SKILL.md
|-- contracts/
|   `-- skill-scripts.json
|-- references/
|-- scripts/
`-- assets/

.agent-evals/public/<skill-name>/
|-- evals.json
`-- fixtures/
```

`SKILL.md` and `contracts/skill-scripts.json` are mandatory. A skill with no
executable scripts stores the closed empty script map in that contract file;
the other directories are omitted when unused. `SKILL.md` contains the trigger
description and core procedure. Detailed schemas, rubrics, and examples move
to `references/`. Deterministic helpers move to `scripts/`. Templates and
static outputs move to `assets/`.

Public trigger and deterministic fixtures live outside the publishable bundle.
Promotion holdouts are not stored in either tree. They live as an encrypted,
content-addressed artifact in the Operator/CI-owned eval vault outside every
provider workspace and are released one case at a time only to the trusted eval
coordinator. A provider sees the current case input, never the holdout index,
other cases, expected labels, or decryption material.

One release-root-signed `EvaluationHoldoutVaultPolicyV1` makes that custody
executable. It binds the vault service/build/designated requirement, encrypted
corpus digest and case count, envelope suite, append-only vault-key epochs,
separate decrypt-coordinator and grader identities, maximum one live case per
evaluation arm, lease/deadline/zeroization policy and rotation/revocation rules.
Publication creates one public `SkillPairFixtureSetV1` with a complete fixture
for **every** pair disposition. It is invariant across private holdout
assignments, so the complement of the public set contains no membership signal.
Separately, release-private `SkillPairSplitInventoryV1` maps each pair to that
mandatory public fixture plus zero or more encrypted private cases. A
release-private `HoldoutPairCommitmentSetV1` stores fixed-capacity padded opaque
envelope slots; true case count, pair count, padding disposition, split digest
and commitment digest never appear in candidate/provider manifests, registry
readback, broker inputs or ordinary reports. The registry publisher, holdout
vault and evaluator may read those private objects only through their exact
authority rows after public gates pass.
Each `EncryptedHoldoutCaseEnvelopeV1` contains an opaque random case ID,
ciphertext, nonce/tag, public suite/key-epoch metadata and AAD binding suite,
candidate-independent corpus revision and split assignment. It exposes no case
index, input/label digest, provider/model or expected result outside the vault.

For one predeclared arm the holdout controller creates one
`HoldoutCaseReleaseLeaseV1` under unique `(evaluation_epoch, arm_id,
opaque_case_id)`. Its predecessor-linked lifecycle is `available -> reserved ->
decrypted -> input_dispatched -> result_collected -> graded -> settled`, with
`available | reserved -> expired | revoked` only after zero-disclosure proof and
every post-decrypt failure entering `zeroization_hold` until independent memory,
pipe, scratch and process-clearance receipts are terminal. The decrypt
coordinator can decrypt only the lease's one envelope into locked bounded memory
and can send only case input over the arm's already admitted prompt channel. The
grader receives expected labels only after result collection and never shares
them with the provider or decrypt coordinator. Neither process can enumerate
another case or choose the next ID.

Exact release replay joins or returns the same lease and cannot decrypt or
dispatch twice. Crash before decrypt resumes the same reservation; crash after
decrypt closes the arm, zeroizes memory/scratch, and either proves no input bytes
or records exactly one dispatched input before any replacement is considered.
Key rotation rewraps unopened envelopes into a successor epoch under a signed
private inventory and commitment set without changing any candidate-visible
byte; a live/ambiguous lease remains on its predecessor until settlement.
Revocation fences new leases immediately and forces every affected live lease
through zeroization hold. Retained fixtures crash at reserve/decrypt/send/result/
grade/zeroize boundaries, replay the same release, attempt a second concurrent
case, rotate and revoke keys, substitute corpus/candidate/arm identity and scan
provider/log/report/storage bytes for case indexes, labels and plaintext. A
missing custodian, stale policy/key epoch, incomplete zeroization or ambiguous
lease blocks evaluation and promotion; there is no public-case fallback.

Plugin publication copies are generated from the canonical source through one
signed `SkillHostRoutingContractV1`. Host-neutral `SKILL.md` procedure,
references, contracts, scripts and assets retain exact digest parity. Generated
host adapters are compared byte-for-byte only when their host-contract digest
is equal.

One trusted `reviewer_routing_input_collector` creates
`ReviewerRoutingInputSetV1` before selection. It snapshots exact proposal and
repository identities, normalized review mode, explicit authorized reviewer
include/exclude requests and sorted digests of the evidence manifest, reviewer
registry, every rubric, plugin catalog, repository router configuration,
selection mappings, path-classifier policy, authorized override set,
selection-changing research policy, questions and results, tool/capability
inventory, the complete sorted standalone/Chainworks host-routing-contract set
and canonical selection-engine build. If research is authorized, the collector
first signs a preliminary input set containing the closed research questions;
the bounded research broker's signed results then produce exactly one
predecessor-linked terminal input set before selection. Selection cannot run on
the preliminary object and no research result may be added or changed after the
terminal plan exists. With research disabled, the terminal object carries empty
question/result sets under the same schema. Environment discovery, mutable home
configuration, newest-file lookup, implicit plugin enumeration and caller paths
are not inputs. The canonical selection function accepts only this terminal
object and emits `AgentSelectionPlanV2` binding its digest. Given the same input-
set digest, the standalone controller and workflow-owned Chainworks controller
must produce byte-identical plan bytes, including reviewer ordering, cap overflow
and reason codes.

Approved HEAD's `AgentSelectionPlanV1` is frozen as a separate compatibility
schema with exactly its current fields and `schema_version`; it is never wrapped
in the V2 signature contract or decoded as V2. New selection emits only
`AgentSelectionPlanV2`. Strict decoders reject the other discriminator and every
missing/extra cross-version field before use. Before review routing opens, an
`AgentSelectionPlanMigrationReceiptV1` exact-sets every stored V1 plan. Terminal
historical plans remain byte-preserved V1 readback. Each active/prebound V1 plan
is either reconstructed from its complete stored input-snapshot hashes into one
semantically equal V2 input/plan pair or placed in an explicit migration hold;
there is no default synthesis. Reviewer identity/order, fingerprint, mode,
selected/rejected/ineligible rows and plan hash must map exactly. Crash or replay
returns the same migration receipt, and no active adapter accepts a V1 plan
after the migration seal.

The `standalone_router` contract owns intake, fingerprinting and selection only
inside a release-owned standalone runner admitted by
`ReviewerRouterSandboxPolicyV1` and a fresh
`ReviewerRouterSandboxAttestationV1`. The outer host's current
`danger-full-access` setting is explicitly untrusted and never satisfies this
boundary. The admitted runner receives one immutable read-only evidence
snapshot, no writable repository/home mount, no generic shell/process spawn,
no edit/write API and no direct network. It can call only exact bounded
read-only intake/path-classifier/research-broker RPCs and the RPC that submits a
signed handoff write intent; the release-owned writer remains the only
filesystem mutator. Direct filesystem write, shell/edit invocation, unbound
configuration/plugin change, wrong-host input or missing attestation fails
before selection/fan-out and emits zero write intent.

The `chainworks_prebound_plan` adapter forbids intake/fingerprinting/selection
and accepts only the signed, assignment-bound `AgentSelectionPlanV2` plus its
exact `ReviewerRoutingInputSetV1` digest supplied by the Chainworks execution
controller. It verifies both and invokes selected reviewers; it cannot rescan
evidence or change membership. Wrong-host package, input-set, selection owner,
sandbox attestation where required, or adapter digest fails before reviewer
allocation. Example-only duplicate skill sources are removed.

### Reviewer Selection Handoff

The sole durable handoff from proposal review to implementation audit is
`<proposal>.review/reviewer-selection.yaml`, encoded as
`ReviewerSelectionHandoffV1`. No production reader searches for
`reviewer-selection.md`, infers selection from a review report, or chooses the
newest matching filename. The release-owned `reviewer_handoff_writer` is the
sole filesystem writer. The admitted standalone controller and Chainworks
review controller are selection-authority producers: after final synthesis each
may submit one signed `ReviewerSelectionHandoffWriteIntentV1` under its admitted
host-routing contract. Every intent and resulting handoff repeats the exact
`ReviewerRoutingInputSetV1` and `AgentSelectionPlanV2` digests; a standalone
intent also carries its fresh sandbox-attestation digest, while that field is
forbidden for the Chainworks arm. The Chainworks adapter is therefore no longer a
read-only dead end; it cannot write bytes itself or alter the frozen reviewer
plan. The dispatcher and implementation-audit skill remain read-only consumers.

Producer provenance is one closed tagged union in both intent and handoff:

- `standalone_router` requires the standalone `SkillHostRoutingContractV1`
  digest, `ReviewerRouterSandboxAttestationV1` digest and attested runner
  process/one-use nonce identity; it forbids every Chainworks controller or
  prebound-plan field;
- `chainworks_prebound_plan` requires the Chainworks
  `SkillHostRoutingContractV1` digest, the exact signed prebound-plan contract
  digest that admitted the already frozen `AgentSelectionPlanV2`, and the
  Chainworks execution-controller identity; it forbids sandbox-attestation,
  standalone runner and one-use standalone nonce fields.

The union discriminator, allowed/required fields and source controller must
agree with the host kind embedded in the bound routing contract. A missing,
extra, mixed, copied or cross-host field set is schema-invalid and produces no
write intent or filesystem mutation.

Filesystem authority is fixed by one release-root-signed
`ReviewerHandoffPathPolicyV1`. It registers the repository and proposal-root
identities, expected device/inode/owner/mode, the server-owned mapping from a
proposal artifact ID to one relative `<proposal>.review/reviewer-selection.yaml`
path, and the admitted writer component/build. A write intent carries only that
artifact ID and policy digest; caller-supplied absolute/relative paths,
components, roots, filenames and symlink resolutions are not fields in any
request or intent.

The writer opens the registered root descriptor with no-follow semantics,
verifies its stored device/inode/owner/mode, and resolves every existing or
new path component dirfd-relative with `openat`-family no-follow checks. Every
ancestor and final predecessor must remain on the registered device, owned by
the expected account, non-world/group-writable, non-symlink and stable in
device/inode from preflight through commit. A linked predecessor or temporary
file with an unexpected link count is rejected. The random `0600` temporary
file is created with exclusive/no-follow flags in the destination directory,
written, fsynced and reverified. Revision one uses atomic no-replace rename;
successors additionally CAS the opened predecessor's identity and content
digest before atomic replacement. The destination directory is fsynced and all
ancestor identities are rechecked before success is signed. Root escape,
`..`, alternate Unicode/path spelling, symlink insertion, ancestor swap,
mount/device change, hardlink substitution, predecessor replacement and crash
at every open/write/fsync/rename boundary are retained zero-escape or
same-operation-recovery fixtures.

The handoff binds proposal path/MD5 and repository revision, source review
operation ID/revision/digest, the exact tagged host-provenance arm above, selected
and rejected reviewer rows with evidence IDs, fingerprint, required changes,
metric/checkpoint/research summary, predecessor handoff revision/digest,
selection-authority/host identity, writer component/build, and created/updated
times. The intent binds those complete canonical values, source selection-plan
and terminal synthesis digests, expected predecessor or explicit absence, and a
lowercase UUIDv7 operation key, registered proposal artifact ID and active
handoff-path-policy digest. The writer authenticates the standalone adapter or
Chainworks controller over the release-owned local boundary and verifies the
live peer's audit token, process-birth identity, code requirement, host-routing
contract, selection authority and path policy. For the standalone arm it
additionally requires the fresh attestation's one-use peer nonce and exact live
process identity. One authority prepare transaction reserves, but does not yet
consume, the live nonce/Chainworks authorization and write intent and creates
revision one `ReviewerHandoffWriteJournalV1` in `prepared`. A copied, expired,
wrong-process or replayed attestation cannot reserve even byte-identical
content. Chainworks uses its separately prebound controller identity and forbids
the standalone attestation field. Before each temporary-file write, file fsync,
no-replace or predecessor-CAS rename and destination-directory fsync, the writer
advances the same predecessor-linked journal to `applying` with the exact
expected pre/post file identities. It then follows the dirfd-relative commit
protocol above.

After directory fsync and final target/ancestor reobservation, authority finalize
atomically consumes the reserved authorization, marks the journal `committed`
and emits one `ReviewerHandoffWriteReceiptV1`. Crash before a filesystem effect
retries only that journal step; crash after an effect rereads the exact pre/post
identity and either advances the same step or writes
`reconciliation_required`. A final target equal to the intended canonical bytes
may finalize the original journal; absence may retry it; any third content,
predecessor or directory state requires reconciliation and cannot allocate a new
nonce or intent. Exact operation replay returns the stored terminal receipt and
same bytes. Changed selection requires a new predecessor-linked handoff revision
and journal. A stale, partial, duplicate, wrong-root or wrong-proposal write
performs no replacement. Fault vectors cover authority prepare, every write/
fsync/rename boundary, final readback, authority finalize and response loss.

At migration, `ReviewerHandoffLegacySourcePolicyV1` fixes exactly one registered
proposal root, the canonical relative V2 YAML name, the closed legacy YAML
relative name at the same bytes, exact legacy Markdown name
`<proposal>.review/reviewer-selection.md`, and only the same-directory historical
audit regex
`<escaped-proposal-stem>_IMPLEMENTATION_AUDIT_R([1-9][0-9]{0,3}).md.review/reviewer-selection.md`.
The proposal stem is server-derived and regex-escaped; the regex is ASCII/raw-
byte matched and has no path separator wildcard. It admits no caller path, glob,
recursive search,
sibling root or external root. The writer enumerates candidates dirfd-relative
only after direct no-follow probes of the two exact YAML/Markdown names. The
single 2000-millisecond correlated durable-clock budget starts before the first
direct probe, not before the later scan. The writer checks and reserves the
remaining clock budget before and after each exact-name probe, at historical-
scan entry, before and after each directory entry, before each payload open and
after each bounded payload parse. The remaining historical-regex scan is
nonrecursive and also bounded before payload reads to 4096 directory entries,
255 raw filename bytes per entry and depth one. Entry 4097, name-plus-one,
exact-stage deadline plus one or arithmetic overflow is
`selection_traversal_budget_exceeded` and
performs zero migration write. Admitted entries are ordered by raw bytes; the
writer opens them dirfd-relative, rejects any symlink, hardlink,
mount/device escape or non-regular file before reading payload bytes, and stops
after the twenty-first candidate solely to emit
`selection_inventory_overflow`; it never reads that candidate's content. More
than twenty candidates performs zero migration write. An external-root or
policy-invalid candidate is a path-policy denial; multiple, stale or
semantically divergent in-policy candidates are `selection_ambiguous`.
Exact-limit and plus-one fixtures exercise the first and second direct probe,
historical-scan entry, final directory entry, payload-open and post-parse clock
check independently; no stage receives a fresh deadline.

The signed policy limits each candidate to 262144 raw bytes and all at-most-
twenty payloads to 2097152 raw bytes, using checked unsigned arithmetic before
allocation or read. YAML permits one UTF-8 document, depth 32, 4096 nodes,
65536 bytes per scalar and collection width 1024; aliases, anchors, custom tags
and duplicate keys are rejected. Legacy Markdown uses a streaming line scanner
bounded to 4096 lines, 16384 bytes per line and 128 extracted reviewer rows; it
does not build an unbounded Markdown AST. For each first-twenty regular file the
writer opens dirfd-relative/no-follow, verifies device/inode/mode/owner/
`st_nlink == 1` and `st_size` before reading, reserves the aggregate budget,
performs a bounded read that rejects a size-plus-one byte, then repeats `fstat`
and requires the complete identity/size tuple unchanged. Oversize, aggregate
overflow, parser limit, concurrent growth/shrink/replacement or checked-
arithmetic failure is terminal `selection_payload_too_large` or
`selection_parse_budget_exceeded` and performs zero migration write. Exact-
limit/plus-one and concurrent-size-change fixtures cover every bound. The count
limit is applied before payload reads, so the twenty-first candidate can reveal
only inventory overflow, never its size or contents.

Exact-limit/plus-one traversal fixtures cover nonmatching entries, filename
bytes and deadline ticks independently from the candidate/payload/parser limits.
A directory mutation between enumeration and open is detected by the same
entry/dirfd identity fence and cannot restart with an unbounded rescan.

`ReviewerSelectionHandoffMigrationReceiptV1` records the complete at-most-twenty
exact absent/current/stale/ambiguous/oversized inventory, stable file identities,
byte and parser counts and disposition:

- one current V2 YAML is retained and no migration write occurs;
- one complete legacy YAML matching the proposal path/revision is converted to
  revision one V2, including explicit omission of its legacy JSON-null metric
  placeholders;
- one complete legacy Markdown selection may be converted only when no YAML
  candidate exists;
- byte-distinct YAML/Markdown candidates are accepted together only when their
  normalized selections and proposal identity are equal, in which case YAML is
  the predecessor and Markdown receives a retired-source receipt;
- missing candidates produce `selection_missing`; stale, multiple,
  parse-incomplete or semantically divergent candidates produce
  `selection_ambiguous` and require a fresh router synthesis.

Migration uses the same no-replace/predecessor-CAS writer and is exact-replay
idempotent. After the V2 publication opens, neither legacy YAML nor Markdown is
a fallback.
Generated plugin copies must contain the same canonical V2 path plus closed
legacy-source policy and `reviewer_selection_handoff_sha256`; parity tests fail
if router, dispatcher, audit skill or Chainworks adapter searches another root,
pattern, path or schema.

### Workflow and Catalog Source Budgets

`WorkflowSourceBudgetPolicyV1` is release-owned and supplies identical generated
constants to Rust and Swift before either parser builds an object tree. V1
admits exactly one UTF-8 YAML document and sets these inclusive limits:

| Dimension | Workflow YAML | Agent catalog YAML |
|---|---:|---:|
| raw file bytes | 1 MiB | 2 MiB |
| one decoded scalar | 256 KiB | 256 KiB |
| nesting depth | 64 | 64 |
| total scalar/sequence/mapping nodes | 50,000 | 50,000 |
| one sequence or mapping width | 10,000 | 10,000 |

Aliases, anchors, merge keys, custom tags, duplicate mapping keys, additional
documents, non-UTF-8 bytes and parser extensions are forbidden. Admission first
checks raw bytes, then runs a bounded streaming event scan that enforces scalar,
depth, node, width, document and forbidden-event rules, and only then permits
normal tree materialization. A parser that cannot expose an equivalent bounded
event stream is unsupported; allocation failure or counter overflow is a typed
source-budget denial, not a retry with an unbounded parser. Candidate, workflow
or environment input cannot raise a limit.

The current protected catalog is a one-time migration input rather than an
exception to that rule. It contains anchor `x_p060_score_weights` and aliases at
the exact catalog pointers inventoried by
`CatalogAliasEliminationReceiptV1`. During `schema_prepared`, the release-owned
catalog migration tool uses the frozen legacy parser only for the pinned source
commit, resolves each alias to the same concrete mapping, emits a single-document
alias-free candidate catalog with the mapping repeated at every consumer, and
binds source bytes/tree, ordered source pointers, normalized semantic-object
digests, output bytes/tree and generator build. Rust and Swift parse both the
legacy source through this one migration harness and the materialized output
through the V2 parser and must produce byte-identical normalized catalog values.
Any unknown anchor/alias, merge key, changed pointer, semantic difference,
partial output or second migration attempt holds. The source catalog is retired
before `open_v2`; production parsing never enables aliases or falls back to the
legacy parser.

For the pinned source revision, the migration input is exactly anchor mapping
`/x_p060_score_weights` plus these twelve aliases, each ending in
`/routing/score_weights`: `proposal_reviewer_product_owner`,
`proposal_reviewer_ux`, `proposal_reviewer_ui`, `proposal_reviewer_architect`,
`proposal_reviewer_apple_architect`, `proposal_reviewer_macos`,
`proposal_reviewer_rust_architect`, `proposal_reviewer_reliability`,
`proposal_reviewer_performance`, `proposal_reviewer_security`,
`proposal_reviewer_api_contract`, and
`proposal_reviewer_observability_rollout`. Their complete JSON Pointers are
`/agents/<listed-id>/routing/score_weights`; ordering is the catalog's existing
agent order. An added, removed, reordered or redirected alias is source drift,
not another admitted migration input.

Shared fixtures cover zero, exact limit and limit plus one for every numeric
dimension, deeply nested collections, one 256 KiB scalar and one-byte overflow,
alias/anchor expansion, merge keys, duplicate keys, custom tags, multi-document
input, invalid UTF-8 and counter overflow. A retained positive migration fixture
for the current `x_p060_score_weights` source proves semantic equivalence and a
negative set mutates every source pointer/value/cardinality. Rust and Swift must return the same
closed reason before Run creation. `workflow_source_budget_policy_sha256` is
bound by normalized plans, candidate manifest, evaluation trust policy and the
deterministic gates.

### Validation

`SkillBundleAdmissionV1` validates the Agent Skills frontmatter and bundle
before creating a run:

- `name` matches the bundle directory and allowed name grammar;
- `description` explains both capability and trigger boundaries;
- unknown or malformed required metadata fails closed;
- `SKILL.md` and resources obey byte and file-count caps;
- absolute paths, traversal, symlink components, and root escape are rejected;
- executable scripts are explicitly inventoried and hashed;
- resource references resolve inside the bundle;
- duplicate canonical skill names are rejected.

Normative limits are:

- `SKILL.md`: at most 128 KiB and 500 lines;
- one resource file: at most 8 MiB;
- one bundle: at most 256 regular files and 32 MiB total exact bytes;
- one portable path: at most 240 ASCII bytes and eight components below the
  skill root;
- one task composition: at most four bundles, 64 MiB aggregate resources, and
  256 KiB aggregate injected `SKILL.md` bodies.

Size accounting includes `SKILL.md`, frontmatter, scripts, and every resource
byte. An executable Git mode is accepted only below `scripts/` and is recorded
in the manifest; executable files elsewhere fail admission.

Portable relative resource paths use the ASCII grammar
`[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+`, contain no empty, `.` or `..` component, and are sorted by
raw ASCII bytes in manifests. Production Git trees accept tree and regular-blob
modes only and reject symlink/submodule modes, path aliases, and case-fold
collisions. Test-only path fixtures additionally reject hard links, sockets,
devices, FIFOs, symlinks, and files that change while being read.

### Coherent Same-Byte Snapshot Publication

A live working-tree directory is never a production admission source because a
portable POSIX walk cannot prove one coherent generation during concurrent
rename/add/remove operations. Every promotable skill is committed first.
`SkillSourceTreeV1` identifies repository identity, commit OID, subtree path,
exact Git tree OID and the active `RepositoryDiscoveryBudgetPolicyV1`. Dirty or
path-only skill sources are permitted only in
test-only fixture admission and cannot produce a production candidate receipt.

The production `skill_source_tree` policy uses direct OID/path probes for every
declared source and permits a complete tracked-root sweep only under exact
positive ceilings: Git tree depth 64, 250000 tree entries/nodes, 250000 object
lookups, 8388608 bytes per object, 268435456 aggregate object bytes and 30000
correlated durable-clock milliseconds. All counters use checked unsigned
arithmetic, start before the first tree/root lookup and are reserved before
object load; there is no preliminary count, recursive pre-scan or retry with a
larger/unbounded iterator. Node, object, object-byte,
aggregate-byte, depth or deadline plus-one fails with
`repository_discovery_budget_exceeded` and creates no bundle, migration,
publication or candidate row. A concurrent object replacement or missing OID is
object-integrity failure, never permission for a mutable filesystem fallback.
Exact-limit/plus-one fixtures exercise each counter independently. The
8388608-byte object ceiling deliberately equals the single-resource-file
ceiling, so the retained exact 8 MiB resource fixture is reachable; its one-byte
overflow is rejected by both resource admission and repository discovery.

Validation, hashing, copying, and publication operate on one immutable Git
object set through a structured Git object API owned by the Rust control plane,
not provider shell commands:

1. Resolve the declared commit and subtree once, require the expected tree OID,
   and retain object handles for the complete operation.
2. Enumerate that immutable tree recursively in raw portable-path byte order.
   Accept Git tree and blob objects only; reject symlink mode, submodule mode,
   duplicate/case-colliding paths, and any object missing by hash.
3. Read each blob by OID into a bounded staging spool once. Validate exact bytes,
   frontmatter, references, modes, per-file and aggregate limits, and compute
   resource digests from that same spool.
4. Build `SkillBundleManifestV1` with source commit/tree OIDs, normalized paths,
   byte lengths, exact content digests, and normalized modes. Compute
   `bundle_sha256` from its canonical bytes.
5. Write only the spooled bytes into a control-plane-owned temporary directory
   on the same filesystem, fsync files and directories, and perform a
   no-replace atomic rename to the content-addressed final snapshot path.
6. Commit only the immutable bundle-staging receipt after the rename is
   durable. Registry/classification/graph/harness, per-pair proofs, terminal
   proof set and publication receipt are built later in the acyclic order
   below; candidate/run references are later still.
   A database failure leaves an unreferenced
   content-addressed directory for bounded startup cleanup; it never exposes a
   partially published bundle.

If the final content-addressed directory already exists, admission verifies its
complete manifest before reuse. Any mismatch fails closed. Failure cleanup may
remove only the request-owned staging directory and never follows links.

The Swift `ExternalSkillLoader` becomes diagnostic/readback code for V2. It
does not independently admit or publish production bundles. Rust/Swift parity
fixtures consume the same published manifest and bytes, so installed tools,
working-tree races, directory enumeration order, and host filesystem timing
cannot change the decision.

### Skill Registry and Trigger Authority

`SkillRegistryV1` is the sole production skill-registry truth. Its complete
input is one signed `SkillRegistrySourceV1`, never a path or repository state
chosen by the candidate. The source binds the protected repository identity,
base ref, exact commit and tree OIDs, the admitted upstream lock, every
production skill root, immutable bundle/contract/public-eval input object, the
neighbor-graph and trigger-harness source objects, protected-branch and required
CI receipts, the predecessor registry digest, and the trusted collector and
publisher identities. Every collection list is complete and sorted by raw
canonical bytes. A branch name, mutable worktree, local `HEAD`, untracked file,
host-installed skill, environment value, candidate manifest or caller path is
not a publication input.

The OS-isolated release-owned Rust `skill_registry_publisher`, pinned by the
active trust policy, is the only semantic writer. It reads raw Git objects from
the source repository through bounded trusted descriptors with repository
configuration, hooks, filters, alternates outside the admitted object set and
worktree discovery disabled. It verifies the source commit is the protected
branch receipt's exact head, every required object is reachable from that
commit, and the CI receipt covers the same tree and publisher schema set. A
missing object, graph node, contract, eval input or protected-source receipt
fails before authority prepare. The candidate cannot nominate the source,
publisher, path, ref or predecessor.

Operator maintenance invokes the exact command
`runtime.agent_context.skill_registry.publish`. It accepts only the signed
`SkillRegistrySourceV1`, expected predecessor registry revision/digest and both
request IDs. The publisher validates and stages every bundle, then one
authority-only operation reserves the source, predecessor registry, next
revision, every bundle/contract digest, every pair-disposition row, the complete
pair-disposition set, graph, harness, release-private complete split inventory,
all-pairs declarative public fixture set, release-private padded holdout
commitment set and
request identities. Candidate-bound execution proofs do not exist at registry
publication time and are invalid inputs to this operation. Holdout prompt,
label, true count, split digest, commitment digest and pair-mapping bytes are
invalid public operation inputs; the publisher verifies them only through its
private vault descriptor.
The operation uses the same anchor sequencer, exact-request record and
same-store authority projection outbox as other authority mutations; it has no
control-plane write phase and remains callable while the candidate is stopped.
Finalize publishes every public immutable object, commits the private split
inventory and padded commitment set under their separate access policies, sorts complete registry
entries by raw `skill_id`, increments the registry revision, writes
`SkillRegistryPublicationReceiptV1`, advances the anchor and only then exposes
the new registry and all-pairs public fixture set. The private publication
receipt retains split/commitment identities, while candidate/provider
projections omit both fields rather than returning redacted digests. Exact replay returns the same registry and publication
receipt. A conflicting predecessor, protected-source head or publication set
performs zero mutation. Unreferenced staged content is bounded startup cleanup;
no partial registry becomes servable.

A registry entry contains skill ID, trigger-description digest, source
commit/tree, bundle, script-contract-set and public-eval digests. It never
contains the publication receipt, neighbor graph, harness or any other object
that depends on the registry. Catalog, workflow, prompt, provider and filesystem
discovery cannot add or override an entry. Any entry, description, contract,
bundle or source change creates a new registry digest and invalidates the
candidate and every start selection that referenced the predecessor. The
candidate daemon has read-only registry projections and no publication
capability. Registry, graph, harness and publication receipt are each carried
in `chainworks_signed_contract_v1` with the publisher purpose; a digest in an
unsigned control-plane row is not admissible.

`SkillNeighborGraphV1` is a complete versioned graph, not evaluator
configuration. Its checked-in protected-base source lists every production
skill node exactly once and every semantic-neighbor edge in canonical
`left_skill_id < right_skill_id` order. Edges are symmetric by construction;
unknown nodes, duplicate/reversed duplicates, omitted production nodes or an
unpaired trigger-bearing skill fail generation. The publisher derives a
complete sorted `SkillPairDispositionV1` row for every unordered pair of the
registry's `n` production skills, exactly `n*(n-1)/2` rows. Each row binds both
skill/bundle/description digests and disposition `semantic_neighbor |
non_neighbor` plus a closed release-owned reason code. The neighbor edge set is
exactly the rows marked `semantic_neighbor`. One signed
`SkillPairDispositionSetV1` binds registry, `n`, expected pair count and every
sorted classification row digest and contains no executable-proof or harness
digest; the graph binds that set digest. The graph cannot assert
completeness without this independently countable pair set. The graph digest is pinned by
the release trust policy, candidate, pair corpus and harness. Its payload binds
