the predecessor `skill_registry_sha256`; the registry never contains the later
graph digest.

Every pair disposition requires one public declarative fixture and one executed
public proof during candidate evaluation; neither classification nor fixture is
executable evidence. A `semantic_neighbor` row names one public
`SiblingSkillTriggerPairV1`, and a `non_neighbor` row names one complete public
bidirectional cross-trigger fixture. The signed `SkillPairFixtureSetV1` binds
all `n*(n-1)/2` pair dispositions and contains no private split, commitment,
candidate, baseline, arm admission, result or proof digest. The private
`SkillPairSplitInventoryV1` repeats that complete public mapping internally and
may add opaque holdout envelopes to any pair. Therefore the same public bytes
are valid for two different private assignments, and no public complement or
count identifies a holdout pair.

After candidate registration, the release-owned evaluation controller executes
each public fixture with the frozen `SkillTriggerSelectionHarnessV1`. Only
after all deterministic and public trigger gates pass may the holdout vault
release one opaque committed case at a time under its existing one-use lease.
For every
non-neighbor pair it takes the protected positive-trigger corpus of skill A and
executes it with B present but not selected, then takes B's corpus and executes
it with A present but not selected, in both presentation orders, for every
production profile and required repetition. The closed expected outcome names
the target skill and forbids the other; free-form rationale or an unexecuted
reason code is insufficient. There is no omitted-direction or sampling branch.

One terminal signed `SkillPairProofSetV1`
binds the registry, disposition set, graph and harness, exact expected pair
count and every sorted public
`(pair_disposition_sha256, proof_kind, proof_sha256)` row. It contains no
private split, commitment, binding, lease, settlement, count, timing or digest.
The evaluator signs this set after the public corpus alone is complete. A
semantic-neighbor row names one
`SiblingSkillTriggerExecutionProofV1` that itself binds the immutable
`SiblingSkillTriggerPairV1` fixture and all executed result rows; a
non-neighbor row names one `NonNeighborCrossTriggerProofV1`. Missing, stale,
wrong-profile, one-direction, candidate-generated, duplicate-branch or
unexpectedly cross-triggering evidence fails candidate evaluation and
promotion, never retroactively changes the published registry. Shared fixtures
deliberately add trigger overlap to every non-neighbor direction and prove the
harness catches it during candidate evaluation; this makes the complete
`n*(n-1)/2` proof corpus mechanically countable independent of graph
classification.

`SkillTriggerSelectionHarnessV1` is the authoritative selector execution
identity. It pins the release-owned harness binary/build, deterministic selector
algorithm, tokenizer/framing versions, complete provider/model/tool inventory,
neighbor graph and `SkillTriggerSelectionResultV1` schema. The candidate can be
an observed arm but cannot choose the graph, selector, result decoder or
expected pair set. The registry publisher materializes the graph, harness,
and all-pairs public-fixture-set before candidate registration; changing any
public object changes the candidate and invalidates all later pair proofs. The
private split/commitment objects are fixed by the release authority before the
candidate exists but are intentionally absent from the candidate/public digest
graph.
Shared vectors cover every node/edge, both pair directions, reversed
order, unknown/duplicate nodes, missing public coverage, ciphertext/padding
drift, private-object projection and graph/harness digest drift. A retained
non-interference vector constructs two different valid private assignments and
requires byte-identical registry, graph, harness, public fixture, candidate
core, target declaration, candidate manifest and provider-visible readback.

The public digest order is `skill bundles/contracts -> skill registry -> sorted
pair-disposition rows -> classification-only pair-disposition set -> neighbor
graph -> trigger harness -> all-pairs public fixture set -> candidate core ->
quality-target declaration -> candidate manifest -> candidate registration`.
The private order is `release-private split inventory -> padded holdout
commitment set -> private registry-publication receipt -> candidate core +
quality-target declaration -> candidate_holdout_binding -> fixed-capacity
one-use leases -> private_holdout_settlement -> promotion authority check`. The
public proof set and the private settlement are sibling inputs checked atomically
by promotion; neither contains the other's digest. The candidate
core, target declaration, manifest, provider prompt and public readback contain
no private-order digest. No earlier object contains a later digest, so generated
dependency and information-flow checks reject cycles and private-to-public
edges before candidate creation.

The private vault executes exactly the policy's fixed slot capacity for every
candidate/profile/repetition, not only real cases. Every real or padding slot
receives an identically shaped opaque lease, isolated arm, provider request
budget, tool inventory, timeout class and terminal cleanup path. Padding slots
carry release-authored decoy prompts and private `padding` grades; their
disposition is unavailable to the provider, candidate, ordinary worker and
public proof writer. The scheduler uses a release-owned fixed cadence and emits
no per-slot public status, count or timing. `PrivateHoldoutSettlementV1` records
all slot dispositions and grades only in the authority/vault boundary. Promotion
atomically requires its terminal pass together with the public proof set, but
returns neither its identity nor its true-count/timing metadata. Retained non-
interference vectors run two different private assignments with the same fixed
capacity and require equal candidate/public bytes, provider request count,
request-size buckets, cadence class and externally visible lifecycle.

The frontmatter is metadata and is not injected as raw prompt text. The engine
injects the exact admitted `SKILL.md` body from its content-addressed snapshot.
Providers cannot read `.agents/skills`, the Git object database, the eval vault,
or snapshot-storage paths. The only wire URI grammar is
`skill://sha256/<64-lowercase-hex>/<portable-relative-path>`. The authority is
the literal `sha256`; the first path component is the bundle digest without a
`sha256:` prefix; the remaining non-empty components use the portable-path
alphabet, and scripts must begin `scripts/`. Userinfo, port, query, fragment,
percent encoding, uppercase hex, empty/dot components, a symbolic skill ID or
any authority alias is invalid. Authoring tools may resolve a symbolic skill ID
before compilation, but no frozen assignment, prompt, broker request or receipt
contains it as a URI. Resources are exposed through bounded runtime
tools `skills.resource.read` and, when the permission profile allows execution,
`skills.script.run`. Those tools reopen only the immutable object by digest,
verify the manifest entry and byte hash, cap output, and never resolve a mutable
authoring path. `skills.resource.read` is limited by the bundle manifest and the
P096 per-call/cumulative output budgets; `skills.script.run` is also subject to
the permission profile, runtime timeout, and P096 line/byte caps.

### Invocation-Scoped Skill Broker

Authority finalize of the claimed work admission creates one durable signed
`SkillBrokerGrantV1` in state `prepared` in the same authority transaction as
the claimed admission transition; the control-plane attempt pin stores only its
signed digest projection. It binds run, stage/task, agent execution,
attempt generation, daemon instance, preallocated logical provider session and
session fingerprint, context generation, permission profile,
`SkillCompositionV1` digest, exact allowed resource/script entries, immutable
assignment effect-slot IDs with their script/operation bindings, usable dispatch
states, expiry, revocation state, and decimal-string `grant_install_epoch`.
There is no broker bearer or token field in this schema or lifecycle.

Before provider spawn, the broker grant remains `prepared` and binds only the
preallocated dispatch/session and immutable expected broker-tool inventory. No
broker socket, pipe, Mach-send right, file descriptor, token or endpoint is
inherited by the provider process.

After the real provider process and `ProviderProcessLaunchClosureV1` are
registered, the `provider_sandbox_launcher` signs one distinct
`ProviderProxyLaunchExpectationV1` and registers one
`ProviderBrokerProxyAdmissionV1` with the release-owned private XPC broker. The
admission binds grant/install epoch, consumed attempt launch authorization,
spawn journal, exact observed provider parent process/session, sealed privileged
proxy executable/designated requirement, broker XPC protocol, launcher identity
and a short connection deadline. In the same durable transition the grant CASes
`prepared -> proxy_admission_prepared`.

The provider-facing `session/new.mcpServers` entry does **not** spawn that
privileged proxy. ACP may spawn only a sealed unprivileged stdio bootstrap shim
whose executable digest is frozen in the adapter policy. The shim owns the ACP
stdin/stdout pipes but has no broker Mach right, workspace/data access, network,
credential channel, signing key or generic local IPC permission. It can perform
only one audit-token-authenticated connection to a narrow release-owned
bootstrap Mach service using the pre-registered admission identity. The release
launcher then creates the privileged proxy under its own launch
expectation/closure, connects a one-use relay between that proxy and the shim's
stdio, and writes `ProviderBrokerStdioBootstrapReceiptV1`. The receipt is
required before accepted-server installation and proves the shim, relay,
privileged proxy, parent provider session and grant/install epoch are the exact
predeclared graph. The provider can neither launch nor directly contact the
privileged proxy; alternate shim argv/env, a second relay, direct bootstrap call
from the provider and a reused admission all fail before MCP request parsing.

The privileged proxy authenticates to the private XPC broker with its kernel
audit token/designated requirement and the proxy-auth Secure Enclave P-256
challenge key declared by the active custody profile, whose opaque
representation/ACL admits only that proxy build. The broker also verifies the
pre-registered admission, exact parent provider process/session/install epoch
and one-live-connection constraint. A direct provider XPC call fails
designated-requirement and client-key verification before request parsing.
Starting another copy of the genuine proxy cannot widen authority: only the one
current admission may connect, every request still crosses the proxy's closed
MCP parser, and a duplicate/race places the epoch in `identity_hold` rather than
yielding a raw broker stream.

The broker accepts MCP initialize and `tools/list` while the grant is
`proxy_admission_prepared`, but all
resource, Git and script calls return the non-enumerating
`skill_grant_activation_pending` denial. Observing the exact proxy process,
accepted XPC admission, session binding and tool inventory CASes the grant to
`activation_pending`. Only a matching signed
`ProviderBrokerAcceptedServerReceiptV1`, `ProviderSandboxAttestationV1` and
`ObservedProviderBindingReceiptV1` can create
`SkillBrokerGrantInstallReceiptV1` and atomically CAS
`activation_pending -> installed`. Thus installation depends on observed
provider bootstrap, not on a grant that had to be installed before spawn.

The lifecycle is closed:

```text
prepared -> proxy_admission_prepared -> activation_pending -> installed -> revoked
prepared | proxy_admission_prepared -> abandoned | expired [no accepted proxy receipt and verified no provider/proxy process]
activation_pending -> revoked                 [post-accept verified session/process loss]
proxy_admission_prepared | activation_pending -> identity_hold
identity_hold -> installed | abandoned | expired | revoked | failed_reconciled  [typed reconciliation only]
installed -> revoked                            [session loss or settlement]
```

Startup reconciles the signed proxy admission, spawn journal, proxy accept,
sandbox and provider-binding receipts. A server accepted before the install
transaction resumes only that installation; verified process absence before
any accepted-server receipt abandons the epoch, while verified loss after
acceptance revokes it and produces the attempt's signed `failed_no_effect`
settlement. Post-accept state can never become `abandoned`. Any
descriptor/process ambiguity enters `identity_hold`. Recovery
never launches a duplicate provider or proxy and never creates a second admission
for the same live epoch. Installed grants survive restart only through the
already-attested live process/session/XPC connection; session loss, settlement,
cancellation, session replacement, generation hold or attempt replacement
revokes the grant transactionally.

The grant's correlated deadline is an **installation** deadline and applies
only in `prepared | proxy_admission_prepared | activation_pending`; an installed
grant is instead bounded by its attempt/session lifecycle. Every broker request
rechecks state, clock-baseline relation and deadline directly, so delayed
cleanup cannot make an overdue grant usable. The independently leased
`skill_grant_expiry_controller` scans finalized noninstalled grants at startup
and continuously. Before any accepted-server receipt and with verified process
absence it appends `expired`; after acceptance, or whenever process fate is not
provably absent, it appends `revoked` and settles or holds the same attempt.
Baseline mismatch is deny-and-reconcile, never a fresh deadline. Exact expiry
replay returns the same signed transition and no restart can reinstall that
epoch.

`identity_hold` is not an unbounded terminal dead end. Operator-only
`runtime.agent_context.skill_broker.reconcile` accepts both request IDs, grant
ID/install epoch, exact grant/revision/digest, attempt/reducer checkpoint and
the existing proxy/process/apply observation set; it accepts no desired state.
The release-owned `skill_broker_reconciliation_controller` independently
observes the registered provider/proxy/XPC/process and effect state and derives
exactly one legal successor: complete the already accepted installation,
terminalize a never-started epoch as `abandoned | expired`, revoke a lost
post-accept session while settling the attempt, or append
`failed_reconciled` plus the signed failed attempt settlement when no effect can
remain. Ambiguous evidence stays in the same hold and emits a bounded required
observation; it cannot launch or allocate a successor. Once the complete
observation set is available, the command must terminalize the hold in one
authority transaction.

Operator-only `runtime.agent_context.skill_effects.reconcile` similarly binds
the exact request/effect registry, immutable intent and apply-journal revision.
The controller compares each target with the signed pre/post images: complete
post-state settles `committed`, complete pre-state resumes the already prepared
apply once, and any third state settles `failed_reconciled` with quarantine and
attempt evidence. It never reruns the script or creates another logical effect.
Both commands use the generic authority exact-request/operation lifecycle;
exact replay returns the same terminal transition, a different intent
conflicts, and only the reducer transaction that consumes the terminal
reconciliation may issue at most one successor attempt.

Canonical grant/request/effect truth is not stored in candidate-owned
control-plane SQLite. The release-owned `skill_broker_service` is the semantic
writer and the keyless `authority_store_coordinator` is the sole physical writer
of `SkillBrokerGrantV1`, `SkillScriptRequestRecordV1`, `SkillScriptEffectIntentV1`,
`SkillScriptEffectRegistryV1`, `SkillScriptExecutionIntentV1`,
`SkillScriptApplyJournalV1` and terminal execution receipts. The broker holds a
canonical `RuntimeOwnerLeaseV1` specialization
`skill_effect_writer_lease`; every state transition is a purpose-signed
append-only revision that binds predecessor row/revision, grant/install epoch,
request or slot identity and the observed process/filesystem receipt. Candidate,
provider, proxy and control-plane writer identities have no authority-store
write credential or directory capability for these tables.

Control-plane rows are signed bounded readback projections delivered through
the authority projection outbox. They can schedule/wait for a broker result but
cannot create, omit, advance, duplicate or settle a request/effect. A lost XPC
acknowledgement re-reads the same authority row by exact request or stable slot;
it never infers absence from a missing projection. Broker writer handoff uses
deadline plus exact owner-absence proof and one higher lease epoch; a stale
broker process performs zero authority mutation. Fault tests cover crash before
and after request claim, process registration, apply entry, terminal receipt,
anchor finalize, projection delivery and writer handoff.

Broker tool payloads do not accept run ID, execution ID, attempt generation,
session ID, snapshot path, or bundle path. The authenticated grant and live ACP
session supply those values. `skills.resource.read` accepts only the logical
`skill://` URI and a bounded byte range. `skills.script.run` accepts only the
logical script URI, one contract-declared input object, a UUIDv7
`idempotency_key`, and the conditionally required non-null assignment-owned
effect slot for write scripts; read-only scripts omit that field. Each call
verifies the installed proxy-XPC/grant epoch, active session fingerprint,
dispatch state, generation continuation state, permission profile, composition
membership, manifest entry, and exact object digest before revealing object
existence. Any wrong run/session/generation/composition/bundle combination
returns the same non-enumerating `skill_resource_unavailable` denial.

Review, audit and security roles receive authoritative Git evidence without
direct `.git` access through two additional read-only broker tools.
`workspace.git_evidence.capture` accepts only
`git_evidence_capture_request_v1 { schema_version, idempotency_key }`, where the
key is a lowercase UUIDv7; every successful capture
contains the complete status/manifest/diff section set. It accepts no path,
root, ref, revision, glob, view selector or command. The grant supplies a
`workspace_id`, and the Rust
service resolves that ID through the frozen run's registered workspace row. It
opens the live workspace, linked-worktree gitdir and common Git directory with
trusted no-follow descriptors only long enough to verify three separately
registered identities: workspace root, linked-worktree gitdir root and common-
gitdir root. Each identity includes registration revision/digest, APFS volume
UUID, device, inode/vnode and volume-relative path; no root is inferred from
another root or a `.git` text pointer. The release-owned
`workspace_snapshot_service` then creates one APFS filesystem snapshot through
its fixed-volume XPC operation, mounts it read-only at a service-owned random
directory and signs `WorkspaceSnapshotReceiptV1`. The Git service reopens the
workspace/gitdir/common-dir solely through the receipt's volume-relative paths,
verifies the snapshot/mount plus all three corresponding snapshot-root vnode
identities and performs every subsequent
object/index/worktree read from that immutable mount. It compares only the
run-pinned base commit/tree, snapshot HEAD commit/tree, snapshot index and
snapshot worktree. The service requires both commit graphs and trees
to be present in the admitted object database, computes relation exactly
`equal | ancestor | diverged`, and records the merge-base commit/tree when
relation is `diverged`. Missing base/HEAD/merge-base objects, shallow ambiguity,
replace/graft configuration or graph disagreement is
`git_evidence_incomplete`; it never silently substitutes current `HEAD` as the
run base.
Root `/`, a home/repository prefix, sibling worktree, alias/symlink, changed
device/inode or unregistered Git directory fails `git_evidence_scope_invalid`.
Workspace, linked-worktree gitdir and common Git directory must all resolve to
the same admitted APFS volume and one snapshot generation; a cross-volume Git
layout is `git_evidence_unavailable` because independently timed snapshots
would not prove one generation.

The immutable snapshot does not waive file-link confinement. Before parsing any
regular file from the workspace, linked-worktree gitdir or common-gitdir roots,
the Git service enumerates it dirfd-relative from one of those three registered
snapshot root descriptors, opens it with no-follow flags, and records volume
UUID, device, inode/vnode, mode, size, generation/change counter and link count.
It requires the file to remain on the receipt's admitted snapshot volume and
`st_nlink == 1`; a same-root or external hardlink is
`git_evidence_scope_invalid`, even when both names resolve inside the mounted
snapshot. It repeats `fstat` after the bounded read and requires the complete
identity tuple and bytes-read extent to match. Directory entries, Git loose
objects, pack/index files, refs, HEAD, worktree files, index and configuration
are all covered; no parser opens a path independently or follows an alternate,
graft, replace, symlink or hardlink target. The pre/post sorted file-identity
inventory digest is bound by both `WorkspaceSnapshotReceiptV1` and
`GitEvidenceSnapshotV1`. Any failed check publishes no partial snapshot/evidence
object and schedules only receipt-bound cleanup.

Retained adversarial fixtures cover an external hardlink into each root, a
same-root hardlink, symlink replacement, directory-entry rename, inode/object
replacement between enumeration/open/read, link-count change during read and
Git object/pack substitution. Every case returns the typed scope/race denial,
emits zero provider-visible bytes and cannot fall back to the live tree.

`WorkspaceSnapshotReceiptV1` carries the three live registration identities and
the three post-mount snapshot identities as separate required rows, all bound
to one snapshot UUID and mount descriptor. Snapshot acquisition captures each
pre-request registered-root identity and each post-mount snapshot-root identity
in the receipt. A root/volume/workspace
registration change across that boundary returns
`git_evidence_capture_raced` and publishes nothing. An unsupported filesystem,
missing snapshot privilege, writable mount or unavailable snapshot API returns
`git_evidence_unavailable`; there is no mutable-tree fallback. External editors,
Git clients, IDEs and provider processes may continue writing the live tree
after snapshot creation, but those writes cannot enter any phase of this
capture. The ordinary workspace mutation revision is retained only as
diagnostic metadata and is never the isolation proof.

The capture scans the immutable mount under P096 budgets. Success stores immutable
`GitEvidenceSnapshotV1` bytes and returns only snapshot/digest, base/HEAD OIDs,
base/HEAD tree OIDs, relation/optional merge-base, status/manifest digests,
the signed workspace-snapshot receipt, stable freshness fence and bounded
section inventory. After all evidence bytes are materialized and verified, the
service unmounts/deletes the ephemeral snapshot under a durable cleanup
journal; the signed receipt and content-addressed Git evidence remain. A clean index/worktree
does not erase committed changes since the run-pinned base: the committed lane
is derived only from immutable Git trees and is mandatory even when every
working-tree lane is empty.
`workspace.git_evidence.read` accepts only that authorized snapshot ID, logical
section ID, offset and `max_bytes = 1...32768`; it returns a digest-bearing
base64 chunk with exact EOF semantics. Paths are normalized safe display data,
never resolver inputs. Snapshot expiry or generation/grant mismatch is the same
non-enumerating unavailable response. The provider still cannot execute Git or
read any Git metadata path.

Raw Git content is classified before any broker result is materialized. One
release-owned `GitEvidenceSecretPolicyV1` pins scanner build/rule-set digest,
path classes, known credential/private-key formats, entropy bounds, allowlisted
test-fixture fingerprints and redaction format. The trusted Git service scans
raw path bytes before decoding or display and scans immutable base/HEAD/index
blobs and captured worktree bytes before patch rendering. A path containing a
credential/token value, private identity, secret-only component or undecidable
non-UTF-8/high-entropy component is `sensitive_path`. Within one snapshot every
occurrence of that same raw path receives one random 128-bit `path_alias_id` for
cross-section correlation; the ID is not derived from path bytes, object ID,
position or another snapshot and a rename with either sensitive endpoint hides
both endpoints. Provider-visible path becomes
`[CHAINWORKS_REDACTED_PATH:<path-class>:<path-alias-id>]` plus only bounded
component-count and extension-class metadata. Raw path bytes, normalized path,
basename, old path and path digest remain release-internal. A safe path retains
its normalized display form.

Matching content spans are replaced with
`[CHAINWORKS_REDACTED:<rule-id>:<finding-id>]`. `finding_id` is a random
128-bit identifier allocated independently for each occurrence and each
snapshot; it is not derived from secret bytes, path, position, object ID or
another finding and is never reused for equal spans. Provider-visible finding
rows contain only safe normalized display path or the random path alias, rule
ID, bounded line/byte range, random finding ID and closed classification. They contain no raw span/blob/
object/content digest. Entire secret-only or binary credential files expose
only mode, a coarse closed size bucket (`0_1k | 1k_16k | 16k_256k |
over_256k`), random finding IDs and the closed classification. The trusted
release service may retain a separately keyed HMAC correlation value in its
provider-inaccessible internal snapshot record, but that value and its key
never enter broker, prompt, result, log, receipt, report or ordinary readback.
Scanner errors or undecidable oversized content make the snapshot incomplete
and block review; they never fall back to raw output.

`GitEvidenceSnapshotV1` binds the secret-policy and scanner-build digests, a
complete sensitive-finding inventory and per-section redacted-byte digests.
The broker can return only those preclassified redacted sections. Prompt,
provider result, log, receipt, health and report paths have shared fixtures for
`.env`, PEM/private keys, OAuth/API tokens, high-entropy secrets, allowed dummy
fixtures, low-entropy known credentials, repeated equal secrets in one file,
the same secret repeated across snapshots and paths, token/email/private-key
material embedded in a filename, non-UTF-8 secret-bearing path components and a
rename with one sensitive endpoint; no raw matching content/path bytes or
deterministic provider-visible correlation value may appear on any surface.
Equal secret occurrences receive distinct finding IDs, while exact replay of
one already finalized authorized snapshot returns its stored redacted bytes.
Reviewers still receive exact change/finding evidence and stable redacted patch
bytes for that snapshot. Exact safe paths remain visible; sensitive paths are
correlatable only within that snapshot through random aliases, while secret
values and path bytes remain unavailable.

The implementation uses one pinned `gix` library/version with external diff,
textconv, clean/smudge filters, hooks and repository configuration disabled.
`GitEvidenceSnapshotV1` has these mandatory, raw-path-byte-sorted sections:

- `status_v1`: one internal entry per raw path with closed `committed_state`, `index_state`
  and `worktree_state` values `unchanged | added | modified | deleted |
  typechange | conflicted | untracked`, committed/index/worktree mode, optional
  old path and object digests, except that every provider projection applies the
  sensitive-path alias rule and a sensitive/secret-only object uses the policy's
  mode/class/coarse-size/random-finding projection and exposes no object/content
  digest;
- `changed_files_v1`: the same path identity plus Boolean `committed`, `staged`,
  `unstaged`, and `untracked` lanes and binary/oversized classification, with
  the same sensitive-path alias and sensitive-object digest overrides;
- `committed_changed_files_v1`, comparing the run-pinned base tree to captured
  HEAD tree with the same raw path, rename, mode and object-digest identities;
- `committed_patch_v1`, comparing the run-pinned base tree to captured HEAD;
- `staged_patch_v1`, comparing pinned HEAD tree to captured index;
- `unstaged_patch_v1`, comparing captured index to worktree;
- `untracked_patch_v1`, comparing `/dev/null` to each captured untracked text
  object.

Rename detection is content-exact only: one deleted object and one added object
with the same mode/blob digest become a rename, with raw-path ordering breaking
otherwise ambiguous pairs; modified renames remain delete plus add. Conflict
stages are reported and make the snapshot `complete = false`. Binary means a
NUL byte in the first 8,000 captured bytes; binary sections contain only path,
mode, size and old/new object/content digests, never binary bytes. A binary or
text object classified sensitive/secret-only instead exposes only the closed
coarse size bucket and random finding IDs and omits those digests. Text patches
use LF line splitting, three context lines, no color and base64 wire chunks so
non-UTF-8 path/content bytes remain unambiguous. A text object or aggregate
section beyond its declared P096 line/byte cap is recorded as oversized with
its complete digest and required byte count, sets `complete = false`, and
returns `git_evidence_incomplete`; audit/security/pre-push gates cannot treat
that snapshot as canonical evidence. No truncation marker is a passing diff.
For sensitive oversized content, the complete digest remains only in the
release-internal keyed record and is omitted from provider-visible sections.
Committed comparison applies the same rename, binary and oversize rules and is
never optional. A captured HEAD that diverges from the pinned base remains
readable with the merge-base recorded, but `complete = false` until the
workflow contract explicitly admits divergence; review gates otherwise block
on `git_evidence_base_diverged` rather than reviewing an accidental branch.

`ProviderBrokerProjectionV1` is built by the release-owned
`provider_sandbox_launcher`, not catalog, candidate or provider input. It binds
the `proxy_admission_prepared` grant, signed proxy-admission receipt and consumed
spawn authorization; later activation binds the observed bootstrap/provider/
proxy process identities. It grants no private-broker descriptor, raw XPC
endpoint or credential to the provider; the only provider-visible process is
the sealed unprivileged stdio bootstrap shim. The privileged proxy is never an
ACP command and is created only by the release launcher after the bootstrap
connects under its one-use admission. The exact Rust domain payload preserves the
implemented `AcpMcpServerPayload { id, extensionId, transport }` serializer
contract:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "provider_broker_projection_v1",
  "grant_sha256": "sha256:...",
  "provider_broker_proxy_admission_sha256": "sha256:...",
  "provider_attempt_launch_authorization_transition_sha256": "sha256:...",
  "acp_server_payload": {
    "id": "chainworks-broker",
    "extensionId": "chainworks-skill-broker-v1",
    "transport": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "<release-bundle>/Contents/Helpers/chainworks-broker-stdio-bootstrap",
      "args": [],
      "env": {}
    }
  },
  "acp_broker_server_wire_sha256": "sha256:...",
  "acp_broker_server_list_sha256": "sha256:...",
  "provider_broker_projection_sha256": "sha256:..."
}
```

`command` is resolved by the release authority to the absolute sealed bootstrap
path inside its signed bundle and verified by vnode/digest/designated
requirement; it is never caller input. Resolution to the privileged proxy path,
any other helper or any caller-controlled path is rejected before ACP spawn.
`provider_broker_projection_sha256` covers the complete
Chainworks wrapper; `acp_broker_server_wire_sha256` separately covers the
implemented serializer's external wire projection and
`acp_broker_server_list_sha256` covers its one-element array. The wrapper is
authority/readback input and is never itself serialized as an ACP server.
Existing ACP serialization deserializes the nested object as
`AcpMcpServerPayload`, rejects every other transport arm, and byte-validates
the output of `mcp_servers_wire_value`, producing exactly this sole ordered
`session/new.mcpServers` wire entry:

```json
{
  "name": "chainworks-broker",
  "type": "stdio",
  "command": "<resolved-sealed-bootstrap-path>",
  "args": [],
  "env": []
}
```

The extracted object must reproduce both stored ACP digests before launch; any
extra/missing member or wrapper/payload confusion fails admission. The proxy speaks
MCP only behind the release-owned relay. The bootstrap owns ACP stdio, performs
the one-use authenticated bootstrap call, and has no direct private-broker
connection. The release launcher separately creates and validates the
privileged proxy, connects the relay and publishes both
`ProviderProxyLaunchClosureV1` and `ProviderBrokerStdioBootstrapReceiptV1`.
The grant cannot transition to `installed` without both receipts and the exact
accepted-server inventory. ACP contains the necessary sealed bootstrap command
path but no grant/token, workspace/repository
path, root, endpoint, header or caller-selected server definition; args and env
are exactly empty. Proxy audit-token/client-key identity plus the pre-registered
one-use admission and server-side attempt/session/process checks are the
authorization channel. The provider sandbox permits lookup of the private Mach
bootstrap service only to the exact sealed bootstrap child; that service rejects
the provider's own audit token and can only consume the pre-registered one-use
admission. The private broker Mach service is visible only to the separately
release-launched privileged proxy. The provider profile denies daemon Unix/TCP
sockets and localhost discovery, and neither provider nor bootstrap receives a
reusable broker credential.

Each production adapter must prove from its actual initialize/session-new
exchange that it passes those exact domain and wire digests, preserves
the sealed bootstrap command/args/env and cannot replace them. FD inventory from the
actual provider and every provider child proves that no raw broker endpoint is
present; direct provider XPC probes are denied while the sealed proxy succeeds.
The
release-owned proxy records the provider's MCP initialize and tools/list calls
and emits signed `ProviderBrokerAcceptedServerReceiptV1` with dispatch/session,
domain/wire/list digests, server name, observed broker protocol/tool inventory,
proxy process identity and launcher key epoch. Static adapter claims or a
candidate-authored terminal status are not acceptance evidence. The
`SkillBrokerGrantInstallReceiptV1` binds that receipt digest. A provider that
lacks stdio MCP, never initializes the declared broker channel, or closes/replaces the declared
stdio server is unsupported for every role requiring broker resources, Git evidence or
scripts; unsandboxed/HTTP/header fallback is forbidden.

#### Broker wire and semantic effect identity

The broker surface has four exact, unknown-field-denying schemas. None
accepts grant, run, execution, attempt, session, filesystem path, or target-root
identity from the provider:

| Tool | Exact request | Exact successful result | Exact error |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skills.resource.read` | `skill_resource_read_request_v1 { schema_version, uri, offset, max_bytes }`, where `offset` is a canonical unsigned decimal string and `max_bytes` is `1...32768` | `skill_resource_read_result_v1 { schema_version, uri, resource_sha256, offset, bytes_read, next_offset, eof, content_encoding = base64, data_base64, chunk_sha256 }` | `skill_resource_read_error_v1 { schema_version, error: skill_broker_error_v1 }` |
| `skills.script.run` | `skill_script_run_request_v1 { schema_version, idempotency_key, script_uri, conditional effect_slot_id, arguments }`, where the key is lowercase UUIDv7, `effect_slot_id` is required for write scripts and must be omitted for read-only scripts, explicit JSON `null` is always invalid, and `arguments` must match the contract's closed schema | `skill_script_run_result_v1 { schema_version, outcome, conditional effect_id, conditional effect_slot_id, script_intent_sha256, script_receipt_sha256, output_contract_sha256, output_json }`; both effect fields are required for a write script and forbidden for a read-only script | `skill_script_run_error_v1 { schema_version, error: skill_broker_error_v1 }` |
| `workspace.git_evidence.capture` | `git_evidence_capture_request_v1 { schema_version, idempotency_key }`, where the key is lowercase UUIDv7; no resolver or partial-view input is accepted | `git_evidence_capture_result_v1 { schema_version, snapshot_id, git_evidence_sha256, base_commit_oid, base_tree_oid, head_commit_oid, head_tree_oid, relation, conditional merge_base_commit_oid, conditional merge_base_tree_oid, complete, status_sha256, committed_changed_files_sha256, workspace_manifest_sha256, freshness_fence_sha256, sections }` | `git_evidence_capture_error_v1 { schema_version, error: skill_broker_error_v1 }` |
| `workspace.git_evidence.read` | `git_evidence_read_request_v1 { schema_version, snapshot_id, section_id, offset, max_bytes }` with canonical decimal range fields | `git_evidence_read_result_v1 { schema_version, snapshot_id, section_id, section_sha256, offset, bytes_read, next_offset, eof, content_encoding = base64, data_base64, chunk_sha256 }` | `git_evidence_read_error_v1 { schema_version, error: skill_broker_error_v1 }` |

Before calling the APFS snapshot service, the broker claims one authority-store
`GitEvidenceCaptureRequestRecordV1` keyed by grant scope and provider UUIDv7.
It preallocates immutable `snapshot_id`, APFS snapshot name, registered three-
root identity and retention deadline and transitions
`prepared -> snapshot_created -> evidence_materialized -> completed`, with
`prepared -> failed_no_snapshot` only after verified absence and any ambiguous
create/delete fate entering `identity_hold`. Snapshot create observation and
cleanup each have their own predecessor-linked action receipt. Cleanup cannot
run before the request is terminal and its retention/read leases are released.

Same key and canonical request joins or replays the original record and result;
same key with different bytes conflicts. Lost response after snapshot creation
resumes materialization for that same immutable snapshot, and lost response
after completion returns the original result. It never creates a second APFS
snapshot or substitutes a fresh workspace view. Retention cleanup preserves
the terminal receipt/digests and makes later reads return a typed expired-
snapshot result; it does not make capture replay executable again. Restart and
fault fixtures cover every create, mount, Git parse, receipt and cleanup
boundary.

At exact EOF, resource read returns zero bytes, unchanged next offset and
`eof = true`; an offset beyond EOF is `skill_resource_range_invalid`. Base64 and
decoded lengths, chunk digest, manifest digest and P096 cumulative budget are
verified before return. Script `outcome` is exactly `completed`,
`failed_no_effect`, or `failed_reconciled`; `reconciliation_required` is a typed
non-retryable error until operator reconciliation settles the existing effect.
All result objects are bounded by P096 and contain no raw stderr or path.

The provider never chooses semantic effect identity. Before accepting a write
script, the broker builds `SkillScriptLogicalEffectIdentityV2` from the parent
agent-execution ID, immutable run generation, assignment digest, composition
digest, immutable assignment-owned `effect_slot_id`, bundle/script/contract
digests and operation class. Runtime arguments, resolved target set, attempt
generation, grant, provider session, install epoch and request ID are excluded.
The unique claim key is exactly `(agent_execution_id, effect_slot_id)`; the
derived `logical_effect_id` is a stable receipt identity, not a second way to
claim the slot.

The first admitted request for a slot stores one immutable
`SkillScriptEffectIntentV1` containing that logical identity, canonical complete
arguments digest, `normalized_target_set_sha256`, target-resolver version,
precondition digest and script input-contract digest. Every later request for
the slot must byte-match this intent. Same slot plus different arguments,
targets, script, contract or operation class is
`skill_effect_intent_conflict`, performs zero spawn/apply and cannot allocate a
second effect row. Two intentional writes, including byte-identical writes,
require two distinct immutable assignment slots.

A production write contract declares closed JSON pointers and
`target_resolver_version`; the broker resolves their logical targets under the
grant's directory capabilities before spawn. A target that cannot be completely
derived is not executable. Read-only scripts do not create a logical-effect
identity or registry row and omit both effect fields; there is no serialized or
internal effect sentinel that can accidentally dedupe independent reads. For
budgeting only, the broker derives `read_retry_series_sha256` from execution,
assignment, script, canonical arguments and contract identities. Its monotonic
attempt counter does not cache a result or prevent a contract-admitted rerun;
attempt/grant/session remain audit fields. The broker
verifies that a write request's slot belongs to
the active assignment and grant and binds the same script/operation class; an
unknown or mismatched slot is the non-enumerating unavailable denial. Wire field
`effect_id` is the domain-separated `logical_effect_id` of that
complete object; a separate `effect_attempt_sha256` binds the authorizing
attempt/grant/session for audit only.

Request replay, logical-effect dedupe and contract retry are three separate
layers:

1. Every call first claims a `SkillScriptRequestRecordV1` keyed by grant scope
   and provider UUIDv7. Same key plus byte-equal canonical request joins in-flight
   or returns that request's terminal result. Same key plus different bytes is
   `skill_request_idempotency_conflict`. This layer never authorizes a new run.
2. Only a write script claims `SkillScriptEffectRegistryV1` under stable unique
   `(agent_execution_id, effect_slot_id)` and stores the first immutable effect
   intent. A different request, attempt,
   grant or session for a completed or ambiguous write consults this row before
   spawn/apply and returns the original receipt, `skill_effect_in_flight`,
   `skill_effect_intent_conflict`, or
   `skill_script_reconciliation_required`; it cannot apply twice.
3. A new request may execute only when the admitted contract's explicit retry
   rule and current terminal state permit a new **execution attempt**. Read-only
   retries never consult an effect registry. A write retry remains under the
   same logical-effect row and advances its monotonic effect-attempt revision;
   it never changes logical identity.

A contract that legitimately needs two identical writes must declare and
select two distinct control-plane-owned effect slots in the immutable
assignment; retrying either slot remains within only that slot's effect row.
The provider cannot invent a slot.

The closed decision matrix is:

| Side-effect/state | Same request key | New request/attempt | Spawn/apply rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| write slot already claimed with a different immutable intent | request conflict when bytes differ | `skill_effect_intent_conflict` | zero spawn/apply; slot identity cannot vary by arguments or targets |
| read-only `running` | join/in-flight | same retry series waits/returns `skill_request_in_flight`; an unrelated series follows its own contract concurrency cap | no duplicate process for one retry-series revision |
| read-only `completed` | replay original request result | rerun only when contract says `rerunnable_read_only` and retry budget remains | creates a new request/execution receipt, no effect row |
| read-only `failed_no_effect` | replay failure | retry only when `rerunnable_read_only`, failure code is admitted and budget remains | new execution attempt after verified process absence |
| write `prepared`, `running`, or `applying` | join/in-flight | return `skill_effect_in_flight` | never spawn/apply a second effect attempt concurrently |
| write `completed` or `committed` | replay original result | return original terminal result from the effect registry | never spawn or apply again |
| write `failed_no_effect` before workspace apply | replay failure | retry under the same effect row only when contract says `retry_failed_no_effect`, admitted failure code and budget allow it | increment effect-attempt revision after verified process absence |
| write `reconciliation_required` | replay typed error | same typed non-retryable error | no spawn until Operator reconciliation |
| write `failed_reconciled` with verified no effect | replay terminal receipt | retry only when contract explicitly admits `retry_failed_reconciled`; CAS advances registry revision | no retry when any effect may remain |

Reusing one UUIDv7 key with different canonical request bytes is
`skill_request_idempotency_conflict`. The closed `skill_broker_error_v1` wire
contains code, retryability, retry mode, canonical request ID when authorized,
and bounded safe detail. Its codes are exactly `invalid_request`,
`skill_resource_unavailable`, `skill_resource_range_invalid`,
`skill_request_in_flight`, `skill_request_idempotency_conflict`,
`skill_effect_in_flight`, `skill_effect_intent_conflict`, `skill_retry_not_permitted`,
`skill_script_runtime_unavailable`,
`skill_script_output_budget_exceeded`,
`skill_script_reconciliation_required`, `skill_grant_activation_pending`,
`git_evidence_unavailable`,
`git_evidence_scope_invalid`, `git_evidence_capture_raced`,
`git_evidence_output_budget_exceeded`, `git_evidence_incomplete`, and
`git_evidence_base_diverged`.
`skill_retry_not_permitted` is non-retryable for the current assignment/series;
`skill_request_in_flight` and `skill_effect_in_flight` permit only bounded wait
or exact readback, never immediate duplicate spawn.
Grant/scope/session/object/snapshot
mismatch and revocation all collapse to the same non-enumerating unavailable
response where disclosure would reveal existence.

### ProviderExecutionSandboxV1

The skill broker is not a security boundary while the same-UID provider can
open its backing stores directly. Every V2 production adapter therefore launches
the provider wrapper and all descendants under one outer
`ProviderExecutionSandboxV1` Seatbelt profile before provider initialization.
Provider-native sandbox settings are defense in depth only and cannot relax the
outer profile. `danger-full-access`, advisory-only execution, or unsandboxed
fallback is invalid for a V2 candidate.

The profile is default-deny for filesystem and local IPC. It always denies
the checkout `.git` entry, resolved linked-worktree gitdir and shared common Git
directory, `.agents/skills`, `.agent-evals`, the eval
vault, content-addressed skill snapshots, control-plane database/auth/state,
other run meta-roots, source provider homes, user credentials/keychains, and
daemon Unix/TCP sockets. The private broker Mach service may be looked up only
under its protocol name, but it authenticates the sealed proxy audit token and
rejects the provider process itself.
It allows only:

- the isolated provider runtime home and exact adapter-owned transport paths;
- sealed provider/wrapper/tool executables and declared read-only toolchain
  roots;
- invocation scratch/cache roots with bounded ownership and lifetime;
- declared run output roots and workspace source/test roots in read-only mode,
  while nested deny roots above remain denied. No provider process or provider
  child receives a workspace/output write capability; every accepted write is a
  broker-staged apply under an assignment-owned effect slot;
- the one preconnected local credential-channel descriptor declared by the
  provider-process launch expectation. The provider wrapper and every provider
  descendant have `network_class = none`: no remote socket creation, DNS,
  localhost discovery, listener, raw socket or connection to another provider's
  runtime home is permitted.

Provider authentication and all model-transport egress are owned by a separate
release-signed `provider_credential_proxy`, never by copied source-provider
homes or plaintext API/OAuth material in provider-readable files, argv or
environment. The credential proxy is not a child of the provider, uses its own
release-owned launch expectation/closure and network sandbox, and is the only
process whose profile admits the policy-selected upstream host/method/path,
DNS/TLS and redirect classes. Provider, broker proxy and their descendants are
not members of that network profile. For each dispatch, before any PID exists,
the launcher finalizes one `ProviderCredentialChannelAdmissionV1` bound to the
dispatch/attempt/session, launch expectation, adapter, admitted upstream
host/method/path classes, request/byte budget, correlated expiry and initial
connected-channel sequence. There is no filesystem or Mach-service endpoint to
discover. Before provider `exec`, the launcher gives the exact provider process
one inherited `AF_UNIX/SOCK_SEQPACKET` descriptor at the policy-fixed FD number;
all other descriptors are close-on-exec. The proxy side verifies
`LOCAL_PEERPID`, UID, process birth, provider-session registration and channel
nonce against the launch closure before parsing the first frame. The nonce is
framing correlation, not authority: copying it without the registered connected
peer cannot open or rebind a channel. Children receive no descriptor unless the
adapter policy names their measured executable and process-group role.

Provider credential-channel bootstrap is race-free and its signed-object graph
is acyclic. The launcher first creates the connected socket pair with both ends
close-on-exec, then signs a pre-spawn
`ProviderProcessLaunchExpectationV1` containing only authority-selected
provider identities and expected process/configuration facts. The credential-
channel admission binds that expectation and is finalized before spawn; neither
object contains a PID, observed process fact, launch-closure digest or broker-
proxy receipt. The launcher then uses the pinned Darwin
`POSIX_SPAWN_START_SUSPENDED` path to create the provider wrapper with only the
child endpoint duplicated to the policy-fixed FD. While the exact process is
suspended, it registers PID/process-birth/vnode/code/sandbox identity and the
credential proxy verifies `LOCAL_PEERPID`, UID and registered birth. The
independent observer compares the provider process with the expectation and
signs `ProviderProcessLaunchClosureV1`. Only that closure plus a signed
`ProviderCredentialChannelBindingV1`, which binds the observed PID/birth/session,
peer registration and separately launched credential-proxy identity back to the
pre-spawn admission, permits resume; timeout or
mismatch closes both endpoints and proves process reap. This graph is distinct
from and contains no edge to the later broker-proxy admission/launch graph.

The outer Seatbelt profile denies `process-fork` and descriptor passing for a
channel-bearing process. Adapter-declared children are launched separately by
the release launcher after independent process registration and receive a new
child-scoped channel; they never inherit the parent's descriptor. The proxy
rejects ancillary data, an unregistered PID/birth, another process group or a
sequence shared by two peers. `dup`, `fork`, `SCM_RIGHTS`, pre-bootstrap exec,
copied-FD and declared-child fixtures prove an inherited or duplicated
descriptor cannot authenticate from an unregistered child. An adapter that
cannot operate under this launch model is unsupported rather than granted a
transferable credential channel.

`provider_credential_proxy_protocol_v1` uses length-prefixed canonical frames
with channel sequence, one authority-issued `ProviderSendIntentV1`, closed
request class, policy-owned host ID, relative path class, method, bounded header
names/values excluding authorization/cookies, bounded body bytes/digest and
deadline. Before the credential proxy can load a Keychain credential or write
an upstream byte, it validates and atomically consumes that one-use intent. The
intent is derived from the frozen dispatch/profile and the admitted prompt turn,
not provider input, and binds the exact adapter, model, account/project,
operation class, body-schema version, semantic body digest,
`ProviderContextBudgetStateV1`, prompt reservation, channel sequence and
deadline.

Each `ProviderAdapterCredentialPolicyV1` owns a closed parser for that adapter's
request body. The proxy rejects unknown fields and verifies every
authority-selected model, project/account, operation and bounded generation/
sampling parameter against the intent; where the upstream protocol permits it,
the proxy inserts those fields itself and forbids the provider from supplying
them. A mismatch, duplicate field, alternate body encoding or unrecognized
operation returns `provider_send_intent_mismatch`, consumes no intent and sends
zero upstream bytes. Thus an authorized host/path cannot be used as a confused
deputy for a different model, project, account or provider operation.

The frame accepts no URL, IP literal, proxy method, CONNECT, caller DNS answer,
credential header or redirect target. The proxy resolves DNS itself, rejects
private/link-local/loopback results unless a policy fixture explicitly names
them, pins the resolution for the request, requires Host/SNI/certificate name
equality and the policy's TLS version/trust/conditional SPKI set, and performs
zero redirects. A `3xx` is returned as a sanitized typed response; the provider
must obtain a new independently validated intent for any admitted follow-up.
Method/path/host, parsed body, frame size, streamed byte, request-count and
deadline limits are checked before the proxy loads the non-exportable
Keychain-held credential.

The proxy performs the upstream TLS request itself, inserts only the
policy-selected credential, strips authentication, cookie, refresh-token and
proxy headers from the response, caps/dechunks response bytes and returns one
sequenced frame. It never exposes the underlying secret or a reusable refresh
token. Unexpected frame sequence, reconnect, half-open ambiguity, proxy restart,
session loss, cancellation, expiry or settlement revokes the channel before
process reuse. The provider sandbox denies direct egress and allows only the
connected descriptor. Adapters that cannot use this exact framed channel are
unsupported for V2; readable-credential, copied-home, loopback-proxy and direct-
network fallback are forbidden.

The active trust policy pins one signed
`ProviderAdapterCredentialPolicyV1` per adapter. Its checked-in host/method/TLS
sets, rather than this descriptive table, are exact; the table fixes the
supported authentication shape and fail-closed runtime-home rule:

| Adapter | Admitted auth class and sole channel | Isolated runtime-home requirement | Failure disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Codex | `openai_codex_oauth_or_api_key_v1` through the process-bound credential proxy and policy-pinned OpenAI host/method/TLS set | generated `CODEX_HOME` contains sanitized config only; `auth.json`, API keys, refresh/access tokens and source-home links are absent | any build requiring readable auth files/env or direct upstream network is excluded from the candidate |
| Claude | `anthropic_oauth_or_api_key_v1` through the same opaque channel protocol and Claude-specific host/method/TLS set | generated Claude config/cache roots contain no credential/token database and cannot read the source profile | interactive login, Keychain read, credential env or direct-network requirement is unsupported |
| Gemini | `google_gemini_oauth_or_api_key_v1` through the Gemini-specific proxy policy | isolated Gemini home contains non-secret settings only; Google credential stores, ADC files and source-home links are denied | browser/device login or readable ADC/token fallback is unsupported |
| Auggie | `augment_service_token_v1` through the Augment-specific proxy policy | isolated Auggie home contains no service token or reusable session credential | an adapter version that cannot bind all auth requests to the opaque channel is removed from production profiles |
| Junie | `jetbrains_junie_account_bridge_v1` only when its exact release build supports the process-bound proxy protocol | isolated Junie/JetBrains runtime view exposes no IDE account store, source profile or Keychain capability | otherwise Junie is explicitly unsupported and a production catalog reference blocks candidate registration/open |

Credentials live only in the proxy-only Keychain access group declared by one
release-root-signed `ProviderCredentialStorePolicyV1`. The policy fixes adapter,
authentication class, canonical account/project binding, Keychain service and
opaque generation-account derivation, proxy/controller designated requirements,
refresh protocol, overlap duration and deletion/zeroization rules. Provider,
candidate, broker, ordinary daemon, app readback and eval worker have neither
the entitlement nor an API returning a persistent reference or secret digest.
Startup compares the complete active/pending/revoked metadata inventory with
the Keychain item-generation inventory through the sealed credential controller;
missing, duplicate, foreign or ambiguous items are failed-serve.

Whenever the proxy or provisioning/import controller must transiently hold a
bearer, API key, OAuth access/refresh token or equivalent provider secret, it
uses only the Rust-owned non-`Clone` `TransientSecretBufferV1` governed by the
release-signed `TransientSecretMemoryPolicyV1`. The policy fixes the maximum
allocation, guard-page layout, page alignment, `mlock` requirement,
`MADV_DONTDUMP`/platform-equivalent disposition, `RLIMIT_CORE = 0`, allocator
component/build and explicit-zeroization routine. Allocation, guard-page or
memory-lock failure is fail-closed before Keychain extraction or provider send;
there is no ordinary heap/string/vector fallback. Secret-bearing types do not
implement `Debug`, `Display`, `Serialize`, `Clone` or equality/hash traits and
cannot enter argv, environment, logs, metrics, panic payloads, crash reports,
temporary files, SQLite, signed contracts or provider-visible frames.

Normal return, error, cancellation, timeout, refresh replacement and unwinding
all run `explicit_bzero` (or the release-pinned non-optimizable equivalent) over
the full allocated capacity before unlock/unmap. The proxy process installs no
core-dump path and contains no persistent plaintext, so uncatchable `SIGKILL`
leaves only locked anonymous pages reclaimed by the kernel at process death;
restart reloads the credential from Keychain under a new bounded buffer rather
than recovering plaintext. The active `EvaluationTrustPolicyV1` pins the exact
secret-memory-policy digest for every credential-bearing component. Retained
tests force allocation/guard/lock failures, normal/error/cancel/timeout/unwind
cleanup, refresh replacement and process termination, then scan allocator,
logs, serialization, environment, argv, temp/storage and crash artifacts for
secret canaries. Any recoverable plaintext or missing zeroization receipt blocks
candidate registration and serving.

Each immutable `ProviderCredentialGenerationV1` binds only adapter, auth class,
account/project, generation, predecessor, opaque Keychain account identity,
issue/not-before/expiry, refresh capability, state and policy digest. Its
predecessor-linked lifecycle is
`prepared -> installed -> verified -> active -> overlap -> replaced | revoked |
expired`, with `prepared | installed -> failed_no_secret` only after the
controller proves no item and `installed | verified -> reconciliation_hold` for
ambiguous fate. Exactly one generation is active per adapter/account binding.
Every transition is journaled by `ProviderCredentialLifecycleTransitionV1` in
the authority store before Keychain mutation, then finalized by CAS after the
proxy verifies the upstream account/project through a credential-stripped
response. Readback exposes only state, account-binding ID, generation, policy,
expiry and repair action.

Initial provisioning has two closed sources. During `schema_prepared`, the
one-time `provider_credential_import_controller` may open only the release-pinned
source-provider credential records named by a complete migration inventory. It
binds no-follow vnode/mode/owner/source format, imports one credential into a new
generation, verifies the account binding, zeroizes plaintext and unlinks or
redacts the old source under `ProviderCredentialMigrationReceiptV1`; it never
copies a provider home. For a credential without an importable source, the
Operator uses the release-root-signed local provisioning helper under one
`ProviderCredentialProvisioningHelperPolicyV1`. The policy pins the helper's
component/build/designated requirement, exact minimal entitlements, OS-secure
input class, private XPC service and message schema, controller peer audit-token
identity, admitted adapter/account-binding set, maximum secret bytes,
monotonic deadline, locked-memory/zeroization rules and crash/replay
disposition. The helper has no network, provider-launch, authority-store,
candidate-store, broker, generic Keychain-read or proxy credential entitlement.

Before the secure input surface opens, the credential controller issues one
`ProviderCredentialProvisioningIntentV1` bound to the target generation,
adapter/auth/account/project, store and helper policies, helper/controller
identities, random one-use nonce, maximum bytes and deadline. The helper
authenticates the controller peer and the controller authenticates the helper
audit token before either parses payload bytes. Secret bytes travel once in a
length-delimited private XPC message directly from OS-secure input to locked
helper memory and the credential controller. They never occur in MCP, GraphQL,
ACP, argv, environment, files, logs, crash reports, candidate storage or
readback. The controller consumes the intent in the same lifecycle operation
that installs and account-verifies the target Keychain item, then writes a
`ProviderCredentialProvisioningReceiptV1` containing only bounded byte-count,
peer, transition, account-verification and zeroization evidence.

A wrong peer, expired/replayed intent, oversized input, account mismatch or
helper crash before Keychain commit produces `failed_no_secret` with zero
generation transition after verified buffer/input teardown. A crash at or
after an ambiguous Keychain boundary enters `reconciliation_hold`; restart
reconciles the same intent and item identity and can never open another secure
input window or install twice. Interactive provider login, device-code flow
inside a provider process and readable-file fallback are forbidden.

Refresh and rotation always allocate a successor generation and new Keychain
item before touching the active pointer. OAuth refresh consumes one
authority-issued refresh intent, lets only the proxy read the active refresh
credential, validates the returned account/project, installs the successor and
CASes it active before placing the predecessor in bounded overlap and deleting
its secret at overlap end. API-key rotation follows the same transition using
the provisioning helper. Revocation first fences every credential channel and
provider session bound to the generation, then marks it revoked and deletes the
Keychain item; deletion failure remains a release-blocking reconciliation hold.
Crash/replay at every journal, Keychain add/update/delete, account-verification,
pointer-CAS and channel-fence boundary resumes the same generation/action. It
never imports twice, activates two generations, resurrects a revoked credential
or falls back to a source home. Rotation, expiry, account mismatch, refresh
rejection, policy change and controller-key revocation fixtures prove this full
lifecycle without secret-bearing persistence or readback.

The policy contains no secret and is validated before dispatch. For every row,
provider direct egress is denied, the connected peer/sequence is accepted only
from the registered process/session, DNS rebinding, cross-host redirects,
certificate mismatch, duplicated frames, wrong child, channel restart and
deadline loss fail closed, proxy responses strip credential material, and
channel revocation precedes process/session reuse. Escape fixtures cover each
accepted auth class and prove no credential bytes occur in runtime-home files,
argv, environment, ACP payloads, prompts, receipts, logs or provider-visible
headers.

The trusted launcher resolves every configured root component with no-follow
directory descriptors, records device/inode and canonical path, rejects
symlink/alias overlap between allow and deny roots, and emits Seatbelt literals
only from that table. Workspace allowances are capabilities for the declared
run root, not broad home/repository prefixes; protected nested roots remain
denied even when their parent workspace is readable.

The release-owned `provider_sandbox_launcher` owns the Seatbelt profile bytes,
canonical allow/deny root table, network class, executable identities and policy
version. The candidate manifest, generation and dispatch intent may select only
an admitted policy digest; candidate code cannot supply profile bytes or launch
the process. The production daemon's own outer profile denies direct
`posix_spawn`/`exec` of provider and privileged proxy binaries, so the XPC
launcher is their sole process creator. ACP's only process-creation exception is
the exact sealed unprivileged stdio bootstrap executable described above; it
cannot launch a provider, credential proxy or privileged broker proxy. Before
`provider_bound`, the launcher observes
the real child/process group and signs `ProviderSandboxAttestationV1` with its
purpose-bound release key. The receipt contains launcher component/build/key
epoch, process-group/birth identity, adapter/profile digest, runtime-home
identity, effective root table, outer-sandbox handshake, and results of
versioned denial probes against sentinels in every protected root class. A
candidate wrapper/status is untrusted telemetry and cannot substitute for this
receipt. The adapter receipt is accepted only when the release signature,
attestation and observed provider binding match the pin.

The provider-visible MCP stdio command is a sealed, hardened-runtime
`chainworks-broker-stdio-bootstrap` shim with no broker/XPC/data capability and
`network_class = none`; it is not the privileged `chainworks-broker-proxy`.
Before
parsing provider bytes it closes every inherited descriptor
except stdin/stdout/stderr, clears the environment without reading values,
changes to a release-owned empty directory, applies fixed umask/rlimits and
verifies library validation. Loader variables (`DYLD_*`, `LD_*` and adapter-
declared equivalents), unexpected inherited descriptors, writable executable
or library mappings, an unapproved cwd, arguments or supplementary IPC handle
are terminal launch-closure failures; there is no best-effort sanitization
branch after a violation.

The release launcher separately spawns the privileged proxy from the registered
admission, then independently inspects that exact proxy PID and signs
`ProviderProxyLaunchClosureV1` only after comparing the signed launch
expectation with observed
executable vnode/digest/designated requirement, parent provider audit token and
session, argv, initial environment-name inventory, initial and post-bootstrap
FD maps with descriptor types/rights/targets, cwd, umask, rlimits, sandbox
identity, loader-variable presence, and complete loaded-image CDHash/team/
library-validation inventory. The receipt proves the same PID crossed the
bootstrap barrier; a self-reported process ID or child replacement is invalid.
Only then may the broker admit the proxy XPC connection and connect the one-use
stdio relay to the already measured shim. MCP initialize or grant installation
also requires the resulting `ProviderBrokerStdioBootstrapReceiptV1`. The
accepted-server and install receipts bind both launch-closure and bootstrap-
receipt digests; the earlier proxy admission binds only the expectation.

The two launch families have separate digest orders and no schema or object is
valid in both:

```text
provider-process launch expectation -> credential-channel admission
                            -> suspended provider process
                            -> provider-process launch closure
                            -> credential-channel binding -> provider resume

broker grant -> proxy launch expectation -> proxy admission
             -> ACP unprivileged stdio bootstrap
             -> release-launched suspended privileged proxy -> launch closure
             -> one-use relay/bootstrap receipt -> accepted-server receipt
             -> install receipt
```

Every edge points to an already finalized object. Generation rejects any schema
or implementation in which a provider-process object carries a broker-proxy
digest or vice versa, an expectation/admission references a later closure, or a
closure omits the matching same-family expectation and admission when that
family has one.

Retained vectors inject inherited repository/runtime-home FDs, Mach rights,
sockets, secret-bearing environment names, hostile cwd, loader variables,
extra dylibs, altered entitlements and same-PID executable/library identity
drift through each adapter's real ACP launch path. Every case fails before tool
advertisement or broker access; the clean vector proves exact stdio framing and
that the observed closure, sandbox attestation and provider binding name the
same parent/session/proxy process identities. Adapter body fixtures also mutate
model, project/account, operation, body encoding and generation parameters and
prove the proxy emits zero upstream bytes before any credential access.

Codex, Claude, Gemini, Auggie and Junie each have retained launch/escape
fixtures that attempt direct skill, Git, workspace-outside-profile, eval,
control-plane, sibling runtime-home, credential and local-IPC access from the
actual provider process and an allowed child. Every protected access must fail,
while declared workspace reads and broker-mediated command/output operations
must succeed; direct writes under every workspace/output root must fail. An adapter
that cannot produce this evidence is excluded from production profiles; if it
is still referenced by a production catalog, candidate evaluation and
`open_v2` fail closed.

### SkillScriptExecutionContractV1

The sole authoring source for executable policy is
`<skill-root>/contracts/skill-scripts.json` in the pinned immutable skill Git
tree. It is a closed object with `schema_version = skill_script_contract_set_v1`
and a map keyed by the normalized `scripts/...` manifest path; each value is one
complete `SkillScriptExecutionContractV1`. `SKILL.md`, catalog YAML, workflow
YAML, prompts and runtime arguments may reference a script but cannot define,
merge or override its contract. An executable manifest entry without exactly one
matching contract, a contract without an executable entry, duplicate normalized
paths or unknown fields fails bundle publication. The publisher JCS-canonicalizes
that source, stores its source-blob digest plus contract-set digest in
`SkillBundleManifestV1`, and copies the unchanged per-script canonical contract
into the bundle index. Runtime consumes only that admitted copy and verifies it
against both source digests.

Each closed `SkillScriptExecutionContractV1` fixes:

- immutable script and interpreter/runtime digests;
- input JSON Schema and 64 KiB canonical-stdin cap;
- side-effect class `read_only`, `run_artifact_write`, or `workspace_write`;
- exact read roots and, for either write class, permission-profile-derived write
  roots expressed as already-opened directory capabilities;
- timeout, CPU, memory, process-count, file-count and written-byte limits;
- child executable digest allowlist, empty by default;
- closed retry policy: read-only `no_retry | rerunnable_read_only`, write
  `no_retry | retry_failed_no_effect | retry_failed_reconciled`,
  canonical decimal max execution/effect attempts, exact retryable failure-code
  set, backoff schedule and output-contract schema; incompatible side-effect/
  retry combinations fail publication;
- sandbox policy and version digest.

The migration manifest additionally contains an exact
`LegacyRequiredToolMigrationSetV1`. Its key set is every normalized
`required_tools` entry and every executable permission-profile/allowlist command
reachable from a production catalog assignment. Each row binds all consumers
and exactly one disposition: `broker_script`, `git_evidence_tool`, or
`retired_before_open`. A `broker_script` row names one immutable bundle script
and `SkillScriptExecutionContractV1`, a closed command family, exact executable
and child-executable digests, a logical cwd selected by the contract rather than
the provider, closed argv JSON schema, fixed environment-name/value-source set,
scratch/cache policy, side-effect class, output cap and effect-slot binding.
`cargo`, `swift`, `xcodebuild`, linters and test runners therefore execute only
inside the trusted skill-runner sandbox; the provider cannot fork or exec them
directly. Build products and caches are request/generation-owned scratch data
and cannot become workspace evidence. A write-capable command emits only the
staged write manifest consumed by the apply journal below.

`git status`, `git diff`, `git rev-parse` and every other Git executable map only
to the two structured Git evidence tools and have no broker script. Unknown
shell text, command concatenation, shell expansion, caller cwd/path/env,
unbounded argv or a catalog tool row missing from this exact set fails compile,
candidate registration and `open_v2`. Migration fixtures enumerate the current
Cargo/Go/Swift/Xcode and repository-read requirements and prove each is either
usable through its closed broker contract or retired before open; no provider
profile may pass merely because direct process execution is denied.

Production macOS has one executable backend,
`macos_seatbelt_exec_v1`. The broker invokes the sealed-system
`/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` with a generated Seatbelt profile and a bundled trusted
`chainworks-skill-runner`; there is no unsandboxed, advisory, container, shell,
or direct-provider fallback. Because Apple marks the underlying interface
deprecated, daemon startup verifies the executable's canonical path, owner,
mode, vnode and Apple code-signing identity and executes a versioned escape
self-test on every supported macOS build. The test proves allowed descriptor
I/O and denial of network, Mach/Unix/localhost IPC, process escape, keychain and
credential reads, undeclared file access and child execution. Missing primitive,
identity drift or any self-test escape sets
`skill_script_runtime_unavailable`; the candidate cannot become `live_passed`,
probe or open on that host. A future backend requires a new manifest/policy
version and full promotion evidence, never a runtime fallback.

Before spawn, the broker copies the exact admitted script and any non-system
interpreter/child bytes into a request-owned content-addressed execution root
that the provider sandbox cannot read or write. It opens every component with
`openat` plus `O_NOFOLLOW`, verifies regular-file type, owner/mode, device/inode,
size and digest, seals the parent against untrusted writes, and rechecks the
same identities immediately before `posix_spawn`. System executables must live
on the sealed system volume and pass their pinned Apple signature requirement.
Only those private immutable paths appear in trusted argv. The Seatbelt profile
allows execute only for the runner, pinned interpreter and allowlisted child
objects; all children inherit the profile and join one recorded process group.
An untrusted writer therefore has no path mutation window between verification
and exec. Any identity mismatch before spawn produces `failed_no_effect`; an
ambiguous spawned identity produces a process hold.

Model-controlled data is canonical JSON on stdin, never argv or environment.
Cwd is a fresh broker-owned directory. The environment is rebuilt from a fixed
allowlist (`LANG`, `TZ`, a scratch `HOME`) with no inherited `PATH`, auth,
provider, Git, daemon, proxy, cloud, or user variables. The profile denies
network and IPC, device files, credential/keychain paths, `.git`,
`~/.chainworks`, daemon state, provider homes, skill/eval stores other than the
selected read-only objects, and all undeclared filesystem access. CPU, address
space, file-size, descriptor and process-count limits are installed before user
code. Cancellation, timeout, grant revocation, or daemon shutdown terminates and
verifies the complete process group; ambiguous fate creates an identity hold
and permits no retry. Stdout/stderr use P096 per-call and cumulative caps.

Executable skills never receive direct network, Git, control-plane or external
publication access. Those effects remain separate authenticated runtime tools
with their existing durable side-effect contracts. A `workspace_write` or
`run_artifact_write` script also cannot write its destination directly:
Seatbelt exposes the workspace and run output roots
read-only and one broker-owned staging root writable. The script emits a closed
relative write manifest and staged bytes. After runner settlement, the trusted
broker validates path bounds, declared write roots, file count/bytes and staged
digests before any workspace mutation.

The durable script state machine is closed:

```text
prepared -> spawning -> running -> runner_settled
prepared|spawning -> failed_no_effect  [only after verified process absence]
spawning|running -> process_identity_hold
running -> failed_no_effect  [verified group reap; reason records cancellation or failure]
runner_settled -> completed  [read_only]
runner_settled -> apply_prepared -> applying -> committed  [workspace_write | run_artifact_write]
apply_prepared|applying -> reconciliation_required -> committed|failed_reconciled
```

Before spawn, the broker writes `SkillScriptExecutionIntentV1` and claims the
tool idempotency key in the same transaction. Spawn registration records process
group, PID/birth identity and sandbox handshake before state `running`. A crash
after spawn but before `runner_settled` reattaches to the registered group; if
verified absent without a terminal runner receipt, staging is quarantined and
the attempt becomes `failed_no_effect`. It cannot have changed the workspace.
One request record may resume only from nonterminal `prepared`; once it reaches
