`failed_no_effect`, the exact UUID always replays that terminal failure. A live
or ambiguous process never reruns. Any admitted retry uses a new UUID: after a
terminal read-only receipt it may run only under `rerunnable_read_only` plus
remaining budget, and a write retry remains under the same slot/effect row and
its next effect-attempt revision. Changing request, attempt, grant or session
cannot bypass that registry.

For `workspace_write` or `run_artifact_write`, `apply_prepared` creates one immutable
`SkillScriptApplyJournalV1` with ordered relative paths, operation
`create | replace | delete`, expected preimage digest or explicit absence,
postimage digest or deletion, staging digest, directory-capability identity and
journal digest. Before each dirfd-relative no-follow atomic rename/delete, the
broker durably records entry state `pending`; after fsync of file and parent it
records `applied`. Recovery compares actual bytes with preimage and postimage:
preimage resumes that entry, postimage marks it applied, and any third value
enters `reconciliation_required` without overwrite or script rerun. The journal
commits only after every entry and parent directory is fsynced. This is
side-effect truth even though a multi-file filesystem update is not globally
atomic.

One immutable `SkillScriptExecutionReceiptV1` records intent/request/grant IDs,
execution and attempt identity, process fingerprint, observed sandbox/backend
identity, state transitions, bounded output digests/truncation, staging manifest
digest, optional apply-journal digest and final workspace write-set digests.
Receipts never contain secret environment values or raw unbounded output.

### Selection

Chainworks keeps deterministic skill selection. The workflow task names an
ordered `skills` list, and the agent catalog declares an unordered
`allowed_skills` set. Compilation rejects an unknown or disallowed pairing,
more than four entries, or a duplicate skill ID.

`SkillCompositionV1` records each task-order position, skill ID,
`bundle_sha256`, `SKILL.md` byte length and digest, and resource-manifest digest,
plus aggregate body/resource byte counts. Bundle resources remain namespaced by
bundle digest, so equal relative paths in two skills do not collide and
cross-bundle relative references are invalid. The fixed renderer injects bodies
in task order with versioned length-bearing headers. The composition digest and
the prompt manifest's exact rendered-skill-section digest make ordering and
bytes independently verifiable.

Agent Skills descriptions still receive trigger evals so the bundles remain
portable to metadata-driven Agent Skills hosts. Production Chainworks does not
delegate required skill selection to the provider model.

### LegacySkillMigrationManifestV1

Migration is governed by one machine-readable
`LegacySkillMigrationManifestV1`, not the human table above. The materialized
manifest is stored at
`docs/evidence/agent-context/legacy-skill-migration-v1.json`, is pinned by
`AgentContextCandidateManifestV1`, and contains:

- `schema_version`, source commit, catalog/workflow tree digests, Rust and Swift
  builtin/role-map digests, generator version, sorted source-node inventory,
  sorted fragment rows, coverage summary, and
  `legacy_skill_migration_sha256`;
- separate complete raw-path-byte-sorted `source_root_inventory` and
  `materialized_target_root_inventory` sets for every tracked `SKILL.md` root in
  the protected migration-input and materialized candidate Git trees, not only
  catalog-reachable roots. Each source row
  binds root/tree/file digests, declared host contract and exactly one
  disposition: `canonical_production`, `generated_host_copy`,
  `independent_non_production`, or `retired_before_open`. A generated copy binds
  its canonical root and `SkillHostRoutingContractV1`; an independent row must
  be unreachable from every production catalog, plugin publication and package;
  a retired row binds a reviewed removal receipt and is absent from the open
  tree. Each target row binds its canonical/generated/independent disposition,
  exact source-row lineage when applicable and candidate tree/file digests; no
  target row may be `retired_before_open`;
- for every source node, portable path, YAML/JSON pointer or Rust/Swift symbol,
  source kind, decoded UTF-8 byte length and exact source-node SHA-256;
- for every fragment, stable `fragment_id`, source-node ID, non-overlapping
  decoded-value byte range, `fragment_sha256`, originating skill/agent/mode,
  exactly one disposition, closed execution modes, effect class,
  partial-failure policy, and target identity/digest or retirement reason.
- for every production `backend_profile.mcp` binding reachable from the frozen
  catalog and assignment set, including current `xcode` and `context7` rows,
  the profile/pointer, exact normalized configuration digest, complete sorted
  consumer assignments and exactly one disposition `brokered_replacement` or
  `retired_before_open`. A brokered row binds the canonical broker
  operation/skill-contract/tool-inventory digest that replaces it; a retired
  row binds a reviewed removal receipt and has no runtime endpoint.
- one complete `production_skill_lineage_inventory` keyed by every retained
  production catalog skill ID. Each row binds the catalog source node, canonical
  bundle root/ID/digest, all consuming agents/tasks, script-contract-set digest
  and migration fragment set. The deprecated `proposal_review_triad` alias is a
  separate `retired_before_open` source disposition and cannot count as one of
  the retained skills. The packaged lifecycle dispatcher is a production host
  adapter with its own canonical bundle but is not a twelfth catalog skill ID.

Source nodes include every production skill description/body, complete agent
`prompt`, `skill_role` specialization, inline/builtin registry value, hardcoded
role/mode map, workflow task instruction fragment, and renderer-owned injected
role/skill text reachable by the frozen catalog. For each decoded source value,
fragment ranges must form an exact partition from byte zero through byte length:
every boundary must be a UTF-8 scalar boundary, and no gap, overlap, duplicate
fragment, or unaccounted whitespace is permitted.

The tracked-root inventory is derived with the structured Git object reader
from the exact protected commit and compared as an exact set with all tree
entries whose basename is `SKILL.md` anywhere in that repository tree.
That complete sweep consumes the same traversal-policy counters and deadline;
it does not perform an unbounded pre-scan before applying them.
Filesystem discovery, current checkout state and catalog
reachability cannot hide a tracked root. The gate fails on an omitted or extra
root, duplicate canonical owner, generated copy without matching source/host
contract, production reachability from an `independent_non_production` row, or
a retained path marked retired. Catalog-reachable fragment coverage is then
checked as a strict subset of this complete root inventory.

For the protected source revision reviewed by this proposal, that exact set has
seven roots. The migration generator must emit these seven source rows exactly
once; this is the frozen input disposition contract, not an illustrative subset:

| Migration-input `SKILL.md` root | Target disposition | Required migration/host contract |
|---|---|---|
| `.agent/skills/proposal-implementation-audit/SKILL.md` | `retired_before_open` | remove the legacy host copy after the plugin audit skill is qualified; bind the reviewed removal receipt and prove no production catalog or package path still resolves it |
| `docs/brand/SKILL.md` | `independent_non_production` | documentation-authoring input only; prove it is absent from every production agent catalog, skill registry and plugin/app package |
| `examples/skills/proposal-implementation-audit/SKILL.md` | `retired_before_open` | remove the duplicate example source, bind its reviewed removal receipt and prove no production/example package still resolves it |
| `examples/skills/proposal-review-triad/SKILL.md` | `retired_before_open` | remove the legacy example-only triad source, bind its reviewed removal receipt and prove no package still resolves it |
| `plugins/proposal-lifecycle-review/skills/proposal-implementation-audit/SKILL.md` | `generated_host_copy` | generated from `.agents/skills/proposal-implementation-audit/` under its signed standalone host-routing contract |
| `plugins/proposal-lifecycle-review/skills/proposal-lifecycle-review/SKILL.md` | `generated_host_copy` | generated from `.agents/skills/proposal-lifecycle-review/`; packaged thin dispatcher whose closed table may select only the two named production skills and cannot run review logic itself |
| `plugins/proposal-lifecycle-review/skills/proposal-review-router/SKILL.md` | `generated_host_copy` | generated from `.agents/skills/proposal-review-router/`; standalone router adapter signs a reviewer-selection write intent under its host-routing contract, while the release-owned handoff writer alone materializes the handoff |

The plugin manifest publishes the whole `skills/` directory, so the dispatcher
row is production-reachable and may not be omitted, treated as documentation or
silently generated from either child. A protected-tree change that adds,
removes, renames or changes the disposition of any tracked root requires a new
manifest revision and candidate digest. Open fails when the generated exact set
is not byte-for-byte equal to the structured Git inventory or when an
`independent_non_production`/`retired_before_open` row remains reachable.
The materialized candidate/open tree has an explicit sixteen-row exact set:

| Materialized open-tree `SKILL.md` root | Open disposition | Required lineage/host contract |
|---|---|---|
| `.agents/skills/proposal-implementation-audit/SKILL.md` | `canonical_production` | canonical migrated audit bundle with source-fragment and target digest coverage |
| `.agents/skills/proposal-lifecycle-review/SKILL.md` | `canonical_production` | canonical thin dispatcher with the closed two-target routing contract |
| `.agents/skills/proposal-review-router/SKILL.md` | `canonical_production` | canonical standalone selection producer and signed handoff-intent author; it has no filesystem-write authority |
| `.agents/skills/docs-quality-guardian/SKILL.md` | `canonical_production` | canonical bundle for catalog skill `docs_quality_guardian`; replaces the builtin-agent registry row before open |
| `.agents/skills/orchestrator-core/SKILL.md` | `canonical_production` | canonical bundle for catalog skill `orchestrator_core` |
| `.agents/skills/proposal-writer-core/SKILL.md` | `canonical_production` | canonical bundle for catalog skill `proposal_writer_core` |
| `.agents/skills/code-writer-core/SKILL.md` | `canonical_production` | canonical bundle for catalog skill `code_writer_core` |
| `.agents/skills/security-checker-core/SKILL.md` | `canonical_production` | canonical bundle for catalog skill `security_checker_core` |
| `.agents/skills/prepush-review-core/SKILL.md` | `canonical_production` | canonical bundle for catalog skill `prepush_review_core` |
| `.agents/skills/github-commit-push/SKILL.md` | `canonical_production` | canonical bundle for catalog skill `github_commit_push` |
| `.agents/skills/connect-publisher/SKILL.md` | `canonical_production` | canonical bundle for catalog skill `connect_publisher` |
| `.agents/skills/steward-core/SKILL.md` | `canonical_production` | canonical bundle for catalog skill `steward_core` |
| `docs/brand/SKILL.md` | `independent_non_production` | unchanged independent documentation-authoring root with empty production reachability |
| `plugins/proposal-lifecycle-review/skills/proposal-implementation-audit/SKILL.md` | `generated_host_copy` | byte/digest lineage to the canonical `.agents` audit root and signed standalone host contract |
| `plugins/proposal-lifecycle-review/skills/proposal-lifecycle-review/SKILL.md` | `generated_host_copy` | byte/digest lineage to the canonical `.agents` dispatcher root and signed standalone host contract |
| `plugins/proposal-lifecycle-review/skills/proposal-review-router/SKILL.md` | `generated_host_copy` | byte/digest lineage to the canonical `.agents` router root and signed standalone host contract |

The three retired input roots are absent, and no other `SKILL.md` exists. The
eleven retained catalog IDs map bijectively to eleven canonical catalog-skill
bundles above (`proposal_review_router_skill` maps to
`proposal-review-router`, and `proposal_implementation_audit` maps to
`proposal-implementation-audit`); the lifecycle dispatcher is the one
additional canonical host-adapter bundle. Both
sets bind their exact protected Git revisions/tree digests in the same manifest.
The implementation cannot reuse the source inventory as target proof or keep
the count sixteen without exact path/digest equality.

Disposition is exactly one of `role`, `skill_body`, `skill_resource`,
`runtime_policy`, `permission_profile`, `output_contract`,
`workflow_assignment`, or `retired`. A non-retired row requires target logical
ID, schema version, portable target path or registry key, and exact target
content digest. `retired` requires a closed reason
`compatibility_alias | duplicate_text | obsolete_behavior | non_production` and
has no target. Execution modes use only the modes in the inventory table.
Effect class is `none`, `run_artifact_write`, `workspace_write`,
`control_plane_command`, `git_external_effect`, or `network_external_effect`.
Partial-failure policy is `fail_before_effect`, `settle_output_generation`,
`reconcile_durable_intent`, or `retired` and must be compatible with the effect
class.

The generator first emits a planned manifest, but V2 compile and package gates
accept only `materialized` state, where every target digest resolves to the
candidate tree. Rust and Swift independently recompute source coverage and
target ownership. Package golden tests render every declared execution mode and
prove that each legacy fragment appears exactly once in the intended protected,
skill, policy, assignment or output-contract section, or is absent under a
reviewed retirement row. The V2 catalog fails closed on an omitted/extra
tracked skill root, source node or production MCP binding, extra target text
without provenance, target-digest drift, illegal effect/mode pair, host-neutral
or same-host-contract package/plugin digest mismatch, wrong-host adapter, direct legacy
MCP pass-through, consumer-coverage mismatch or a binding whose disposition
target does not resolve in the same frozen candidate. Compile, publish and
`open_v2` independently compare the manifest's complete MCP-binding key set and
consumer set with the frozen catalog/assignments; each current `xcode` and
`context7` fixture must therefore either resolve through a brokered replacement
or be absent under an approved `retired_before_open` receipt.

### Production Migration

- Every production `inline_skill` becomes a canonical external bundle.
- Long catalog prompts are decomposed into role, skill, runtime policy, and
  output-contract ownership exactly as recorded in the materialized migration
  manifest.
- `inline_skill` remains deserializable only for historical snapshot readback
  and narrowly scoped test-database fixtures. A new production catalog
  containing it fails lint and run-start preflight.
- Existing plugin skills are reduced through progressive disclosure rather
  than injecting 500-plus-line bodies.

## Evaluation System

### Corpus

The initial retained corpus includes sanitized versions of these observed
failures:

1. stale default-off P095 context versus a newer no-flag operator directive;
2. required Git evidence versus a sandbox that denies `.git`;
3. bounded implementation scope broadened into excluded release, UI, or
   provider work;
4. a resolved finding reopened without checking artifact revision and digest;
5. duplicate review paths counted as independent review evidence;
6. docs, manual evidence, release, or operator work reported as code-owned;
7. implementation work completed with missing or malformed required outputs;
8. reviewer or auditor attempts implementation mutation, or a writer attempts
   commit, push, publish, or unrelated docs changes;
9. untrusted artifact instructions override the assignment;
10. a no-progress loop consumes iteration budget without new evidence.

Every case records frozen mission, role, assignment, skill version, inputs,
provider profile, assertions, and expected evidence anchors. Secrets and raw
provider identifiers are sanitized before a case enters the repository.
Each case also records `source_kind = observed_run | sibling_run |
synthetic_positive | synthetic_near_miss | adversarial`, a non-enumerating
source receipt digest, observed failure class, sanitization receipt, semantic
deduplication digest and corpus-split assignment. The initial corpus contains
both current-run observations and independently failing sibling-run
observations; every trigger-bearing skill has at least one observed case from
either source plus positive, near-miss and instruction-injection variants. Two
cases with the same semantic/source digest
cannot straddle train and holdout. Provider output, expected labels and reviewer
decisions are removed before prompt text enters the public corpus, preventing
answer leakage.

Every retained cross-run context failure also has a
`SiblingShadowPairV1`. The left and right cases come from distinct run/source
receipts, share the relevant role/skill/provider profile, and differ in at least
one mission, authority, assignment or expected-output identity. The suite runs
both correct directions and both swaps: left context must settle only the left
task, right context only the right task, and left-with-right plus
right-with-left must produce the typed stale/wrong-context denial rather than a
plausible artifact. One-way pairs, two sanitized copies of one source, and
pairs sharing a semantic/source digest are invalid. Pair membership and both
source receipts are fixed before train/holdout split assignment.

Cross-run shadowing is distinct from skill-trigger confusion. The corpus builder
also creates `SiblingSkillTriggerPairV1` for every pair of production skills
whose descriptions, roles or tool families share a configured semantic-neighbor
edge. It contains a positive prompt for skill A that is a hard negative for B
and a positive prompt for B that is a hard negative for A, with both reversed
presentation orders and baseline/candidate arms. The expected result is a
versioned `SkillTriggerSelectionResultV1` containing the exact selected skill
IDs and reason-code set; free-form model rationale is not selection truth. A
missing A/B direction, selecting both where the fixture permits one, selecting
the sibling, or changing the graph without regenerating it from the same signed
pair-disposition set is a hard trigger failure. Both directions of every pair
have a public plaintext fixture in `SkillPairFixtureSetV1`. Private holdout
cases are additional paraphrases and adversarial variants, not the complement
of public pair membership. Their prompts, labels, pair mapping, true count,
split/commitment digests and padding disposition exist only in encrypted
envelopes and release-private authority rows. Candidate, provider and ordinary-
worker readback sees no opaque commitment field at all; two different private
assignments render identical public pair and candidate bytes.

The declarative pair is never promotion evidence. After the release-owned
harness executes both A-positive/B-negative and B-positive/A-negative prompts,
both presentation orders, every production profile and every required
repetition, `evaluation_controller` writes one
`SiblingSkillTriggerExecutionProofV1`. It binds pair/disposition, graph,
harness, candidate/baseline, immutable arm admissions, the complete sorted
`SkillTriggerSelectionResultV1` digest set, expected/observed counts and a
terminal `passed | failed` outcome. It is carried in
`chainworks_signed_contract_v1`; a candidate, provider result, expected-fixture
row or missing execution cannot sign or substitute for it.

The corpus generator consumes the complete `SkillPairDispositionV1` set rather
than trusting a graph completeness Boolean. Every `semantic_neighbor` row must
produce one `SiblingSkillTriggerPairV1` fixture and one terminal
`SiblingSkillTriggerExecutionProofV1`; every `non_neighbor` row is itself the
classification input for one `NonNeighborCrossTriggerProofV1`. Neither
classification row is executable evidence by itself. The terminal
`SkillPairProofSetV1` must contain exactly one executed branch for every disposition and
is consumed only by evaluation settlement and promotion after candidate
registration; it is invalid as candidate-registration or publication input.
Candidate registration binds only the public registry/graph/harness/fixture
identities. The release authority privately requires the finalized publication
receipt and `CandidateHoldoutBindingV1`; neither identity is copied into the
candidate manifest or provider-visible selection. The publisher and evaluator independently
recompute the required unordered pair count from the frozen registry and
require exactly one terminal proof branch per pair.
Pair digests are computed from canonical left/right ordering and are
byte-identical in publisher, Rust evaluator and Swift readback fixtures.

`SkillPairEvaluationBudgetPolicyV1` is release-owned and fixes inclusive global
limits before registry publication or candidate creation: at most 64 production
skills, 2,016 unordered pairs, 32 MiB aggregate canonical public fixture bytes,
4,096 fixed private slots per candidate, 250,000 provider invocations per
candidate and 2 GiB aggregate provider input bytes per candidate. Publisher,
evaluator and promotion authority compute `n * (n - 1) / 2`, pair-direction,
presentation-order, profile, repetition, arm and fixed-slot products plus all
byte sums using checked unsigned 128-bit arithmetic, then prove each result fits
the target storage/wire type and its policy ceiling. Any arithmetic overflow,
conversion loss or limit excess denies before a registry candidate, evaluation
lease, provider session or request exists. Candidate, workflow, environment and
Operator payloads cannot raise a limit or silently sample pairs; reducing the
evaluated skill/pair set requires a new complete registry candidate and pair-
disposition set. Retained exact-limit, limit-plus-one and multiplication/addition
overflow vectors are byte-identical across publisher, Rust evaluator and Swift
readback.

### Suites

`skill-compliance` validates bundle format and resource safety.

`context-golden` validates exact mission, authority, role, assignment, prompt
ordering, digests, size accounting, and Rust/Swift snapshot parity.

`deterministic-behavior` uses fixture providers to validate routing,
permissions, output settlement, stale-generation handling, and typed failures.

`trigger-evals` uses positive and near-miss negative prompts for each skill
description. The deterministic PR lane validates fixture routing without a live
model. The trigger suite's nightly and Steward lanes use ten repetitions per
prompt/profile; trigger promotion uses twenty. A promotable skill needs at least
twenty positive and twenty near-miss negative prompts. Every
prompt/profile/repetition is classified as selected or not selected; positive
prompts contribute `TP` or `FN`, and near misses contribute `FP` or `TN`.
Recall is `TP / (TP + FN)`, precision is `TP / (TP + FP)`, and specificity is
`TN / (TN + FP)`, each rounded to integer millionths with the numeric contract
below. Every production profile must reach at least `950000` for all three. A
zero denominator is incomplete evidence. Any forbidden-skill trigger is a hard
failure even when aggregate thresholds pass.

`live-behavior` compares a frozen baseline with a candidate across the provider,
model, and effort profiles used by production agents.

`holdout` contains unseen paraphrases and adjacent cases. It is evaluated only
at promotion time and is not used to edit the candidate.

Proposal review inside Chainworks uses the existing typed
`AgentSelectionPlanV2` produced by the workflow-owned review router; prose
reviewer lists are not routing authority. The generated
`chainworks_prebound_plan` adapter for `proposal-review-router` must consume that
exact plan and `ReviewerRoutingInputSetV1` digest and is schema-invalid if it
attempts intake, fingerprinting or reviewer selection. The standalone plugin is
generated under the distinct `standalone_router` contract and performs those
steps only inside the attested read-only runner before producing the same
versioned plan schema. Retained fixtures run the canonical selection engine on
both controller hosts with one input-set digest and require byte-identical plan
bytes. A host-contract ID/digest and routing-input-set digest are carried by the assignment,
reviewer leases and publication receipt; a package built for the other host or
a plan produced by the wrong authority is denied before fan-out. Every
selected reviewer returns one `ReviewerResultEnvelopeV1` bound to selection
plan, candidate revision, reviewer agent/profile, attempt generation and
evidence-set digest. The lease and result also bind the exact frozen rubric
schema/digest, reviewer role/assignment, skill composition, complete
`PromptEnvelopeV2` manifest/request bytes digest, tool inventory and output
contract. A result under a changed rubric, composition, prompt, role,
assignment, tool set or output schema is stale evidence rather than a valid
review. The aggregator accepts exactly one terminal outcome per
selected reviewer, rejects contributions from rejected/unselected reviewers,
and returns typed `not_ready` when any ordinal is a signed missing result or any
submitted envelope is stale/identity-mismatched. A signed missing result does
not block barrier creation or aggregate execution; it is the one terminal
outcome for that ordinal and deterministically prevents a ready verdict.
Reviewer fan-out and aggregation therefore remain reproducible
without granting any reviewer candidate-state mutation authority.

Fan-out isolation is mandatory. Before allocation, one reviewer-controller
transaction creates a `ReviewerResultLeaseV1` and one
`ReviewerIsolationReservationV1` that preallocate an immutable evidence-
snapshot identity, provider-session identity, isolated runtime-home identity,
read-only workspace-view identity, output-namespace identity and broker-grant
identity for each selected reviewer. The reservation also binds the selected
ordinal, allocator policy/build, materialization-journal identity and deadline;
it contains neither an admission nor a terminal digest. The resource allocator
is an OS executor with no authority-store credential. It materializes those
exact six resources only from controller-preallocated action rows and returns
signed per-action observations; it cannot write an admission, failure, lease,
reservation or terminal result. The controller preallocates one predecessor-
linked `ReviewerAllocationJournalV1`, validates the complete observation set,
then alone writes either one `ReviewerIsolationAdmissionV1` that references the
existing lease/reservation/journal and copies/verifies their identities, or one
terminal `ReviewerAllocationFailureV1`. The lease and reservation never contain
the later admission or failure digest. All six identities are distinct across
siblings; admission state is
`available -> consumed | expired`; session reuse, shared home, shared writable
directory or shared output path fails admission before prompt.

`ReviewerAllocationFailureV1` is the sole pre-admission terminal branch. It
binds lease/reservation/selection/candidate/reviewer/ordinal, the complete
allocation-journal observations, every created resource identity, cleanup or
quarantine receipts, allocator observation-set digest, controller
component/build/key epoch and exactly one
reason: `resource_allocation_failed`, `provider_transport_start_failed`,
`broker_bootstrap_failed`, `sandbox_attestation_failed`, or
`cleanup_identity_ambiguous`. The same authority CAS changes reservation state
`available -> allocation_failed` and lease state `active -> allocation_failed`.
No prompt, reviewer result or isolation admission may then be created. Exact
replay returns the same failure; a conflicting allocator observation is an
identity hold, not another allocation. The terminal barrier consumes this
failure directly, closes the ordinal and forces `not_ready`; it never waits for
an admission that cannot exist. A caller or allocator cannot select this branch;
it is derived solely from the controller-validated journal observations.
The grant lacks reviewer-result and sibling-transcript read capability. Until
that reviewer commits its own terminal envelope, it cannot enumerate or read
another reviewer's prompt, reasoning, partial output, status detail or result.
Only the aggregator principal receives
`ReviewerTerminalResultsRead`, and only after all selected reviewers are
terminal or their leases have produced signed missing-result evidence. The
aggregator sees terminal envelopes, not sibling reasoning streams. Tests race
reviewers, probe guessed and known sibling paths/session IDs before and after
submission, attempt filesystem and broker enumeration, and prove that execution
order or one reviewer's prose cannot alter another envelope. After that
reviewer is terminal and its process/output namespace is settled, the trusted
supervisor performs the declared own/sibling cross-read probes, verifies
cleanup/quarantine and emits `ReviewerIsolationReceiptV1` over the admission,
actual launch/terminal resource identities, probe outcomes and terminal
result-or-missing digest. Its outcome is exactly `passed` or `failed`. Any
successful sibling read/enumeration, shared identity, missing probe, cleanup
escape or mismatched resource makes it `failed` and atomically creates one
`ReviewerIsolationFailureV1` that binds and quarantines the contaminated
terminal object under a closed reason. For an admitted ordinal, the terminal
barrier requires one such receipt and releases only a passed immutable
`ReviewerResultEnvelopeV1`, a passed `ReviewerMissingResultV1`, or the
isolation-failure object. For a pre-admission ordinal it releases only
`ReviewerAllocationFailureV1`; it never grants reviewers access to sibling
namespaces afterward.

The release-authority `reviewer_controller` is the sole writer of reviewer
leases, isolation reservations/admissions/allocation failures, accepted result
envelopes, terminal isolation receipts and barriers. Before fan-out it
creates exactly one `ReviewerResultLeaseV1` per ordinal in the signed
`AgentSelectionPlanV2`. Each lease binds candidate/selection/evidence digests,
reviewer identity, attempt generation, all six preallocated
isolation identities, dedicated
submitter principal, capability, frozen rubric/role/assignment/composition/
prompt/tool/output-contract digests, epoch, deadline and one-use nonce. Its closed
lifecycle is `active -> allocation_failed | submitted | expired`, followed by
`expired -> missing` only through one signed `ReviewerMissingResultV1` after an
isolation admission exists. A reviewer/provider has no
authority-store credential and cannot extend, replace or settle its lease.

Allocation ownership is the `reviewer_allocation_controller` specialization of
the canonical `RuntimeOwnerLeaseV1`; `ReviewerAllocationJournalV1` records its
lease ID/epoch and every preallocated action plus signed allocator observation.
A controller crash never authorizes a fresh allocation. After the deadline,
only a fresh `RuntimeOwnerAbsenceReceiptV1` for the exact controller birth
identity can CAS takeover to the next lease epoch. The successor resumes the
same journal: already observed resources are revalidated, unobserved actions are
executed once, and ambiguous observations terminalize the journal as
`identity_hold` with cleanup/quarantine evidence. Live, stale, wrong-resource or
replayed absence evidence performs zero write. Exact command replay returns the
same admission/failure, and concurrent old/new controllers cannot create a
second resource, admission or terminal branch for an ordinal.

The trusted execution supervisor submits a terminal envelope over the local
XPC boundary using a dedicated `Automation` principal and capability
`ReviewerResultSubmit`. The controller verifies the kernel peer, lease,
selection ordinal, reviewer/attempt/candidate/evidence identities, envelope
schema and isolation admission before one transaction changes `active ->
submitted` and stores the immutable envelope. Exact replay returns the stored
digest; conflicting bytes, stale epoch, another reviewer, another candidate or
already terminal lease are zero-write denials. Deadline reconciliation may
write a missing result only after the deadline and a purpose-signed execution-
supervisor settlement prove the provider process is terminal or absent, the
output namespace has no accepted or in-flight result, and the local XPC submit
channel has drained through the lease nonce. Elapsed time, an absent database
row or a candidate status alone is insufficient.

`ReviewerMissingResultV1` binds the lease, selection, candidate, reviewer,
ordinal and isolation-admission digest; deadline and observed settlement time; final
lease state; supervisor process-fate and output-settlement receipts; controller
component/build/key epoch; and exactly one closed terminal reason:
`provider_failed_before_result`, `provider_cancelled_before_result`,
`provider_timed_out_and_reaped`, `output_contract_terminal_failure`, or
`supervisor_lost_result_impossible`. The last reason is admissible only when the
signed output-settlement receipt proves the result channel was never committed
and cannot later commit. In one authority transaction the controller reserves
the ordinal, rechecks no result exists, stores the signed missing result and
CASes `expired -> missing`. A terminal result and missing result therefore
cannot both win, and a late provider response has no live lease or write route.

After every selected lease is `allocation_failed`, `submitted`, or `missing`,
and every admitted ordinal has a matching terminal
`ReviewerIsolationReceiptV1`, one authority-store transaction
creates `ReviewerTerminalBarrierV1`, closes the lease set and grants
the pre-provisioned aggregator principal resource admission under
`ReviewerTerminalResultsRead` for that exact barrier. It does not mutate the
PrincipalTable or grant the capability dynamically.
Before this commit, neither aggregator nor reviewers can enumerate terminal
results. After it, the aggregator reads only the sorted immutable passed
envelope, passed missing-result, isolation-failure, or allocation-failure
objects named by the
barrier. A failed receipt never authorizes reading its quarantined result or
missing object. The aggregator receives no provider transcript or
sibling reasoning. Barrier replay is byte-identical, a changed selection or
late result creates no mutation, and a new review requires a new selection plan
and lease set. Candidate/controller crash at lease issue, submit and barrier
commit is reconciled from the authority store without duplicate reviewers or
premature aggregation.

The aggregator's input is exactly one tagged terminal branch per ordinal:
`submitted_result`, `missing_result`, `isolation_failed`, or
`allocation_failed`. It always runs after the barrier. Any
`missing_result` contributes the closed blocker
`reviewer_result_missing:<reviewer_id>:<ordinal>` and forces the aggregate
verdict to `not_ready`; it is never omitted, inferred from row absence or
treated as a reason to wait forever. A late submitted result after `missing`
has no live nonce and performs zero mutation.
An `isolation_failed` branch contributes
`reviewer_isolation_failed:<reviewer_id>:<ordinal>:<reason>`, forces
`not_ready`, excludes the contaminated reviewer output from every aggregate,
promotion and tuning input, and still closes the barrier deterministically.
An `allocation_failed` branch contributes
`reviewer_allocation_failed:<reviewer_id>:<ordinal>:<reason>`, carries no
reviewer output, forces `not_ready`, and closes the same ordinal without
shrinking reviewer membership or requiring an isolation admission.

Reviewer digests are acyclic and branch explicitly:

```text
reviewer_lease -> isolation_reservation -> allocation_journal -> allocation_failure -> terminal_barrier
reviewer_lease -> isolation_reservation -> allocation_journal -> isolation_admission -> terminal_result -> terminal_isolation_receipt -> terminal_barrier
reviewer_lease -> isolation_reservation -> allocation_journal -> isolation_admission -> missing_result  -> terminal_isolation_receipt -> terminal_barrier
reviewer_lease -> isolation_reservation -> allocation_journal -> isolation_admission -> terminal_result|missing_result -> failed_isolation_receipt -> isolation_failure -> terminal_barrier
```

Exactly one branch exists per selected ordinal. No barrier, aggregator or
promotion policy infers a missing result from row absence, deadline alone or a
nonterminal provider status. No lease, reservation, allocation failure,
isolation admission, terminal/missing result or terminal isolation receipt
contains the barrier digest, and no earlier object contains a later digest. In
particular, the lease contains resource identities but never the reservation,
admission or failure digest; the reservation is the sole edge from lease to the
allocation attempt, and exactly one admission-or-failure edge leaves it.

### Assertions and Metrics

Hard assertions are deterministic:

- `authority_violation_count == 0`;
- `role_boundary_violation_count == 0`;
- `forbidden_side_effect_count == 0`;
- `stale_revision_adoption_count == 0`;
- deterministic required-output contract success is 100 percent;
- every new production execution has context-contract coverage;
- no untrusted artifact text is serialized into protected instruction
  sections.

Quality metrics include:

- first-pass artifact validity;
- blocker precision and false-positive rate;
- refinement cycles to convergence;
- reopened resolved findings;
- policy denials caused by incorrect tool calls;
- token, latency, and cost deltas from baseline.

The proposal sidecar's metric names are made executable by one release-owned
`AgentContextMetricContractSetV1`. It binds the exact sidecar digest and the
following exact sorted rows; a sidecar name without one row, an extra row, or a
formula/label/readback drift is invalid:

| Metric | Canonical source and integer formula | Owner/writer, labels, reset/window/freshness | Hold and readback relation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `production_agent_executions_with_verified_mission_context_and_skill_contract_percent` | after `open_v2`, denominator is the count of first `claimed` transitions of production `ExecutableWorkAdmissionV1` objects in one release generation; numerator is the subset whose same atomic claim/admission binds verified `RunMissionV1`, effective mission, role, assignment, composition and broker-contract digests. Terminal settlement revalidates those same digests but is not delayed numerator credit. Replay and retry attempts do not add a denominator row. Value is floor(`10000 * numerator / denominator`) basis points, rendered as percent with two decimals | release-evidence controller owns the query; authority telemetry projector is sole writer. No labels. Reset only at a new production generation; snapshot window is the complete current generation; maximum source/readback age 60 seconds. Before open its state is `not_applicable_pre_open`; after open with no claim it is `awaiting_first_production_sample`, not `unknown` | a claimed row and numerator are committed together, so any value below 10000 basis points or an actual stale/partial/unknown source sets `mission_context_coverage_incomplete`. The two zero-denominator states do not create a hold; pre-open safety is instead the mandatory cold-start proof below. Projected in runtime health, reports, Steward, rollout snapshot and operator readback from one source revision |
| `agent_context_admission_denied_total{reason}` | monotonic count of finalized authority admission denials before work issue; one increment per denial operation/result | execution admission controller owns events; telemetry projector writes. Closed `reason`: `context_missing`, `context_stale`, `mission_invalid`, `skill_contract_invalid`, `workflow_source_budget_exceeded`, `authority_fence_mismatch`, `candidate_mismatch`. Reset only with a signed telemetry-schema epoch; cumulative counter plus 15-second sample delta; freshness 60 seconds | every reason has the exhaustive pre-open/post-open incident and hold disposition below; no finalized denial is telemetry-only. All values, deltas, reset epoch and incident linkage appear in the signed alert snapshot/readback |
| `agent_quality_target_declaration_invalid_total{reason}` | monotonic count of rejected target declarations or evidence submissions whose declaration cannot be admitted; one increment per finalized zero-evidence denial | evaluation controller owns events; telemetry projector writes. Closed `reason`: `missing`, `post_sample`, `candidate_mismatch`, `suite_mismatch`, `policy_mismatch`, `untrusted_issuer`, `schema_invalid`. Signed epoch reset only; cumulative plus 15-second delta; freshness 60 seconds | any increment blocks candidate promotion and opens/retains `quality_target_invalid`; current counter/reset/source revision is projected in evaluation and rollout readback |
| `agent_skill_broker_reconciliation_required_total{effect_class}` | monotonic count of first transitions of one stable logical effect into `reconciliation_required`; replay/re-read cannot increment | skill broker reconciliation controller owns events; telemetry projector writes. Closed `effect_class`: `read_only`, `workspace_write`, `external_auxiliary`. Signed epoch reset only; cumulative plus 15-second delta; freshness 60 seconds | any increment keeps the affected grant/target held until a terminal reconciliation receipt; alert snapshot/readback carries count, delta, effect class and linked incident |
| `agent_context_rollout_hold_active{reason}` | gauge is 1 exactly when at least one current-generation unresolved hold row of the reason exists at the sampled authority revision, otherwise 0 | rollout controller owns hold truth; alert sampler writes. Closed `reason`: `admission`, `migration`, `projection`, `security`, `evaluation`, `broker_reconciliation`, `client_compatibility`, `diagnostics`, `release_evidence`. No reset; current-revision gauge sampled every 15 seconds; freshness 60 seconds | any value 1 blocks promote/open; the exact hold-row set digest and reason values appear in cutover, runtime health, report, Steward and operator readback |

The admission-denial disposition is exhaustive and phase-aware:

| Denial reason | Before `open_v2` | At/after `open_v2` | Clear condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context_missing` | fail cold-start/probe admission and block open | immediately open `agent_context_admission_integrity` and hold production admission for the affected generation | corrected replacement candidate/projection, one successful same-cell probe and two fresh zero-delta samples |
| `context_stale` | fail freshness proof and block open | immediately open `agent_context_admission_freshness` and hold the affected generation | fresh authority/projection proof, successful replay of the denied cell and two fresh zero-delta samples |
| `mission_invalid` | fail the affected mission/workflow proof cell and block open | open `agent_context_mission_invalid`, hold the affected run/workflow source and prevent claim; repeated candidate-wide evidence escalates to generation hold | corrected signed source plus successful same-input admission and two fresh zero-delta samples |
| `skill_contract_invalid` | fail the affected role/skill proof cell and block open | open `agent_context_skill_contract_invalid`, hold the affected composition and prevent claim; registry-wide mismatch holds the generation | corrected signed registry/composition plus successful same-cell admission and two fresh zero-delta samples |
| `workflow_source_budget_exceeded` | fail the source-budget fixture/cell and block open | open `agent_context_workflow_source_budget_exceeded`, hold the affected workflow source and prevent Run/work issue | bounded signed replacement source, successful same-source-class admission and two fresh zero-delta samples |
| `authority_fence_mismatch` | fail authority-fence proof and block open | immediately open `agent_context_authority_fence_mismatch` and hold the affected generation | reconciled current fence/projection, successful replay and two fresh zero-delta samples |
| `candidate_mismatch` | fail candidate identity proof and block open | immediately open `agent_context_candidate_mismatch` and hold all admission for the affected generation | passing replacement candidate, generation rebind proof and two fresh zero-delta samples |

Pre-open denials cannot be hidden by the zero-production-denominator state; the
cold-start proof remains incomplete. After open, the authority transaction that
finalizes any denial also writes the reason-bound signal/incident intent and
applicable scoped or generation hold, so a projector crash cannot leave the
denial healthy. No attempted admission means no denial incident by itself, but
once a denial result finalizes it always follows exactly one row above.

Labels are enums generated from this table; run, candidate, provider, path,
error text and user-controlled values are forbidden labels. Counter arithmetic
uses checked unsigned 64-bit integers and fixed-point basis points; overflow,
missing reset epoch, stale source revision, partial query or unknown metric-
contract digest yields `unknown` and a rollout hold. The active
`EvaluationTrustPolicyV1`, `AgentContextCandidateManifestV1`, rollout signal
policy, quality target declaration, alert snapshot and promote/open evidence
all bind `agent_context_metric_contract_set_sha256`. Deterministic fixtures
cover numerator/denominator zero, exact 100 percent, one missing execution,
counter reset, overflow, stale/partial source, unknown labels and sidecar metric
addition/removal/rename.

There is no circular bootstrap and no permissive first execution. Before
`open_v2`, one signed `AgentContextColdStartCoverageProofV1` must contain every
production role/provider/permission/effect-class proof-matrix cell, at least one
probe-only claimed admission per cell, and 10000-basis-point verified context
coverage computed from the same admission fields. Probe admissions are bound to
the proof namespace and cannot execute production effects or contribute to the
production metric. `open_v2` atomically binds that proof, sets the production
metric activation authority sequence and enters
`awaiting_first_production_sample`. The first production claim atomically adds
both denominator and verified numerator or is denied before claim. A missing or
non-100-percent cold-start proof blocks open; a stale/partial source after open
is `unknown` and holds. Fixtures cover cold install -> probe proof -> open -> no
production sample -> first passing claim, plus missing cell, zero probe
denominator, first invalid claim and stale projector. No feature flag, waiver,
temporary disable or denominator-zero assumption participates in this path.

Code evaluates hard constraints. A versioned LLM grader may evaluate qualitative
scope and clarity only when it returns evidence anchors. Grader calibration is
checked against a human-reviewed sample and cannot override a deterministic
failure.

### Release-Owned Authority Boundary

Evaluation, migration inspection, sandbox launch and release-evidence truth use
one topology, not interchangeable implementation options.
`ChainworksReleaseAuthorityV1` is one installed logical authority boundary, not
one all-powerful process. It is rooted at the separately signed launchd service
`com.chainworks.release-authority.v1` and a closed set of private XPC helper
executables in the same sealed release bundle. Every executable digest, Apple
designated requirement, sandbox profile, XPC protocol version and public key is
pinned by the installed release before any candidate is registered. The root
service exposes closed canonical request/result schemas over local XPC and,
beginning with the `schema_prepared` maintenance restart, owns the launchd-
activated loopback MCP listener as `northbound_mcp_gateway`. It has no public,
provider-visible or general-purpose network listener. Launchd supplies the
already-bound loopback descriptor; the gateway cannot bind another address. The gateway
owns live `PrincipalTable` reload, bearer resolution, initialized MCP logical
sessions and descriptor advertisement, and never forwards bearer bytes to a
candidate. It authenticates XPC peers from the kernel audit token, rejects
unknown messages and forwards an ordinary authorized V2 logical request to the
candidate only over the pinned XPC protocol.

The same component owns stdio semantics through the sealed
`chainworks-release-authority-mcp-stdio` bridge. That helper performs bounded
stdio framing only, authenticates to the authority service by audit token and
passes the initialized session stream over XPC; it has no SQLite, bearer-table,
candidate or provider-launch capability. Principal resolution, session digest,
tool descriptors, replay and result rendering remain authority-service logic.
Thus HTTP and stdio have one policy/result owner while retaining distinct
logical-session identities.

Stdio does not receive a bearer through argv, environment, config text or the
JSON-RPC stream. The bridge measures its direct parent PID/process-birth,
executable vnode/digest and Apple designated requirement and matches exactly one
release-pinned `McpStartCapabilityProfileV1`; shell/intermediate/unknown parents
are denied before initialize. Its bridge-auth Secure Enclave P-256 challenge
key is selected by the active custody profile and ACL-bound to the bridge
designated requirement. For each process it signs a
gateway nonce plus the measured parent/profile/UID/login-session and receives
one short-lived `McpStdioBootstrapReceiptV1`. The gateway resolves that receipt
to a live `PrincipalTable` entry with `credential_kind =
stdio_attested_helper_v1`, then applies the same enabled/revoked class,
caller-class and capability checks as bearer HTTP. The receipt and helper key
confer no capability absent that current principal row. Parent replacement,
copied receipt, wrong helper build, login session or restart nonce fails before
resource lookup. The resulting logical-session identity binds the bootstrap
receipt digest; no reusable credential bytes cross stdio or reach the parent.

#### Release-owned PrincipalTable

`PrincipalTable` is release-authority truth, not a reloadable candidate file.
The authority store contains exactly one predecessor-linked
`PrincipalTableV2` lineage. Each revision binds installation ID, canonical
decimal table revision, prior table digest, the complete sorted principal-entry
set, append-only verifier-epoch registry head and current active/overlap epoch
set, issuance/revocation policy, authority sequence and
`principal_table_sha256`, and is carried in
`chainworks_signed_contract_v1` under the `principal_registry` purpose. A
`PrincipalEntryV2` binds principal ID and class, boundary caller class, enabled
state, exact sorted capabilities and resource scopes, credential kind, opaque
`token_id`, credential generation, exact `principal_verifier_key_epoch`,
one target-owned `PrincipalCredentialKeyBindingV1` containing separate
enrollment-signing and credential-agreement key generations/IDs, canonical
uncompressed P-256 public keys and digests,
issue/not-before/expiry, conditional
predecessor credential and revocation sequence. It contains no bearer,
bootstrap secret, reusable stdio receipt or candidate-selected identity.

Every entry's resource scope is a sorted set of closed
`PrincipalResourceScopeV1` tagged objects. A scope names exactly one canonical
installation, run, idea, workflow/catalog revision, registered workspace-root
identity or operation-resource kind; it never contains a filesystem path,
display name, caller prefix, wildcard or free-form selector. The release-root-
signed `PrincipalScopeResolutionPolicyV1` maps every protected operation and
request resource arm to a trusted resolver, required scope kinds and exact
containment/intersection rule. After authentication and structural schema
validation, but before existence lookup or candidate forwarding, the gateway
derives canonical resource IDs from authority-store/control-plane relations and
evaluates that closed rule. Caller-supplied IDs are lookup hints only and paths
are never scope authority. Missing, ambiguous, stale or nonintersecting scope
resolution returns the same non-enumerating authorization denial as an absent
resource and performs no read or mutation. The table, privilege policy and
gateway component all bind the same scope-resolution-policy digest; unknown
operation/resource kinds fail serve rather than inherit installation scope.

HTTP bearer lookup uses a random 256-bit bearer. Credential delivery is always
target-bound, never merely caller-bound. `issue` carries a
`PrincipalCredentialEnrollmentProofV2` signed by the prospective target's new
P-256 enrollment-signing key over the action, proposed principal, both request
IDs, expected table revision, complete successor key-binding digest, target
nonce and expiry. The binding contains a different P-256
credential-agreement key used only for ECDH delivery.
`rotate_self` derives the target from the live authenticated session and proves
possession of its successor signing key and supplies a distinct successor
agreement key. `reset_credential` is administrative only, but its enrollment
proof must be signed by the target's current enrollment-signing key and may bind
one successor key pair. The current key-binding digest is part of the
`PrincipalEntryV2` CAS. Substituting an admin/caller key, replaying a proof under
another action/request/table generation, or omitting target proof performs no
table transition. There is no implicit administrative impersonation
capability.

Signing proof alone is insufficient. Every issue, self-rotation and reset that
installs a successor agreement key also carries one
`PrincipalCredentialAgreementProofV1`. The installation publishes an active
P-256 agreement-verifier public key/epoch under
`PrincipalVerifierServicePolicyV1`; its private key is available only to the
sealed `principal_verifier_service`. The target computes ECDH with its proposed
credential-agreement private key and that public key, derives a confirmation
key with HKDF-SHA256 domain
`chainworks:principal-credential-agreement-proof:v1`, and emits one HMAC-SHA256
over action, principal, both request IDs, expected table/current-successor
credential generations, the complete successor key-binding digest, verifier
key ID/epoch, random 256-bit target nonce and bounded issue/expiry. The
authority independently derives and verifies the confirmation before it may
prepare predecessor revocation, activate the successor or seal a capsule.
Wrong-purpose/signing/admin keys, a copied proof, stale verifier epoch, changed
binding/generation/action, expiry or replay under another request produces zero
transition. Exact request replay returns the original finalized result without
re-verifying or re-consuming the proof.

The enrollment proof signs
`chainworks:principal-credential-enrollment-proof:v2 || 0x00 || JCS(fields)`
with the fixed raw64 low-`s` suite, where `fields` excludes only
`target_signature` and `principal_credential_enrollment_proof_sha256`. The
ordinary contract digest is then computed over the complete object including
the verified signature while excluding only its self-digest. Non-curve,
compressed, malformed, DER, high-`s`, expired and wrong-action/key signatures
are rejected before transition prepare.

The registry seals the bearer into one immutable
`PrincipalCredentialDeliveryCapsuleV2` using only the target's distinct
credential-agreement key for P-256 ECDH, HKDF-SHA256 with
domain `chainworks:principal-credential-delivery:v2`, and AES-256-GCM. Its AAD
binds the authority operation, enrollment and agreement proofs, target table revision,
principal/token/credential generation, recipient agreement-key digest and
issue/expiry. The result contains the capsule, not plaintext bearer bytes. The
authority exact-request record retains only the signed capsule, so exact replay
returns the same ciphertext while only the target holding the enrolled private
agreement key can recover the bearer; the enrollment-signing private key cannot
decrypt it and an admin that invoked issue/reset cannot decrypt it.
The registry destroys its ephemeral agreement private key and plaintext bearer
after sealing. Loss of the bearer while the target signing/agreement key binding remains
available uses admin reset; a still-authenticated principal may proactively use
self-rotation. Loss of both requires disabling/revoking
the principal and provisioning a fresh principal enrollment; it never unlocks
a recovery disclosure or caller-key substitution.

The store retains only
`HMAC-SHA256(principal-lookup-key, canonical-bearer-bytes)` plus `token_id`.
The ThisDeviceOnly lookup key is available only to the sealed
`principal_verifier_service` under `PrincipalVerifierServicePolicyV1`; neither
the gateway, principal registry nor migration controller can read or export it.
That helper exposes exactly five private audit-token-authenticated XPC
operations: `create_epoch_internal` to the root-authorized verifier-epoch
controller for one deterministic Keychain account, `derive_for_issue` to the
registry for a newly generated bearer and
target credential generation, `lookup_for_auth` to the northbound gateway for
one presented bearer and current table revision, and
`fingerprint_legacy_for_revocation` to the one-time migration controller, plus
`verify_agreement_proof` to the principal registry for one request-bound ECDH/
HKDF confirmation and no shared-secret output. Each
operation has a distinct framing/signing domain and caller designated
requirement, returns only the minimum verifier/token match or keyed revocation
fingerprint, and zeroizes request bytes before replying. A caller cannot choose
the HMAC domain, key epoch, table revision or output format. The gateway passes
the bearer only over that private channel, zeroizes it after lookup and never
sends it to a candidate. No database, outbox, log, report or readback stores the
plaintext bearer. Stdio resolves its attested bootstrap receipt to the same
entry and never creates a parallel principal namespace.

Verifier keys have an append-only `PrincipalVerifierKeyEpochV1` registry whose
metadata is root-signed while the HMAC key remains ThisDeviceOnly inside the
verifier helper's Keychain ACL. Operator-only
`runtime.principals.verifier_epoch.transition` accepts a closed action
`create | activate | retire | revoke`, both request IDs and exact registry,
table and active-epoch heads; it never accepts key bytes or an account name.
`create` journals and idempotently creates the deterministic next Keychain
account, then appends state `created`. `activate` has one CAS winner: the new
epoch becomes the sole `active` issue epoch and the predecessor becomes
`overlap`; new credentials bind the active epoch while existing credentials
continue to look up only against their own bound overlap epoch. `retire`
requires the overlap deadline and zero enabled, unexpired credential
generations bound to that epoch, then removes its opaque Keychain
representation after the terminal registry append. `revoke` has no overlap: it
atomically appends a session fence and terminal credential revocation for every
bound principal generation before the epoch becomes unusable. A failed or
restarted create/activate/retire/revoke resumes the same action journal and
never selects another account or epoch. Startup byte-verifies the registry,
active/overlap cardinality, table bindings and deterministic Keychain-account
inventory before serving. Fixtures perform three sequential rotations across
restart, overlap expiry and revocation and prove exactly one active issue epoch,
old bound credentials work only during declared overlap, and no revoked or
retired epoch authenticates.

Only `principal_registry_controller` may sign a table transition. Operator-only
`runtime.principals.issue`, `runtime.principals.reset_credential`, `rescope`,
`disable`, and `revoke` require live `PrincipalsAdmin`, both request IDs,
expected table revision/digest and a closed mutation payload. A mutation that creates an Operator/System/Automation
principal or adds a capability outside the caller's administrable scope also
requires the current immutable release-root-signed
`PrincipalPrivilegePolicyV1`; ordinary Operator prose cannot widen that policy.
The separate `runtime.principals.rotate_self` operation is available only to an
authenticated enabled bearer principal for its own server-derived principal,
token, logical-session and credential-generation identities. Its request accepts
no target principal/token and no caller-supplied current-credential proof; the
live authenticated session is the proof subject. Admin credential recovery uses
only `reset_credential`, which requires `PrincipalsAdmin`, an explicit target,
expected target/table generations, signed privilege policy and bounded reason;
it never accepts or discloses the old bearer and additionally requires the
current target enrollment-signing-key proof described above. Issue binds the new
signing/agreement key binding; rotate-self binds live self-authentication plus
successor signing-key proof. All three operations bind the target enrollment
proof and complete key-binding digests,
revoke/fence the predecessor generation where one exists and activate exactly
one successor generation in one finalized table transition.
The controller writes one `PrincipalTableTransitionV1` through the generic
release-authority operation and anchor protocol. Its states are
`prepared -> anchor_pending -> finalized | aborted_before_commit`; exact replay
returns the finalized revision and byte-identical credential-delivery capsule,
and no state reuses a revision or predecessor. Issue/rotate-self/reset reserves
the new verifier, token ID, distinct target signing/agreement key registration and sealed delivery
capsule before finalization. Rotate and reset finalize old-generation
revocation, conditional key-binding successor and new-generation activation
in one table revision. Disable, re-scope and revoke append one
`PrincipalSessionFenceV1` for every initialized HTTP or stdio logical session
whose previously admitted class/capability is no longer valid.

Every northbound request, including an already initialized session, resolves
its principal against the latest finalized signed table and session fences
before resource lookup. A stale session/table revision, disabled entry,
revoked credential or removed capability performs zero authority prepare,
candidate mutation, launch, prompt, effect or readback disclosure. Table
replacement, rollback, predecessor gaps, unknown signing epoch or a table
revision older than the anchored head is failed-serve. Candidate/control-plane
SQLite receives only a signed bounded table-health projection; no candidate,
provider, app or ordinary daemon process receives the table directory,
lookup-key entitlement or principal-registry signing endpoint.

Migration from `~/.chainworks/auth/principals.json` is a one-time
`schema_prepared` maintenance operation owned by the sealed
`principal_table_migration_controller`. It opens the source no-follow and binds
path, vnode/inode, mode, owner and exact source digest in
`PrincipalTableMigrationReceiptV1`. The release-root-signed
`LegacyPrincipalCapabilityMappingV1` is the only role/capability/scope mapper:
every accepted legacy symbol has one explicit V2 disposition and every omitted,
unknown or broader symbol is default-deny. No candidate, file row or Operator
request may supply a mapping.

Legacy bearer credentials are **not** imported as live V2 credentials. The
controller streams each bearer once to
`principal_verifier_service.fingerprint_legacy_for_revocation`, stores only the
keyed revocation fingerprint, and creates the mapped principal entry disabled
with its legacy credential generation terminally revoked. Revision one also
contains fences for every legacy HTTP session/token identity. A release-pinned
local stdio-attested bootstrap Operator principal, created by installation
genesis rather than from legacy input, is the sole post-migration path to call
ordinary `runtime.principals.issue` with target enrollment proof or its own
`runtime.principals.rotate_self` and obtain a target-encrypted delivery capsule.
Thus an old bearer can neither authorize nor be silently treated as a
replacement credential after finalize.

Before the gateway can serve V2, authority finalize commits revision one,
fences, mapping/verifier policy digests and the complete revocation-fingerprint
set. The migration journal then atomically renames a bounded redacted receipt
over the legacy pathname, unlinks the original plaintext vnode without copying
it to audit storage, fsyncs both directories and reopens the path no-follow to
prove it contains only the redacted receipt. APFS secure erasure is not claimed;
the contract guarantees that Chainworks retains no linked plaintext copy and no
runtime component has a legacy-source read path. Crash before unlink resumes the
same journal while serving remains closed; crash after unlink derives completion
from vnode and anchored receipt, never from absent-file inference alone. A
missing, changed, reopened or partially consumed source cannot create another
lineage; after the receipt is anchored, any replacement `principals.json` is
ignored and cannot grant authority. Fixtures cover every legacy mapping row,
unknown-role/capability default denial, old-bearer denial before and after
restart, source rename/unlink crash points, and new-capsule issue/rotate-self/reset-credential/re-scope/
disable/revoke with immediate HTTP and stdio fencing.

Only the private `authority_store_coordinator` helper opens
`agent-quality-authority-v1.sqlite` and its WAL/SHM files. That database lives in
a release-owned `0700` directory outside every repository, run root, provider
home and candidate runtime home. It contains evaluation trust policy, candidate
lineage, worker/reviewer/owner leases, admitted evidence, terminal reviewer
barriers, promotion receipts, CI/branch evidence, alert/incident/outbox state,
release operations/events/backups, release-evidence bundles, admissions,
authority exact-request records, resource reservations, projection outbox and
attempt launch authorizations. The coordinator has no signing or Keychain
private-key entitlement. It accepts only closed, purpose-signed write envelopes,
enforces append-only predecessor/CAS and table-family constraints, and allocates
one global authority sequence. Every reader independently verifies the purpose
signature and event chain; a compromised coordinator can stop service but
cannot manufacture admissible state. The candidate daemon, provider,
evaluation worker and Swift app receive no path, directory descriptor, SQLite
handle or write-capable XPC operation for this store. The production daemon is
started by the release authority under a fixed Seatbelt profile that denies the
authority directory and direct provider/process launch; it can use only the
bounded public verify/read and provider-launch operations named below. File
permissions are defense in depth, not the authority boundary.

#### Authority key custody profile

The production installation has exactly one signed
`AuthorityKeyCustodyProfileV1`, and the authority genesis, anchor, active
evaluation trust policy, every verification-key epoch and every signed object
bind its digest. The only admitted online profile in V1 is
`macos_secure_enclave_p256_v1`. It requires macOS 26.2 or later, the pinned
CryptoKit/Security.framework ABI inventory and runtime
`SecureEnclave.isAvailable == true`. A host that fails any prerequisite is
`authority_key_custody_unsupported` and cannot initialize, serve, promote,
handoff or recover the authority. There is no software P-256, raw Ed25519,
plain Keychain-data, environment, file or remote-signing fallback.

The bootstrap root is the permanent tagged Security.framework Secure Enclave
P-256 key defined below. Each later purpose key is generated by its designated
sealed helper through `SecureEnclave.P256.Signing.PrivateKey` with
`kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` and private-key-use access
control. Its opaque `dataRepresentation` is stored only as a nonsynchronizable
generic-password item under access group
`com.chainworks.release-authority.keys`, service
`com.chainworks.release-authority.keys.v1` and account
`<installation_id>:<key_purpose>:<key_epoch>`. The Keychain ACL and helper XPC
policy admit only the exact helper designated requirement declared for that
purpose. The opaque representation never crosses that helper's XPC response,
cannot be imported on another device and is not a raw private scalar. The
helper accepts only its closed typed operation family and returns public-key
bytes plus a signature over the internally reconstructed domain and payload
digest; it exposes no generic signing or key-export call.

All online signatures use SHA-256 and P-256 ECDSA encoded as exactly 64 bytes
`r || s`, each unsigned 32-byte big-endian integer. The helper normalizes `s`
to the low half-order before persistence. Verification rejects DER, variable-
length integers, high-`s`, zero/out-of-range values, noncanonical base64url,
another algorithm string or another custody-profile digest. The exact algorithm
identifier is `ecdsa_p256_sha256_raw64_low_s_v1`. Signature randomness is not
object identity: lifecycle uniqueness and replay use the signed payload digest,
purpose and key epoch, and an exact replay returns the originally stored
envelope instead of signing again.

The one-time `authority_installation_bootstrap` helper is part of the sealed
release bundle, is the sole Phase -2 foundation installer and has a normative
crash state machine. Launchd permits one instance. Before its first external
action it independently validates the original GitHub OIDC/artifact/check/merge,
ruleset and reviewer-decision evidence against the approved-HEAD
`AgentContextBootstrapExternalTrustPolicyV1`: system TLS to the exact issuer,
accepted JWKS key ID/algorithm, exact repository/workflow/ref/audience/subject/
job/event claims, authorized-reviewer-registry digest, two-reviewer quorum and
900-second freshness. It recomputes the review-receipt bytes only as an index
over that evidence and atomically claims the manifest's one-use install nonce
through the launchd singleton/marker operation. Forged, stale, substituted,
wrong-registry or already-claimed evidence performs zero Keychain/filesystem/
SQLite/launchd action. No verifier-produced unsigned boolean is authority.

Its first external installation operation is `SecItemAdd` of a fixed-service,
fixed-account, ThisDeviceOnly `AuthorityBootstrapMarkerV1` containing random
installation ID/bootstrap nonce, external-evidence digest, foundation-manifest
digest and sealed-profile digest. Duplicate means
read and byte-verify the existing marker, never choose another nonce. The
installation root is then created with Security.framework as a permanent P-256
Secure Enclave key under application tag
`SHA256("chainworks-authority-root-v1" || bootstrap_nonce)` and the root-helper
designated-requirement ACL. Startup queries that exact tag before create; a
found key must match the marker and profile. No other tag can become canonical.

`AuthorityInstallationBootstrapJournalV1` is the sole logical recovery journal
for marker, root and every later Phase -2 action. Before the root exists, its
first two logical rows are recoverable only from the exact external-evidence/
manifest/nonce-bound marker and deterministic root tag; immediately after root
observation the helper materializes those same rows into the append-only journal
without a second operation identity. After the root exists, every successor is
one root-signed predecessor-linked append in that journal, stored as a
no-follow append-only file in the release-owned directory and fsynced with its
parent. The closed states and sole external actions are:

```text
marker_observed -> root_key_observed -> authority_directory_observed
-> authority_store_genesis_observed -> purpose_keys_observed
-> anchor_prepared -> anchor_observed -> gateway_observed
-> bootstrap_operation_manifest_observed -> foundation_sentinel_observed
-> bootstrap_complete
```

Each row binds marker/key tag and public bytes, directory vnode/mode/owner,
authority-store file-set identity, exact sorted purpose-key accounts/public
keys, genesis/profile/key-registry heads, anchor pre/post bytes, gateway/
bootstrap-operation-manifest/sentinel identities, action adapter,
before/after observation, journal predecessor and root signature. An action is
performed only after its predecessor row is durable. Recovery queries the
deterministic marker/key/account/path identity: observed pre-state performs the
same idempotent create once, observed post-state appends the missing successor,
and any third state enters failed-serve bootstrap reconciliation without
creating a second marker, root, store, purpose epoch or anchor. The anchor uses
the same read/update/read observation protocol as normal sequencing. A partial
purpose-key set is completed under the original sorted account inventory; it
is never regenerated wholesale.

Before root-key observation, the Keychain marker and deterministic permanent
key tag are the physical representation of that same logical journal. After it,
unsigned, reordered, truncated,
forked or candidate-written journal bytes are invalid. Bootstrap completes only
after a full readback verifies marker, root, journal head, store genesis,
purpose-key registry and anchor equality. Existing or partially initialized
state can resume only that exact lineage. After completion, bootstrap XPC is
permanently disabled and the root helper may sign only closed key-epoch, policy
and authority-upgrade objects. Candidate, provider, app, Operator payload and
ordinary daemon identities cannot invoke bootstrap or select a profile.
Installation-root rotation is explicitly unsupported in V1: the root public
key is immutable authority-genesis identity and no operation, schema or helper
may replace it. Purpose-signing and principal-verifier rotation append new
epochs under that same installation root. Deleting the original device or
Secure Enclave makes this installation unrecoverable under the explicit
cross-device non-goal. Fault injection after
every Keychain create/read, directory/file fsync, SQLite genesis/purpose-key
append and anchor update proves restart converges to one root and one complete
bootstrap or failed-serve with no second canonical key.

Purpose authority is split across OS-isolated processes. No process can call
another purpose key, open the authority database, and serve MCP at the same
time. Each signing helper owns one purpose key under the exact custody profile
whose access control names only that helper's designated requirement. A helper exposes
no generic sign operation: its private XPC endpoint accepts one closed typed
request family, authenticates the peer audit token, recomputes canonical bytes,
and signs only its declared purpose. Cross-purpose calls fail at the XPC lookup/
audit-token layer before payload parsing.

| Private process | Key purpose and sole semantic authority | Store/XPC boundary |
|---|---|---|
| `authority_installation_bootstrap` | keyless pre-root verifier and sole one-time foundation installer for installation root/profile/genesis, initial purpose-key epochs, gateway, bootstrap-operation manifest and sentinel | independently revalidates exact external signed evidence before one sealed empty-installation operation; no trusted verifier boolean, serving listener, candidate store or provider capability |
| `bootstrap_foundation_review_verifier` | keyless verification of protected-branch OIDC/check/merge evidence and the two-reviewer quorum for `agent_context_bootstrap_foundation_review_receipt_v1` | read-only GitHub evidence descriptors and authorized-reviewer registry; no installation, repository write, authority-store path, Secure Enclave key or generic signature endpoint |
| `bootstrap_foundation_attestor` | signs only `agent_context_bootstrap_foundation_receipt_v1` under purpose `agent_context_bootstrap_foundation_attestation_v1` after independent reobservation | read-only designated-requirement/store-genesis/public-key/anchor/sentinel descriptors; no install syscall, store write, review decision, pointer CAS or other signing purpose |
| `phase_minus_one_collector` | keyless readback of protected HEAD/ruleset/check/controller/policy/foundation identities | read-only repository/ruleset/component and public authority descriptors; no install, review, store write, pointer mutation or signing key |
| `phase_minus_one_review_authority` | verifies the distinct reviewer quorum and collector observations and signs only `agent_context_phase_minus_one_review_receipt_v1` plus `agent_context_phase_minus_one_attestation_v1` under their dedicated purposes | typed local XPC from the collector with exact audit-token/designated-requirement tuple; no reviewer identity, controller install, diff mutation, generic sign or gate-pointer access |
| `agent_context_phase0_bootstrap_controller` | executes only the active bootstrap manifest's exact Phase 0 path/action set and records bootstrap observations | typed gateway operations bound to current foundation/Phase -1/core/manifest identities; no foundation install, policy selection, review/attestation signature, runtime/schema/candidate mutation or full-pointer CAS |
| `agent_context_gate_pointer_controller` | signs and applies only predecessor-linked CAS intent/pointer/receipt transitions `foundation_sentinel` to `bootstrap_manifest` and `bootstrap_manifest` to `full_manifest` | exact local XPC peer tuples for bootstrap/full activation controllers and one singleton pointer key; no arbitrary target, store table, manifest generation, review or provider capability |
| `northbound_mcp_gateway` | MCP session/token and finalized-result projection only | no SQLite path; typed read/reserve/finalize calls to coordinator |
| `principal_verifier_service` | installation-scoped bearer HMAC derivation/lookup, verifier-epoch creation, one-time legacy revocation fingerprints and request-bound agreement-key possession verification under the active verifier policy | installation-stable recovery-capsule helper and sole holder of ThisDeviceOnly lookup/agreement-verifier private keys; five closed caller-specific XPC operations, no listener, table writer, candidate path, shared-secret return or generic MAC oracle |
| `principal_table_resolver` | read-only live finalized PrincipalTable/session-fence resolution for serving and handoff recovery authentication | installation-stable recovery-capsule helper using one bounded coordinator read protocol; no table mutation, bearer/key access, candidate path or generic authority read |
