| `principal_registry_controller` | signed PrincipalTable issue/rotate-self/reset-credential/re-scope/disable/revoke transitions and session fences | principal-family signing only; no bearer lookup key, listener, candidate writer or arbitrary capability-policy mutation |
| `principal_table_migration_controller` | one-time no-follow legacy principal import into revision one | maintenance-only source descriptor plus principal-family operation; no post-migration source read or serving listener |
| `candidate_lineage_controller` | candidate registration and every candidate-state transition | signs lineage transitions only; coordinator applies signed CAS |
| `evaluation_controller` | evaluation leases, evidence admission and aggregate receipts | signs evaluation rows/intents only; cannot write lineage |
| `ci_release_candidate_dispatcher` | dispatches only the protected reusable `release_candidate_forced` workflow for one authority-approved repository/base/head request | distinct GitHub App installation/credential with bounded Actions write; no Administration write, evidence-signing key, candidate execution or receipt insertion authority |
| `branch_protection_activation_controller` | owns only the required-check ruleset prepare/CAS/observe/conditional pre-adoption restore journal | distinct GitHub App installation and credential with Administration write; no Actions dispatch, evidence-signing key, collector credential, candidate/repository content access or receipt insertion authority |
| `ci_evidence_collector` | verifies protected-base gate manifests, GitHub OIDC/artifact attestations and independently signs complete gate-execution/selection/branch-protection receipts | distinct read-only GitHub App installation and credential with metadata/actions/rules read; no workflow dispatch, Administration write, activation credential, candidate execution, registration or policy selection |
| `release_build_executor` | executes the complete native build-input inventory under the active native-build sandbox policy and writes only `NativeBuildObservationJournalV1` | keyless non-signing/no-Keychain principal; fixed source/toolchain descriptors and output roots, no network, attestation purpose key, production authority access, candidate registration or release signature capability |
| `native_build_confinement_attestor` | independently observes the build executor/process tree, verifies the immutable observation journal and signs only `NativeBuildConfinementReceiptV1` under purpose `native_build_confinement_attestation_v1` | read-only source/toolchain/journal/output descriptors plus kernel observation feed; no process spawn, build-input execution, output write, candidate registration or other signing purpose |
| `native_abi_probe_executor` | executes only the registered disposable ABI fixture matrix and writes `NativeAbiProbeObservationJournalV1` | keyless non-signing fixture-only principal; no production path, Keychain purpose key, receipt insertion, candidate registration or shipping-artifact write |
| `native_abi_probe_attestor` | independently observes the fixture probe, verifies installation/mapping/journal completeness and signs only `NativeAbiProbeReceiptV1` under purpose `native_abi_probe_attestation_v1` | read-only fixture/journal/production-deny observations; no fixture execution, output write, production-state access, candidate registration or other signing purpose |
| `release_transition_controller` | release operation cores, generation/run admissions and release-evidence bundles | signs release inputs/admissions only; cannot launch or write lineage |
| `release_evidence_issuance_controller` | issuance state, one-use consumption and deterministic expiry settlement under `release_evidence_expiry_lease` | signs issuance-family transitions only; cannot select evidence, promote, open or edit clock baselines |
| `rollout_policy_controller` | predecessor-CAS rollout-policy activation and complete continuity/successor/retired-hold incident migrations | signs only release-published policy/migration rows; cannot sample alerts, resolve incidents or turn a retired hold into healthy evidence |
| `skill_registry_publisher` | protected-source attestations, skill registry, neighbor graph and trigger-harness publication | trusted Git-object read plus skill-family signing only; cannot register candidates |
| `reviewer_routing_input_collector` | snapshots and signs the exact proposal/evidence/reviewer/rubric/plugin/config/mapping/path-policy/override/tool/host-contract/selection-engine input set | read-only registered source descriptors and bounded research-broker metadata; no selection, reviewer launch, handoff write or ambient home discovery |
| `standalone_reviewer_router_runner` | executes canonical intake/fingerprint/selection against one routing input set and submits a signed handoff intent | attested default-deny sandbox with immutable read-only snapshot and exact RPC inventory; no generic shell, edit, filesystem write, direct network or reviewer-result authority |
| `reviewer_router_sandbox_attestor` | independently measures standalone runner code/process/mount/RPC/sandbox identity and negative confinement probes | signs sandbox attestations only; no routing input, selection, handoff write or reviewer launch authority |
| `reviewer_handoff_writer` | sole dirfd-confined no-replace/predecessor-CAS writer and migrator for canonical reviewer-selection YAML | accepts only signed standalone-router or Chainworks review-controller intents carrying a registered artifact ID and active handoff-path-policy digest; no caller path, reviewer-selection authority or arbitrary write capability |
| `reviewer_controller` | reviewer leases, terminal envelopes, signed missing results and barriers | signs reviewer family only |
| `holdout_vault_controller` | encrypted-case/key-epoch inventory and one-use case-release leases | may release only one opaque case to the admitted decrypt coordinator; cannot evaluate, grade or enumerate cases to providers |
| `runtime_owner_inspector` | runtime-owner observation and absence evidence | read-only authenticated lease-head view; signs absence only |
| `runtime_identity_attestor` | independent candidate executable/process measurement and runtime admission | observes launchd/audit-token/vnode/code identity; signs admission only |
| `execution_admission_controller` | canonical reducer checkpoints and one-use executable-work admissions | reduces only signed frozen-plan/run/work/settlement truth; candidate rows are projections |
| `attempt_admission_issuer` | one-use provider-attempt authorization | requires finalized executable-work admission and verifies its matching attempt projection; cannot spawn |
| `provider_sandbox_launcher` | provider/proxy spawn, process registration and sandbox/binding attestations | consumes issuer authorization; has no admission-signing key |
| `provider_prompt_gateway` | predecessor-linked per-turn prompt series reservations and `available -> send_prepared -> send_started -> sent or failed_no_bytes` transitions | sole holder of the registered provider input descriptor and prompt-family signing purpose; no candidate writer, provider launch, retry or authority-append capability |
| `provider_prompt_reconciler` | independent byte-count/provider-turn observation for nonterminal `send_started` or `ambiguous_send_hold` reservations | may sign only `failed_no_bytes`, `sent` or continuing-hold evidence for the same reservation; no descriptor write, resend, successor admission or arbitrary terminal choice |
| `provider_session_partition_controller` | sole authority-store writer for immutable provider-session legacy/authority partitions, the approved-HEAD partition migration receipt and atomic authority-v2 session/partition creation | exact provider-session/run/work/dispatch-hold inventory only; no process clearance, provider launch, session shutdown, control-plane partition write or caller-selected partition |
| `workspace_snapshot_service` | immutable APFS workspace snapshots and signed snapshot receipts for Git evidence | fixed registered-volume/root operations only; no Git parser, provider channel or mutable snapshot mount |
| `control_plane_snapshot_attestor` | coherent main/WAL/SHM transaction snapshot and immutable SQLite backup receipt for cross-store verification | read-only registered control-plane directory capability and pinned SQLite VFS/backup APIs only; no candidate or authority mutation |
| `skill_broker_service` | canonical signed grant/request/effect/apply state plus skill/Git tools under `skill_effect_writer_lease` | accepts only sealed-proxy XPC identity; no provider credential, candidate-store or launch authority |
| `skill_grant_expiry_controller` | correlated installation-deadline scan and terminal noninstalled-grant transition | may append only `expired`, `revoked` or identity hold under the existing grant/attempt; cannot install, extend or mint a grant |
| `skill_broker_reconciliation_controller` | typed same-grant and same-effect hold reconciliation plus attempt settlement | observes only registered process/XPC/pre-post identities; cannot spawn a new script/provider, choose a target or allocate another logical effect |
| `provider_credential_controller` | proxy-only credential import/provision/refresh/rotation/revocation/delete generations and account-binding CAS | sole Keychain write/metadata transition owner; no provider launch, model request, broker or candidate authority |
| `provider_credential_provisioning_helper` | one-use OS-secure-input capture for one authority-issued provisioning intent | private audit-token-bound XPC to credential controller only; pinned build/designated requirement, no network/provider/broker/authority-store/candidate-store/generic Keychain capability, bounded locked memory and mandatory zeroization |
| `provider_credential_proxy` | process/session-scoped upstream authentication, active-generation Keychain read and secret injection | read-only active credential ACL plus policy-bound upstream channel; no lifecycle mutation, broker, work or candidate authority |
| `rollout_soak_controller` | release-owned same-generation soak aggregation and terminal receipt signing | reads only protected rollout contract, signed alert samples/clock correlations, probe receipt and incident-set head; cannot sample, edit policy, register/promote/open a candidate or waive duration |
| `alert_sampler` | policy-bound telemetry samples and alert snapshots only | cannot mutate incidents, authorize repair or repair itself |
| `incident_controller` | incident open/acknowledge/ordinary resolve and retired-signal settlement transitions | consumes signed snapshots/migration evidence; cannot sample or execute repair |
| `incident_repair_controller` | one-use incident repair authorizations | derives slots from incident plus rollout policy; independent of sampled component |
| `incident_repair_executor` | one-use incident repair actions and exact pre/post health receipts | may restart/reconcile only admitted component/resource slots; cannot launch providers or mutate incident state |
| `incident_notifier` | durable local notification delivery/requeue receipts | owns notification lifecycle only; cannot mutate incident state |
| `notification_watchdog` | independent delivery-exhaustion alert snapshots | reads notification state and signs operator-health alert only; cannot deliver or requeue |
| `authority_key_registry_controller` | root-signed append-only public verification-key epochs | sole post-bootstrap release-root signing entitlement; no domain-state or anchor authority |
| `authority_upgrade_controller` | root-approved successor admission and N-to-N+1 authority-generation handoff | coordinates only sealed release generations; cannot reinterpret domain state or bypass drain/anchor predicates |
| `authority_recovery_gateway` | installation-stable local read/reconcile transport for one admitted authority handoff while ordinary serving is closed | private launchd Mach/XPC service only; live Operator authentication plus exactly `authority_upgrade.get` and same-handoff `authority_upgrade.reconcile`, no TCP/MCP listener, domain/provider/candidate mutation or generic OS action |
| `authority_handoff_reconciler` | crash reconciliation of one admitted generation-handoff action journal | no serving listener or domain mutation; may invoke only the exact journal-bound Keychain/XPC/launchd/lease observation adapter |
| `authority_local_diagnostics_exporter` | bounded redacted local startup/crash/launchd evidence export while all serving transports are unavailable | sealed read-only helper with fixed diagnostic-directory and launchd-label inventory; no gateway, network, database mutation, Keychain secret or arbitrary path access |
| `authority_anchor_sequencer` | monotonically advances the event/backup Keychain anchor | installation-stable recovery-capsule helper and sole anchor entitlement; no MCP, candidate or domain-transition key |
| `authority_store_coordinator` | physical append/fsync/CAS and global sequence allocation | installation-stable non-signing recovery-capsule helper and sole SQLite directory capability; no private signing/anchor key |

`AuthorityLocalDiagnosticsContractV1` covers every critical component/helper row
above, the bridge/candidate daemon, each fixed launchd label and every startup
phase that can fail before MCP, GraphQL or private XPC serving is available. For
each component it defines a closed phase vocabulary, closed safe failure-code
vocabulary, build/designated-requirement identity, launchd label, expected
startup predecessor, crash-loop threshold and the exact redacted fields allowed
in local diagnostics. Unknown component, phase or code is itself
`diagnostic_contract_mismatch` and blocks release evidence.

Each component writes bounded canonical JSONL to
`$HOME/Library/Logs/Chainworks Forge/release-authority/<component>.jsonl` and
atomically replaces
`$HOME/Library/Logs/Chainworks Forge/release-authority/status/<component>.json`
after every phase change. The directory is opened no-follow, owner-only and
created by the sealed release. JSONL rotates at 2 MiB, retains at most eight
files per component and seven days, and the complete diagnostics tree has a
64 MiB hard cap with oldest closed files removed first. Status files are at
most 32 KiB and are never deleted by rotation. Writes above a cap emit one
bounded `diagnostic_retention_exhausted` status and drop detail rather than
blocking the component or growing without bound.

Allowed fields are schema/component/build, launchd label, installation and boot
opaque IDs, startup-attempt UUID, correlation UUID, phase, safe failure code,
monotonic sequence, wall time, process-birth hash, exit/signal class, restart
count, last-success phase and bounded safe detail enum. Raw paths, argv values,
environment values, bearer/session/provider IDs, prompts, artifacts, database
rows, Keychain labels, secrets and free-form error text are forbidden. The
writer maps native/system errors to closed codes before persistence. A stderr
fallback emits only schema/component/attempt/correlation/phase/code and remains
subject to the same line cap.

The sealed `authority_local_diagnostics_exporter` and Swift System screen can
read these files and fixed `launchctl print`/OS crash-report projections without
contacting the gateway, candidate, database, network or provider. The exported
`AuthorityOfflineDiagnosticsBundleV1` includes the active diagnostics-contract
digest, component/build inventory, current status files, bounded log tails,
launchd loaded/PID/restart/last-exit state and redacted crash-report metadata;
it never includes a crash dump or raw process memory. It works in failed-serve,
bootstrap failure, authority-store unavailability and gateway/XPC outage.

Fault fixtures crash every declared startup phase, trigger a launchd crash
loop, corrupt/truncate one status/log tail, exhaust rotation and keep the
gateway unavailable. In every case the offline Swift export identifies the
component, attempt, phase and closed next-action code without secrets or
unbounded growth. Candidate registration, trust policy, release bundle and
open evidence bind `authority_local_diagnostics_contract_sha256`; a missing,
stale or mismatched diagnostics contract is release-blocking.

The active `EvaluationTrustPolicyV1` pins every row in this matrix, including
the exact caller/callee audit-token allowlist and table/schema family. Private
XPC endpoints are handed only to their declared peers; they are not globally
discoverable Mach services. A foreign-purpose request, copied endpoint or
helper replacement is an OS-level denial and emits no signed object. The
coordinator persists `AuthorityWriteEnvelopeV1` objects only after verifying
the matching purpose signature, expected predecessor, reservation and global
sequence; consumers reject any unsigned direct row even if the database file is
tampered with. `chainworks-migration-bootstrap` is a separately signed private
helper in this matrix, not a mode of the candidate or an arbitrary executable.

The phase-to-process/store contract is closed:

| Cutover phase | MCP/auth/session owner | XPC route/operation owner | Authority semantic signer / physical writer | Control-plane SQLite writer | Provider/proof worker owner | MCP response owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `not_started / legacy_bridge` | current bridge daemon, V1 descriptors | bridge-internal legacy command path; release XPC is evaluation-only | declared evaluation helper signs; store coordinator is sole physical writer | bridge daemon for legacy operations | bridge daemon under existing contract | bridge daemon |
| `schema_prepared` through `legacy_execution_sealed`, `closed_v2_pending`, `probe_v2`, or `emergency_hold_v2` | release-authority gateway, V2 HTTP plus sealed stdio bridge | gateway routes only to the private purpose helper and maintenance bootstrap over audit-token-authenticated XPC; candidate daemon is absent | declared purpose helper signs; store coordinator is sole physical writer | separately signed maintenance bootstrap, using the sole maintenance writer lease | only authority-launched identity-attestation/proof worker under a probe admission; no ordinary provider/effect work | release-authority gateway after operation finalize and anchor receipt |
| `open_v2` | release-authority gateway, V2 HTTP plus sealed stdio bridge | gateway routes ordinary logical requests to candidate XPC and release/launch commands to the private purpose helper | declared purpose helper signs; store coordinator is sole physical writer | candidate daemon for ordinary run/execution transactions; maintenance bootstrap only during an explicit maintenance stop | release-owned launcher after production run/attempt admission | release-authority gateway after finalized outcome and anchor receipt |

No phase has two control-plane writers. The gateway returns `service_unavailable`
while ownership is changing and does not queue a request across the handoff.
Black-box promote, probe, reprobe, open, incident, owner-inspection and
replacement commands therefore remain callable with the candidate daemon
stopped; ordinary execution remains unavailable in maintenance phases.

That table is enforced by one canonical authority-store
`RuntimeOwnerLeaseV1` specialization with resource kind
`control_plane_writer_lease`, not by process convention. The canonical lease
binds the control-plane database identity, writer role `legacy_bridge |
maintenance_bootstrap | admitted_candidate`, exact executable/build/process-
birth/self-admission identity, cutover phase/generation, writer epoch,
predecessor lease, acquired/heartbeat/deadline and specialization state
`active | draining | released | fenced`. A release-authority operation issues,
renews, drains or releases it; candidate and maintenance code cannot write the
lease. `ControlPlaneWriterLeaseV1` is only its bounded signed readback
projection and is never accepted as lifecycle input. Every write transaction
presents the canonical runtime-owner lease digest and epoch to the connection
authorizer and commits that digest into the transaction fence row. An inactive,
projected-only, expired or stale-epoch writer performs zero mutation.

The canonical writer-lease specialization handoff is
`active -> draining -> released -> active(new epoch)`. The
old writer first stops admission, commits its terminal database head and signs
a drain receipt. The authority verifies exact process absence or a clean
release, then issues the successor against that head. Ambiguous/living owners
block handoff; there is no timeout-only takeover. `RuntimeOwnerLeaseV1` includes
`control_plane_writer_lease` in its closed resource kinds so generic owner
absence and one-use takeover rules apply. `cutover.get` and authority-operation
readback expose current writer role/epoch/deadline/state and pending handoff.
Crash vectors at every drain/release/issue boundary prove that at most one epoch
can commit and that a stale connection cannot resume after successor issue.
`RuntimeSelfAdmissionReceiptV1` in those phases is produced by the external
`runtime_identity_attestor`. The authority launches the candidate only in a
nonce-bound self-description mode with no MCP descriptor, control-plane writer,
provider-launch or work-claim capability; its output is untrusted comparison
input, while the attestor independently measures code/process/resource identity
and signs the receipt. The candidate then exits. It is not the ordinary daemon
and cannot sign admission or execute a migration transition itself.

#### Coherent control-plane SQLite observation

No authority decision verifies candidate rows by opening only a database path
or file descriptor. The release-owned `control_plane_snapshot_attestor` is the
sole reader used by cross-store finalize and launch admission. It receives a
no-follow directory capability for the registered control-plane database,
verifies the main database, `-wal` and `-shm` vnode/inode/device/mode/owner
identities, opens the pinned SQLite VFS in read-only mode, starts one read
transaction and acquires the exact WAL snapshot token before reading any row.
The admitted native inventory requires SQLite snapshot/backup support; absence
is failed-serve rather than a path-only fallback.

Within that transaction the attestor records schema/user versions, database
header/change counter, page size/count, WAL salt and frame range, SHM read-mark
set, checkpoint sequence, `PRAGMA data_version`, transaction snapshot token and
the candidate transaction fence row. It then uses the pinned SQLite backup API
to materialize one immutable read-only snapshot file in a release-owned
temporary directory while retaining the source snapshot, fsyncs file and
directory, reopens it through an immutable VFS, verifies integrity and the
expected signed rows, and emits `ControlPlaneSqliteSnapshotReceiptV1`. The
receipt binds all live file identities and sizes observed before and after the
copy, snapshot/checkpoint/transaction facts, immutable backup vnode and digest,
registered database identity, writer lease/epoch, candidate transaction ID/head
and attestor component/build/key epoch. It is purpose-signed and one-use for the
named authority operation or attempt admission.

Authority controllers inspect only the immutable snapshot named by that
receipt. A main/WAL/SHM replacement, symlink, concurrent database replacement,
checkpoint/snapshot mismatch, missing sidecar, changed writer epoch or row that
does not match the receipt fails before authority mutation. A concurrent normal
checkpoint may complete, but cannot alter the pinned read transaction or
immutable backup and therefore cannot produce a mixed observation. Snapshot
cleanup occurs only after the consuming authority operation finalizes or
aborts; a lost response resumes the same receipt. Fault fixtures replace each
file and race commits/checkpoints at every copy boundary, proving that no
mixture of database, WAL and SHM generations can authorize a finalize, launch
or effect.

Candidate/projection rows in the control-plane database are readback caches of
signed authority objects and are never candidate or promotion truth. The
authority store and its `candidate_lineage_controller` are the one canonical
candidate lineage owner. Evaluation and release-transition components submit
purpose-signed transition intents, but only the lineage controller validates
the exact predecessor/evidence set and CASes any candidate state; the
control-plane database never writes a candidate state, even inside a
promote/open transaction. A forged cache row, copied database file or
candidate-authored receipt cannot advance candidate, cutover, generation or
work-admission state.

Every release-authority mutation uses one durable
`ReleaseAuthorityOperationV1`. Its operation core declares whether a
control-plane write is semantically required, and exactly one of these paths is
legal:

```text
control_plane_effect = required: prepared -> control_plane_committed -> anchor_pending -> finalized
control_plane_effect = none:     prepared --------------------------> anchor_pending -> finalized
either class before first non-authority effect: prepared -> aborted_before_commit
```

Each phase is an append-only operation revision with predecessor-operation
digest; the authority store never updates hashed operation bytes in place.

Prepare is one coordinator transaction. It verifies the purpose-signed
`ReleaseAuthorityOperationCoreV1`, expected authority head, candidate/cutover/
generation revision and one-use nonce; inserts one
`AuthorityExactRequestRecordV1` in `in_flight`; and reserves the operation's
complete sorted `AuthorityResourceReservationV1` set. Reservation keys cover
every canonical object the operation may consume or advance, including the
candidate/generation/cutover row, run or incident/owner lease, evidence bundle,
admission, caller request identity and semantic-effect identity where relevant.
The coordinator acquires raw canonical keys in ascending byte order and permits
only one live reservation per key. An exact duplicate joins the same operation;
a conflicting request cannot prepare, so two prepared operations can never
race later on the same resource.

When a command selects CI, branch, alert, incident-set, policy or other
release evidence, that same transaction also writes one immutable
`AuthorityEvidenceFenceV1`. It binds the operation, exact
`authority_evidence_revision`, current rollout-signal-policy digest, sorted
selected row schema/key/revision/digest set, freshness deadline and state
`held | released_finalized | released_aborted`. Evidence writers do not wait on
a process lock: before advancing a selected key they check the durable fence.
A conflicting write may prepare only a successor evidence revision after the
fenced operation finalizes, or it fails with `authority_evidence_fenced`; an
unrelated evidence key may continue. Thus the selected revision survives crash
and restart as data, not as a transient SQLite lock.

The prepare transaction commits and releases every SQLite lock before any XPC
request, control-plane transaction, Keychain call, process operation or
filesystem fsync begins. No authority or control-plane SQLite transaction is
held across another store or OS service. Every later phase opens a fresh bounded
transaction, verifies the complete reservations/evidence fence and predecessor
operation digest, appends exactly one successor revision and commits before the
next external step.

For `control_plane_effect = required`, the phase-selected control-plane writer
then commits only the signed prepared
operation digest, the applicable `pending_authority_finalize` projection,
canonical command **outcome core**, required projection intents, and observed
transaction ID/head. That row is provisional: it is excluded from the existing
MCP success cache, command aliases and every servable success readback. The
writer reports it over authenticated XPC; the coordinator verifies the exact
row through the immutable snapshot named by a one-use
`ControlPlaneSqliteSnapshotReceiptV1` and appends the
`control_plane_committed` operation revision. For
`control_plane_effect = none`, no candidate or maintenance control-plane writer
is started and this phase is forbidden; the prepared operation advances
directly to authority finalize. Skill-registry publication, release-evidence
bundle issue, incident acknowledge/repair-authorize/notification-requeue and
incident resolve are authority-only operations. Their control-plane readbacks
are delivered later only through the authority projection outbox.

Finalize first asks the purpose controller and candidate-lineage controller,
where applicable, for the exact signed state transition. In one coordinator
transaction it verifies all reservations and predecessors, writes the domain
state/event and immutable outbox-intent rows as `pending_anchor`, appends each
outbox intent's first `AuthorityProjectionDeliveryRevisionV1 = pending`,
allocates the next global authority sequence, and advances the operation to
`anchor_pending`; none of those rows is
servable authority yet. The sole `authority_anchor_sequencer` verifies the
event/operation chain and performs the serialized predecessor-checked Keychain
read/update/read from exactly the prior sequence/head to the pending successor,
then returns a purpose-signed
`AuthorityAnchorAdvanceReceiptV1`. A final coordinator transaction verifies that
receipt and atomically marks the state event/admissions servable, advances the
operation to `finalized`, releases reservations, appends one predecessor-linked
`AuthorityProjectionDeliveryRevisionV1 = ready` per immutable outbox intent,
and stores the canonical logical result in
`AuthorityExactRequestRecordV1 = finalized_success`. Neither the signed outbox
intent nor an earlier delivery revision is updated in place.

The gateway returns success only from that finalized exact-request record. A
control-plane command outcome core or `anchor_pending` row is never replayable
as success. For a required control-plane effect, crash before its commit permits
only `aborted_before_commit` and reservation release; crash after that commit
can only resume the same operation. For an authority-only effect, prepare is
still non-servable and recovery either aborts it before anchor allocation or
continues the same pending-anchor/finalize path. Crash before or after the
Keychain item update is
resolved from the pending event plus signed anchor receipt/current anchor and
cannot allocate a second sequence. Neither path repeats a candidate transition,
launch, effect or command outcome. Startup reconciles every nonterminal
operation and exact-request record before accepting a conflicting mutation.

Operator-only `runtime.agent_context.authority_operations.get/list` are
strictly read-only authority-store snapshot queries. They expose bounded
operation kind/revision/phase, exact-request state, reservation/evidence-fence
summary, conditional control-plane transaction/head, pending-anchor/receipt,
allowed next action and safe error code; they mutate zero rows and do not infer
completion. `runtime.agent_context.authority_operations.reconcile` is the only
northbound recovery mutation. It requires both request IDs, exact operation ID,
revision/digest and expected phase, plus capability
`RuntimeAgentContextAuthorityOperationReconcile`. The declared purpose helper
and coordinator re-observe already-recorded control-plane/anchor/process facts
and append one legal successor or typed `identity_hold`; they cannot create a
new domain intent, Run, launch, effect, evidence selection or anchor sequence.
Exact replay returns the same reconciliation outcome. Startup may invoke the
same internal reconciler before mutation service, but ordinary GET never does.

The control-plane candidate cache written at commit is explicitly
`pending_finalize` and references the prepared operation, not a fabricated
final candidate event. It is never served as canonical candidate state. After
authority finalize, the same-store authority projection outbox copies the signed
`ReleaseAuthorityStateEventV1` and marks that cache current; until then readback
reports pending and every work/launch/effect admission requires the finalized
operation/admission directly from authority truth. Projection lag therefore
cannot grant authority, and projection failure leaves a visible pending/degraded
cache without rolling back or repeating the finalized transition. Outbox claim,
delivery receipt, retry and terminal-degraded state are sequenced by authority
event ID; a finalized authority mutation can never lack its outbox entry.

For generation transitions, that generic operation core binds one specific
`ReleaseGenerationTransitionCoreV1`; incident, owner, reviewer and run-start
operations bind their own complete typed input digest rows instead. No generic
core contains an output, admission, state-event or finalized-command-outcome
digest; a northbound operation binds only the already computed
`CanonicalCommandOutcomeCoreV1` input digest.

Release-transition digests form an acyclic graph. First the controller creates
`ReleaseGenerationTransitionCoreV1`, containing only expected predecessor
state and verified inputs. Promote then creates its proof admission; probe
start/reprobe/open instead sign the applicable generation admission. The
versioned generation row references that admission object and its previous row
digest. Finally the canonical command outcome references the transition core,
admission and generation-row digests. No core or admission contains a
generation-row or command-outcome digest. The exact dependency orders are:

```text
promote_transition_core -> proof_admission -> generation_row -> command_outcome
probe_or_open_transition_core -> signed_generation_admission -> generation_row -> command_outcome
```

Promotion creates only the one-use `AgentContextProofAdmissionV1` and a
transition core. `probe_start` consumes it, preallocates and commits the exact
proof run/epoch/fixture namespace, and finalizes a
`ReleaseGenerationAdmissionReceiptV1` with `admission_scope = probe_only`
before that run becomes claimable or any proof provider can launch. It binds
the generation, candidate, proof matrix, exact proof run, probe epoch,
immutable fixture namespace, and the complete allowed provider/effect cell
set. That scope rejects ordinary runs, production workspaces,
publication/network effects and any cell absent from the matrix. Reprobe
supersedes it with another probe-only receipt for the new proof run and leaves
the predecessor linked and revoked. Open atomically supersedes the latest
passing probe receipt with
`admission_scope = production`, bound to the passing probe receipt and both
promote/open evidence sets. At no time can one receipt authorize both scopes.

A production `runs.start` is additionally prepared by the gateway as a signed
`ReleaseRunAdmissionReceiptV1` for its preallocated run ID, verified production
generation admission, logical session/request, frozen binding, workflow,
catalog, registered workspace, precomputed canonical outcome-core digest and
immutable authority operation-core digest.
The receipt never references the prepared operation revision. That revision is
written only after the receipt exists and references both the core and receipt.
One append-only `ReleaseRunAdmissionTransitionV1` starts at revision one in
`prepared` and binds the immutable receipt. The control-plane run transaction
stores the closed production admission arm as `pending_authority_finalize`;
authority finalize appends transition revision two `prepared -> active` before
the gateway returns the Run. The receipt itself never changes. A later
settlement or revocation appends another predecessor-linked transition and
cannot rewrite the receipt or active revision. Probe runs use the probe admission and fixed proof
namespace through the tagged probe admission arm, never a production run receipt. Forging a Run row or copying
a run admission across generation, session or workspace is denied before work
claim.
The run-start digest order is `preallocated run ID + generation binding ->
canonical command outcome core -> release authority operation core -> signed
run admission -> prepared operation revision -> Run row/final snapshot ->
anchored authority event/finalized canonical command outcome`. The outcome core
excludes admission/operation identities; the binding, operation core, receipt
and prepared revision exclude every later snapshot/row/final-result digest; the
final snapshot stores the receipt only after signature verification. Mutation
vectors reject an admission that names an operation revision, an outcome core
that names an admission/operation, or any other reverse reference.

Every real provider spawn requires a fresh
`ProviderAttemptLaunchAuthorizationV1`. The candidate may submit only a
control-plane dispatch identity to the OS-isolated
`attempt_admission_issuer`, never to a signing API. The issuer independently
reads the finalized `ExecutableWorkAdmissionV1` and reducer checkpoint from the
authority store, verifies their signatures, semantic key, one-use state and
run/proof scope, then obtains a one-use
`ControlPlaneSqliteSnapshotReceiptV1` for the registered control-plane
transaction. From that immutable coherent snapshot it requires the parent current-attempt
pointer, work claim, dispatch intent, assignment/provider/model/sandbox/grant/
workspace identities and current holds to byte-match the signed work admission.
Only then does it create one purpose-signed authority-store authorization in
an immutable object plus revision-one
`ProviderAttemptLaunchAuthorizationTransitionV1` in state `available`.
The issuer cannot spawn a process; the launcher cannot mint or revise an
authorization. A forged cache/attempt row without the complete admitted
run/proof/work-admission/parent/assignment chain is denied even if all of its
candidate-controlled foreign keys are mutually consistent.

An available authorization has a TTL of exactly 30 seconds under the authority
clock baseline. The launcher consumes it only through one authority-store
transaction that appends its transition `available -> consumed` and creates
`ProviderSpawnJournalV1` in `spawn_pending`; the immutable authorization never
changes state in place. The journal binds
the unique `(run_id, agent_execution_id, attempt_generation,
dispatch_intent_sha256)`, provider-session/cancellation epoch, authorization,
one-use wrapper-credential hash, supervisor spawn nonce, expected executable/
sandbox identities and issue time. Only then may it call `posix_spawn`.
Registration of the sealed wrapper's PID/process-group/UID/birth and spent
launch credential advances the same journal to `process_registered` and emits
one signed `ProviderSpawnReceiptV1`. A synchronous spawn failure with verified
absence advances it to `failed_no_process` and emits a terminal no-process
receipt. If restart or lost acknowledgement cannot distinguish a child from
absence, the journal advances to `identity_hold`, records all bounded process
evidence and blocks retry until the existing process-absence clearance settles
the attempt.

The closed authorization/journal lifecycle is:

```text
authorization transition: available -> consumed | expired | revoked
consumed authorization -> spawn journal spawn_pending -> process_registered
spawn_pending -> failed_no_process | identity_hold
identity_hold -> failed_no_process  [verified absence only]
```

No transition returns to `available`, and no recovery path calls `posix_spawn`
again for the same tuple. A repeated exact request returns the existing
available authorization, in-progress journal, or terminal spawn receipt; a
conflicting dispatch digest is a zero-write invariant denial. Startup
reconciles every `spawn_pending` journal from supervisor syscall evidence,
wrapper registration and process birth before admitting another attempt. Stale
generation, wrong proof cell, ordinary workspace under probe scope or wrong/
expired authorization performs zero launch. External-effect admission performs
the same generation/run scope checks in addition to the stable logical-effect
registry, so probe cells can touch only their fixture namespace.

Authority-store recovery uses signed append-only state events, SQLite WAL
recovery, a monotonic writer epoch, `ReleaseAuthorityStateEventV1`, and
`ReleaseAuthorityBackupManifestV1`. Store genesis creates canonical decimal
`authority_evidence_revision = 0`; every accepted CI, branch, alert, incident
or bundle mutation increments it exactly once in its finalized authority
operation. Startup verifies the store genesis, purpose signatures, event chain,
active key epochs, latest backup manifest, anchor receipts and control-plane
projection digests before serving mutation operations.

Only one global authority sequence may be `anchor_pending`. The
`authority_anchor_sequencer` is the sole process with the Keychain anchor
entitlement; domain helpers and the store coordinator cannot read a private
anchor key or advance it. It processes pending state events and predecessor-
linked backup manifests strictly by sequence, fsyncs the candidate event/
manifest first, and performs one concrete serialized Security.framework update.

The anchor is a generic-password Keychain item in a release-only access group,
with `kSecAttrService = com.chainworks.release-authority.anchor.v1`, one fixed
account, `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, no synchronizable
or cloud copy, and an ACL/designated-requirement that admits only the anchor
sequencer. Its canonical value is
`AuthorityAnchorStateV1 { sequence, event_head, backup_manifest_sha256,
key_registry_head, predecessor_anchor_sha256, anchor_sha256 }`. Security.framework
does not supply a conditional-update primitive, so this proposal does not claim
one: launchd enforces one sequencer instance and its serial queue performs
`SecItemCopyMatching -> exact predecessor comparison -> SecItemUpdate ->
SecItemCopyMatching verification` while no other executable satisfies the ACL.
The Keychain item replacement is the single atomic external write. A mismatch,
duplicate item, update error or failed readback leaves the SQLite event
non-servable and enters failed-serve/reconciliation; it never retries with a
new sequence. The sequencer signs the observed before/after values in
`AuthorityAnchorAdvanceReceiptV1`.

A later operation cannot enter `anchor_pending` until the prior receipt is
finalized in SQLite. Startup accepts only equality with the anchor or the single
documented SQLite-pending/Keychain-advanced successor that can be completed from
the current item and pending bytes; two pending successors, a skipped sequence,
duplicate Keychain item or an item without the exact pending event is
failed-serve. An older SQLite/backup/event head, missing item, fork or
unexplained revision cannot be rebuilt from candidate-controlled control-plane
rows.

Historical signature verification uses an append-only
`AuthorityVerificationKeyEpochV1` registry, not a bounded cache of old keys.
The installation root public key and custody-profile digest are immutable
members of authority genesis and the ThisDeviceOnly anchor created by the
sealed empty-installation bootstrap; every later bundle carries those values as
expected observations rather than replacing them. The root key and every
purpose key use the concrete Secure Enclave profile above. Each epoch row binds
purpose, exact algorithm/profile, public key bytes, activation and optional
revocation authority sequences, predecessor key-registry head and a root
signature. All public epoch rows are retained for the lifetime of the authority
history. Only the current non-revoked purpose epoch may sign new objects; token
protocols may additionally accept a specifically declared previous epoch only
within their TTL, while old signed state remains verifiable against its
historical sequence after any number of rotations. Removing or rewriting a
public epoch is failed-serve. Retired opaque key representations may be deleted
after their signing window because history needs only public bytes, but they
can never be exported, copied to another installation or regenerated from
backup.

Operator-only `runtime.agent_context.key_epoch.transition` makes purpose-key
rotation executable with closed action `create | activate | retire`, both
request IDs and exact authority/key-registry/custody-profile heads. It accepts
no key material, Keychain account, helper identity or arbitrary overlap. The
root-authorized `authority_key_registry_controller` derives the deterministic
next account from installation/purpose/epoch. `create` journals the exact
Security.framework action, idempotently creates the helper-ACL-bound opaque key
and appends one root-signed `created` public epoch. `activate` CASes exactly one
`created` epoch to the sole `active` signing epoch and the predecessor to
`overlap` with the policy-fixed deadline. `retire` requires that deadline to
have elapsed, no live token window or nonterminal authority object to require
new signatures from the predecessor, appends `retired`, then permits deletion
of only the predecessor opaque representation. Emergency invalidation remains
the separate root-authorized `key_epoch.revoke` operation below and ends any
overlap immediately. Every action is predecessor-linked and crash-reconciled
against deterministic Keychain account/public-key observations. Three
sequential purpose-key rotations across authority and helper restart must leave
one active epoch, at most one policy-declared overlap epoch, all public history
verifiable and every retired/revoked private epoch unable to sign.

Signature verification has two non-interchangeable entry points.
`verify_historical_at_sequence(object, finalized_sequence)` verifies the root-
signed epoch and object signature as they existed at that finalized authority
sequence and returns a readback-only verdict; it can never satisfy an admission,
lease, token, grant, request, launch or mutation precondition.
`authorize_live_now(object, current_authority_sequence)` additionally requires
the key epoch to be active and non-revoked at the current sequence, the object
to be current/nonterminal under its own lifecycle and every successor/fence
check to pass. A previous token epoch is accepted during a declared TTL overlap
only while that epoch is not revoked and the token was issued before rotation;
explicit revocation ends the overlap immediately.

The authority store maintains a complete reverse index from
`(key_purpose, key_epoch)` to every signed object and its current lifecycle
revision. Revocation is initiated only by Operator-only
`runtime.agent_context.key_epoch.revoke` carrying a current immutable release-
root-signed `AuthorityKeyEpochRevocationAuthorizationV1`; an Operator cannot
author, widen or substitute its purpose/epoch/reason/successor. Key revocation
is one predecessor-CAS authority operation owned by
`authority_key_registry_controller`; prepare reserves the epoch and every
available/nonterminal indexed object. Finalize writes the epoch revocation
sequence and one `AuthorityKeyEpochRevocationFenceV1`, and in the same pending-
anchor transaction appends the object-specific terminal transition: available
tokens/admissions/grants/repair slots become `revoked`, active leases become
`fenced`, pending broker/effect requests become typed reconciliation holds, and
prepared/nonfinal authority operations become `revoked_epoch_hold`. A launched
provider or worker whose live authority depended on that epoch is cancelled and
settled through its existing reducer before successor work can be admitted.
There is no generic grandfathered-live branch.

Already finalized outcomes/events remain historically verifiable and readable
at their recorded sequence but cannot authorize replay as a new action. Gateway,
broker, launcher, evaluator and projection worker consult current authority key
state directly before every live use, so delayed control-plane projection cannot
extend a revoked capability. Rotation/revocation fixtures cover each object
family, an in-flight operation, prior-epoch TTL token, projection lag and
restart, proving the revocation anchor and all fences finalize once and no
pre-revocation nonterminal object remains usable.

Restore never imports a database or backup older than the current Keychain
anchor. The restored file set must already contain and verify the complete event
and key-registry chain through the exact current anchor state and backup
manifest. After equality is established, restore emits a newly sequenced
forward `restore_completed` event through the same pending-anchor protocol. A
backup that ends before the current anchor, a copied older Keychain item, a
newer database with an older item, or a key-registry gap is rejected without
mutation; there is no operator override that rewinds sequence or head.

Release-authority software upgrade is a separate forward-only generation
handoff, not candidate replacement or ordinary restore. Operator-only
`runtime.agent_context.authority_upgrade.begin` is served by generation `N` and
accepts both request IDs, the immutable release-root-signed successor bundle
manifest, expected generation/authority/anchor/writer heads and complete
compatibility proof, plus one complete signed
`AuthorityGenerationDrainInventoryV1` head/digest and its zero-active aggregate.
`authority_upgrade_controller` verifies the new sealed
bundle, helper matrix, launchd labels, XPC protocols, store schemas, entitlements
and ABI receipts and issues one `ReleaseAuthorityUpgradeAdmissionV1`. The new
bundle first runs in non-serving self-admission mode: it has no listener, store
writer, anchor/key private operation, provider launcher or broker capability.

Handoff requires one complete authority-derived
`AuthorityGenerationDrainInventoryV1`. It enumerates canonical heads,
revisions, counts and row digests for northbound logical sessions; every
non-handoff authority operation; every `RuntimeOwnerLeaseV1` specialization;
provider sessions and full process trees; prompt reservations; broker grants,
proxy admissions, privileged proxy and stdio-bootstrap processes and accepted
servers; skill request/effect registries, effect attempts, script processes and
apply journals; external auxiliary effects; incident-repair journals;
projection workers/outboxes; and all registered helpers. Every row has a
terminal, active or ambiguous disposition and the inventory carries one
zero-active-or-ambiguous aggregate over all families. Missing/unknown family,
truncated page, active effect/process/grant/lease or ambiguous fate blocks
handoff. Its head/digest and all per-family heads are bound into the begin
request, upgrade admission, operation, every action journal, handoff/recovery
receipt and later gateway-open CAS. A caller-supplied Boolean, family subset or
truncated page is invalid.
Generation `N`
stops new sessions and mutations, drains its gateway/helpers, records every
closed session and released lease, and enters `handoff_pending`. One authority
operation consumes the upgrade admission, predecessor-CASes the singleton
authority-generation row and reserves a complete ordered
`ReleaseAuthorityGenerationHandoffActionJournalV1` set before the first
external write. The closed external action order is: old listener/session
closure observation; old gateway/store/anchor lease release; Keychain purpose-
key ACL transition with the installation anchor/coordinator ACLs unchanged;
private XPC/Mach-service generation transition;
launchd plist/label/bootstrap transition; new helper process observation; new
gateway/store/anchor lease acquisition; and old-generation process fencing.
Every action row binds its fixed release-owned adapter, exact pre-state and
expected post-state, old/new vnode/designated-requirement/process identities,
authority/anchor heads and a handoff-scoped idempotency key. The authority
transaction finalizes state `prepared` before the adapter syscall and never
holds SQLite across that call. A fresh observation then appends only
`applied_observed`, `reconciled` or `identity_hold`; no row is overwritten.

There is intentionally a bounded interval with no serving authority; there is
never an interval with two. Launchd may start generation `N+1` only after the
old serving/owner rows are observed released and the generation CAS is
anchored. The new generation independently verifies the same store, anchor,
event, key-custody and action-journal heads plus its self-admission, acquires
one-higher owner epochs, and finalizes
`ReleaseAuthorityGenerationHandoffReceiptV1` only after every action journal is
`reconciled`. Opening the gateway is a later compare-and-swap that consumes that
receipt and re-reads the complete drain inventory and every family head. Any changed head or
nonzero current aggregate leaves N+1 non-serving and resumes the same handoff
reconciliation; it cannot silently take a fresh empty snapshot. The old
generation is permanently fenced and cannot resume if its process survives.

The sealed `authority_handoff_reconciler` is rooted in the installation trust
profile rather than either serving generation. It has no MCP listener, domain-
mutation schema, candidate/control-plane writer, provider launcher, generic
Keychain call or general launchd operation. During the no-serving interval it
can read only the one admitted handoff, its action journals and the fixed OS
observations named by those rows, and can invoke only the matching typed
adapter. The non-signing `authority_store_coordinator`, the
`authority_anchor_sequencer`, the key-confined
`principal_verifier_service`, and the read-only `principal_table_resolver` are
the complete installation-stable recovery capsule. Their designated
requirements, private protocols, custody-profile entries and read/write
capability sets are fixed by the custody profile and must be byte-identical in
N and N+1; V1 upgrade admission rejects changing any member or omitting its
positive/negative ABI probe. Thus the reconciler can submit purpose-signed handoff-journal envelopes
to the same coordinator and have the same sequencer anchor them while neither
generation serves. No recovery-capsule helper can both authenticate, derive a
domain transition and write/anchor it, and only the recovery gateway may open
the private client listener. For each `prepared` row, an observation byte-equal to pre-state means
execute that same idempotent action once; byte-equal to expected post-state
means append `applied_observed` without repeating it; any third, live-both,
partially changed or unverifiable state appends `identity_hold` and performs no
further external action. It signs one
`ReleaseAuthorityGenerationHandoffRecoveryReceiptV1` over the complete ordered
journal and observed serving inventory. Root recovery therefore resumes the
same handoff on the same device; it is not an override, a new handoff or a
cross-device lineage import.

Normal MCP closure does not remove the operator recovery path. The custody
profile also pins one installation-stable `authority_recovery_gateway` private
launchd Mach service and sealed `chainworks-authority-recovery` app/CLI client;
their designated requirements, protocol and helper identities are immutable
across N and N+1 and cannot be changed by the upgrade admission. The gateway has
no TCP/HTTP/stdio-MCP listener. It authenticates the client audit token and a
fresh live Operator principal through the stable principal-verifier/table
helpers, then exposes only the exact logical schemas for
`runtime.agent_context.authority_upgrade.get` and
`runtime.agent_context.authority_upgrade.reconcile`. Authorization is checked
before handoff existence, and the reconcile request still contains no desired
OS action or target state. The gateway forwards the authorized request to the
handoff reconciler and returns the canonical signed result; it cannot serve any
run, approval, principal, provider, effect, incident or generic authority
operation. It remains launchd-available throughout the zero-serving interval
and is disabled for reconciliation once the handoff is terminal, while GET
continues as bounded audit readback.

The recovery gateway never caches a startup PrincipalTable snapshot or mints a
handoff-duration credential. On every GET or reconcile request it asks the
verifier service to resolve the presented bearer against its bound verifier
epoch, then asks the table resolver for the latest finalized table revision and
session fences from the coordinator's read-only protocol. Revocation,
disablement, re-scope, verifier-epoch revocation or table-head drift therefore
denies the next request during handoff. Neither helper exposes raw table bytes,
bearer bytes, verifier output or a reusable authorization receipt to the
gateway, reconciler, N or N+1.

An `identity_hold` has a bounded same-handoff resolution contract. Operator-
only `runtime.agent_context.authority_upgrade.reconcile` accepts both request
IDs, handoff ID, expected handoff/action-journal/recovery-receipt revisions and
digests, and no requested OS action or target state. The recovery-capsule
readback returns the exact marker/anchor/store heads, old/new process and
serving-lease identities, every journal pre/post observation, the generation-
CAS side and one closed derived action. `authority_handoff_reconciler`
independently rereads those resources and may use only the already named action
adapter and idempotency key.

Before the generation CAS, a valid pre-state may restore `N` serving and abort
the successor handoff. After the generation CAS, `N` remains fenced and only
`N+1` may be completed. Exact pre-state executes the prepared action once;
exact post-state records it; a recoverable third state uses one explicitly
declared compensating observation/action pair from the original action journal.
When neither the old nor new declared state can be re-established without
inventing a key, anchor, service or process identity, the reconciler appends
`terminal_unrecoverable`, preserves zero serving generations and exposes only
forensic export plus new-installation guidance. It never leaves an indefinitely
actionable hold.

The closed recovery transitions are
`identity_hold -> reconciled -> recovered_serving_n | recovered_serving_n_plus_1`
or `identity_hold -> terminal_unrecoverable`. The final same-handoff authority
transaction proves serving-generation count is exactly one for a recovered
branch or zero for terminal unrecoverable, anchors the complete recovery
receipt and consumes the repair request. Exact replay returns that result;
another handoff ID/revision conflicts, and no command can un-fence `N` after
the generation CAS. Fault fixtures cover every third/partial/live-both OS state
and prove convergence or explicit terminality after restart.

Crash before admission consumption leaves `N` active. Crash after drain but
before generation CAS resumes the same handoff under `N`. Crash after CAS, or
between any external syscall and its observed journal append, is reconciled
from that exact prepared row; only `N+1` may become serving and `N` remains
fenced. Wrong/replayed/expired admission, incompatible schema/ABI, live helper,
nonempty provider/effect set, anchor mismatch, stale old/new process identity,
missing journal or ambiguous external state performs no next handoff action.
Upgrade readback and the authority watermark expose old/new generation,
admission, phase, each journal revision/state, recovery receipt, exact helper
matrix and required next action.

Fault fixtures kill N immediately before and after ordinary gateway closure,
then use only the recovery-only transport to read and reconcile the handoff.
They prove authentication failure is non-enumerating, crash/replay converges to
one serving generation or explicit terminal-unrecoverable state, and no test can
invoke a third logical operation through that transport.

Additional recovery-capsule kill vectors terminate N, N+1, the recovery
gateway, verifier, table resolver, coordinator, sequencer and reconciler
independently before and after session closure, verifier lookup, table/fence
read, action observation, action execution, envelope persistence and anchor
advancement. Each restart must reauthenticate against the current table, resume
only the same handoff and produce either one serving generation or
`terminal_unrecoverable`; a revoked or re-scoped Operator, changed capsule
helper, stale table revision, missing verifier epoch or copied authorization
attempt performs zero handoff mutation.

Cross-device host-loss recovery is explicitly **unsupported in V1**. The anchor
is `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`; if the original device,
Keychain item or its release access group is unavailable, no database/backup,
exported public key, Operator approval or replacement host may resume that
authority installation or serve its runs as current. An operator may initialize
a new installation with a new installation/genesis ID and empty authority
lineage; copied old bytes remain quarantined forensic material and are not
imported. A future independently rooted disaster-recovery ceremony requires a
separate reviewed proposal and cannot be inferred from this backup contract.

### EvaluationTrustPolicyV1

Evaluation authority is rooted outside the behavior candidate. The release
authority installation anchors its Secure Enclave root public key/profile in
genesis and the ThisDeviceOnly anchor and installs a root-signed
`EvaluationTrustPolicyV1`; a candidate daemon is only an observed subject and
cannot act as that authority. The policy names its trust epoch and predecessor,
the complete admitted release-authority component/build/key-purpose matrix,
the installation-bound authority-key-custody-profile digest and exact admitted
signature/verification ABI receipt,
the authority-source mapping-policy and runtime-constraint-policy publishers
and exact policy digests,
workflow-source-budget and skill-pair-evaluation-budget policies,
operation-manifest/schema-set/error-registry/authorization-inventory generator/
source digests, Phase 0 change policy/bootstrap receipt/full-gate manifest,
reviewer-routing input/sandbox plus selection-handoff/path/legacy-source policy
publishers/host contract, native dependency/FFI inventory, dependency-risk
publisher/advisory-key/exception policy and ABI-probe policy, provider proxy/
credential/transient-secret-memory policy publishers, local-diagnostics contract/publisher, metric-
contract publisher, rollout-projection schema/mapping/fixture and rollout-policy publisher/controller and protected-base CI gate-
manifest/collector identities, distinct bounded-Actions CI dispatcher,
branch-protection activation-writer and read-only evidence-collector GitHub App
installations/credentials,
protected rollout-contract source/publisher and
`rollout_soak_controller` identities,
evaluator binary/build digest, deterministic promotion-policy and
numeric-algorithm digests, evaluation-lane retry-policy digest,
evidence-admission and reviewer-controller public
keys, admitted worker, reviewer supervisor and CI collector
executable/principal identities, holdout-custody policy and validity interval.
The signed policy artifact is bundled read-only and its
verified digest is installed into the authority store by a predecessor-linked
release transition; the control-plane database stores only its signed readback
projection. No candidate, provider, evaluation worker, Steward action, ordinary
MCP command or environment value can create, edit or select it.

Candidate registration does not accept authority-mapping/runtime-constraint,
evaluator, promotion-policy or evidence-key fields from the candidate payload.
The Rust registration service resolves
the one active trust-policy digest and rejects the candidate before inserting a
row unless every evaluator/policy/key identity required by its suites is admitted
by that policy and every release component, reviewer supervisor, skill
publisher and trigger harness required by the proof matrix matches the policy's
closed component matrix. It materializes the candidate core's mapping-policy,
runtime-constraint-policy and evaluation-trust-policy digests from that active
signed policy; candidate-supplied alternatives are schema-invalid. The
candidate core records only those resolved identities for provenance.
Rotation requires a new signed
release policy whose predecessor matches the active digest and a forward
database transition; rollback, unsigned replacement and same-epoch key changes
fail startup. Candidate and worker credentials cannot call that transition.

Every worker lease, evidence admission and `live_passed` transaction re-reads
the active policy under the same SQLite transaction and binds its digest and
trust epoch. A candidate-selected evaluator cannot register, acquire a lease or
write evidence; a previously admitted evaluator under a superseded or expired
policy can only finish bounded reconciliation and cannot produce a promotable
receipt. Tests substitute candidate-controlled evaluator binaries, policies and
keys and prove rejection before candidate state exists.

### AgentContextCandidateCoreV1 and AgentContextCandidateManifestV1

Live evidence is valid only for one complete behavior candidate. Registration
uses an acyclic two-object construction. The release controller first
preallocates a random `candidate_id` and creates immutable
`AgentContextCandidateCoreV1`; the core contains every behavior-affecting input
but neither a quality-target-declaration digest nor the final candidate-manifest
digest. The core contains:

- Rust daemon source commit, build profile, target triple, binary SHA-256, and
  workflow/context compiler and prompt renderer build IDs;
- Swift app source commit, bundle build identity, and supported request/readback
  capability versions;
- canonical digest/JCS implementation version, generated operation manifest/
  operation-schema-set/error-registry digests and every wire-schema digest;
- Agent Skills upstream lock, prompt-token-budget policy/tokenizer, runtime
  constraint policy, authority-source mapping policy, workflow-source-budget
  policy, skill-pair-evaluation-budget policy, provider-sandbox/credential/
  transient-secret-memory policies, Phase 0 change policy/bootstrap receipt/full-
  gate manifest, reviewer-routing/sandbox/handoff/legacy-source policies,
  installation-bound authority-key-custody profile, resolved release-owned evaluation
  trust-policy, operation-authorization inventory, reviewer-selection handoff,
  authority-local-diagnostics contract, agent-context metric-contract set,
  native dependency-risk disposition set, proof-matrix policy,
  client-capability support-policy, rollout-projection schema/mapping/positive-
  and-negative-fixture identities and protected rollout-contract digests; each is resolved from the active
  evaluation trust policy and is not candidate input;
- exact `workflow_v2` and `agent_catalog_v2` schema digests, workflow/catalog
  source and compiled normalized-plan digests, plus compiled
  assignment-template digests for every task in every production workflow;
- catalog, role registry, permission policy, output-contract registry, public
  skill registry, complete
  sorted `SkillHostRoutingContractV1` digest set for standalone and Chainworks
  publication targets, complete
  all-pairs disposition set, semantic-neighbor graph,
  trigger-selection harness and all-pairs public declarative pair-fixture-set
  digest; the private publication receipt, split inventory, holdout commitment
  set and candidate-holdout binding are explicitly absent,
  ordered skill composition, materialized legacy-skill-migration manifest,
  runtime tool policy, Git secret and immutable workspace-snapshot policies,
  broker/proxy protocol and launch-closure policy, every provider-adapter
  credential policy, native dependency/FFI inventory, exact dependency-risk
  disposition set and provider adapter digests;
- provider, model, effort, model-parameter, and MCP/tool capability profiles;
- public suite digest, grader role identity, release-resolved promotion-policy/
  evaluator identities copied from the active evaluation trust policy for
  observation only, and the release-owned evaluation-lane retry-policy digest;
  no private holdout object or digest is present;
- required cutover and context-envelope versions.

All lists are complete, sorted sets unless a schema marks order semantic. The
core has no wildcard, mutable path, `latest`, environment-derived default, or
omitted production workflow. After the core digest exists, the evaluation
controller issues exactly one `AgentQualityTargetDeclarationV1` bound to
`candidate_id + candidate_core_sha256`. It never references the not-yet-created
manifest. The final `AgentContextCandidateManifestV1` then contains only the
candidate ID, core digest, declaration digest, resolved active trust-policy
digest and manifest schema revision. Registration validates that topological
order and stores the final manifest digest. Before registration and sample
zero, the release authority separately creates one private
`CandidateHoldoutBindingV1` over the core/declaration and the already committed
private publication/split/padded-commitment objects. The public candidate row,
manifest and every candidate/provider projection omit its ID and digest; only
the evaluation authority, vault and grader can resolve it. Registration
requires that a matching private binding exists without copying it into public
truth. Any cycle, declaration over another core, missing private binding, or
manifest created before its declaration is schema-invalid and creates no
candidate row or case lease.

The eval coordinator records the actual binary,
workflow, catalog, skill, provider, and tool identities observed for every
sample and rejects a sample whose observation differs from the candidate
manifest.

An assignment-template digest covers the static state/task purpose, done-when,
input/output contract declarations, downstream consumers, permission profile,
and ordered skill IDs; it excludes run IDs and run-specific artifact
generations. Any candidate-core or candidate-manifest digest change is behavior-affecting for
promotion purposes. This includes a workflow-only purpose, assignment,
transition, required-output, permission, or skill-order change even when no
skill or model changes. Such a change must run the complete deterministic and
five-repetition live promotion lane. A previous receipt is valid only when its
candidate manifest digest is byte-equal.

### Evaluation Ownership and Candidate State

The `evaluation_controller` purpose component inside
`ChainworksReleaseAuthorityV1` is the only writer of evaluation leases, sample
admission and aggregate receipts. Its
observed executable/build digest and principal are pinned by the active
`EvaluationTrustPolicyV1`; it is outside candidate workspaces and holds the sole
writer lease for those tables. It submits purpose-signed deterministic
transition intents through `live_passed`, but only
`candidate_lineage_controller` writes the candidate row. A candidate daemon
cannot host, replace or invoke either role. Eval workers can submit bounded
immutable sample receipts but cannot update candidate rows. The
`release_transition_controller` likewise submits later transition intents; the
same lineage controller alone CASes `live_passed -> probe_active -> promoted |
probe_failed | superseded`. The control-plane database receives signed
projections through `ReleaseAuthorityOperationV1`; it never owns or advances
those states.

The early state machine is closed:

```text
candidate_registered -> deterministic_running -> deterministic_passed
deterministic_passed -> trigger_running
trigger_running -> trigger_passed | trigger_retry_wait | rejected
trigger_retry_wait -> trigger_running | trigger_exhausted
trigger_passed -> live_pending -> live_running
live_running -> live_passed | live_retry_wait | rejected
live_retry_wait -> live_pending | live_exhausted
candidate_registered|deterministic_running|deterministic_passed|trigger_running -> rejected
candidate_registered|deterministic_running|deterministic_passed|trigger_running|trigger_retry_wait|trigger_passed|live_pending|live_running|live_retry_wait -> superseded
```

`trigger_exhausted` and `live_exhausted` are terminal non-promotable states
with no outgoing transition.

After the immutable candidate core is created and before candidate registration
or the first deterministic, trigger or live sample sequence is allocated,
the release-owned evaluation controller signs one immutable
`AgentQualityTargetDeclarationV1`. It binds preallocated candidate ID,
candidate-core digest, baseline, suite, promotion policy, exact production
profiles and retained-case inventory, and
exactly one tagged target: either a metric ID with direction and threshold, or
a retained historical failure-case identity that must pass. The declaration is
issued at an authority sequence strictly before candidate registration and
sample sequence zero and cannot be replaced for that candidate core. The final
candidate manifest and registration bind its digest;
`EvaluationWorkerLeaseV1`, every arm/sample admission,
`AgentQualityEvidenceAdmissionV1` and the final promotion receipt must repeat
it. A missing, post-sample, mismatched or candidate-selected declaration blocks
lease issuance and evidence admission. Metrics and retained cases may therefore
not be selected after results are visible.

Trigger and live retry are governed by one release-owned
`EvaluationLaneRetryPolicyV1` resolved from the active trust policy and bound by
the candidate core. Each lane permits exactly three total attempts: ordinal 1
is immediate, an infrastructure-inconclusive ordinal 1 may allocate ordinal 2
after 30 seconds, and ordinal 2 may allocate ordinal 3 after 120 seconds. The
only retryable reasons are `provider_transport_unavailable`,
`evaluation_worker_crash_reconciled`, `arm_cleanup_reconciled`, and
`external_runner_capacity`; identity mismatch, cross-arm access, behavioral
failure, unknown evidence, cleanup ambiguity, policy drift and any other reason
are terminal rejection or hold, never retry. Deadlines use the durable clock
baseline/correlation contract. No environment value, candidate field, Operator
request or Steward recommendation can raise the attempt count or shorten the
backoff.

Every lane ordinal is one immutable `EvaluationLaneAttemptV1` with a
predecessor-linked `EvaluationLaneAttemptTransitionV1`. The evaluation
controller is the sole transition-intent writer and the lineage controller is
the sole candidate-state CAS writer. One predecessor-linked
`EvaluationLaneRetryTransitionV1` consumes each terminal
`infrastructure_inconclusive` attempt. The first authority CAS records
`waiting` with the policy-derived durable deadline; after that deadline the
same transition either becomes `successor_allocated` and preallocates exactly
one next ordinal, or becomes terminal `exhausted` when the consumed attempt is
ordinal 3. Candidate `trigger_retry_wait | live_retry_wait` and
`trigger_exhausted | live_exhausted` are projections of that object, not states
of the terminal attempt. Crash or exact replay returns the same retry transition
and successor; a competing controller loses the predecessor CAS. Exhaustion
is non-promotable and has no automatic or manual retry command; another
evaluation requires a new candidate core, declaration and manifest. Restart
recovery may reconcile the same running attempt or materialize its
already-authorized successor, but cannot skip an ordinal, reopen a terminal
attempt or create a fourth attempt.

Every transition is an authority-store SQLite CAS over candidate ID/digest, expected state,
state revision, evaluation epoch, policy digest, and exact expected evidence-set
digest. Starting a lane commits its complete pair inventory and a bounded
lease. Sample identity is unique on candidate, suite, case, profile,
repetition, baseline/candidate arm, and attempt. Exact submission replay returns
the stored row; conflicting bytes fail closed. Lease expiry never implies pass
or absence of provider work. A replacement worker reconciles each expected pair
and resumes the same epoch.

Evidence admission has an independent trust boundary. The service issues one
canonical `RuntimeOwnerLeaseV1` with resource kind `evaluation_worker`,
candidate/evaluation-epoch resource identity and the generic owner-lease
transition chain. Its purpose-signed `EvaluationWorkerLeaseV1` is a bounded
readback/admission projection of that same lease, not a second lifecycle. It is
signed with the current Secure Enclave P-256 evidence-admission purpose key from
the active custody profile and delivered to a
dedicated principal-table entry with
`PrincipalClass::Agent`, stored `CallerClass::Automation` override and only
capability `AgentQualityEvidenceSubmit`. The canonical lease binds candidate and baseline
digests, the pre-sample quality-target declaration, evaluation epoch, exact pair/arm/profile/repetition inventory,
provider-sandbox policy, worker binary identity, lease epoch/deadline and key
ID. Its private key is isolated by the custody profile outside provider and
candidate workspaces; the active `EvaluationTrustPolicyV1`, not the candidate
manifest, pins the accepted public key set and rotation overlap. An expired or
superseded lease cannot submit or renew itself. Renew, absence verification and
takeover occur only through the generic runtime-owner lease controller;
takeover increments the canonical epoch after reconciling every prior attempt
and then emits a new immutable evaluation projection. No evaluator-specific
row may issue, renew, fence or take over ownership.

The evaluation controller preallocates and signs one
`EvaluationArmIsolationAdmissionV1` for **each**
`(suite, case, profile, repetition, pair, baseline_or_candidate, attempt)` before
that arm can launch. Baseline and candidate arms, different repetitions and a
retry attempt never share a runtime home, immutable workspace snapshot/view,
provider session, output namespace, broker grant, credential channel, process
group or sandbox instance. Each identity is random and purpose-scoped, all
directories are sibling-enumeration denied, and every grant/channel is bound to
only that arm's candidate digest and provider process. This prelaunch admission
contains allocated identities and canary digests only; it cannot contain an
observation, process result, sample result or cleanup fact. The worker lease
carries the complete expected admission set; launch rejects an absent, reused,
cross-arm or unrecognized identity before reading case bytes.

Each isolated namespace contains a unique signed canary unavailable to every
other arm. Pre-prompt and post-settlement probes attempt cross-read of sibling
runtime homes, workspace views, outputs, broker resources and credential
channels; any success, ambiguous result or provider-session reuse makes the
whole pair `inconclusive` and blocks promotion. Crash reconciliation revokes the
exact channel/grant/session/process first, then removes only that arm's runtime
home/workspace/output roots and emits `EvaluationArmCleanupReceiptV1`; cleanup
absence or namespace ambiguity prevents lease takeover. Neither arm can read a
sibling terminal output or grader result before both evidence admissions are
finalized.

Only after provider/process settlement and both canary probes does the
controller sign `EvaluationArmIsolationReceiptV1`. It binds the immutable
prelaunch admission, independently observed actual identity matches, probe
outcomes and terminal session/process/grant/channel facts. Exactly one terminal
