receipt may consume one admission; a missing terminal observation produces an
inconclusive missing-evidence branch, never a synthesized receipt. No object is
signed before launch with fields that can be known only after settlement.

Every public raw sample and pair aggregate binds its arm-isolation admission,
terminal isolation receipt and cleanup receipt, and the public promotion receipt
binds the complete public proof set. Private arm/sample/isolation/cleanup
identities terminate only in `PrivateHoldoutSettlementV1`; none is copied into a
public aggregate or promotion receipt. Inside the release authority/vault
boundary, promotion checks global uniqueness of all eight isolation identities
across both public evidence and every fixed private slot and rejects even byte-
identical observations produced through reused infrastructure. Retained canary,
worker-crash, retry and cleanup-failure fixtures prove no baseline/candidate,
repetition or attempt leakage without publishing private membership.

Workers receive one opaque case at a time through the trusted harness and may
submit only bounded raw observations plus provider/runtime attestations. They
cannot register or supersede candidates, compute a pass decision, alter the
expected pair inventory, read expected labels/holdout indexes, promote, probe
or open. Candidate/provider processes have no evidence-submit credential or
route. `AgentQualityEvidenceAdmissionV1` verifies the signed lease, matching
quality-target declaration, principal,
worker binary, attempt, observed candidate/provider/sandbox identities and raw
evidence digest, then computes deterministic assertions inside the evaluation
service. Writer and evaluator credentials are distinct; no artifact asserting
its own pass state is admissible. Key rotation, lease expiry, worker crash and
duplicate/conflicting submission have byte-exact fixtures.

The evaluation controller may submit a `live_passed` transition intent only in the
transaction that verifies the active evaluation trust-policy digest/epoch, the
unchanged pre-sample quality-target declaration and
all required deterministic, trigger, retained, profile and public identity
receipts plus one terminal passing private settlement; recomputes the public
aggregate from immutable public sample bytes; and writes the public promotion
receipt without a private identity. The lineage controller re-verifies the
signed intent, public rows and vault-owned settlement predicate before it alone
CASes `live_running -> live_passed`; its public event/result still omits the
settlement ID/digest/count/timing.
Incomplete or infrastructure-inconclusive trigger evidence terminally settles
the current lane attempt and produces `trigger_retry_wait` only when the signed
retry policy authorizes a successor; the same condition in the live lane
produces `live_retry_wait`. The third such settlement produces
`trigger_exhausted` or `live_exhausted`. A behavioral failure or observed
candidate-identity mismatch produces `rejected`. No file,
dashboard, Steward recommendation, LLM grader, or caller-supplied aggregate can
set those states.

### Deterministic Numeric Contract

Promotion schemas contain no JSON floating-point values. Rates, deltas,
confidence bounds, normalized grader scores, and ratios use signed integer
millionths (`fixed_decimal_micro_v1`); for example `950000` denotes 95 percent
and `1150000` denotes 115 percent of the baseline. Cost is integer micro-USD,
latency is integer milliseconds, tokens/cycles/counts are integers, and
timestamps are excluded from scoring. Multiplication uses checked signed
128-bit intermediates and division rounds ties to the even integer. Overflow
makes evidence incomplete.

Paired bootstrap version `paired_bootstrap_sha256_counter_v1` is exact:

1. order paired observations by pair ID raw bytes;
2. derive `seed = SHA256("chainworks:paired_bootstrap_seed_v1" || 0x00 ||
   policy_digest_32 || suite_digest_32 || baseline_manifest_digest_32 ||
   candidate_manifest_digest_32)`;
3. for replicate `0...9999` and draw `0...n-1`, derive each candidate word as
   the first 64 big-endian bits of `SHA256("chainworks:paired_bootstrap_v1" ||
   0x00 || seed_32 || u32be(replicate) || u32be(draw) ||
   u32be(rejection_counter))`; accept only a word below
   `floor(2^64 / n) * n`, computed in unsigned 128-bit arithmetic, then select
   `word mod n`;
4. compute the resampled mean delta in millionths with checked arithmetic and
   ties-to-even rounding;
5. sort the 10,000 integer statistics and take zero-based element 499 as the
   one-sided fifth-percentile bound.

Median for an odd count is the middle sorted integer; for an even count it is
the ties-to-even mean of the two middle values. For non-empty input, P95 uses
zero-based nearest-rank index `((95 * n + 99) / 100) - 1` with integer
division. A ratio is
`round_ties_even(candidate * 1_000_000 / baseline)`; zero-baseline handling is
the explicit rule below. Rust golden vectors include PRNG blocks, rejection,
overflow, rounding ties, medians, p95s, bootstrap arrays and final receipt
bytes. The Swift app only decodes/displays these integers; it never recomputes
promotion authority.

### Live-Eval Policy

Deterministic suites run on every relevant pull request. Live provider evals do
not run in every ordinary PR gate.

- Nightly runs three paired repetitions for every retained case and production
  provider/model/effort profile.
- Steward runs the same three-repetition lane for targeted cases after every
  completed run and observed regression.
- Promotion of any changed `AgentContextCandidateManifestV1`, including a
  workflow/assignment-only change, runs five paired repetitions for every
  retained and holdout case.
- Baseline and candidate use the same case bytes, profile, repetition index,
  model parameters, tool fixtures, and execution ordering. A sample pair is the
  atomic scoring unit.

The versioned `agent_quality_promotion_policy_v1` evaluator makes the promotion
decision. Its thresholds are normative:

1. All deterministic gates and deterministic trigger fixtures pass before live
   calls begin; the live trigger thresholds above pass before retained/holdout
   behavior is evaluated.
2. Candidate hard failures are zero across every completed sample. Provider
   refusal caused by candidate behavior, malformed output, permission misuse,
   timeout after provider admission, and contract failure are behavioral
   results, not infrastructure exclusions.
3. For first-pass artifact validity, blocker precision, false-positive rate,
   and refinement cycles, a seeded paired bootstrap with 10,000 resamples
   computes a one-sided 95 percent confidence bound. The seed is the SHA-256 of
   the policy, suite, baseline, and candidate digests. Every delta is oriented
   so positive means the candidate is better. The candidate is non-inferior
   only when the fifth percentile is at least `-20000` for rate metrics and at
   least `-250000` for refinement cycles.
4. Every candidate declares one target metric and direction before results are
   visible. A rate target must improve by at least `50000` absolute millionths
   and a cycle target by at least `500000` mean-cycle millionths; the fifth percentile of its
   improvement-oriented paired delta must be greater than zero. A correctness
   candidate may instead name one retained failure case: the baseline must
   fail at least three of five repetitions and the candidate must pass five of
   five.
5. Candidate median input-plus-output tokens, billed cost, and wall latency
   must each have a fixed-point ratio no more than `1150000`. Their p95 ratios
   must each be no more than `1250000`. A missing supported usage or cost field is
   incomplete evidence, not zero cost. If a baseline value is zero, the
   candidate value must also be zero; no ratio is synthesized.
6. A typed provider outage, rate-limit exhaustion before model admission,
   runner loss, or network failure is retried at most twice with the same pair
   identity. All attempts remain evidence. If any pair is still incomplete, or
   if baseline and candidate did not observe equivalent infrastructure, the
   decision is `inconclusive`; it can never promote.

Rules 2, 3, and 5 must pass both for the complete corpus and independently for
each production provider/model/effort profile. Rule 4 is evaluated for the
candidate's predeclared target cases and profiles. Aggregate improvement cannot
hide a regression in one production profile.

`pass`, `fail`, and `inconclusive` are the only evaluator decisions. An
inconclusive nightly or Steward lane does not fail an unrelated pull request,
but a promotion remains pending until a complete five-repetition comparison
passes. The LLM grader, when used, has a frozen provider/model/prompt/rubric
version and contributes only the declared qualitative metric; deterministic
assertions remain authoritative.

The public lane writes immutable raw public-sample receipts and one
`AgentQualityPromotionReceiptV1` **before private settlement**. Its canonical
payload contains only policy/suite/target/candidate/baseline identities, the
public `SkillPairProofSetV1` digest, exact public provider profiles and
repetition policy, public excluded/retried attempt dispositions, public
aggregate scores/confidence bounds/cost/latency ratios, public grader and
numeric/PRNG/percentile algorithm versions, public evaluation epoch, public
expected/admitted evidence-set digest, candidate-state revision and decision
`public_eligible | public_failed | public_inconclusive`. It contains no opaque
holdout digest, pair/case/envelope/lease/assignment identity, private count,
private attempt, private aggregate, private grader result, private timing or
private settlement reference. Public pair IDs remain only inside the invariant
all-pairs `SkillPairProofSetV1`; the promotion receipt does not repeat them.
Every numeric field names its integer unit in the schema, and a pure offline
evaluator reproduces the public decision from those public bytes.

The release-authority promotion transaction consumes a `public_eligible`
receipt by digest and independently checks the sibling private predicate
`PrivateHoldoutSettlementV1.state = passed` under vault-only authorization.
That lookup returns only a boolean predicate to the transaction and contributes
no ID, digest, count, outcome detail or timing to the authority operation,
public result, receipt, projection or readback. A private failure writes only a
release-private terminal settlement and creates no public promotion operation.
For the same public inputs, any two valid passing private assignments therefore
reuse byte-identical public promotion-receipt payload and public readback; the
private assignment can change only the vault-private sibling settlement. A
candidate manifest or public observed-identity mismatch makes the public
receipt invalid rather than merely stale.

### Production Proof Matrix and Client Capability

`live_passed` is necessary but does not by itself authorize production open.
`AgentContextProofMatrixV1` is derived from the immutable candidate manifest and
contains no caller-selected omissions. It inventories:

- the Cartesian product of every provider/model/effort/permission-profile
  combination referenced by a production agent with effect modes `read_only`,
  `workspace_write_staged`, `control_plane_command_fixture`, and
  `external_effect_reconcile_fixture`;
- one compatibility row for every Swift app build capability version still
  supported by the release policy, against every request, readback, cursor,
  replay and error schema required by that version;
- one live-transport row for every supported MCP start capability profile,
  covering initialize, advertised tool schemas, start selection, receipt
  binding, start, replay and closed errors against every supported daemon build;
- required sandbox, broker, output-contract, effect-reconciliation and
  projection assertions for each cell, plus the exact fixture namespace and
  expected receipt schema.

Effect fixtures run in isolated probe workspaces and an Operator/CI-owned test
namespace. They exercise prepare, apply, replay, cancellation and reconciliation
but cannot publish, push, mutate a real external system or access another run.
Every provider/effect cell must produce an observed-provider binding,
`ProviderSandboxAttestationV1`, broker/effect receipts and terminal assertion
receipt. A mode prohibited by that permission profile passes only by producing
the exact pre-effect policy denial and zero effect intent; allowed modes must
complete their declared fixture. Every app and MCP-client row must produce its
signed live-transport qualification receipt from the checked-in contract
harness. Unsupported or infrastructure-inconclusive
cells keep the matrix incomplete; removing a cell requires first removing that
profile/app/client capability from production support in a new candidate.

The proof orchestrator may execute the matrix as one fan-out proof run, but
`AgentContextProbeReceiptV1` is terminal only after it binds the matrix digest,
complete sorted cell inventory, every cell receipt and the recomputed aggregate
digest. `runtime.agent_context.promote`, probe, reprobe and open all bind the
same `proof_matrix_sha256`. A passing receipt for a subset, another generation
or another support matrix cannot open production.

`ClientCapabilitySupportPolicyV1` is release-owned and enumerates every current
Swift operation-document family and MCP start capability profile discovered
from the checked-in app/client registry. Each entry is exactly `qualified`,
`migrated`, or `retired_before_open`, with source/build identity and the daemon
versions to which that disposition applies. Candidate input cannot omit or
reclassify an entry. A current consumer absent from the policy, a supposedly
qualified consumer without a matching live receipt, or a retired profile still
advertised by the daemon makes the proof matrix incomplete.

Each supported macOS release embeds a signed `ClientCapabilityManifestV1` with
bundle/build/source and designated-requirement identity, supported request and
readback schema versions, and the proof-matrix cell that qualified it. The
checked-in Swift contract harness executes each supported operation document
against the exact daemon SDL/error/readback fixtures and, in an isolated
authenticated test database, over the real GraphQL HTTP and WebSocket
transports of every supported daemon build. Static decoding without successful
live transport execution is incomplete. The harness emits a release-signed
`ClientCapabilityQualificationReceiptV1` binding the app operation-document
digests, daemon build/SDL, transport/auth mode and observed outcomes. That
receipt is build-time proof, not a live principal credential or an input to
`runs.start`.

The support policy also enumerates closed `McpStartCapabilityProfileV1` rows,
not arbitrary client product claims. A black-box harness executes real MCP
initialize, start-selection, receipt-copy/wrong-session/expiry, `runs.start`
and exact replay vectors against each supported daemon build and emits
`McpStartCapabilityQualificationReceiptV1`. The live negotiation receipt must
match one passing profile by normalized protocol and tool-schema inventory.
`open_v2` requires one current passing receipt for every supported Swift build
and MCP start profile. Missing, stale, unsupported or schema-incomplete evidence
keeps the proof matrix incomplete. The matrix covers every supported old/new
client and daemon pair; there is no feature flag, fixture-only qualification or
optimistic fallback.

### Trusted Release Evidence Ingestion

Release evidence enters only the authority store. A job name or green-check
assertion is never sufficient. The protected base commit owns
`agent-quality-selector.yaml`, `agent-quality-gates.yaml` and the gate driver;
the release-pinned generator converts the latter into
`AgentQualityGateManifestV1`. A pull-request head cannot replace or weaken
those bytes. The manifest fixes driver/build digest, exact ordered argv for
every constituent command, bounded environment-name/value policy, required
suite/test IDs and minimum observed count, expected artifacts and terminal
outcomes. Empty selection, skipped command, zero discovered tests, unknown test
ID, early-success/no-op branch, output truncation or missing receipt is a failed
gate, never a passing selection.

`AgentQualityCiSelectionV1` is a closed tagged union. The `executed` arm has a
second closed discriminator `execution_trigger = governed_path_match |
release_candidate_forced`. `governed_path_match` requires a nonempty governed-
path match set. `release_candidate_forced` requires an empty match set, the
protected-base classification proof and one release-candidate request for the
exact repository/base/head; it is forbidden in an ordinary pull-request
selector run. Both executed triggers require the exact gate-manifest digest and one passing
`AgentQualityGateExecutionReceiptV1`. The CI runner emits one immutable
machine-readable command event before and after each process and one test-
discovery/result event per required suite. The GitHub artifact attestation
covers the protected-base driver and manifest, repository/base/head/merge-base,
exact argv/environment digests, expected and observed test IDs/counts, per-
command exit/status/start/end, and every output/artifact digest. The release-
owned `ci_evidence_collector` verifies those events against the manifest and
signs the execution receipt; it cannot synthesize a missing event or turn a
nonzero/zero-test/skipped outcome into pass.

The `not_applicable` arm requires an empty governed match set and the complete
protected-base path-classification proof and forbids both gate-manifest and
execution-receipt fields. It may satisfy the always-present branch check for an
unrelated pull request, but it is never agent-context release evidence:
candidate registration, `live_passed`, release-evidence selection, bundle
issuance, promote and open all require an `executed` arm for the exact head.
Changing a governed path to ungoverned, omitting an unclassified path or
supplying either forbidden gate field invalidates the selection.

Before candidate registration or live evaluation consumes an unrelated-only
HEAD, the release-owned `ci_release_candidate_dispatcher` consumes one
authority-approved exact-head request and dispatches a protected reusable
workflow pinned by repository ID, protected-base workflow ref/digest and gate
manifest. It has no evidence key. The workflow checks out that exact HEAD read-only, executes every
manifest command and emits a `release_candidate_forced` selection plus normal
passing execution receipt. The candidate cannot request, edit or attest this
run. Repository/base/head mismatch, empty test discovery, skipped command or a
head-controlled workflow performs no candidate registration. The read-only
collector only verifies the resulting run and cannot dispatch or rerun it.
Thus the branch
check may remain `not_applicable`, while release evidence for the same exact
HEAD has a protected executed path and never treats N/A as proof.

The `evaluation_controller` verifies the GitHub artifact attestation for that
selection against the pinned issuer/JWKS, protected workflow path and digest,
repository, base/head and job/run claims before insertion. The release-owned
read-only `ci_evidence_collector` GitHub App submits
`BranchProtectionReceiptV1` under its pinned collector principal and
evidence-purpose key; the authority revalidates repository/ruleset/head/check/
ETag, finalized activation-journal identity, signature and expiry. The `alert_sampler` writes only the policy-
bound alert snapshot under its own writer lease; the independent
`incident_controller` derives and writes the current unresolved-incident set.
Candidate, PR workflow, ordinary daemon and Operator payloads cannot insert or
choose any of these rows.

The required `CI / agent-quality` branch check is installed through one staged
`BranchProtectionActivationJournalV1`, not an unversioned settings write. The
release-owned `branch_protection_activation_controller` uses a dedicated
GitHub App installation and credential with Administration write to read the
authenticated current ruleset preimage and ETag, prepare the exact additive
required-check patch, then apply it with `If-Match`. It rereads the ruleset and
records the observed postimage in the journal, but it has no evidence-signing
key and cannot create or insert `BranchProtectionReceiptV1`. After journal
finalization, the separately designated `ci_evidence_collector` uses a distinct
read-only GitHub App installation and credential to reread the exact ruleset,
ETag, HEAD, required check and protected workflow and then signs the receipt
linked to that finalized journal. The collector has no Administration write
and cannot invoke the activation endpoint. The authority accepts only that
collector-signed receipt. A concurrent ruleset edit, missing check, changed
workflow, same installation or credential on both sides, activator-signed
receipt, or third state enters a release hold. Before any candidate or release-
evidence issuance or selection depends on the postimage, a failed installation
may restore the exact
authenticated preimage with a second writer-App ETag CAS recorded in the same journal.
After candidate or release-evidence adoption, or after authority migration,
automatic removal is forbidden: repair is forward-only and the
mandatory check remains required. There is no disable, permissive, waiver or
caller-selected bypass path. Fixtures cover prepare crash, CAS loss, observed
third state, pre-adoption exact-preimage restore, post-adoption attempted
removal denial, same-App credential reuse, activator-signed evidence,
collector write attempt and wrong installation/process/key identity.

This proposal's current proposal-readiness declaration is the single sidecar
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-agent-mission-context-skills-evals-design.rollout-contract.json`.
It is the proposal-level `rollout_contract_v1` consumed by
`scripts/lint-rollout-contract`; no duplicate inline object exists. Its gates,
migrations, metrics, four readback lanes, hold conditions, forward-repair
disposition and negative fixtures must validate during proposal review. This
existing linter is the only executable command required to declare the design
ready. The two proposal-specific aliases and their runtime-aware adapter do not
exist yet and are Phase 0 implementation deliverables. Proposal readiness does
not pretend that an absent future alias has passed.

The chain begins with **Phase -2 foundation**, because approved HEAD has no
release-authority gateway, authority store, purpose-key registry or active-gate
pointer that a later phase may assume. A protected predecessor change carries
only `AgentContextBootstrapExternalTrustPolicyV1`,
`AgentContextBootstrapFoundationManifestV1`, the protected bootstrap-operation
manifest, minimum gateway/coordinator/store/bootstrap helpers, their focused
tests and existing required-check wiring. The external policy is fixed in the
approved commit and pins GitHub's exact issuer/JWKS algorithms and key IDs,
system-TLS policy, repository/workflow/ref/audience/subject/job/event claims,
protected-ruleset readback, reviewer-registry source/digest and 900-second
freshness. The foundation manifest is authenticated by those current signed
OIDC/artifact/check/merge and ruleset bytes rather than by a not-yet-created
Chainworks authority.
`AgentContextBootstrapFoundationReviewReceiptV1` requires at least two distinct
authorized approving reviewer principals and credential epochs; neither may be
the installer, collector or later attestor, share their signing key, or approve
their own patch. Missing quorum, stale ruleset/head, same principal/key or a
changed diff performs no installation. The receipt is only a canonical index
over the original evidence. The sole `authority_installation_bootstrap` helper
independently revalidates every signed evidence byte and claim, recomputes the
receipt, and consumes the manifest-bound one-use nonce before its first external
action; it never trusts a verifier boolean or unsigned handoff.

That helper executes the exact reviewed manifest through a one-time launchd job
and persists the single `AuthorityInstallationBootstrapJournalV1` logical
lineage across marker, root-key, store, purpose-key, anchor, gateway,
bootstrap-operation-manifest and sentinel steps. Before root creation the exact
evidence/manifest/nonce-bound Keychain marker and deterministic root tag are the
physical recovery representation; after root observation the same logical rows
are materialized and every successor is root-signed. No second foundation
journal exists. The only pointer created by installation is the fixed
`foundation_sentinel` `AgentContextGatePointerV1` at revision one. A distinct
read-only `bootstrap_foundation_attestor` reobserves
the installed designated requirements, store genesis, root and purpose-key
epochs, anchor, bootstrap-operation manifest and exact sentinel bytes and signs
`AgentContextBootstrapFoundationReceiptV1` under the dedicated foundation-
attestation purpose. The installer cannot review or attest; the reviewers and
attestor cannot install, write the store or advance the pointer. Crash/replay/
concurrency at every syscall converges to one foundation lineage or
`reconciliation_required`, never a second root, store, pointer or gateway.

`AgentContextBootstrapOperationManifestV1` is the sole callable-contract owner
before the production operation registry exists. It exact-sets the seven Phase
-2/-1 launchd/private-XPC operations, each request/result/error triplet,
authenticated peer, resource resolver and replay policy. The manifest bytes are
part of the foundation review/install/receipt and cannot be changed by Phase -1
or candidate code. Migration later imports every row, triplet and policy
byte-identically into `operations.yaml` under disposition
`frozen_bootstrap_compatibility`; an omitted, duplicated or changed import fails
generation before serve.

Phase 0 has a separate predecessor-linked
`AgentContextBootstrapGateManifestV1`, but the current rollout linter is only
the proposal-readiness checker and is not its executor. Before any candidate
branch is admitted, release engineering installs one separately attested
`agent_context_phase0_bootstrap_controller` from the protected predecessor
revision after the foundation receipt is current. It runs outside the candidate
checkout and consumes the manifest through the now-installed minimal release-
authority gateway. Its executable/build, signer and
`AgentContextPhase0ChangePolicyV1` are pinned by protected-base CI and branch
protection. This is a distinct precursor change: its source/policy are reviewed,
gated and merged to protected base under the pre-existing repository gates, then
its resulting commit/build/attestation becomes the predecessor of every Phase 0
implementation branch. Controller/policy bytes may not appear in the Phase 0 or
full candidate diff, and the precursor cannot contain an agent-context runtime,
schema, migration or candidate implementation. The candidate branch, ordinary daemon, provider and Operator cannot
replace that controller or policy, select their digest, or authorize a policy
change. A change to the controller or policy requires a new predecessor review,
independent controller attestation and the complete full gate; it cannot be
bootstrapped by the revision it would authorize.

That controller precursor is **Phase -1** and has its own exact installation
gate. Its
only admitted diff is the controller executable/source, the closed
`AgentContextPhase0ChangePolicyV1`, their focused tests and the pre-existing
required-check wiring; the Phase -1 gate exact-sets the complete diff and runs
without any candidate-supplied policy. After merge, a release-owned read-only
collector independently rereads protected HEAD, the required-check ruleset,
the current foundation receipt/sentinel pointer and the installed signed
controller, then emits one keyless immutable
`AgentContextPhaseMinusOneObservationV1`. The collector cannot sign a review or
attestation, install the controller or classify a Phase 0 diff. A separate
`phase_minus_one_review_authority` verifies the typed foundation receipt,
distinct reviewer quorum and exact collector observation, signs the
`AgentContextPhaseMinusOneReviewReceiptV1`, and then signs the sole
`AgentContextPhaseMinusOneAttestationV1`. The attestation binds that review
receipt and observation plus repository/base commit, passing CI receipt,
ruleset revision/ETag, controller source/build/designated requirement,
change-policy digest and dedicated purpose-key epoch. The review authority is
not a reviewer, installer or collector and has no other signing family. A
protected required-check readback must prove that exact attestation current
before a candidate can create a
full-gate core or bootstrap manifest. Missing, stale, wrong-HEAD, self-signed,
same-principal, changed-ruleset or changed-controller evidence creates zero
Phase 0 work and leaves the active gate pointer at the foundation sentinel.

The bootstrap manifest carries four runtime fields rather than embedding a
self-referential literal in this document: exact approved proposal
bytes/SHA-256, sidecar bytes/SHA-256, positive fixture bytes/SHA-256 and
negative fixture bytes/SHA-256. It also binds the predecessor review receipt,
existing linter build, expected `aliases_absent / adapter_absent` prestate,
external controller/policy identities and two domain-separated fixture
submanifest digests. The projection submanifest is exactly JCS of
`{"schema_version":"agent_context_rollout_projection_mutation_manifest_v1","cases":[...]}`
where `cases` is the ordered sixteen-case array from the negative fixture; its
digest is `SHA256("chainworks:agent_context_rollout_projection_mutation_manifest_v1" ||
0x00 || JCS(payload))`. The preflight submanifest is exactly JCS of
`{"schema_version":"agent_context_mandatory_preflight_manifest_v1","cases":[...]}`
where `cases` is the ordered six-case array from that fixture; its digest is
`SHA256("chainworks:agent_context_mandatory_preflight_manifest_v1" || 0x00 ||
JCS(payload))`. Array order and every case byte are authoritative; a raw array
hash, schema-free wrapper or differently ordered reconstruction is invalid.

`AgentContextPhase0ChangePolicyV1` is an exhaustive classifier over the complete
candidate diff against its protected predecessor. Each changed path appears
exactly once with canonical relative path, file identity, action
`create | modify | delete | rename_from | rename_to`, and one closed
disposition. The only allowed dispositions name creation or update of the two
`scripts/test-gate.sh` aliases, their one shared adapter/validator, generated
gate manifests, directly named tests/fixtures and the matching
`docs/reference/test-gates.md` entry. Runtime behavior, database migrations,
public schemas, candidates, providers, catalogs, workflows, release policy,
the bootstrap controller/policy themselves, deletions, unpaired renames,
symlinks, hardlinks, submodules and every unclassified path/action are denied.
The controller enumerates the complete diff independently, proves exact-set
equality with the classified rows and rejects duplicate, missing or extra rows
before any write. Repository CI applies the same protected-base policy to every
changed path; no catch-all or caller-selected exemption exists.

Before bootstrap execution, the protected generator creates one immutable
`AgentContextFullGateManifestCoreV1`. The core binds the same approved proposal,
sidecar and fixture SHA-256 values, both submanifest digests, both intended
aliases, their one shared adapter revision, all ordered commands/selectors,
producer/schema/operation manifests and the sole passing result tuple. It
contains no Phase -1 attestation, bootstrap manifest, bootstrap receipt, active
pointer or full-activation digest. The bootstrap manifest binds that already
computed core digest; neither object can point to a future receipt. Before
executing its changed-file actions, the gate-pointer controller persists
one `AgentContextGatePointerCasIntentV1` containing only the exact foundation-
sentinel predecessor and bootstrap-manifest successor, then CASes to a new
`AgentContextGatePointerV1` that references that pre-CAS intent. After
independent pointer readback it writes
`AgentContextGatePointerCasReceiptV1`, which references both intent and final
pointer; the pointer never references the receipt. Only that committed pointer
plus matching receipt admits bootstrap execution. CAS loss, crash, replay or a
concurrent manifest leaves either the exact sentinel or the one expected
bootstrap pointer and recovery finalizes the same receipt or records
`reconciliation_required`; it creates no ordinary work.

Bootstrap completion writes one immutable
`AgentContextBootstrapGateReceiptV1` through the release authority. The receipt
binds the Phase -1 attestation, bootstrap manifest, unchanged core digest,
observed four artifact SHA-256 values, both reconstructed domain-separated
submanifest digests, the exhaustive changed-file/action set and the committed
sentinel-to-bootstrap CAS intent/pointer/receipt tuple. It contains no full-
manifest digest. Only
after that receipt is finalized does the authority
construct `AgentContextFullGateManifestV1` as a thin activation envelope over
the same core plus that receipt, then persists a second pre-CAS intent and
CASes the active pointer from the exact bootstrap-manifest revision/digest to a
full-manifest pointer referencing only that intent. Independent readback emits
the second post-CAS receipt. The activation envelope
cannot add or replace a command, selector, policy, adapter or artifact identity.
In the bootstrap transaction the authority requires both aliases to resolve
physically to the core's shared adapter, validates the complete projection/
preflight fixture contents, and records their observed digests and nonzero
selector inventory. Ordinary Chainworks implementation work remains held until
the later activation-pointer CAS is finalized. It never treats unimplemented
later-phase selectors as passing. Full-manifest activation authorizes only the
next declared implementation phase; each phase transition executes and passes
its predecessor selector subset, while final closeout requires every selector
in the core. A crash before the first CAS leaves the sentinel; a crash after it
resumes the same bootstrap manifest. A crash before receipt finalize resumes
bootstrap, a crash between receipt and full activation resumes construction/
the second CAS of the unique envelope, and a crash after the second CAS replays
the same core/receipt/full-manifest identity. The singleton pointer names
exactly one of foundation sentinel, bootstrap manifest or full manifest at
every committed revision; no state can activate two targets or infer activation
from file presence.

The resulting acyclic trust order is exactly `approved-HEAD external evidence
-> sole Phase -2 authority-installation journal/foundation receipt/sentinel ->
Phase -1 observation/review/attestation -> full-gate manifest core -> bootstrap
manifest -> first CAS intent -> bootstrap pointer -> first CAS receipt ->
bootstrap receipt -> full-manifest activation -> second CAS intent -> full
pointer -> second CAS receipt`. An unknown alias, string-only name scan,
environment-skipped required command, unbound revision, digest mismatch or
divergent alias digest fails before activation and creates no runtime/schema/
migration/candidate row.
Its final closeout branch executes, in order:

1. `scripts/lint-rollout-contract` on the sole sidecar;
2. current producer generation and exact four-lane/nullable-variant validation;
3. all sixteen digest-bound projection mutations and all six mandatory-
   preflight cases with exact producer records, reasons and zero-work assertions;
4. normative schema, canonical-digest, generated operation exact-set and
   GraphQL/MCP/Swift projection checks;
5. deterministic Rust/Swift authority, attempt/effect, reviewer-isolation,
   credential/helper, path-confinement, authorization, migration, metrics,
   security and crash/replay selectors declared by this proposal.

The sole final passing tuple is `status = pass`, `decision = release`,
`enforcement_mode = enforce`, `waiver_state = none`,
`enabled_state = enabled`, `disabled_reason_code = absent`, no hold condition,
current projection integrity and zero skipped required selectors. For this
proposal ID and its runtime successor policy, real producer records for
`waived/waive`, `not_applicable/not_applicable`,
`pass/release + permissive`, and
`not_applicable/not_applicable + disabled` are inadmissible even when generic
P084 preflight would allow them. The proposal adapter returns
`agent_context_mandatory_rollout_policy_violation`, holds scheduling/open and
creates no implementation work. Six separately digest-bound cases cover
missing alias with installed adapter, installed aliases with missing adapter,
and those four producer-faithful relaxed states. Every case requires
`decision = hold`, `implementation_work_rows = 0` and a complete four-lane
readback whose only next step is `repair_rollout_contract`. The readback must
not surface waiver, disable, permissive or bypass guidance even when the nested
legacy producer record contains it. After bootstrap begins,
an absent alias or adapter is `missing_contract`; it cannot be combined into a
single synthetic case or treated as a passing implementation gate.

The referenced fixture is
`agent_context_rollout_projection_fixture_v1`, not a synthetic replacement for
the existing `operator_readback_v1`. It contains exactly four complete payload
objects under `parity_lanes`: `run_report`, `mcp`, `release_receipt`, and
`graphql`. Every lane is one `agent_context_rollout_projection_v1` object with
exactly the sidecar field inventory. Its nested `operator_readback` is the
complete, unmodified output of the current
`RolloutContractCheck::operator_readback_json_for_lane(...)` producer,
including `schema_version = operator_readback_v1`, authoritative record/run/
proposal metadata, waiver/adoption/update metadata and the P083 compatibility
fields. The first three lanes retain the producer's snake-case object. GraphQL
stores the exact current generated camel-case producer projection under
`operatorReadback`, including the producer's intentionally unchanged legacy
snake-case compatibility keys. The existing Swift run-report and GraphQL DTOs
must decode those nested bytes; a proposal-only decoder is not proof.

The outer prefixed fields are temporary `rollout_contract_v1` sidecar
compatibility aliases, never decision authority. The fixed mapping version is
`operator_readback_v1_to_agent_context_rollout_projection_v1`:

| Compatibility alias | Sole canonical `operator_readback_v1` source |
|---|---|
| `rollout_contract_status` | `status` |
| `rollout_contract_decision` | `backend_decision` |
| `rollout_contract_failure_reasons` | `failure_reasons` |
| `rollout_contract_waiver_state` | `waiver_state` |
| `rollout_contract_waiver_expires_at` | `waiver_expires_at` |
| `rollout_contract_enforcement_mode` | `enforcement_mode` |
| `rollout_contract_enforcement_mode_reason` | `enforcement_mode_reason` |
| `rollout_contract_hold_conditions` | `hold_conditions` |
| `rollout_contract_rollback_disposition` | complete `rollback_disposition` |
| `rollout_contract_source_lane` | `source_lane` |
| `rollout_contract_enabled_state` | `enabled_state` |
| `rollout_contract_disabled_reason_code` | `disabled_reason_code` |
| `rollout_contract_action_id` | `action_id` |
| `rollout_contract_operator_message` | `operator_message` |
| `rollout_contract_projection_integrity` | `projection_integrity` |
| `rollout_contract_cutover_policy_revision` | `cutover_policy_revision` |
| `rollout_contract_diagnostic_redaction` | `diagnostic_redaction` |
| `rollout_contract_next_steps` | mandatory-policy adapter over producer `next_steps`; output is exactly `repair_rollout_contract` for every held mandatory-policy case and never includes waiver/disable/permissive/bypass guidance |

The projection generator first obtains the canonical lane payload from that
single producer, then derives every alias from this table. It cannot accept
caller-supplied alias values. All aliases except `rollout_contract_next_steps`
are direct mappings. The mandatory
`AgentContextMandatoryRolloutReadbackPolicyV1` adapter consumes the preserved
producer `next_steps`, backend decision and hold reason and emits a repair-only
V2 next-step set. It maps any legacy
`repair_rollout_contract_or_apply_privileged_waiver`, waiver, disable,
permissive or bypass suggestion to exactly `repair_rollout_contract`; it can
never add authority or suppress the hold. The nested `operator_readback_v1`
bytes remain unmodified compatibility evidence, but no V2 operator-facing
surface presents their forbidden recovery suggestion as an allowed action.
GraphQL applies the existing producer camel-case
adapter and the generated outer adapter; reverse normalization must reproduce
the exact nested snake-case semantics. Thus no producer field is dropped, the
policy-derived next-step field is checked against the signed adapter revision,
the remaining alias set cannot drift independently, and `rollout_contract_v1` compatibility
does not rename the public runtime contract. Removing aliases requires a future
`rollout_contract_v2` sidecar migration and does not alter
`operator_readback_v1`.

`diagnostic_redaction` and its alias use only `none | partial | full`; this
fixture uses `partial`. The retained validator requires exact lane and field
sets, correct lane-native casing, canonical nested producer schema/field sets,
alias recomputation, recursive semantic equality for every non-source field and
the exact lane-specific source value. The generated producer matrix also emits
a nullable variant with `cutover_policy_revision = null` and all other declared
producer nullable fields null, then proves the exact snake-case and GraphQL
compatibility keys remain present rather than omitted or synthesized. The
checked-in negative set binds the positive fixture SHA-256 and the canonical
digest of its ordered mutation manifest. Its sixteen closed projection mutations cover:
array shape, missing lane, extra lane, missing field, extra field, wrong
top-level GraphQL casing, wrong nested rollback-discriminator casing, invalid
enum, duplicate normalized key, semantic divergence, missing producer rollback
schema, sidecar rollback-step drift, producer-message drift, P083 rollback-TTL
recasing, P083 preflight-hash omission and a snake/camel duplicate P083 key.
Each has one closed expected reason; both gate aliases must execute all sixteen and fail if a mutation passes, returns
another reason, is skipped or is absent from the gate manifest. Adding,
removing or reordering a case requires new fixture, mutation-manifest and gate-
manifest digests. The same file separately binds six producer-faithful
`agent_context_mandatory_preflight_validator_v1` cases: missing alias with the
adapter installed, missing adapter with aliases installed, `waived/waive`,
`not_applicable/not_applicable`, `pass/release + permissive`, and
`not_applicable/not_applicable + disabled`. They have their own canonical
manifest digest. Each case also carries one generated readback-set digest over
all four complete lane-native payloads and asserts identical hold/reason/zero-
work/repair-only semantics, presence of all four lanes and absence of every
forbidden next step. Projection and scheduling mutations are never counted as
one interchangeable corpus.

The protected base also owns
`docs/reference/agent-context/rollout-contract.yaml`. The release generator
normalizes it into signed `AgentContextReleaseRolloutPolicyV1`; candidate/PR bytes, an Operator
request and the active signal-policy publisher cannot replace or weaken it. The
contract binds its repository/base/commit/tree and publisher, the compatible
rollout-signal-policy family, the maximum active signal window, minimum soak,
required sample spacing/completeness, restart treatment and required terminal
healthy state. Generation fails unless `minimum_soak_seconds` is at least the
maximum window of every active signal used for open; V1 permits no disable,
waive, zero-duration or caller-selected override. Candidate registration,
evaluation trust, release-evidence selection/bundle and open all bind the exact
`agent_context_release_rollout_policy_sha256`.

`AgentQualityCiSelectionV1` and its gate-execution receipt are immutable and do
not expire merely because wall time advances. They are live-eligible only for
the exact repository/base/head/workflow/gate-manifest/native-build-policy tuple
and accepted collector/key/policy epochs recorded in the receipt. A changed
HEAD, workflow/manifest/policy digest, revoked attestation/collector key or
invalidated native-build confinement receipt is a mismatch/revocation, not
time-based expiry, and requires a new CI run. By contrast,
`BranchProtectionReceiptV1` has a normative 15-minute deadline because ruleset,
ETag and required-check state are mutable. Its collector records the current
durable clock-baseline ID/revision, monotonic issue tick and fixed 900-second
budget. Selection computes age from that baseline; after restart or baseline
rollover it requires a signed `RolloutClockCorrelationReceiptV1` whose
conservative lower bound cannot move the issue time forward and whose upper
bound must remain within the budget. Unknown correlation, wall-clock rollback,
forward jump beyond budget or boot identity without a correlation receipt makes
the branch receipt stale. The release-evidence bundle remains one-use with its
30-second deadline. Deterministic fixtures select the same CI
receipt immediately before and after arbitrary wall-clock advance and daemon
restart, then change each exact identity and revoke its key. Only the identity/
revocation cases fail; a branch receipt fails on identity drift, deadline,
unknown baseline or non-conservative correlation.

Release-evidence selection and bundle issuance accept only the exact `executed`
selection arm and include its gate-manifest and execution-receipt digests.
Retained CI vectors mutate the PR-head selector,
skip each constituent command, discover zero/too few/wrong tests, return success
after an inner failure, omit an artifact, submit `not_applicable` as promotion
evidence and replay another base/head receipt; all are rejected before
selection becomes eligible. A real protected-base run executes every manifest
command and proves the advertised nonzero test counts.

For each `promote` or `open`, an Operator first calls the read-only
`runtime.agent_context.release_evidence.selection.get`. It returns the complete
current signed selection, eligibility and closed blocker codes from one
authority-store read transaction; it returns no token and accepts no caller-
selected evidence rows. The selection includes canonical decimal
`issuance_generation` and the current issuance state
`none | available | reserved_for_operation | consumed | expired`. Issuance and
terminal settlement do not share one transition rule: `issue` changes `none`
to `available` within the current generation, while only terminal `consumed` or
`expired` settlement appends generation `g+1` in `none` before another token can
be issued. Both arms
bind the protected rollout contract. The `promote` arm omits soak fields; the
`open` arm is ineligible unless the latest terminal soak receipt is `passed`,
matches candidate/generation/probe/policy/contract exactly, covers at least the
contract minimum by conservative clock lower bound, has a complete healthy
sample sequence and names the current empty unresolved-incident set. The
Operator submits those exact nested bytes to
`runtime.agent_context.release_evidence.issue`. The issue command is served by the
release gateway and `release_transition_controller` while the candidate is
stopped. Its authority-only operation reserves the exact transition/candidate/
cutover/evidence tuple and one nonce, rechecks the complete evidence revision,
rollout contract and conditional open-soak receipt in
one authority-store transaction, appends the issuance event through the anchor
sequencer, and returns one compact signed
`ReleasePromotionEvidenceBundleV1` token plus
`ReleaseEvidenceBundleIssueReceiptV1`. No filesystem step, hidden CLI, direct
SQLite edit or candidate RPC can mint or discover a bundle. Exact request replay
always returns the original historical logical result, even when its token is
now consumed or expired; that replay does not make the token reusable. A
different request may join/alias only the same current generation while its
issuance is `available`. Once consumed or expired, a different request carrying
the old selection is `stale_precondition` with zero mutation. The Operator must
call selection GET again to obtain the incremented generation and then issue a
new request. Generic semantic alias lookup is therefore bounded by one current
one-use issuance generation and can never resurrect a terminal token.

The canonical lifecycle is an append-only
`ReleaseEvidenceIssuanceStateV1` chain per transition/candidate/cutover
semantic key:

```text
generation g: none -> available -> reserved_for_operation -> consumed
generation g: none -> available -> expired
generation g: reserved_for_operation -> available  [abort before control-plane commit and deadline still valid]
generation g: reserved_for_operation -> expired    [abort before control-plane commit and deadline elapsed]
terminal generation g -> generation g+1: none
```

The generated transition-truth fixture enumerates every legal edge with
pre/post generation, state, predecessor digest and token identity. In
particular `issue` asserts `(g, none) -> (g, available)`, reserve and pre-commit
abort retain `g`, and only finalized consume/expiry assert `(g, terminal) ->
(g+1, none)`. Any implementation or prose-derived vector that advances on
issue, reuses a terminal generation or publishes two `available` rows fails
both rollout gate aliases.

Issue atomically appends `available` with exact bundle/issue receipt, correlated
durable clock-baseline ID, monotonic issue tick and 30-second deadline budget.
Promote/open authority prepare must CAS that exact available revision to
`reserved_for_operation`, binding operation ID and the already-established
deadline before any control-plane commit. While the operation is
`prepared | control_plane_committed | anchor_pending`, the expiry controller
cannot select or expire that issuance and no second operation can consume it.
If the operation aborts before control-plane commit, the same abort transaction
releases it to `available` when the deadline remains valid, or lets the expiry
transition win when correlated time is at/after the deadline. Once
`control_plane_committed`, the reserved operation must finalize the same
`consumed` revision even if the deadline passes: eligibility was linearized at
reserve and cannot be stranded by expiry. Authority finalize appends its
`consumed` revision plus generation `g+1` in `none`. The independent
`release_evidence_issuance_controller` owns a canonical
`release_evidence_expiry_lease`; after restart it scans only finalized available
rows, correlates their stored baseline to the current monotonic baseline using
the P083 durable-clock relation, and prepares one authority-only expiry
operation when the stored budget is exhausted and the row is still
`available`. Finalize CASes the exact generation/revision/digest from
`available` to `expired`, writes one signed
`ReleaseEvidenceIssuanceExpiryReceiptV1`, advances the anchor, and creates
generation `g+1` in `none` in the same transaction.

Consumption and expiry reserve the same issuance key, so exactly one can win;
the loser observes the terminal signed revision and performs zero mutation.
Controller crash at prepare, anchor-pending or finalize resumes that exact
operation ID and cannot advance another generation. Lease takeover requires
deadline plus owner-absence proof and a higher lease epoch. Wall-clock changes,
GET/list calls, token verification and exact replay never settle expiry or
advance a generation. Historical exact issue replay continues to return the
original signed result for audit, but live authorization consults the current
issuance chain and rejects that terminal token. Restart, baseline rollover,
T-1/T/T+1 reserve-versus-expiry races, abort before control-plane commit, crash
in every authority phase and double-controller fixtures prove one and only one
terminal transition and one successor generation; a reserved
`control_plane_committed` operation is never expired or stranded.

Operator-only `runtime.agent_context.release_evidence.issuance.get` reads the
same authority transaction and exposes the exact issuance state/digest,
deadline/baseline relation and expiry-controller owner plus lease
ID/epoch/revision/digest. If the controller is stopped, its lease is expired and
the exact owner-absence receipt is available, the sole allowed mutating next
action is `runtime.agent_context.release_evidence.expiry.reconcile`. That command
accepts the complete readback identities and no desired outcome. It reserves the
issuance, old lease and absence receipt together, installs one higher controller
lease epoch, and runs the same expiry operation. Finalize consumes the receipt,
marks generation `g` expired and creates exactly one `g+1 / none`; exact replay
returns those bytes. A live/ambiguous owner, renewed or mismatched lease,
unexpired budget, consumed issuance or stale generation performs zero mutation.
The readback and repair operations are served by the release gateway while the
candidate is stopped and do not depend on the missing controller process.
Fault fixtures kill the controller before scan, after reservation, after anchor
and before successor projection and prove one terminal expiry plus one successor
generation through northbound readback alone.

The token uses the same canonical base64url/JCS/P-256 raw-low-`s` framing and
active custody-profile rules as the run-start token but signature domain
`chainworks.release-evidence.v1`. Its payload binds transition kind, one-use
nonce, authority trust/writer epoch, custody-profile/signing-key epoch and evidence revision, candidate/promotion/
proof-matrix digests, exact repository/base/head/workflow/job CI selection,
quality-gate manifest/execution receipt, branch-protection/ruleset/ETag
receipt, current healthy alert snapshot,
active rollout-signal-policy digest, empty unresolved-incident-set digest,
expected cutover generation/revision and
probe epoch where applicable, issue time and 30-second expiry. A bundle for one
transition or expected revision is invalid for another.

The release authority executes the transition while the ordinary daemon is
stopped. One short authority-store prepare transaction verifies the bundle
signature/canonical bytes and every selected immutable row, freshness,
candidate/head/ruleset/alert/incident/cutover expectation, then writes the
prepared `ReleaseAuthorityOperationV1`, complete sorted resource reservations
and `AuthorityEvidenceFenceV1`. That transaction commits before any external
call; no `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` lock crosses XPC, another SQLite store, Keychain or
filesystem I/O. The phase-selected control-plane writer then
commits only that prepared operation digest, a `pending_finalize`
cutover/generation projection, all component digests, the canonical command
outcome core, and audit/projection intents. It does not consume the bundle or
advance candidate/admission truth. Authority finalize verifies that committed
row in a new transaction, revalidates the durable evidence fence and
reservations, asks the candidate-lineage
controller to sign the canonical candidate CAS, and writes the bundle
consumption, admission transition, signed state event and projection outbox as
`pending_anchor`. The anchor sequencer then performs the sole serialized
Keychain read/update/read, and
the final coordinator transaction makes those rows servable and releases both
the evidence fence and resource reservations. The gateway returns no success
before that finalized exact-request record. Crash before the control-plane commit permits only
`aborted_before_commit`; crash after it can only finalize the same immutable
operation and cannot repeat the transition. A concurrent evidence update waits,
or fails its conflicting fence check, then creates a higher evidence revision
after finalize and, when applicable, an immediate hold/incident. Unrelated
evidence keys may advance without violating the complete selected-row fence.

Wrong head/candidate, mismatched or revoked CI evidence, expired branch receipt,
changed ruleset/ETag already
ingested before the fence, stale/unknown/firing alert, nonempty incident set,
bundle replay or evidence-revision drift performs zero control-plane mutation.
The cutover singleton/readback exposes bundle, CI selection, quality-gate
manifest/execution, branch protection, rollout policy, alert snapshot,
incident-set, notification-watchdog alert and authority-evidence-revision
digests for both the promote and open transitions.

### Production Promotion and Cutover

Promotion state is durable rather than inferred from files or the currently
running app. The evaluation controller may submit intents for the early states
defined above; the release-transition controller may submit only these later
intents, and the candidate-lineage controller remains the sole state writer:

```text
live_passed -> probe_active -> promoted
promoted -> probe_active  [runtime.agent_context.reprobe only]
probe_active -> probe_failed -> superseded
live_passed|probe_failed -> superseded
```

Only the MCP command `runtime.agent_context.promote`, protected by the
`RuntimeAgentContextPromote` capability and the northbound boundary matrix, may
move a `live_passed` candidate to `probe_active`. It requires both request IDs,
candidate ID and digest, passing receipt digest, expected candidate state,
proof-matrix digest, cutover generation/revision and a fresh promote-scoped
release-evidence bundle token. The release authority, not the candidate daemon,
executes the command and
recomputes the matrix from the candidate and production support registries; a
caller cannot select or omit cells. The command-specific fields in the
intent table, never either request ID, form its semantic hash. Authority
prepare records the candidate CAS, evidence set and one
`AgentContextProofAdmissionV1` in state `available`; the control-plane commit
records catalog/skill heads, evidence-component projections, generation row,
cutover marker and canonical outcome core; authority finalize then advances
the canonical candidate and consumes the evidence bundle under the operation
protocol above. No success is visible between those phases.
The result and singleton readback expose that proof admission ID. Replay returns
the original admission; stale generation, mismatched intent, unauthorized
caller, concurrent loser, or a non-passing receipt fails without changing
production truth.

The control-plane SQLite projection owns one singleton
`agent_context_cutover_v1` row for runtime fencing and readback. Every mutation
of that row is bound to the prepared authority operation, and no row becomes
admission truth until authority finalize; provider, work and effect admission
always recheck the finalized authority-store admission. The row contains:

- state `legacy_bridge`, `closed_v2_pending`, `probe_v2`, `open_v2`, or
  `emergency_hold_v2`;
- monotonic generation;
- required context, prompt-envelope, role, assignment, skill-snapshot, digest,
  and promotion-policy versions;
- production catalog, skill registry, and passing promotion-receipt digests;
- candidate manifest, proof-matrix and client-capability support-policy digests,
  proof admission ID, optional proof run/receipt IDs, promoting/opening command
  IDs, promote/open release-evidence bundle, CI-selection, branch-protection,
  quality-gate manifest/execution, rollout-signal-policy, alert-snapshot,
  incident-set, notification-watchdog alert and authority-evidence-revision digests, audit
  event IDs, `release_generation_admission_sha256`, and timestamps.

SQLite stores one versioned `agent_context_generations` lineage per promoted
generation. Candidate/proof identity is immutable; each status transition CASes
the current canonical decimal `row_revision`, closes it and inserts one
successor with `predecessor_generation_row_sha256`; update-in-place is
forbidden. The current revision has independent
`new_run_status = probe_only | open | retired` and
`continuation_status = allowed | held`, the proof/open evidence and
active `release_generation_admission_scope` and
`release_generation_admission_sha256`, all covered by that revision's
`generation_row_sha256`. A probe-start/reprobe successor carries `probe_only`;
open carries `production` and links the superseded probe admission. A
candidate-controlled process cannot choose a predecessor or revise this row.
A later V2 promotion retires the prior
generation for new runs but does not rewrite runs already bound to it. A typed
invariant breach can hold continuation for exactly the affected generation.

The state transitions are closed and durable:

```text
legacy_bridge --schema_prepared--> closed_v2_pending
closed_v2_pending --promote passing candidate--> probe_v2
open_v2 --promote passing candidate--> probe_v2
emergency_hold_v2 --promote explicit replacement-bound forward fix--> probe_v2
emergency_hold_v2 --atomic process-hold reprobe--> probe_v2
probe_v2 --open with passing proof receipt--> open_v2
probe_v2|open_v2 --typed invariant breach--> emergency_hold_v2
```

There is no transition to a legacy/context-absent mode. The database migration
creates `legacy_bridge`; the `not_started -> schema_prepared` migration
transaction changes it to `closed_v2_pending`. The bridge state admits only the
pre-cutover legacy operations in the phase/operation matrix below, not V2 runs.
`closed_v2_pending`, `probe_v2`, and `emergency_hold_v2` reject ordinary
production `runs.start`. Development fixtures use a separate test-only database
and entry point and cannot write production run rows.

`probe_v2` permits one active proof epoch at a time through
`runtime.agent_context.probe_start` and capability
`RuntimeAgentContextProbeStart`. The initial command supplies the one-use proof
admission ID returned by promote, expected generation/revision, candidate
digest, exact `AgentContextProofMatrixV1` digest, fixed
`agent-context-cutover-proof-matrix` workflow digest, and both request IDs. In
one release-authority operation it changes that exact admission from
`available` to `consumed`, increments `probe_epoch`, creates one real V2 run,
stores `proof_run_id`, and finalizes the probe-only generation admission before
making the run claimable. A unique active-epoch constraint and admission CAS
make a second run impossible. Exact replay returns the original run; a consumed,
wrong-generation, or unknown admission is a typed denial. Ordinary run creation
and every other candidate remain closed before, during, and after a crash.

The proof workflow uses the production compiler, prompt renderer, outer provider
sandbox, skill broker, provider adapters, persistence and projection paths. It
fans out only the complete matrix described above. Write/effect cells use
staging and typed reconciliation fixtures, never production publication or real
external targets. Terminal settlement writes one immutable
`AgentContextProbeReceiptV1` that binds run, generation, candidate, proof
matrix, complete cell receipts, actual binary/context/skill/provider/app
identities, and required output/effect proof. The trusted probe
settler classifies the terminal result as exactly `pass`, `candidate_failure`,
or `infrastructure_inconclusive`:

- `pass` permits the open command for that exact latest probe epoch;
- `candidate_failure` moves the candidate to `probe_failed` and the marker to
  `emergency_hold_v2`;
- `infrastructure_inconclusive` records all attempts but keeps the same
  candidate/generation in `probe_v2` with admission closed.

A `pass` does not make open immediately eligible. In the same finalized
authority transition the probe settler creates one `RolloutSoakStateV1` in
`collecting`, bound to that candidate/generation/probe receipt, the protected
`AgentContextReleaseRolloutPolicyV1`, active signal policy, first eligible signed alert snapshot
and durable clock baseline/tick. The release-owned `rollout_soak_controller`
appends only complete signed sampler snapshots at the contract spacing. It may
finalize `passed` only when the conservative correlated elapsed lower bound is
at least `minimum_soak_seconds`, every expected sample is present and healthy,
the policy/contract/generation/probe identities are unchanged and the current
unresolved-incident set is empty. The resulting signed
`RolloutSoakReceiptV1` binds the complete sample and clock-correlation set.

An unknown/firing sample, missing spacing interval, policy/contract/probe drift
or unverifiable baseline transition finalizes that soak revision as `failed`;
it never truncates the interval or treats restart as elapsed time. Restart
treatment is closed by class. A controller/daemon process restart with the same
durable clock baseline and independently verified complete sample coverage
resumes the same collecting revision, original start tick and sample sequence.
A baseline rollover, monotonic discontinuity, generation/probe/policy change or
any unproved sample gap finalizes the old revision as failed and creates a
successor collecting revision with revision plus one and a new start baseline/
tick; a crash gap counts as missing unless the independent sampler proves the
entire interval continuously. Once health is restored under the same still-
current passing probe, that successor preserves the failed history. The
controller cannot edit duration, skip a sample or issue a receipt for another
generation. Early-open, process-restart-resume, baseline-rollover-reset,
clock rollback/jump, sampler restart with and without complete coverage,
missing-middle-sample and cross-generation receipt fixtures must all prove the
declared continuation/reset branch without consuming an ineligible evidence
bundle.

After an infrastructure repair, an Operator calls
`runtime.agent_context.reprobe` with reason `infrastructure_inconclusive`, the
latest inconclusive receipt digest and expected probe epoch. The transaction
is one release-authority operation: it verifies that receipt is latest for the
same active candidate/generation, keeps `probe_active`, mints and consumes one
internal proof admission, increments the epoch, creates the next proof run and
supersedes the old probe admission with a new probe-only generation admission
before claim. There is no interval in which
a caller can observe or reuse an available reprobe admission, no automatic
retry, and no new candidate requirement. Provider refusal after admission,
identity mismatch, malformed output, policy denial caused by the candidate, or
unverified process cleanup is not infrastructure-inconclusive.

Operator-only `runtime.agent_context.open`, protected by
`RuntimeAgentContextOpen`, requires both request IDs, expected generation,
cutover revision and probe epoch, proof run ID, candidate digest, and passing
receipt digest, exact passing same-generation rollout-soak receipt digest and a
separately fresh open-scoped release-evidence bundle that contains the same
rollout contract/soak identities. The
release authority executes one
`prepare -> control_plane_committed -> anchor_pending -> finalized` operation that consumes
that bundle, supersedes the probe-only generation admission with the production
admission, moves canonical `probe_active` to `promoted`, and projects the marker
to `open_v2`. An inconclusive or superseded probe receipt, absent/short/stale
soak, stale evidence or unresolved alert/incident can never open.

`emergency_hold_v2` is not a feature toggle. It is entered only by a persisted
candidate-failure probe or a closed invariant detector for digest mismatch, unsupported
schema, execution-pin corruption, or unverified provider-process ownership. It
blocks new runs and new prompt/side-effect dispatch for affected generations;
an arbitrary operator preference cannot create it or clear it. Digest, schema,
pin, daemon or provider-binding mismatch requires a new passing candidate, a
new generation and proof. A hold whose only invariant is process ownership may
return to `probe_v2` in the same generation only through
`runtime.agent_context.reprobe`. Every affected
`provider_session.mark_process_absent_v2` command first commits verified absence
without changing candidate/cutover state. When all holds are clear, cutover
readback publishes one `process_clearance_set_sha256`. Reprobe verifies that
complete set, atomically moves `promoted -> probe_active` after an open run or
retains `probe_active` when a proof epoch was interrupted, changes the marker to
`probe_v2`, mints and consumes a proof admission, and creates a fresh proof
epoch. Replay returns that run; a new hold invalidates the clearance set. No
hold path selects legacy behavior.

The daemon advertises `AgentContextV2`, `PromptEnvelopeV2`,
`SkillBundleSnapshotV1`, `ProviderExecutionSandboxV1`,
`AgentQualityPromotionPolicyV1`, `AgentContextProofMatrixV1`, the supported
snapshot/read/GraphQL-shell/MCP-client versions and cutover generation through
MCP initialize, `runtime.health`, and the GraphQL capability readback. The
actual MCP run-start caller obtains its server-minted negotiation token from
start-selection discovery; the Swift app contributes only its separately
qualified release-manifest proof-matrix row. After `open_v2`, a start request
must explicitly select the marker's required V2 versions. For an authorized
caller omission is malformed `-32602`; a supplied but stale or mismatched
selection or negotiation token fails with
`agent_context_version_incompatible` or `run_start_client_incompatible` under
`-32009`.
Historical context-absent readback remains supported, but no surface can compile
or persist a new context-absent run.

Cutover uses a maintenance restart and one Rust-owned
`AgentContextMigrationService`, not a mixed-version rolling window or shell
script. Its append-only `agent_context_migration_phase_events` ledger and
singleton `not_started` head are created by the additive V2 persistence
migrations before live candidate evaluation. Those migrations add readers,
candidate/evidence stores and phase state but do not permit V2 or context-absent
mixed writes. Every phase event binds prior phase/head, database migration version and
checksum, daemon self-admission identity, command/journal ID, invariant receipt
digest, active migration-lease epoch/digest, timestamp, and event hash. The
closed phases are:

```text
not_started -> schema_prepared -> admission_closed -> legacy_draining -> legacy_settled
legacy_settled -> legacy_execution_sealed -> self_admission_verified
self_admission_verified|open|emergency_hold -> candidate_probe_admitted -> probe_running
probe_running -> probe_inconclusive -> probe_running
probe_running -> probe_passed -> open
candidate_probe_admitted|probe_running|probe_inconclusive|probe_passed|open -> emergency_hold
```

The un-suffixed values above belong only to the migration phase ledger;
`legacy_bridge`, `closed_v2_pending`, `probe_v2`, `open_v2`, and
`emergency_hold_v2` remain the distinct cutover-marker values.
`probe_inconclusive -> probe_running` requires the atomic reprobe command and
receipt described above. Transition from
`emergency_hold` requires either a newly passing forward-fix candidate or the
verified process-only clearance allowed by the cutover state machine; both
paths re-enter `candidate_probe_admitted` and must execute a fresh proof epoch.

`RuntimeOwnerIdentityV1` and `RuntimeOwnerLeaseV1` are the sole canonical
ownership witnesses for daemon and bounded worker leases. Every named
resource-specific lease object in this proposal, including
`ControlPlaneWriterLeaseV1` and `AgentContextMigrationLeaseV1`, is only a
deterministic bounded projection of that canonical chain. The authority store
is the sole canonical store for the complete lifecycle; control-plane rows are
purpose-signed bounded projections and can never be issue, renew, takeover,
fence or absence-inspection inputs. Their closed `resource_kind` is exactly
`control_plane_writer_lease`,
`migration_lease`, `projection_worker_lease`, `skill_effect_writer_lease`,
`skill_grant_expiry_lease`, `release_evidence_expiry_lease`,
`provider_prompt_gateway_lease`, `provider_prompt_reconciler_lease`,
`alert_sampler_lease`, `incident_notifier_lease`,
`notification_watchdog_lease`, or
`evaluation_worker_lease`. The identity binds one resource kind/ID and
resource-scope digest to owner kind/instance, executable/build, PID plus
process-birth identity, boot/clock baseline and registration event. The lease
binds that identity, lease ID/epoch/revision, state, acquired/heartbeat/deadline,
clock baseline, canonical resource head/revision, and predecessor lease digest.
An object for one resource kind is structurally invalid for every other kind.

Lease issue/acquire is one authority-store transaction that registers the
observed identity and creates the signed active lease. Its same-store projection
outbox may then publish the lease to control-plane SQLite. A control-plane row
without the current finalized authority lease digest is unowned and cannot
renew, publish or take over work. Every control-plane mutation performed under
a lease presents that exact signed lease and expected resource head; a mutation
that advances the resource head uses `ReleaseAuthorityOperationV1` to advance
the authority lease's canonical head before the successor may act. Projection
lag cannot keep an old lease valid.

Operator-only `runtime.owner_absence.verify` asks the
`runtime_owner_inspector` component of `ChainworksReleaseAuthorityV1` to
evaluate that exact registered identity. The request carries resource kind/ID,
owner identity digest, complete lease ID/epoch/digest, resource head/revision
and clock-baseline ID; the caller cannot substitute a PID, path or birth field.
The inspector resolves the owner and current lease in one authority-store read
transaction, rejects any control-plane-only or projected digest, verifies its own current
audit-token/code identity, uses kernel process/birth/boot observations, and signs a
`RuntimeOwnerAbsenceReceiptV1` with the inspector-purpose key. The receipt binds
the complete owner bytes, resource scope, lease ID/epoch/digest,
head/revision/baseline, observation method, inspector component/build/key
epoch, issue time and 30-second expiry. It is written to the authority store in
state `available` before being returned and is useful only once in the exact
matching takeover operation; its lifecycle is `available -> reserved ->
consumed`, `available -> expired`, or `reserved -> available` only when its
operation aborts before any control-plane commit. Takeover prepare reserves the
receipt and current lease atomically. A lease renew creates a signed successor
lease digest in the same authority store and immediately expires every
available receipt for the predecessor; a reserved takeover and renew therefore
have exactly one CAS winner. Live, PID-reused, owner-restarted,
permission-inconclusive, scope-mismatched, stale, unsigned or wrong-purpose
observations are typed denials and leave ownership unchanged. P083
`provider_session.mark_process_absent` remains provider-session-specific and is
never accepted as a migration or projection owner receipt.

Migration ownership is the `migration_lease` specialization of canonical
`RuntimeOwnerLeaseV1`; `AgentContextMigrationLeaseV1` is its signed
control-plane/readback projection, not a second lifecycle. The canonical lease
additionally binds current migration phase/head, selected candidate and
self-admission digests, cutover revision, and `migration_lease_sha256`. The
lease duration is 60 seconds and heartbeat
interval is 15 seconds; deadline evaluation uses the correlated durable clock
rather than mutable wall time alone. Every migration, drain, reconciliation,
replacement and cutover proof-admission write CASes both the expected lease
epoch and migration head through the authority operation protocol.

The lease state machine is exactly:

```text
absent --migration_lease.acquire--> active(epoch = 1)
active --authority-internal renew--> active(same epoch, later deadline)
active --deadline + verified absence + migration_lease.takeover--> active(epoch + 1)
active --migration terminal settlement--> released
released --migration_lease.acquire for a later forward operation--> active(epoch + 1)
```

`runtime.agent_context.migration_lease.acquire` and
`runtime.agent_context.migration_lease.takeover` are Operator MCP commands. They
derive the new owner as the currently observed release-authority maintenance
component; no owner PID/path/build is caller input. Acquire requires expected
phase/head/cutover revision, no active lease, current authority self-admission
and the prior terminal/released lease digest when one exists. Takeover requires
the exact expired lease ID/epoch/digest, phase/head/cutover revision and the
fresh signed owner-absence receipt ID/digest. Takeover prepare atomically
reserves the canonical lease and receipt and fixes the complete successor lease
bytes with incremented epoch inside the `ReleaseAuthorityOperationV1` action
journal while that operation remains in its valid `prepared` phase. It does not
insert or expose a second lease state, and it writes nothing to the control-
plane database. Anchor-finalize consumes the receipt, releases the old lease,
inserts the fixed successor directly as `active`, and creates the immutable
outbox intent plus `ready` delivery revision. Only a later projection worker may
write the control-plane handoff projection; the new owner acts from finalized
authority truth and never from a provisional control-plane row.
Competing renew/takeover commands have one authority-store CAS winner; exact
replay returns the same finalized lease and every loser performs zero mutation.
A wrong resource kind/ID, stale or renewed lease digest, wrong head, wrong
baseline, control-plane-only identity or consumed/reserved-by-another receipt
fails before either store mutates.

Renew is not an Operator action and is not advertised by MCP `tools/list`. The
current owner invokes closed private XPC operation
`runtime_owner_lease.renew_internal_v1` with lease ID/epoch/digest, expected
resource phase/head and current monotonic budget. The purpose-specific owner
controller authenticates its audit token and observed process identity, then
the coordinator CAS-inserts a signed successor lease with unchanged epoch and a
later heartbeat/deadline. It also expires every available predecessor absence
receipt in that transaction and emits the projection outbox entry. A stale
epoch/digest, reserved takeover, phase/head drift, expired lease or wrong
component cannot renew. No control-plane endpoint writes a lease digest, and no
command can decrement an epoch, reopen a released lease or create a second
singleton lease.

A deadline alone never proves ownership absence. Takeover is allowed only after
the deadline and a current `RuntimeOwnerAbsenceReceiptV1` for the exact former
owner identity, lease epoch/head and clock baseline; the winner increments the
