epoch, appends a takeover event and reconciles all prior in-flight rows before
acting. A paused but live owner therefore cannot be stolen from. Any late write
from an old owner fails
`agent_context_migration_lease_fenced` without side effects. Lease expiry,
holder identity, epoch, heartbeat age, takeover eligibility and allowed next
action are Operator readback and alert fields.

Forward repair never rewrites a phase or prior candidate. Operator-only
`runtime.agent_context.replace_candidate` can bind one corrected
`live_passed` candidate after `schema_prepared`, including from a durable
`emergency_hold`, while keeping the current migration phase. The transaction
requires the active migration lease, expected migration head/phase, cutover
generation/revision, old candidate digest, new candidate and passing promotion
receipt, new proof-matrix digest, current fresh inventory and one
`zero_unsafe_digest` proving no unverified provider process or external effect.
An existing effect must first reach a typed terminal/reconciled state; a
process must have P083 absence proof. No timeout or Operator assertion can
stand in for those receipts.

The committed `AgentContextCandidateReplacementV1` records old/new candidate
and receipt digests, phase/head, cutover generation/revision, lease epoch,
inventory and zero-unsafe digests, invalidated admission/proof/self-admission
receipts, replacement generation, command/journal/audit IDs and
`replacement_receipt_sha256`. It atomically supersedes the selected candidate,
invalidates old proof admissions and outstanding run-start negotiation
receipts, makes prior app and MCP-profile qualification rows non-current through
the new matrix digest, increments the
cutover revision, closes ordinary admission, and sets orthogonal
`migration_repair_state = replacement_bound`. It does not start a provider,
move backward, resurrect legacy work or reuse old evidence.

Only a daemon matching the new candidate may then be admitted by the external
`runtime_identity_attestor`. The candidate's nonce-bound self-description is
untrusted input; the attestor independently measures its launchd/audit-token/
vnode/code/process/sandbox identity and signs the receipt. Successful external
admission appends the next forward phase event or resumes the same phase,
sets repair state back to `none`, and requires a complete new proof matrix
before open. A bounded failed self-admission or reconciliation sets
`repair_blocked` with exact blockers and allowed actions. Another explicit
replace command may move `repair_blocked -> replacement_bound`; there is no
automatic candidate loop. The closed repair transitions are therefore
`none -> replacement_bound -> none | repair_blocked` and
`repair_blocked -> replacement_bound`. Original ledger, policy, inventory,
attempt, phase and candidate histories remain immutable and linked.

The additive migration creates migration phase `not_started` and cutover state
`legacy_bridge` together. Before the `not_started -> schema_prepared`
transaction, the bridge daemon is stopped and the final cutover daemon acquires
an exclusive migration lease. The maintenance bootstrap computes a bounded
`LegacyCutoverInventoryV1`; independently, the release supervisor starts the
candidate in no-work self-description mode and the external
`runtime_identity_attestor` creates `RuntimeSelfAdmissionReceiptV1` from
observed executable/process/build/schema/compiler/tool-policy and sandbox
identities. It compares those observations and the candidate's untrusted claims
with the exact `live_passed` candidate manifest and promotion receipt selected
for cutover. The inventory enumerates every producer row, active
provider/process identity, prepared or started external effect, pending
approval/escalation/retry and its exact settlement action. Each external effect
is classified `not_started`, `prepared_not_started`, `running_bounded`,
`reconciliation_supported`, `terminal`, or `unknown_unbounded`; the latter is a
go/no-go blocker. `running_bounded` requires a persisted completion/cancel
deadline, and `reconciliation_supported` requires an existing typed reconciler
and intent identity. Missing rows, unknown owners, unbounded effects, or a
stale inventory abort before any phase change.

Mismatch or a failed go/no-go enters failed-serve without modifying execution
truth; the operator may restart the unchanged bridge. On pass, persisting both
receipts, recording selected candidate/receipt digests, changing cutover state
`legacy_bridge -> closed_v2_pending`, and advancing migration phase
`not_started -> schema_prepared` follows the reserved cross-store authority
operation and is not servable before anchor finalize. Before its control-plane
commit,
legacy bridge behavior remains authoritative; after commit, no new legacy start
or producer admission is possible, while authority readback remains pending
until finalize. The marker rejects any binary whose
candidate digest differs from ordinary work or phase transitions. A daemon
matching the pinned candidate cannot append or verify its own receipt; every
transition requires a current independently signed
`RuntimeSelfAdmissionReceiptV1`, and each phase event binds that exact receipt.

The sole mismatch exception is a durable `MigrationReplacementAdmissionV1` for
the minimal replacement boundary. It is never inferred at daemon startup.
Operator-only `runtime.agent_context.replacement_admission.issue` is the sole
issuance command. During migration it is served only by the sealed release-owned
`chainworks-migration-bootstrap` maintenance mode of
`ChainworksReleaseAuthorityV1`; its executable digest, designated requirement,
XPC component identity and signing key epoch were pinned in the additive-schema
genesis before cutover. Neither the current candidate daemon nor the proposed
replacement binary can host, impersonate or call the issuer for itself. The
Operator request is authenticated at the release-authority maintenance boundary,
which executes the canonical transaction and binds the observed issuer identity and
requires the expected migration phase/head,
cutover generation/revision, old and proposed new `live_passed` candidate,
passing promotion receipt, schema/migration compatibility range, proof-matrix
policy, current inventory and zero-unsafe digests, and either the active exact
migration lease or an expired lease plus a current generic runtime-owner absence
receipt. It inserts one admission in state `available`, with admission ID,
digest, issuer identity, issuing command/journal IDs, exact replacement intent hash and five-
minute expiry. A partial issuance transaction creates no usable row.

The closed lifecycle is `available -> consumed | expired | revoked`. At most
one unexpired `available` admission exists for one old candidate and migration
head. It cannot renew or issue another admission. Wrong candidate, binary,
phase/head, generation/revision, lease/absence, promotion, matrix, inventory or
zero-unsafe evidence is rejected before mutation. Exact command replay returns
the original admission; semantic alias replay points to it; conflicting intent
with the same caller request ID fails. Expiry is evaluated against the bound
durable clock baseline and is irreversible.

The admission authorizes only cutover/lease readback, the fenced lease
acquire/takeover needed by that exact replacement, and
`runtime.agent_context.replace_candidate`. The replacement request must carry
both admission ID and digest. Successful replacement validates and consumes the
admission in the same transaction that binds the candidate; replay returns that
same consumed result, while an expired, revoked, wrong-scope or previously
consumed admission cannot mutate state. The admission cannot claim work, write
another phase, or access provider/effect surfaces. Once replacement commits,
the release supervisor must obtain a new external
`RuntimeSelfAdmissionReceiptV1` for that exact binary and newly pinned candidate
before any other maintenance transition. Recovery is
forward-only with either the currently admitted binary or this bounded
replacement bootstrap.
After the maintenance restart, the release-authority gateway/bootstrap advances
automatically to `admission_closed`; there is no operator command to reopen
legacy admission. It does not start the candidate daemon or bind ordinary
run/approval/effect mutation surfaces between `schema_prepared` and the durable
`admission_closed` commit. The live-auth maintenance gateway remains available
only for `runtime.health`, cutover/lease/blocker and incident readback,
protected skill-registry publication, release-evidence selection/issue,
incident acknowledge/resolve/repair and notification requeue, generic
runtime-owner absence verification,
provider-session-specific P083 clearance, replacement-admission issuance,
fenced lease acquire/takeover for an admitted replacement and
`runtime.agent_context.replace_candidate`; it cannot create or continue
ordinary work.
The schema commit
that installed the additive V2 tables is the database-compatibility point of no
return for binaries that do not know those migrations; `schema_prepared` is the
start of the one-way production cutover.

`legacy_execution_sealed` is the execution point of no return. Its transaction
rechecks the complete drain inventory, writes a `LegacyExecutionSettlementV1`
for every nonterminal context-absent run, terminally cancels every remaining
unprepared work item and pending approval/escalation/retry authority with
`legacy_context_retired`, preserves each prior status and ledger digest for
readback, verifies that the cutover marker remains `closed_v2_pending`, and
records the migration event and projection intents. It commits all or nothing.
From that commit onward no context-absent work is claimable or actionable.

The phase procedure is:

1. after additive schema/readback/evaluator rollout and passing live evidence,
   stop the bridge daemon, acquire the exclusive migration lease, obtain an
   external attestor receipt for the final cutover daemon, build a fresh
   complete `LegacyCutoverInventoryV1`, and
   stop without phase mutation if any go/no-go blocker exists;
2. atomically bind the passing inventory, advance `not_started ->
   schema_prepared`, change `legacy_bridge -> closed_v2_pending`, read back both
   receipts, and then enter `admission_closed` before binding ordinary mutation
   surfaces or workers;
3. rebuild the bound inventory, verify no new producer appeared, persist
   `legacy_draining`, and apply only the operation rows allowed below;
4. quiesce and settle active work under the matrix below; persist
   `legacy_settled` only when the invariant query returns zero unsafe rows;
5. commit `legacy_execution_sealed`, then reverify the current daemon's
   `RuntimeSelfAdmissionReceiptV1` and enter `self_admission_verified`;
6. verify app/daemon capability handshake, candidate, catalog/skill snapshots,
   and passing promotion receipt; promote into `probe_v2` and
   `candidate_probe_admitted`;
7. run one proof epoch; on infrastructure-inconclusive repair use atomic
   reprobe for the same generation, or on pass persist `probe_passed` and
   execute open;
8. read back `open_v2`, generation, migration head, self-admission and proof
   receipts before ordinary run admission becomes available.

The unified admission predicate uses this complete legacy phase/operation
matrix. `allow` still requires all pre-existing permission, ownership,
idempotency and process/effect checks; `settle_only` permits only the named
terminal action and cannot create successor work:

| Migration phase / cutover state | New legacy run or enqueue | Claim/retry/resume/approval/escalation | Pre-prompt provider work | Prompt-committed provider work | Prepare/start external write | Already-started external write | Safety/readback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `not_started / legacy_bridge` | allow existing bridge contract | allow existing bridge contract | allow existing bridge contract | allow settle/cancel | allow existing bridge contract | allow settle/reconcile | allow |
| `schema_prepared / closed_v2_pending` | deny | deny; pending authority may only be retired | `settle_only`: cancel and verified reap | `settle_only`: terminal result or cancel plus late-output quarantine | deny; prepared intent may only cancel | `settle_only`: bounded completion or typed reconciliation from bound inventory | allow |
| `admission_closed / closed_v2_pending` | deny | deny; retire only | `settle_only`: cancel and verified reap | `settle_only`: terminal result or cancel plus late-output quarantine | deny; cancel prepared intent | `settle_only`: bounded completion or typed reconciliation | allow |
| `legacy_draining / closed_v2_pending` | deny | deny; retire only | `settle_only`: cancel and verified reap | `settle_only`: terminal result or cancel plus quarantine | deny; cancel prepared intent | `settle_only`: bounded completion or typed reconciliation | allow |
| `legacy_settled / closed_v2_pending` | deny | deny | deny | deny | deny | deny | invariant read and atomic seal only |
| `legacy_execution_sealed` and later | deny with `legacy_context_execution_prohibited` | deny with `legacy_context_execution_prohibited` | deny | deny; only late-output quarantine for already-settled identity | deny | deny | historical readback, audit and verified process-absence cleanup only |

No generic worker, recovery loop or operator command may interpret
`closed_v2_pending` without the migration phase. The matrix is compiled into
the same `ExecutionAdmissionService` operation registry; adding a producer or
phase without a row is a gate failure and runtime denial.

Initial legacy-to-V2 cutover requires no context-absent provider work or
unsettled external side effect to remain at seal. The drain matrix is:

| Durable pre-cutover state | Required outcome before migration |
|---|---|
| queued/unprepared provider work | terminally cancel in the seal transaction with `legacy_context_retired`; preserve source payload digest for readback |
| prepared but no provider process | cancel and settle the attempt |
| launching/provider-bound before prompt | cancel, verify process-group reap, and settle |
| prompt committed/observing | wait for terminal result or cancel with late-output quarantine; require terminal settlement |
| side-effect prepared but external write not started | cancel/release intent durably |
| external write started | only a preflight-bound `running_bounded` completion/cancel or `reconciliation_supported` reconciler may run; unresolved state blocks `legacy_settled`, while `unknown_unbounded` blocked before `schema_prepared` |
| pending approval/escalation/retry | retire its actionability in `LegacyExecutionSettlementV1`; preserve original decision/ledger history |
| nonterminal legacy run after child settlement | set terminal run status `cancelled` with typed reason `legacy_context_retired` and retain the pre-settlement status in the settlement row |
| terminal run/execution/side effect | unchanged and available for readback |

Recovery is total:

| Last durable migration/probe phase | Authoritative restart action |
|---|---|
| no migration table/head | run the additive persistence migration and create `not_started / legacy_bridge`; no execution state was changed |
| `not_started / legacy_bridge` | existing bridge operations remain governed by the matrix; rebuild go/no-go inventory or continue pre-cutover evaluation, with no V2 execution admitted |
| `schema_prepared` or `admission_closed` | keep new admission closed, rebuild the bound inventory, and execute only phase-matrix settlement operations |
| `legacy_draining` | reconcile every process/effect from durable identity; never infer absence from elapsed time |
| `legacy_settled` | rerun the zero-unsafe-row query, then retry the atomic seal transaction |
| `legacy_execution_sealed` | prove no legacy row is claimable, then resume daemon self-admission |
| `self_admission_verified` | resume exact candidate promotion checks; do not rerun legacy settlement |
| `candidate_probe_admitted` | remain `probe_v2`, mint no second active proof admission, and resume/start the recorded epoch |
| `probe_running` | reconcile the proof run by dispatch/session identity; never create a parallel probe |
| `probe_inconclusive` | remain closed; allow only atomic same-generation infrastructure reprobe |
| `probe_passed` | verify receipt again and replay/execute open |
| `open` | verify marker, generation, self-admission and proof digests; mismatch enters emergency hold |
| any phase with an unexpired migration lease | only the exact owner/epoch may resume; other daemons remain failed-serve/readback-only |
| any phase with an expired lease and live/unknown former owner | retain phase and admission closure; require generic exact-owner absence verification, never time-only takeover or a provider-session receipt |
| any phase after verified lease-owner absence | consume the current generic owner-absence receipt while CAS-incrementing lease epoch, append takeover evidence, reconcile prior work, then continue that same phase |
| `replacement_bound` | admit only the replacement candidate daemon; invalidate old proof/run-start receipts, make old app/MCP-profile qualification rows non-current and require new self-admission plus complete proof matrix |
| `repair_blocked` | retain current forward phase and closed admission; expose blockers and allow only a new explicit replacement or the named reconciliation |
| `emergency_hold` | keep admission/dispatch closed; after an explicit forward-fix replacement or complete process-clearance set, use the authorized promote/reprobe transaction to enter `candidate_probe_admitted` with a fresh proof epoch |

#### Unified Execution Admission

One Rust `ExecutionAdmissionService::authorize_control_plane_materialization_tx`
is the only candidate-side validator for projecting, claiming or dispatching
already authorized executable work. It never creates, signs, settles or derives
an authority admission. Authority-only operations such as approval settlement,
mediation confirmation and attempt reduction commit their canonical outcome and
complete signed outbox set solely in release-authority SQLite. With outbox
delivery paused they create zero candidate queue rows. The projection worker
later validates the finalized `ExecutableWorkAdmissionV1` and idempotently
inserts exactly one queue identity under unique
`(executable_work_admission_sha256, work_semantic_key)`; replay can update
projection health but cannot allocate another work item.

The service is called inside the applicable control-plane SQLite transaction by
signed Run/work-admission projection, work-item claim, projected retry/resume/
continue, escalation materialization, scheduler/recovery projection,
skill-script spawn authorization, side-effect prepare, and external-effect
dispatch. Provider prompt commit is not in this list: it is projected only from
the authority-owned prompt transition above. Repository write functions for
these candidate transitions are crate-private and require the returned
transaction-scoped validation proof.

The predicate binds operation kind, run/execution/attempt, context schema,
cutover and migration phase/revision, generation continuation state, daemon
self-admission, dispatch pin, process hold, provider-binding receipt, permission
profile, and side-effect/script contract. Context-absent runs fail with
`legacy_context_execution_prohibited`; retired work fails with
`legacy_context_retired`; closed/probe/hold generations admit only the exact
maintenance operation named by their phase. The proof is not reusable in
another transaction or operation. Approval settlement cannot call this service
recursively or inside its authority transaction, and candidate code cannot
derive a work admission from an approval row, outcome or outbox payload that
lacks the finalized signed admission.

For provider spawn and external-effect start, this control-plane proof is
necessary but not sufficient. The provider launcher/effect broker must also
verify the authority-store generation scope and active run/proof admission. A
provider spawn additionally consumes the exact
`ProviderAttemptLaunchAuthorizationV1` described above. The candidate daemon
cannot convert an admission proof or forged producer row into a launch ticket,
and a probe-only ticket cannot target an ordinary run, production workspace or
undeclared effect cell.

Startup repair scans every producer table for a row that lacks a corresponding
admission proof or violates current generation/disposition. It quarantines the
row, records a typed invariant event, and enters emergency hold when process or
external-effect ownership is uncertain. Gate-owned inventory tests fail when a
new producer is added without registering its operation kind and proof call.
After `legacy_execution_sealed`, a single invariant query over all producer
tables must prove zero claimable context-absent rows before any later phase can
advance.

For later V2-to-V2 promotions, running executions and already-started side
effects on an earlier allowed generation may finish with their immutable pins.
Queued work in existing V2 runs continues only if that generation's
`continuation_status` remains `allowed`. During an emergency hold, no new prompt
or side-effect dispatch begins for a held generation; prompt-committed work may
settle, cancellation remains available, and write-started effects must settle
or reconcile. These rules survive daemon restart because generation and intent
states are durable.

An old daemon cannot open the migrated database because the existing
newer-than-binary migration preflight fails closed. A new MCP client talking to
an old daemon discovers no V2 selection tool and does not submit a V2 start. An
old MCP client talking to the new daemon omits the required selection/receipt
and receives the exact authorized schema rejection. The Swift app remains a
separate GraphQL compatibility row: supported operation documents must pass the
fixture and live HTTP/WS qualification harness before open, but the app does not
submit `runs.start`.
This compatibility matrix therefore has no state that can create a new
context-absent run after cutover.

| MCP run-start client | Daemon/database | New-run result |
|---|---|---|
| old | old daemon with migrated database | daemon startup fails newer-than-binary preflight |
| new | old daemon before migration | client observes missing V2 selection capability and does not submit |
| old or bridge client | V2 additive schema with `not_started / legacy_bridge` | only the pre-cutover context-absent path is admitted; V2 execution is denied |
| any | migration `schema_prepared` through `legacy_execution_sealed` | all ordinary starts denied |
| old | new daemon in `closed_v2_pending`, `probe_v2`, `emergency_hold_v2`, or `open_v2` | `-32602` with missing `/context_selection` and `/run_start_negotiation_token`, after authorization; no legacy start fallback |
| new | new daemon, `closed_v2_pending` | `agent_context_cutover_not_ready` |
| new | new daemon, `probe_v2` | only one active proof epoch; explicit infrastructure retry is admitted after an inconclusive receipt |
| new | new daemon, `emergency_hold_v2` | `agent_context_emergency_hold` |
| new with missing/stale/copied/wrong-session receipt or unsupported capability profile | new daemon, `open_v2` | `run_start_client_incompatible`; no Run row |
| qualified new capability profile on the same MCP logical session | new daemon, `open_v2` | generation-, selection- and negotiation-token-bound V2 start only |

Rollback is forward-fix only. There is no runtime disable control, legacy fallback,
or downgrade transition. Restoring a pre-cutover database backup would fork
execution truth and is not an operational rollback; it is allowed only as an
offline forensic copy under a separate operator recovery decision. A broken
V2 release persists `emergency_hold_v2` until an explicitly replacement-bound
corrected candidate receives a passing external runtime-attestation receipt and
passes a complete new proof matrix; existing
historical readback remains available throughout.

### Historical Readback Versus Live Continuation

For a context-absent snapshot, `readback` means decode, hash verification,
artifact/report display, and offline deterministic reconstruction without any
provider, tool, workspace mutation, or external side effect. It does not mean
resuming the workflow state machine.

After the atomic `schema_prepared / closed_v2_pending` commit, every action that
could create a provider invocation or side-effect intent for a context-absent
run fails with `legacy_context_execution_prohibited`. This includes approval
settlement that would advance into executable work, retry, resume, escalation,
continuation, and provider-session resurrection. Only the explicitly
`settle_only` operations in the phase matrix remain available before seal; they
cannot create successor work. There is no operator override. Read-only queries
and artifact export remain available, and fixture-only simulation runs against
a separate test database may exercise the legacy reader without a live
provider.

## Steward Tuning Loop

1. Steward analyzes every completed run using frozen run and eval provenance.
2. A failure is classified as `context`, `role`, `skill`, `workflow`,
   `runtime`, or `model` before a change is proposed.
3. A reproducing eval is added before the candidate fix.
4. One ownership layer is changed per candidate.
5. Deterministic suites run before any live provider call.
6. Candidate and baseline run against identical inputs and provider profiles.
7. Holdout runs only when the candidate meets non-holdout thresholds.
8. Promotion requires zero hard regressions and an improvement in the declared
   target metric without an unacceptable cost or latency regression.
9. Steward writes a recommendation, experiment record, and optional candidate
   patch. It cannot modify or promote canonical production skills itself.

Every promotion references the immutable `AgentQualityPromotionReceiptV1` and
the cutover generation that consumed it.

All other symbols in the list either have one byte-equal canonical registry row
or are private nested reasons under that row's bounded detail schema. An
unmapped symbol, a second alias, or a router/SDL/client literal absent from
`errors.yaml` fails generation and `agent-context`; prose cannot create an
exception.

Schema, authority, generation, candidate and broker-scope failures occur before
provider dispatch and preserve the session without implying output quarantine.
Failures after process or side-effect spawn follow their explicit dispatch,
script or reconciliation contract: they may terminate a verified group,
quarantine late output or enter identity hold. Error readback gives the
operator the invalid contract path, safe identifier and next action without
including secret or unbounded prompt content.

Authorization rejection is evaluated before run or head existence is revealed
and uses the shared boundary-denial envelope. Head, duplicate, receipt, and
state conflicts return the current safe revision or expected capability only
to an authorized Operator. Promotion `inconclusive` is a retained evaluation
result, not a provider failure and not authority to promote.

## Persistence and Readback

Run-local artifacts include:

```text
<run-meta-root>/context/run-mission-base.json
<run-meta-root>/context/base-authority-ledger.json
<run-meta-root>/context/authority-overlay/<authority-head>.json
<run-meta-root>/context/effective-missions/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>.json
<run-meta-root>/context/effective-authority/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>.json
<run-meta-root>/context/runtime-constraints/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>.json
<run-meta-root>/context/authority-fences/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>.json
<run-meta-root>/context/assignments/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>.json
<run-meta-root>/context/generation-binding.json
<run-meta-root>/skills/<skill-id>/manifest.json
<run-meta-root>/skills/compositions/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>.json
<run-meta-root>/runtime/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>/prompt-envelope-manifest.json
<run-meta-root>/runtime/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>/dispatch-intent.json
<run-meta-root>/runtime/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>/provider-sandbox-attestation.json
<run-meta-root>/runtime/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>/skill-broker-grant-install-receipt.json
```

One release-generated and signed `RunLocalArtifactMaterializationInventoryV1`
is the exhaustive bridge between those logical paths and durable projection
truth. The protected generator derives it from this closed table, and every
`RunContextGenerationBindingV2` pins its digest. A class missing from the table,
an extra path template, two classes resolving to one target, or a canonical
source without one class fails schema generation and run admission.
Each authority-source cell resolves to the append-only schema-owned row family
named by that payload and the exact tuple shown; the generated row records its
canonical source-writer component/build, physical authority-store table name
and primary-key bytes. A cell explicitly
naming a control-plane table resolves only to that table and committed revision.
No source is selected by latest timestamp, path scan or digest search.

| Artifact class and immutable target template | Canonical source payload | Sole materializer and intent/entity key | Metadata, readback, repair and GC |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run_mission_base`: `context/run-mission-base.json` | finalized `run_mission_v1` at `(run_id, base_head)` in the authority store | `agent_context_projection_worker`; `run_mission_base/(run_id, base_head)` | signed source revision/digest plus no-replace target; retained for run history; mismatch degrades and blocks readback |
| `base_authority_ledger`: `context/base-authority-ledger.json` | finalized `base_authority_ledger_v1` at `(run_id, base_head)` in the authority store | same worker; `base_authority_ledger/(run_id, base_head)` | same immutable metadata; retained with run authority history; rebuilt only from the exact signed source |
| `authority_overlay`: `context/authority-overlay/<authority-head>.json` | finalized ordered `authority_event_v1` chain ending at `(run_id, authority_head)` | same worker; `authority_overlay/(run_id, authority_head)` | one target per head; historical heads remain addressable; GC only with the run-retention tombstone and no cursor/reference |
| `effective_mission`: `context/effective-missions/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>.json` | finalized `effective_run_mission_v1` pinned by the claimed attempt | same worker; `effective_mission/(agent_execution_id, attempt_generation)` | attempt readback carries target/digest; retained with immutable attempt evidence |
| `effective_authority`: `context/effective-authority/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>.json` | finalized `effective_authority_projection_v1` pinned by the claimed attempt | same worker; `effective_authority/(agent_execution_id, attempt_generation)` | authority watermark and target digest must agree; stale-head bytes are historical only |
| `runtime_constraints`: `context/runtime-constraints/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>.json` | finalized `execution_runtime_constraints_v2` derived from the exact attempt-pinned authority and policy | same worker; `runtime_constraints/(agent_execution_id, attempt_generation)` | metadata records both source digests and evaluator build; mismatch blocks claim/spawn and is rebuilt from the same inputs |
| `authority_fence`: `context/authority-fences/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>.json` | finalized `authority_recheck_fence_v1` observed by the attempt admission | same worker; `authority_fence/(agent_execution_id, attempt_generation)` | readback exposes fence epoch/token and target digest; retained through attempt settlement/quarantine |
| `assignment`: `context/assignments/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>.json` | frozen `task_assignment_v1` selected by the owner/admission chain | same worker; `assignment/(agent_execution_id, attempt_generation)` | immutable assignment digest is part of prompt/effect admission; never repaired from catalog HEAD |
| `generation_binding`: `context/generation-binding.json` | canonical control-plane `run_context_generation_bindings` row carrying `run_context_generation_binding_v2` at its committed `(run_id, generation)` revision | same worker; `generation_binding/(run_id, generation)` | path is created once for the run's frozen generation; a different digest at that path is terminal corruption, not replacement |
| `skill_manifest`: `skills/<skill-id>/manifest.json` | protected-registry `skill_bundle_manifest_v1` pinned by the run generation | same worker; `skill_manifest/(run_id, skill_id, bundle_sha256)` | metadata points to registry/publication receipt; retained while any run or evidence cursor pins the bundle |
| `skill_composition`: `skills/compositions/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>.json` | claimed attempt's `skill_composition_v1` | same worker; `skill_composition/(agent_execution_id, attempt_generation)` | composition/readback/prompt digests must match; retained with attempt evidence |
| `prompt_envelope_manifest`: `runtime/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>/prompt-envelope-manifest.json` | canonical control-plane `agent_invocation_dispatches` row carrying committed `prompt_envelope_manifest_v2` at its exact revision; its digest must equal the finalized provider-prompt reservation | same worker; `prompt_envelope_manifest/(agent_execution_id, attempt_generation)` | publication is required before prompt commit; retained with terminal prompt/output evidence |
| `dispatch_intent`: `runtime/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>/dispatch-intent.json` | canonical control-plane `invocation_dispatch_intent_v2` row at its committed revision | same worker; `dispatch_intent/(agent_execution_id, attempt_generation)` | mutation receipt points to the intent; recovery rereads the exact SQLite revision and never infers from provider state |
| `provider_sandbox_attestation`: `runtime/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>/provider-sandbox-attestation.json` | finalized signed `provider_sandbox_attestation_v1` | same worker; `provider_sandbox_attestation/(agent_execution_id, attempt_generation)` | absent/degraded target blocks `provider_bound`; retained through process-clearance and late-output windows |
| `skill_broker_grant_install_receipt`: `runtime/<agent-execution-id>/attempts/<attempt-generation>/skill-broker-grant-install-receipt.json` | finalized signed `skill_broker_grant_install_receipt_v1` | same worker; `grant_install_receipt/(agent_execution_id, attempt_generation, grant_install_epoch)` | absent/degraded target blocks broker use; retained through grant/effect reconciliation and attempt settlement |

All table rows use immutable-target mode `run_local_no_replace`. The worker
writes and fsyncs a request-owned temp file, performs a no-replace rename to the
resolved run-local template, fsyncs the parent, verifies bytes, and only then
CASes the exact `AgentContextProjectionIntentV1` to `applied` with the target
vnode and digest. Crash before rename leaves `pending`; crash after rename but
before CAS verifies and adopts only matching bytes; an existing third digest is
quarantined and marks `degraded` without overwrite. A missing canonical source
is an emergency hold. Run-local GC requires a finalized run-retention
tombstone, no live projection lease/cursor/evidence reference and exact
inventory ownership; it never scans arbitrary files or follows links. Retained
fixtures crash before/after temp write, file fsync, rename, directory fsync and
apply CAS and require convergence to one target digest and one of
`pending | applied | degraded` without a second canonical row.

`run-mission-base.json` and every execution artifact are immutable. Canonical
decimal attempt generation is part of every execution-artifact identity; retry
never replaces a prior attempt path, and a path lacking the attempt component
is invalid for V2. Authority overlay files are bounded projections of one
finalized release-authority-store head and never mutation inputs.

The control-plane SQLite database is authoritative only for its operational
transactions and signed readback projections, never for a post-start authority
decision. It contains:

- `run_authority_event_projections`, `run_authority_head_projections`,
  effective-authority/runtime-constraint/fence projections, approval template/
  binding projections, base-ledger indexes and
  `agent_context_projection_intents`; none can authorize append, approval,
  claim, prompt, retry or effect;
- `run_context_generation_bindings`, attempt-qualified
  `agent_invocation_dispatches`, parent execution current/settled-attempt CAS
  fields, versioned connection rows and execution context pins, including
  base/overlay heads, launch phase, all effective context digests and attempt
  identity;
- signed readback projections of skill source/publication receipts, versioned
  skill registry, neighbor graph and trigger-harness manifests, materialized
  legacy migration manifest, broker grant/request/effect/intent/apply/receipt
  revisions and staging-quarantine state, and the bundle digest referenced by
  each run snapshot; none of these projected broker rows is a claim, retry,
  reconciliation or terminal-settlement input;
- signed readback projections of authority-owned candidate/proof/client evidence,
  consumed promotion/open evidence-bundle digests, run-start token consumption,
  probe receipt indexes, ordinary control-plane command outcomes and provisional
  cross-store outcome cores; only the authority finalized-outcome projection is
  servable for a cross-store command, and none substitutes for authority-store
  verification;
- signed projections of `agent_context_generations` continuation policy and the
  singleton `agent_context_cutover_v1` state, generation, proof fence, and
  required versions;
- purpose-signed bounded projections of proof admissions and generic
  runtime-owner identities/leases/absence receipts; provider process-clearance sets;
  cutover
  inventory, projected fenced migration lease,
  signed replacement-admission/candidate-lineage projections, migration repair
  state and
  migration phase events; legacy
  settlement rows, externally signed daemon self-admission projections, provider-binding and provider-sandbox
  receipts, broker grants/proxy admissions/install receipts, opaque credential
  channel projections, script request records, slot-owned logical-effect
  registries and immutable effect intents, secret-policy-bound Git-evidence snapshots,
  script intents/receipts and process identity holds;
- projected worker leases, applied immutable target identities and cursor
  signing key metadata/retention epochs.

The separate release-authority SQLite store is authoritative for active trust
policy and authority-key-custody profile; the signed PrincipalTable lineage,
principal privilege policy, session fences and legacy-migration receipt;
canonical authority run events/heads,
effective constraint/fence and approval template/binding lifecycles; protected
skill-registry sources, publication receipts, registries,
neighbor graphs and trigger harnesses; the complete candidate lineage; reviewer
leases, isolation admissions/terminal receipts, terminal/missing results and barriers;
worker leases, evidence admissions and immutable samples; promotion receipts;
proof-admission lifecycle, proof/client support and qualification evidence; CI selection, branch
protection, rollout-signal policy, alert snapshots/incidents, repair
authorizations/action journals/execution receipts, notification delivery epochs,
delivery-exhaustion alerts, rollout-policy activation/incident-continuity
receipts and release-evidence selection/bundle issuance/expiry lifecycles;
canonical signed broker grants, request records, stable effect intents and
registries, script execution intents, apply journals, Git capture request
lifecycles, reconciliation receipts, terminal receipts and the
`skill_effect_writer_lease` lifecycle;
all generic
runtime-owner identities, lease lifecycles and absence-receipt lifecycles;
externally attested runtime admissions; release-authority exact-request records,
resource reservations, evidence fences, immutable projection-outbox intents and
their append-only delivery-revision chains,
operations/events/backup/anchor states/receipts and immutable verification-key
epochs; authority-generation upgrade admissions, external-action journals and
handoff recovery/final receipts; control-plane writer leases,
replacement-admission and canonical
candidate-replacement lifecycle; run-start token-consumption lifecycles;
generation/run admissions, immutable work admissions and their signed
transition chains, auxiliary execution occurrences, attempt/owner settlements,
execution-reducer checkpoints and one-use attempt launch authorizations plus
spawn journals/receipts; coherent control-plane SQLite snapshot receipts.
Only signed digests and bounded readback
projections cross into the control-plane database.

Large skill resources, raw bounded eval evidence, and prompt evidence remain
file-spooled and content-addressed. SQLite references them by digest and stores
bounded health diagnostics. Missing or mismatched referenced bytes fail
readback or dispatch closed; they are never silently regenerated from a mutable
catalog.

### Projection Commit and Recovery

The existing P087 projection-invalidation lane is extended rather than
replaced. Its typed control-plane repository/view is
`agent_context_projection_intents`. Every canonical **control-plane**
transaction that changes a dispatch/materialization row, migration projection,
probe projection, legacy settlement or another control-plane-owned operational
row inserts or updates one intent for every affected projection/entity before
commit. It never changes an authority head/binding/fence. Every authority-store
mutation instead inserts its immutable `AuthorityProjectionOutboxV1` entry and
first append-only delivery revision in the same pending-anchor transaction,
then appends a `ready` successor only at finalize; claims and terminal outcomes
are further predecessor-linked delivery revisions. Delivery into the control-
plane projection then creates the corresponding P087 intent. Each
control-plane intent row binds projection kind/entity,
canonical source table and primary key, source head/revision, canonical payload
digest, target logical artifact, status `pending | applied | degraded`, attempt
count, bounded error code and timestamps. If any required intent write fails,
the owning store's canonical mutation rolls back. A filesystem write is never
required inside either canonical transaction.

These rows are latest-head upserts under unique
`(projection_kind, entity_id)`, not an unbounded append queue. They retain the
prior applied head as diagnostic metadata while replacing pending work with the
newest canonical head. The existing P087 writer lane schedules their bounded
consumption, but P087 backlog throttling cannot silently discard a required
agent-context intent. SQLite/storage failure to upsert the required row aborts
the canonical transaction; scheduler saturation after commit leaves the row
durably `pending`.

Before a control-plane intent claim, the authority-store owner service issues a
renewable canonical `RuntimeOwnerLeaseV1` for resource kind
`projection_worker_lease`; its purpose-signed `ProjectionWorkerLeaseV1` is only
a bounded projection of that authority object. It binds projection/entity,
owner worker/process identity, monotonic lease epoch, P083 clock baseline and
deadline budget, exact intent revision/source head and expected payload digest.
The control-plane claim transaction verifies the signed authority lease and
stores its digest while CASing the intent; it does not create, renew, fence or
take over the lease lifecycle. A newer source-head operation first advances the
canonical authority resource head, which fences the old lease, and only then
upserts the projected intent. Takeover requires authority deadline expiry plus
signed worker-process absence proof. Every publish/apply write revalidates the
current finalized authority lease and CASes intent revision plus lease epoch;
projection lag cannot extend ownership.

The projection worker rereads canonical truth at the claimed source revision
and renders bounded bytes under the target mode selected by the signed
inventory. `run_local_no_replace` resolves one exact path from
`RunLocalArtifactMaterializationInventoryV1`; all other readback projections use
the immutable content-addressed target
`projections/<projection-kind>/<entity-id>/<payload-sha256>.json`. Both modes
write and fsync a request-owned temp file, perform no-replace atomic rename,
fsync the parent and verify final bytes. There is no replaceable `current` file
or path-discovery fallback. It may
mark `applied` only by CAS over the still-current intent revision, source head,
payload digest and worker lease epoch, recording that immutable target. A stale
worker can therefore create at most an unreferenced content-addressed file; it
cannot overwrite or publish current truth. For `run_local_no_replace`, a stale
worker can create only the already expected same-digest target; any other bytes
at that semantic path are quarantined. Bounded orphan cleanup deletes only
inventory-owned, unreferenced known-digest files after all live lease, run and
cursor retention windows. Failure leaves `pending` or `degraded` with a typed
safe error and never changes the canonical head.

Startup reconciliation is deterministic:

- pending intent plus missing file is rendered;
- pending intent plus matching file is verified and marked applied;
- applied intent plus missing/mismatched file becomes degraded and is rebuilt;
- a file for an older head is retained only as bounded historical evidence and
  is never served as current;
- an expired worker lease is taken over only after process-absence proof; a
  live/ambiguous owner leaves the intent pending and raises an alert;
- an orphan immutable file is ignored unless its exact intent wins the apply
  CAS, then is removed only by the bounded cleanup rule;
- an intent whose canonical source row is missing or digest-mismatched enters
  emergency hold instead of synthesizing truth.

GraphQL, MCP and report generation read the SQLite head and its exact applied
immutable target first, then join projection status. They never discover a
current file by path convention or fall back from a missing current projection
to a stale file. A mutation success and every replay return the immutable commit
receipt with `projection_status = pending`; they never substitute a later
worker state. Current readback may report `pending`, `applied`, or `degraded`
for that same canonical revision and always exposes explicit repair state.

Every **current** readback is additionally fenced by one signed
`AuthorityReadbackWatermarkV1`. The gateway first snapshots the finalized
authority sequence/head, projection-outbox high watermark and exact required
authority object keys/revisions/digests, then reads the control-plane projection
with its recorded `cp_applied_authority_sequence`, source authority sequence,
database head and writer-lease digest. The watermark contains all of those
values plus current writer role/epoch/state and pending handoff; frozen source-
manifest set and source-mapping-policy identities; selected candidate,
generation/run/work admission and execution-reducer identities where in scope;
and active rollout-signal-policy and incident-set identities. A readback may say
`freshness_state = current` only when every required object digest matches and
`cp_applied_authority_sequence >= required_authority_sequence` under the same
finalized authority snapshot.

If the projection is behind, missing or mismatched, the gateway returns the
typed `authority_projection_pending` or `authority_projection_degraded` error
with the safe signed watermark and repair action. It does not return the prior
payload with `projection_status = applied`, does not label the authority head as
the projected head and does not silently join a newer authority policy to an
older execution row. Authority-owned incident, release-evidence, operation and
policy readbacks are rendered directly from that signed authority snapshot but
still report the independently observed control-plane-applied sequence and
latest outbox delivery revision. They never synthesize equality merely because
the authority payload itself is directly readable;
control-plane-owned execution/readback surfaces fail closed until the matching
outbox projection is applied. A bounded stale row may appear only in the
Operator health diagnostic branch explicitly labelled `historical_projection`,
never as current domain data or a transition/evaluation input.

MCP cutover, attempt, incident and authority-operation readbacks, generated
reports and Steward evidence nest the complete
`chainworks_signed_contract_v1<authority_readback_watermark_v1>` object. GraphQL
cannot claim byte-identical object rendering because field names and selection
sets differ: it exposes the base64url encoding of the exact canonical signed-
contract bytes plus a complete typed projection. Swift stores and verifies those
signed bytes first, then requires every selected typed field to equal the
decoded payload. A resolver that omits a required payload row or disagrees with
the signed bytes returns `authority_projection_degraded`, never partial data.
Those surfaces also expose the active source-mapping policy, ordered source-
manifest set, generation admission, writer lease and rollout-policy identities
from the watermark rather than recomputing them. Cross-surface fixtures pause
outbox delivery, rotate writer ownership and activate a new policy/source
manifest, proving no surface reports `current` or `applied` until the exact
required sequence is visible and all surfaces converge on identical watermark
bytes afterward.

### GraphQL and Swift Compatibility Contract

The checked-in post-migration GraphQL schema contains the following exact
additive excerpt. Existing `approveApproval`, `rejectApproval` and
`approvalsResolve` definitions and argument types remain byte-identical in a
separate compatibility golden and are not redeclared by this extension. New
authority mutations and fields are additive, and the typed unified mutation is
introduced separately. Approved HEAD names its roots `QueryRoot` and
`MutationRoot`; unchanged fields from those full root types remain in the
normative generated SDL fixture. A generated SDL single-definition check
fails any duplicate root field. State-like values are `String!`, not GraphQL
enums, so a future server value remains decodable by an older client.

```graphql
extend type QueryRoot {
  agentContextCutover: AgentContextCutoverReadback!
  agentContextAttempt(runId: ID!, agentExecutionId: ID!, attemptGeneration: String!): AgentContextAttemptReadbackResult!
  agentContextIncidents(state: String! = "unresolved", first: Int! = 50, after: String): AgentContextIncidentConnection!
  agentContextIncident(incidentId: ID!): AgentContextIncidentReadback
  agentContextAuthorityOperation(operationId: ID!): AgentContextAuthorityOperationReadback
}

extend type Run {
  agentContext: AgentContextReadbackResult!
}

extend type Approval {
  authorityBinding: ApprovalAuthorityReadback
}

extend type MutationRoot {
  approvalsResolveAuthority(
    approvalId: ID!
    resolution: ApprovalResolution!
    callerRequestId: CallerRequestId!
    comment: String
    authority: ApprovalAuthoritySettlementInput!
  ): ApprovalsResolveAuthorityPayload!

  resolveLeadMediationAuthority(
    confirmationId: ID!
    mediationId: ID!
    runId: ID!
    conflictFingerprint: String!
    resolution: ApprovalResolution!
    callerRequestId: CallerRequestId!

}
```
