```graphql
  authorityOperationId: ID!
  authorityProjectionStatus: String!
  authorityProjectionReceipt: AuthorityProjectionOutboxSetReceipt!
}

union ApprovalAuthorityReissuePayload = ApprovalAuthorityReissueSuccess | DenialPayload

type AuthorityProjectionOutboxSetReceipt {
  schemaVersion: String!
  signedContractBase64url: String!
  payloadSha256: String!
  keyPurpose: String!
  keyId: String!
  keyEpoch: String!
  authorityKeyCustodyProfileSha256: String!
  algorithm: String!
  signatureBase64url: String!
  authorityOperationId: ID!
  authoritySequence: String!
  entries: [AuthorityProjectionOutboxReceipt!]!
  authorityProjectionOutboxSetSha256: String!
}

type AuthorityProjectionOutboxReceipt {
  schemaVersion: String!
  signedContractBase64url: String!
  payloadSha256: String!
  keyPurpose: String!
  keyId: String!
  keyEpoch: String!
  authorityKeyCustodyProfileSha256: String!
  algorithm: String!
  signatureBase64url: String!
  authoritySequence: String!
  projectionKind: String!
  entityId: ID!
  immutablePayloadSha256: String!
  targetSha256: String!
  statusAtCommit: String!
  authorityProjectionOutboxSha256: String!
}

type MutationProjectionIntentReceipt {
  projectionKind: String!
  entityId: ID!
  projectionIntentSha256: String!
  canonicalSourceRevision: String!
  canonicalSourceHead: String!
}

type MutationProjectionReceipt {
  schemaVersion: String!
  intents: [MutationProjectionIntentReceipt!]!
  statusAtCommit: String!
  projectionReceiptSha256: String!
}

type AgentContextProjectionHealth {
  status: String!
  canonicalRevision: String
  projectedRevision: String
  canonicalHead: String
  projectedHead: String
  pendingSince: String
  lastErrorCode: String
}

input ApprovalAuthoritySettlementInput {
  bindingGeneration: String!
  bindingSha256: String!
  expectedAuthorityChainHead: String!
}

input LeadMediationAuthoritySettlementInput {
  bindingGeneration: String!
  bindingSha256: String!
  expectedAuthorityChainHead: String!
}
```

Attempt-readback nullability follows lifecycle truth. An active attempt has a
non-null claim-set digest and null terminal-set/attempt-settlement digests; a
terminal attempt has the inverse. Successor eligibility and state are both
present only after terminal attempt settlement and remain present after one-use
consumption. `providerPromptTurnCount` is always the canonical decimal count
(`0` before a series exists); a nonzero count requires the series digest.
Output digest/source/outcome are all absent before output settlement and all
present afterward. `lateOutputQuarantineSha256` is present only for the matching
late-output outcome. Mixed partial combinations select the authorized invariant
error branch rather than a partial dispatch object. MCP, reports, GraphQL and
Swift project the same signed `agent_context_attempt_readback_v1` digest.

Cutover nullability is phase-valid and tested. `migrationHeadSha256`, state,
migration phase, cutover revision, freshness/status strings, blocker and action
arrays, authority evidence revision, required versions, and projection are
always present. `promoteReleaseEvidence` is null until one promote transaction
commits and remains immutable afterward; `openReleaseEvidence` is null until
the matching open transaction commits. `releaseGenerationAdmissionScope` and
`releaseGenerationAdmissionSha256` are null until `probe_start` or `reprobe`
finalizes the active `probe_only` admission, are both non-null in that admitted
probe state, and are replaced together by the `production` admission when open
commits. Each non-null evidence object is complete:
none of its component digests can be nullable or synthesized from current CI,
branch, alert or incident state. In
`legacy_bridge`, generation, candidate, promotion, proof and replacement fields
are null. In `closed_v2_pending` before promotion, the selected candidate and
passing receipt may be present but generation and proof fields are null. In
`probe_v2` and `open_v2`, generation, candidate, passing receipt and proof
matrix are non-null; proof admission/run/receipt fields are present only after
their corresponding durable transition. `emergency_hold_v2` preserves whichever
verified generation/proof fields existed on entry. Lease, inventory,
self-admission, replacement and zero-unsafe receipt fields are null until their
own phase creates them. No resolver invents zero UUIDs, empty digests, or
generation zero to satisfy GraphQL non-nullability.

`Run.agentContext.generation` follows the frozen admission union rather than
cutover phase alone. A production Run has `runAdmissionKind = production`, a
non-null `releaseRunAdmissionSha256`, and null `proofRunId`, `probeEpoch`, and
`proofFixtureNamespaceSha256`. A proof Run has `runAdmissionKind = probe`, null
`releaseRunAdmissionSha256`, and all three proof fields non-null together. Both
arms require the matching non-null generation-admission scope/digest. Any mixed
arm, missing required conditional field or fake empty digest renders the
`AgentContextReadbackError` branch with code
`agent_context_readback_invariant_failed`; the non-null union remains present,
so GraphQL null bubbling cannot erase the parent Run.

The normative MCP JSON object omits those phase-inapplicable optional fields in
accordance with the no-JSON-null rule; the GraphQL resolver maps omission to the
nullable fields shown above. Required MCP fields and non-null GraphQL fields are
the same phase-independent set. Shared phase vectors prove both projections.

`agentContext` is a non-null union for every readable Run. In its success branch,
all three connections, their edge lists/page info, and projection are non-null.
`mode` is `legacy_readback_only` or `v2` for a success branch.
Legacy rows set `rawContextSchema = null`, preserve the existing plan-format
integer when representable, return empty connections, set authority/generation
to null, and return projection status `not_applicable` with all
revision/head/error fields null. Unknown context versions expose only the
bounded raw discriminator through an authorized
`AgentContextReadbackError(code = agent_context_readback_unsupported_schema)`;
no partial success object is returned and every execution mutation remains
denied. For
Operator-visible V2 rows, authority and generation are non-null by contract, as
are canonical projection revision/head. A missing value in that mode is a typed
invariant failure, not a nullable success.

The union error branch is generated from the shared error registry and is used
only after successful authentication, authorization, scope resolution and Run
visibility. Its closed codes are
`agent_context_readback_unsupported_schema`,
`agent_context_projection_pending`, `agent_context_projection_degraded`, and
`agent_context_readback_invariant_failed`; these expected visible readback
conditions may carry a safe signed watermark and closed repair actions.
Missing authentication, caller-class/capability/scope denial and the
non-enumerating absent-or-invisible Run outcome are top-level GraphQL errors
only and return no union data, watermark, resource ID, projection revision or
existence-dependent detail. GraphQL non-null bubbling on those authorization
errors is intentional. No condition is emitted through both channels, and no
error path returns a partial `AgentContextReadback` object.

For an authorized Operator, `visibility = operator` and all verified fields are
available. Although `AgentContextReadback.authorityWatermark` is nullable in
SDL for redaction, it is a semantic non-null invariant for every Operator V2
row; absence selects the typed invariant-error branch. Agent,
Observer and ReadOnlyOperator callers receive `visibility = redacted` only for
runs they are otherwise authorized to read; authority, generation and
`authorityWatermark` are null, all connections are empty, and projection status
is `redacted` with all revision/head/error fields null. Thus signed/store/writer
identity and authority-sequence facts are not leaked through the watermark. A run
outside that caller's report authorization remains a non-enumerating not-found
response. Projection health never contains paths or raw errors.

Caller-class fixtures execute every V2 GraphQL mutation and Run agent-context
readback as Operator, Agent, Observer and ReadOnlyOperator. They prove each
manifest denial code uses exactly its declared union-or-errors channel;
authentication, capability, scope and non-enumerating denials appear only in
top-level `errors`, while authorized unsupported/projection/invariant outcomes
appear only in the union error branch. Agent/Observer/ReadOnlyOperator
same-run authorization returns redacted success with a null watermark, and
Operator success has a complete verified watermark. Generated selections also
fail if a redacted child resolver can
recover any authority/store/writer identity through an adjacent field.

The root `agentContextCutover` query and `Approval.authorityBinding` are
Operator-only. The former is the singleton GraphQL equivalent of
`runtime.agent_context.cutover.get`; it never requires a Run ID and returns one
SQLite transaction's cutover, migration, proof, process-clearance and projection
truth. Its release-evidence fields are the immutable component digests and
authority revision committed by promote/open, not a live cross-store join or a
resample of current CI/branch/alert state. The existing `approveApproval` and
`rejectApproval` signatures retain
`requestId: String!` for current Swift documents; their resolvers continue to
validate lowercase UUIDv4 bytes before mutation. They are separate frozen
legacy `approval_legacy_approve_operation` and
`approval_legacy_reject_operation` adapters: they accept only unbound approvals, keep
their existing control-plane journal/projection payload and return the closed
compatibility denial for a bound approval. The already shipped
`approvalsResolve` mutation is the separate
`approval_legacy_graphql_resolve_operation` frozen legacy surface: its existing
arguments and `ApprovalsResolvePayload` retain mandatory `journalId` and no
authority input is added. The additive V2 path is instead
`approvalsResolveAuthority`, mapped to `approval_authority_settle_operation`; it
requires non-null `ApprovalAuthoritySettlementInput`, accepts only a bound
approval, and returns only authority-operation/outbox projection truth. It
never fabricates a control-plane journal to satisfy the legacy payload shape.
`resolveLeadMediationAuthority` is the separately versioned authority path for
lead-mediation confirmations and binds confirmation, mediation, run and conflict
fingerprint; no stage-approval adapter guesses that subject kind.
`reissueApprovalAuthority` performs only the reissue transition defined above.

`operations.yaml` owns separate legacy, stage-authority and mediation-authority
logical operation families rather than
silently changing the old one:

| GraphQL entry point | Operation and canonical request mapping | Canonical result mapping |
|---|---|---|
| `approveApproval` | `approval_legacy_approve_operation`; `approval_legacy_approve_request_v1` maps `requestId -> caller_request_id`, fixed `resolution = approve`, `comment` preserved and no authority fields | render stored `approval_legacy_approve_result_v1` through unchanged `ApproveApprovalPayload` |
| `rejectApproval` | `approval_legacy_reject_operation`; `approval_legacy_reject_request_v1` maps `requestId -> caller_request_id`, fixed `resolution = reject`, `reason` preserved and no authority fields | render stored `approval_legacy_reject_result_v1` through unchanged `RejectApprovalPayload` |
| `approvalsResolve` | `approval_legacy_graphql_resolve_operation`; current caller request, resolution/comment and approval ID only | render the existing stored result through unchanged `ApprovalsResolvePayload`, including mandatory `journalId` |
| `approvalsResolveAuthority` | `approval_authority_settle_operation`; `callerRequestId` plus explicit resolution/comment and exact authority input | render stored `approval_resolve_authority_result_v1` through `ApprovalsResolveAuthorityPayload`, including authority operation and outbox receipt and no journal |
| `resolveLeadMediationAuthority` | `lead_mediation_authority_settle_operation`; confirmation/mediation/run/conflict plus exact authority input | render stored `lead_mediation_resolve_authority_result_v1` through its authority-only payload and no journal |
| `reissueApprovalAuthority` | `approval_authority_reissue_operation`; `requestId -> caller_request_id` plus exact approval/binding/head preconditions | render stored success through `ApprovalAuthorityReissueSuccess`, or every public denial including `stale_precondition` through the shared `DenialPayload` union; no success-shaped denial |

Every V2 adapter uses global `(principal_id, caller_request_id)` lookup before
field-specific state checks. Within one V2 operation family, exact and alias
replay re-render the finalized logical outcome and different intent conflicts.
Frozen legacy adapters instead retain their exact existing command-journal
lookup, conflict and terminal-replay behavior and never create a new generic
semantic-alias row. Reusing a request ID across a legacy and V2 operation is
rejected before V2 prepare; generated vectors preserve each legacy golden and
cover every V2 exact/alias/conflict and cross-family collision. A legacy payload cannot write a binding, authority
event or authority result, and an authority payload cannot create a legacy
journal. The existing MCP `approvals.resolve` remains byte-compatible only as a
frozen legacy descriptor/handler pair. Its stage-approval arm is covered by
legacy goldens; its advertised `lead_mediation_confirmation` arm is not support-
qualified because the current descriptor and handler require incompatible
field names/identifier kinds. That profile is `retired_before_open` no later
than `schema_prepared` and is never used as proof of mediation support. New MCP
tools `approvals.resolve_authority` and
`lead_mediation.resolve_authority` are advertised only to qualified V2 clients.
`provider_session.mark_process_absent_v2` is intentionally absent from this
GraphQL operation map. SDL validation rejects any attempted GraphQL mutation
with that name, while `agentContextAttempt` renders the later bounded
process-fate, dispatch and projection state without mutation authority.
`agentContextAttempt` returns `AgentContextAttemptReadbackResult`: an authorized
visible attempt with complete invariant-valid projection uses
`AgentContextDispatchReadback`; unsupported schema, pending/degraded projection
or invariant failure uses `AgentContextReadbackError`. Authentication, scope and
non-enumerating missing-resource denials remain top-level GraphQL errors. A
resolver never returns a success object with missing process-fate, spawn,
clearance or projection-receipt identities. Each conditional receipt digest and
typed `AgentContextImmutableReceiptIdentity` are present or absent together; the
canonical payload bytes must hash to that digest, match source revision/head and,
when the receipt is signed, decode from the optional exact signed-contract bytes.
Any disagreement selects the invariant-failure union arm rather than partial
success.

Before `open_v2`, every shipped GraphQL consumer is classified in the proof
matrix as `qualified`, `migrated`, or `retired_before_open`; no scalar,
nullability, or field change may silently invalidate a supported operation
document. `CallerRequestId` is the existing lowercase UUIDv4 scalar; MCP
additionally uses its UUIDv7 boundary key for new V2 tools. V2 replay resolves
the original canonical outcome, including its canonical request ID and
operation-declared projection receipt; frozen legacy replay returns only the
exact pre-existing payload and journal fields.

The current shipped Swift operation family that omits `authority` is explicitly
`legacy_unbound`. It remains supported only against unbound approvals in
`not_started / legacy_bridge`. The replacement app operation first reads
`Approval.authorityBinding`, calls `approvalsResolveAuthority`, and submits binding generation/digest/head in
`ApprovalAuthoritySettlementInput`, and treats
public `stale_precondition` with internal reason
`approval_authority_binding_stale` as a
read-refresh boundary: it fetches the new binding and generates a new lowercase
UUIDv4 rather than replaying the old request ID against changed intent. Exact
transport loss with the same binding reuses the original request ID. The live
HTTP/WS harness proves all four paths, lead-mediation authority settlement, and
that the old `approvalsResolve` selection still requires and returns `journalId`
byte-for-byte.

`ClientCapabilitySupportPolicyV1` must therefore record the current shipped
build as either `migrated` to a named replacement build/operation digest or
`retired_before_open`; it cannot mark the unmodified document `qualified` for a
bound V2 approval. At `schema_prepared` the V2 daemon no longer admits legacy
unbound approval mutation, so a retired build receives the closed compatibility
denial and cannot accidentally settle a V2 binding. Open is blocked until the
replacement build's live qualification receipt or explicit retirement record
is present.

The policy independently records the current MCP `approvals.resolve`
mediation profile as `retired_before_open` and records every caller that relied
on it as migrated to `lead_mediation.resolve_authority` or retired. Keeping the
legacy tool name for stage approvals does not qualify or revive the incompatible
mediation arm. A daemon that advertises that arm as supported after
`schema_prepared`, or a live client inventory that still invokes it, blocks
open.

Every GraphQL payload for a V2 state mutation contains the operation manifest's
tagged projection arm. A control-plane-effect operation contains
`projectionStatus = pending` and `MutationProjectionReceipt`; an authority-only
operation, including authority-bound approval settlement, contains
`authorityProjectionStatus = pending` and the finalized signed
`AuthorityProjectionOutboxSetV1` receipt, with the control-plane arm absent.

GraphQL replay uses the release-owned
`GraphqlLogicalResultNormalizationV1`, never an undefined response-
canonicalization step. It parses the executable document, resolves named and
inline fragments, evaluates `@skip`/`@include` from schema-coerced variables,
forms one conflict-checked response-key tree using aliases, and canonicalizes
object keys by raw UTF-8 response key while preserving list order. Present nulls
remain present. IDs, booleans, strings and integer/decimal-string scalars use
their schema wire encoding; floating-point values are forbidden in authority
logical results. Error paths preserve response keys and list indices, and error
extensions come only from the generated error registry in canonical key order.
The normalized document/variable digest selects a rendering of the immutable
stored logical result. Exact or semantic-alias replay with the same normalized
selection returns the same JCS logical projection; different selections render
independently and promise equality only for overlapping logical fields, never
raw HTTP-byte equality. Shared Rust/Swift vectors cover aliases, nested and
repeated fragments, directive inclusion/exclusion, field ordering, explicit
nulls, scalar boundaries, lists and every error extension. The normalization
schema/build/digest is pinned by the operation manifest, candidate and client-
qualification receipt. A caller obtains later `applied | degraded` state only
from the corresponding readback object.

Connection pagination follows one `agent_context_cursor_v1` contract shared by
the three fields. `first` defaults to 50 and must be `1...100`; `after` is an
opaque base64url canonical JSON cursor of at most 2048 bytes and expires after
one hour. It binds cursor version/scope, authenticated run, list kind, a
monotonic `snapshot_revision`, expiry, last ordering tuple, signing-key ID and
HMAC-SHA256 over every other cursor field. The daemon cursor key is outside
SQLite/provider access; current and immediately previous keys remain usable for
at least cursor TTL plus one hour. Signature failure is `malformed`. Ordering is
`(agent_execution_id, attempt_generation)` for role/assignment and skill
composition, and
`(prepared_revision, agent_execution_id, attempt_generation)` for dispatches.
Tuple comparison is component-wise and never lexical for decimal-string
numbers. `attempt_generation` and `prepared_revision` are parsed as strict
unsigned integers with no sign or leading zero and compared through their
SQLite integer or fixed-width numeric sort-key columns; IDs compare by their
canonical raw UTF-8 bytes. The SQL predicate is the explicit keyset expansion
`a > last_a OR (a = last_a AND b > last_b) ...` using those typed columns.
Casting a cursor value to floating point, comparing decimal strings as text, or
using a locale collation is invalid.
The first page pins the current read-model revision. Connection projections are
versioned rows with `valid_from_revision` and optional
`valid_through_revision`; changing state, digests, constraints, sandbox/grant
status, or any other node field closes the prior version and inserts the new
version in the canonical transaction. Later pages select the exact version
valid at the pinned revision, not current mutable rows, and exclude later
inserts. Versions are retained for at least cursor TTL plus one hour. A cursor
for another run/list or a malformed MAC returns non-retryable `cursor_invalid`
with reason `filter_changed | malformed`; an expired cursor or pruned/
unavailable snapshot returns retryable `cursor_snapshot_unavailable` with
reason `expired | snapshot_unavailable`. There is no shared code with
conflicting retryability and no offset fallback.

Swift drains pages until `hasNextPage = false`, rejects repeated cursors or node
identities, and never treats a first page as a complete list. Legacy and unknown
connections return `edges = []`, `endCursor = null`, `hasNextPage = false`,
`cursorVersion = 1`, no expiry, and the run read transaction's revision.
Redacted connections return the same shape with `snapshotRevision = "0"` so
pagination does not reveal hidden row activity. Golden vectors cover zero, one,
100, 101 and 10,000 rows plus inserts concurrent with every page boundary.

Swift uses lossless string wrappers with `.known` and `.unknown(rawValue)` for
every state-like field; it does not use exhaustive generated enums. Non-null
field absence is a typed transport/schema error and cannot default to healthy.
Golden compatibility fixtures cover legacy pre-P066, P066, V2 healthy,
V2 pending/degraded projection, unknown context/schema/status values, redacted
rows, and newer-server/older-client decoding. The macOS surface labels unknown
or degraded truth and never enables actions from it.

GraphQL, MCP reports, run reports, and the macOS read-only run surface expose:

- context schema version;
- base and pinned authority-chain heads, context revision, and conflict status;
- role and assignment identifiers;
- ordered skill IDs, bundle digests, aggregate composition digest, and broker
  health;
- prompt-envelope manifest, complete provider-prompt-series/turn-count,
  active effect-slot claim or terminal-set, conditional successor eligibility,
  terminal attempt settlement, output-settlement source/outcome and conditional
  late-output-quarantine digests;
- candidate manifest, promotion receipt, proof matrix, client-capability support
  policy, run generation, attempt generation, and dispatch phase;
- separate immutable promote/open release-evidence bundle, CI-selection, branch-
  protection, alert-snapshot and unresolved-incident-set digests plus their
  authority-evidence revisions and the opened generation's signed admission-
  receipt digest;
- eval-suite and promotion-policy versions associated with the production
  skill/model promotion;
- current cutover state, proof state, generation continuation status, and
  required capability versions.

Operator readback is bounded and authorization-aware. It does not expose full
operator directives, raw prompts, secrets, or unrestricted artifact content to
non-operator principals.

## Rollout Alerts

Threshold and query meaning is one signed release-owned
`AgentContextRolloutSignalPolicyV1`. It binds policy version/predecessor,
telemetry source and query digests, closed signal names/types/reset semantics,
threshold/window/sample-spacing/freshness rules, incident owner/action mapping,
notification policy, candidate/cutover applicability and activation authority
sequence. The release trust policy pins its publisher identity. Candidate,
sampler and notifier cannot edit or select it; an Operator may only activate a
pre-signed policy through the predecessor-CAS command below and cannot author
or modify its bytes. Every telemetry input,
alert snapshot, incident, release-evidence selection/bundle and promotion/open
operation binds the exact active signal-policy digest. A policy transition
invalidates prior healthy selections and leaves each affected signal `unknown`
until enough complete samples under the new policy exist.

Activation is an explicit Operator-only authority operation
`runtime.agent_context.rollout_policy.activate`, owned semantically by the
OS-isolated `rollout_policy_controller`. Its request contains both request IDs,
one release-signed complete new policy, exact predecessor policy digest and
activation sequence, one release-signed complete
`RolloutSignalMigrationPlanV1`, current unresolved-incident-set digest and
expected authority revision; caller-supplied signal mappings are forbidden. Prepare
reserves the active policy and every unresolved incident key. Finalize verifies
the policy publisher against `EvaluationTrustPolicyV1`, CASes the predecessor,
and atomically writes the new active policy, one
`RolloutSignalPolicyActivationReceiptV1`, every required incident continuity
revision and the projection outbox before anchor advancement. Exact replay
returns that finalized activation; a competing or stale predecessor performs
zero mutation.

For each unresolved incident, the controller compares the old and new
signal-definition digest covering
telemetry source/query, threshold, window, sample spacing, reset/freshness,
clearing, owner/action, notification and repair-contract semantics. When those
bytes are identical, activation appends one incident revision binding the new
`rollout_signal_policy_sha256` and a signed
`IncidentPolicyContinuityReceiptV1`; lifecycle state, owner, timestamps,
acknowledgement and remediation evidence remain unchanged, while any prior
clearing-sample window is reset and must be recollected under the new policy.

When an unresolved signal is renamed, replaced or removed, activation requires
exactly one signed migration-plan row from the release-policy publisher:

| Migration row | Incident result under successor policy |
|---|---|
| `successor_signal` | append `IncidentPolicyMigrationReceiptV1`, rebind the still-unresolved incident to the named successor signal, preserve all history/owner/acknowledgement/remediation, and reset every clearing window; changed semantics can never reuse old healthy evidence |
| `retired_hold` | append the same receipt with state detail `retired_signal_hold`; preserve the incident in the unresolved release-blocking set even though the successor policy no longer samples the old signal |

The migration plan binds both complete policy digests, old/new signal-definition
digests, release-root/publisher purpose and either a successor compatibility
proof or an exact subsystem-removal candidate proof. Missing, duplicate,
candidate-authored or stale rows still fail activation with
`rollout_policy_incident_migration_blocked`, but a permanently unavailable old
telemetry source cannot deadlock successor-policy activation. Activation
reserves and migrates the incident once, releases the predecessor-policy key and
does not block unrelated authority operations.

A `retired_signal_hold` remains unresolved until Operator-only
`runtime.agent_context.rollout_signal.retirement_settle` submits both request
IDs, exact incident/policy/migration revisions and one complete
`RolloutSignalRetirementSettlementV1`. The incident controller accepts only (a)
proof that the monitored subsystem was removed from the active catalog,
workflow, runtime inventory and proof matrix, or (b) two complete healthy
replacement-signal samples under the current policy plus the signed replacement
mapping. Finalize resolves the held incident through the ordinary incident CAS
and preserves the old ledger; missing old telemetry alone is never resolution
evidence. Exact replay is zero-write, and promote/open remain blocked while the
hold is unresolved.

Signals without unresolved incidents may change. Their first snapshot under
the new policy is `unknown`; no old healthy snapshot, release-evidence
selection, clearing sample or notification state is reinterpreted. Every
incident row/revision, readback, mutation result, release-evidence selection,
promote/open result, cutover/report/Steward/Swift projection and authority
watermark carries the active policy digest. Recovery from prepare,
anchor-pending or projection lag resumes the same activation operation and
never exposes a mixed-policy current incident set.

The daemon exposes bounded source counters/gauges, but the release-authority
`alert_sampler` is the only sampler/writer. It reads one authenticated,
revisioned telemetry snapshot plus control-plane read models and publishes the
signed result through `runtime.health`, run reports and Steward evidence. Alert
thresholds are release gates, not advisory dashboard decoration:

| Signal and exact threshold | Owner | Required action |
|---|---|---|
| `agent_context_emergency_hold_active == 1` for any generation | runtime on-call | emit an immediate high-priority local operator notification; retain admission closure, inspect typed invariant and use only process clearance or a passing forward candidate |
| post-open `production_agent_executions_with_verified_mission_context_and_skill_contract_percent < 100.00` or state `unknown`; the closed pre-open/no-sample states are excluded | rollout owner plus execution owner | create/retain `mission_context_coverage_incomplete`, close new admission and forward-fix the exact invalid/stale source; clear only after source freshness plus two 100.00-percent samples at least 30 seconds apart |
| any increment of `agent_context_admission_denied_total{reason}` for any of its seven closed reasons | rollout owner plus the reason-mapped authority/compiler/runtime team | atomically preserve the denial and create the exact reason-bound incident/hold from the exhaustive phase matrix; pre-open it blocks cold-start/open, post-open it applies the declared scoped or generation hold, and it clears only with the reason-specific proof plus two fresh zero-delta samples |
| any increment of `agent_quality_target_declaration_invalid_total{reason}` | evaluation/security owner | invalidate the candidate evaluation epoch before evidence admission, create/retain `quality_target_invalid`, and clear only after a new pre-sample declaration under a successor epoch plus two zero-delta samples |
| `agent_context_rollout_hold_active{reason} == 1` for any closed reason | reason-mapped rollout owner | emit the reason-mapped local notification and keep promote/open/admission closed; resolve only the underlying signed hold row, then require two zero-gauge samples before incident resolution |
| any increment of `provider_sandbox_attestation_failure_total` on a production profile | security plus adapter owner | block candidate/open; if current generation, enter typed emergency hold and preserve attestation/escape evidence |
| `agent_context_projection_degraded_current > 0` or `agent_context_projection_oldest_pending_seconds > 120` | persistence on-call | emit a high-priority local operator notification; stop promotion/open, repair exact intent/lease and verify current immutable target; never serve stale files |
| `agent_context_projection_oldest_pending_seconds > 30` for two samples | runtime owner | warning and backlog diagnosis before the high-priority threshold |
| migration heartbeat age exceeds 45 seconds or deadline expires | migration Operator | alert immediately; do not take over until deadline plus generic exact-owner absence proof; then CAS a new lease epoch |
| `agent_context_cutover_blocker_count > 0` for five minutes or `migration_repair_state = repair_blocked` | rollout owner | keep admission closed and execute the blocker/readback-listed reconciliation or explicit replacement |
| any increment of `agent_quality_evidence_admission_invalid_total` | evaluation/security owner | invalidate the affected epoch, rotate/revoke worker lease when indicated and rerun missing pairs |
| three consecutive `agent_quality_promotion_inconclusive` decisions for one candidate/profile | model operations owner | investigate provider infrastructure; no threshold waiver or promotion |
| any `client_capability_incompatible` from a release marked supported | macOS release owner | block release/open compatibility claim until the signed manifest/matrix row is corrected |
| any increment of `agent_skill_broker_reconciliation_required_total{effect_class}` | effect owner plus runtime on-call | stop new effects for that grant/target, reconcile the durable effect identity and replay the terminal receipt |

One authority-store-owned `AgentContextAlertSnapshotV1` is the only
promotion/readback alert truth. The sampler holds a 45-second fenced writer
lease, samples every 15 seconds, and CASes writer epoch, prior snapshot digest
and sequence. Each snapshot records the active rollout-signal-policy digest,
cutover generation, authority writer epoch,
monotonic sample sequence, durable clock-baseline and daemon/sampler boot IDs,
source read-model revision, per-counter reset epochs, every signal value,
freshness, closed state `unknown | healthy | firing`, first-observed time,
consecutive qualifying/clearing sample counts, linked incident IDs and required
action. A second sampler can take over only after lease deadline plus signed
absence of the exact prior sampler identity; stale writers are epoch-fenced.

An immediate threshold changes `healthy -> firing` in one sample; a two-sample
threshold requires two qualifying samples at least 30 seconds apart under one
clock baseline. Settlement of the first signed firing snapshot through the
incident controller atomically creates one
`AgentContextReleaseIncidentV1` in state `open`, revision `1`, with the
signal-defined owner role and no assigned principal. Incident lifecycle is
strictly `open -> acknowledged -> resolved`; it never disappears, reopens or
skips a state, and another breach after resolution creates a predecessor-linked
successor incident.

The sampler does not create that incident directly. It submits its signed
policy-bound firing snapshot to the independent `incident_controller`, which
verifies current policy/head and performs the authority-only incident CAS.
Ack/resolve use the same controller. A missing or crashed sampler cannot sign an
incident transition or repair authorization, and the incident controller cannot
sample telemetry.

`runtime.agent_context.incidents.list/get` are bounded Operator-only authority-
store readbacks and expose current incident revision, signed object digest,
alert snapshot, acknowledgement/resolution eligibility and allowed next
actions. List pagination pins the authority-store snapshot revision and uses
`AgentContextIncidentCursorV1` with the same size/TTL/key-rotation rules as V2
connections and raw canonical ID ordering. It has no filesystem or
control-plane-cache fallback.

`runtime.agent_context.incidents.acknowledge` requires `open`, exact revision
and incident/snapshot digests. Its `ReleaseAuthorityOperationV1` prepare binds
those inputs with `control_plane_effect = none`; no candidate or maintenance
control-plane writer is started. Authority finalize CAS-records the enabled
Operator principal, bounded comment digest and timestamp, increments incident
revision, changes state to `acknowledged`, and writes the exact-request result
plus authority projection outbox in the same pending-anchor transaction. The
gateway returns only after anchor finalize. The recorded principal is the
accountable owner; another currently enabled Operator may resolve only when it
independently has `RuntimeAgentContextIncidentResolve`, and both principals are
then retained. Principal class, caller class and capability are always checked
live, so a revoked or re-scoped owner has no residual authority.

Resolve requires `acknowledged`, exact revision/digests, two complete healthy
clearing samples at least 30 seconds apart under the current clock baseline,
and a complete closed `AgentContextIncidentResolutionEvidenceV1` of at most 16
KiB canonical bytes. The gateway computes `resolution_evidence_sha256`; a caller
cannot submit a digest without the object. The supplied
`clearing_sample_pair_sha256` and evidence must name those exact samples and
current snapshot;
a sample reset, unknown source, renewed sampler lease, new breach or stale
snapshot invalidates it. One authority-only prepare/anchor/finalize operation changes
state to `resolved`, increments incident revision, records resolving
principal/evidence, removes the incident from the unresolved set and appends
its event during finalize. Exact replay
returns that result; competing acknowledge/resolve commands have one CAS winner
and stale losers perform zero mutation. Until resolve commits, the signal may be
healthy but the incident remains unresolved and promotion/open remains blocked.
Only a new evidence bundle issued after that commit can observe the new empty
unresolved-set digest.

An unresolved incident never grants a general bypass, but it also cannot make
its own repair impossible. For an existing incident whose emergency hold or
firing signal depends on a failed projection worker, admitted candidate process
or exact runtime-owner/process hold, an Operator may call
`runtime.agent_context.incidents.repair_authorize` with scope
`incident_signal`. The authority derives the allowed action set from that exact
incident, signal and active release policy and may admit only
`restart_same_admitted_candidate`, `reconcile_authority_projection`,
`clear_verified_process_hold`, or `restore_telemetry_source`.

Sampler/source failure can prevent creation of a trustworthy incident, so it
has a separate incident-independent `alert_health` scope. That scope requires
the exact current `unknown` or stale alert-health snapshot, active signal-policy
digest, sampler owner and lease, source identity/revision and complete authority
watermark; `incident_id` is forbidden. It may admit only
`restart_alert_sampler` or `restore_telemetry_source` for those exact targets.
Repair cannot mark a signal healthy, create/resolve an incident, mint release
evidence or bypass the ordinary two-sample clear rule; after repair the normal
sampler must produce a complete new sample sequence.

The tagged `notification_delivery` scope admits only
`restart_incident_notifier`. A separate incident-independent
`notification_watchdog` scope requires the exact singleton
`NotificationWatchdogHealthV1` row in `unknown | stale`, watchdog owner/lease, policy and
exhausted-notification inventory head and admits only
`restart_notification_watchdog`; no incident ID is required or accepted. Each
slot binds one exact component build,
resource/lease/head and pre-state digest, expires after five minutes and is
one-use. It cannot change candidate/generation policy, open admission, launch a
provider, run a skill/effect, mint release evidence, resolve the incident or
select a replacement build.

The derivation and signature belong exclusively to the OS-isolated
`incident_repair_controller`, which has no sampler, notifier, provider-launch,
repair-execution or incident-state key. It reads the current signed incident,
active rollout-signal policy, exact target identity and runtime-owner lease from
the authority store and signs only the intersection allowed by their closed
matrix. It remains available when the sampler, watchdog or candidate is stopped.
The sampler cannot authorize `restart_alert_sampler`, the watchdog cannot
authorize `restart_notification_watchdog`, and no component may self-authorize
its own restart.

Every admitted slot additionally names one release-signed
`IncidentRepairActionContractV1`; an action name without the exact active
contract digest is structurally invalid. The active rollout-signal policy pins
the complete contract set, and activation fails if an action in its incident
matrix lacks exactly one contract. These are not generic shell, launchd, signal,
filesystem or SQLite capabilities. Each contract fixes the target resolver,
canonical target identity, precondition and CAS inputs, one built-in release
adapter, the first externally observable operation boundary, required
postcondition observation and the only legal reconciliation outcomes:

| Action | Exact target and authority precondition | Sole operation adapter and externally observable boundary | Required postcondition before `completed` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `restart_alert_sampler` | current sampler component/build plus `alert_sampler_lease`, active signal-policy digest and firing/unknown snapshot; clean release or exact owner-absence receipt is mandatory | sealed `AlertSamplerLaunchAdapterV1`; one fixed launchd-label kickstart with no caller argv/env/path | successor sampler identity and one higher lease epoch, same signal policy, first complete signed sample sequence; a started but unobserved process enters `identity_hold` |
| `restart_same_admitted_candidate` | current candidate/generation, runtime self-admission, control-plane writer lease and exact stopped/absent process; candidate replacement is forbidden | sealed `AdmittedCandidateLaunchAdapterV1`; starts only the already admitted executable/configuration under the pinned sandbox | independently measured same candidate/build, successor process identity and writer-lease epoch, unchanged generation/admission and successful health handshake |
| `reconcile_authority_projection` | exact authority outbox row and control-plane projection intent key/revisions/digests in `pending` or `degraded`, plus conditional expired worker lease and absence receipt | `AuthorityProjectionReconcileAdapterV1`; one CAS claim/render/publish path over the existing content-addressed target | matching immutable target bytes, source head and applied intent revision under the current projection lease; no source/domain row changes |
| `clear_verified_process_hold` | exact dispatch hold, provider session/cancellation epoch, executable-work transition and current reducer checkpoint plus one unused P083 provider-process absence receipt | `VerifiedProcessHoldClearAdapterV1`; one authority operation that consumes the receipt and invokes the typed settlement reducer, never a process syscall | signed attempt and owner settlement, settled work-admission transition and successor-or-terminal reducer checkpoint; the cleared attempt cannot return to active |
| `restore_telemetry_source` | one policy-registered telemetry-source identity, source lease/head and source-specific unhealthy/unknown observation; clean release or exact owner-absence receipt when process-owned | source-kind-specific sealed adapter selected by the policy, with a fixed launchd restart or typed source reconnect operation and no caller-supplied command | same registered source/build and successor lease or connection epoch, new source revision and one complete fresh sample; alert health is still decided by normal subsequent samples |
| `restart_incident_notifier` | exact firing delivery-exhaustion alert, notification epoch/revision/digest, notifier component/build and `incident_notifier_lease`; clean release or exact owner-absence receipt is mandatory | sealed `IncidentNotifierLaunchAdapterV1`; one fixed launchd-label kickstart with no caller argv/env/path | same notifier build under one higher lease epoch, startup scan has reclaimed existing pending/retry-wait rows; watchdog remains firing until a later delivered epoch |
| `restart_notification_watchdog` | exact singleton `NotificationWatchdogHealthV1` in `unknown` or `stale`, active signal policy, exhausted-notification inventory head and `notification_watchdog_lease`; clean release or exact owner-absence receipt is mandatory | sealed `NotificationWatchdogLaunchAdapterV1`; one fixed launchd-label kickstart with no caller argv/env/path | same watchdog build under one higher lease epoch and one complete startup scan; health advances to `healthy` and exactly one alert exists for every previously exhausted `(notification_id, delivery_epoch)` with no duplicate alert |

The authorization stores the selected action-contract digest and target
identity digest; the journal repeats both and CASes the exact precondition before
crossing the contract's operation boundary. An adapter cannot accept a broader
target, command, path or operation than its contract. Any target/precondition
change before that boundary produces `failed_no_action`; after the boundary it
must reconcile the same journal to `completed`, `failed_safe`, or
`identity_hold`. There is no fallback from an unknown action/target kind to a
generic process or database primitive.

`runtime.agent_context.incidents.repair.execute` is served while the candidate
is stopped by the OS-isolated `incident_repair_executor`. It consumes one action
slot by atomically creating one append-only `IncidentRepairActionJournalV1`
before the bounded built-in maintenance operation. The journal binds repair
authorization/action slot, logical action identity, exact target/pre-state,
expected executable/resource and process supervisor identities. Its lifecycle
is:

```text
prepared -> action_pending -> process_registered -> observing -> completed  [process action]
prepared -> action_pending -----------------------> observing -> completed  [non-process action]
prepared -> failed_no_action
action_pending | process_registered | observing -> identity_hold
identity_hold -> completed | failed_safe  [typed reconciliation only]
```

Every repair execute operation returns and durably projects its
`authority_operation_id` plus the current action-journal ID/revision/digest,
including when the journal enters `identity_hold`. That hold is nonterminal and
advertises only `authority_operations.get` and, when the required observation
set is available, `authority_operations.reconcile`. The generic GET readback
uses its incident-repair tagged detail to expose the immutable action contract,
same target/pre-state, same external-action idempotency key, current observed
facts and bounded `requiredObservations`; it does not expose another executable
action slot or authorize a fresh repair.

`authority_operations.reconcile` reauthenticates
`RuntimeAgentContextAuthorityOperationReconcile`, binds the exact operation and
journal revision/digest, and accepts only the action contract's closed
observation schema. The release-owned repair executor independently rereads the
same registered process/resource. Verified post-state appends the missing
`completed` receipt without repeating the external operation; verified
pre-state can perform the already journaled operation only when the journal
proves its operation boundary was never crossed; a safe terminal no-effect
state appends `failed_safe`; every ambiguous third state remains the same hold.
The action name, target, adapter and idempotency key are immutable, and neither
reconcile nor exact/alias replay allocates another slot, process, syscall or
authority operation. The original execute logical result is immutable. If it
returned `identity_hold`, exact and alias replay forever return that same
original hold result and original action-journal revision/digest. A later
terminal successor is a separate canonical `authority_operations.reconcile`
logical result and is visible through `authority_operations.get` as the latest
operation/journal state; it never rewrites the execute exact-request record.
Reconcile exact replay returns its own terminal result, while GET lets an
Operator discover that the previously held execute has since settled.

`action_pending` commits before `posix_spawn`, signal, restart, clear or
reconcile syscall. Process-starting actions register PID/process-group/birth
before observation; non-process actions record an immutable syscall/result
receipt. Crash recovery inspects the existing journal, process/resource fate
and pre/post state and either completes that same action, proves no action, or
enters durable `identity_hold`. It never issues the syscall again when fate is
ambiguous. The terminal row records exact pre/post
process or resource observations and emits
`AgentContextIncidentRepairExecutionReceiptV1`. Crash after consume resumes or
settles only that slot; it never repeats a restart/clear action with ambiguous
process fate. `failed_safe` leaves the slot terminal and the incident unchanged;
a new attempt requires fresh incident readback and authorization. Successful
repair likewise leaves the incident acknowledged and unresolved. The normal
sampler must subsequently produce two healthy clearing samples, after which the
ordinary resolve command closes it. All other paused/hold causes remain
non-repairable without a separately reviewed action contract.

Fault-injection fixtures stop the executor immediately before and after every
listed launchd, spawn, signal, XPC, projection-publish and authority-CAS
boundary, then restart both executor and target. Each fixture proves the action
contract resolver returns the same target, at most one externally observable
operation occurs, ambiguous fate enters `identity_hold`, completed postcondition
bytes are stable, and a retry requires a fresh authorization rather than a
second operation from the old slot. Companion GET/reconcile fixtures prove the
hold survives restart with the same operation/journal IDs, wrong capability or
observation schema performs zero mutation, verified pre/post/third-state inputs
derive only their declared successor, exact reconcile replay is stable and no
path executes the external action twice.

First fire and every acknowledge/resolve transition also inserts one
`AgentContextIncidentNotificationV1` into the authority-store outbox. The
`incident_notifier` delivers only to the local operator inbox,
`runtime.health` notification readback and Steward evidence; this proposal does
not claim an external pager integration. Delivery is at-least-once with unique
`(incident_id, incident_revision, destination_kind, delivery_epoch)` and closed
state `pending -> delivering -> delivered | retry_wait | delivery_exhausted`,
plus deadline wakeup `retry_wait -> pending` for the same delivery epoch and
next attempt ordinal.
Retry waits are exactly 5, 15, 60, 300,
then 900 seconds, capped at twelve total attempts; each attempt has a 10-second
deadline. Success stores a durable delivery receipt, and duplicate delivery is
harmless and cannot change incident state. One `incident_notifier_lease` binds
notifier process, epoch and correlated clock baseline. Entering `retry_wait`
stores the next monotonic wake tick and remaining budget; the notifier or a
fenced takeover CASes that exact row back to `pending` only after the deadline.
Startup scans `pending`, `delivering` and `retry_wait`, re-observes any in-flight
delivery receipt and resumes the same delivery epoch/attempt identity. A
takeover requires lease expiry plus exact owner-absence evidence and increments
the lease epoch; a stale notifier writes zero rows. Exhaustion CASes the row to
`delivery_exhausted`, emits a durable local-inbox/health diagnostic and stops
automatic retries. It does **not** block incident resolve, promotion after the
incident is resolved, or another authority mutation; delivery is redundant
operator notification, not release truth.

Installation bootstrap creates one signed singleton
`NotificationWatchdogHealthV1` in `unknown` before serving; therefore watchdog
health and repair inputs exist even when no notification or delivery-alert row
has ever existed. The independent `notification_watchdog`, not
`incident_notifier`, holds one fenced `notification_watchdog_lease`, samples the authority notification rows
and signs `IncidentDeliveryExhaustionAlertV1` for every newly exhausted
delivery epoch. The unique authority key is exactly
`(notification_id, delivery_epoch)`; restart/takeover scans the complete
authority snapshot and returns the existing alert or creates one missing alert
for each exhausted key, never a second alert.
The alert binds notification/incident/revision/destination/epoch, exhaustion
receipt, rollout-signal-policy digest, first-observed time, owner
`rollout_on_call`, action `inspect_local_inbox_then_requeue_or_repair_notifier`
and state `firing | cleared`. It is exposed directly by the
authority gateway in `runtime.health`, cutover readback and Steward evidence,
so notifier failure cannot suppress its own alert. Clearing requires a later
delivered epoch; notifier-repair evidence without a successful new delivery
keeps it firing. It never changes incident or promotion truth and remains
nonblocking.
Each complete scan CASes the singleton's prior revision/digest, lease and
exhausted-inventory head. Watchdog failure, stale lease or incomplete startup
scan changes or retains singleton state `unknown | stale`, never interpreted as
healthy; only a complete current-policy scan may append `healthy`.
The incident-independent `notification_watchdog` repair scope described above
is the only restart/takeover path. It consumes clean lease release or exact
owner-absence evidence, installs one higher lease epoch and requires a complete
startup-scan receipt before health can become observed. The scan does not clear
firing delivery alerts and cannot mutate incident or promotion truth.

The watchdog-prescribed notifier repair is an authorized narrow action, not
operator prose. `incidents.repair_authorize` has a tagged
`notification_delivery` scope that binds the firing watchdog alert, exact
notification/delivery epoch/revision/digest, notifier component/build/lease and
only action `restart_incident_notifier`. It may be used even when the linked
incident has already resolved because notification truth is separate; live
Operator capability is still required. The signed action contract permits only
the fixed notifier launchd label after clean lease release or exact owner-
absence proof. Repair success requires the same build under one higher notifier
lease epoch and recovery of existing pending/retry-wait rows; it does not clear
the watchdog alert, which still requires a later delivered epoch.

An Operator with `RuntimeAgentContextIncidentNotificationRequeue` may invoke
`runtime.agent_context.incidents.notification.requeue` against the exact
exhausted epoch/revision/digest. The authority-only operation appends a new
delivery epoch in `pending` with a fresh bounded schedule while preserving every
prior attempt and receipt. Exact replay returns that epoch; concurrent or stale
requeue has one CAS winner and zero loser mutation. Requeue cannot change the
incident, alert snapshot or unresolved set. Delivery failure remains visible
and alerting but cannot acknowledge, resolve or silently clear an incident.

Support never reconstructs repair inputs from incident summaries. Operator-
only notification and watchdog get/list tools, plus the always-present
`runtime.agent_context.notification_watchdog.health.get`, return the complete signed
notification revision/digest, notifier and watchdog owner/lease epochs/digests,
target component/build, correlated clock baseline and firing alert identity
required by requeue or `notification_delivery` repair authorization. They read
one pinned authority snapshot and expose no bearer, path or raw delivery body.
The ordinary incident summary remains bounded, but links its notification and
watchdog IDs so the operator can follow with these tools. Retained black-box
fixtures perform `list -> get -> repair_authorize -> repair.execute -> get ->
notification.requeue -> delivered -> watchdog cleared` using only northbound
fields and prove stale lease/revision inputs mutate nothing. The singleton
health GET is the bootstrap source for watchdog repair when the alert list is
empty; no repair authorization may infer health from absence of an alert row.

Notification and watchdog pagination never reuse the incident cursor. A first
notification page mints `IncidentNotificationCursorV1` bound to authenticated
principal, normalized list/filter scope, authority snapshot sequence/head,
expiry and last `(authority_sequence, notification_id, delivery_epoch)` tuple;
a watchdog page analogously mints `NotificationWatchdogCursorV1` with last
`(authority_sequence, alert_id)`. Both are opaque MACed tokens under a distinct
gateway key purpose. Cursor TTL is five minutes and immutable authority history
for both lists is retained for at least 24 hours; if the exact pinned snapshot
is unavailable, the result is `cursor_snapshot_unavailable`, never a page from
current state. Wrong principal/scope/filter/key epoch, forged tuple, expired
cursor and cross-list reuse fail before row disclosure. Fixtures insert rows
between pages, rotate keys and cross-use both cursors while proving stable,
duplicate-free snapshot traversal.

Missing source data, writer-lease ambiguity, counter reset, clock
mismatch or partial sample sets alert state `unknown` and cannot clear an
incident.

Counters, snapshots and incidents persist across both daemon and sampler
restart. Startup resumes the authority-store sequence/epochs and cannot reset a
firing alert, unresolved incident, owner, revision or notification outbox to
zero. An intentional counter-schema reset requires a signed
release migration epoch and leaves the signal `unknown` until a complete
baseline plus next sample is committed.

`runtime.health`, run reports, Steward and promotion all project the same signed
authority snapshot ID/digest and unresolved-incident-set digest. Operator health
also exposes bounded unresolved counts, oldest incident revision/required
action, and pending/delivery-exhausted local notification counts without raw
evidence. A missing
signal, stale sample older than 60 seconds,
unknown reset epoch, clock-baseline mismatch or partial write is `unknown` and
blocks promotion/open. Phase promotion receipts include that exact alert
snapshot and incident-set digests through the consumed release-evidence bundle;
they never join independently sampled gauges. Deterministic
clock/restart fixtures cover firing before restart, restart while firing,
counter continuation, stale/unknown recovery and threshold clear. Thresholds
cannot be relaxed by feature flag, environment or operator preference; changing
them requires a new signed predecessor-linked
`AgentContextRolloutSignalPolicyV1` activation under the release trust policy,
which invalidates old healthy evidence. A promotion-policy transition is also
required only when its separate promotion thresholds change.

## Native Dependency and FFI Ownership

The protected release source contains one generated
`NativeDependencyFfiInventoryV1`, and the candidate manifest, evaluation trust
policy, native-build sandbox policy/confinement receipt, CI gate manifest and
release evidence bind its digest. Cargo crates and features come only from the committed `Cargo.lock`; Swift packages come from
`Package.resolved`; Apple APIs bind the exact Xcode SDK build, deployment range
and runtime probe policy. Registry checksum, source URL/commit, selected feature
set, link mode and license are recorded for every native dependency. An
unlocked Git dependency, unrecorded feature, dynamic library outside the sealed
system/release bundle or host outside the admitted OS/SDK matrix fails candidate
registration.

The inventory also treats every executable build-time input as native trust
surface, even when it does not ship in the final bundle. It records each Cargo
`build.rs`, proc-macro crate and compiler/linker wrapper; SwiftPM/Xcode build-
tool or command plugin; Run Script phase; code/schema generator; linker script;
SDK compiler, linker and signing executable; exact source/tree or binary digest;
declared inputs/outputs/environment-name allowlist; network/process policy and
owning release target. The protected-base generator fails on any executable
build input observed in Cargo metadata, SwiftPM/Xcode build plans or CI command
events that is absent from the inventory. A candidate cannot prove its own
binary identity with an unmeasured generator or plugin.

Dependency inventory is not a substitute for vulnerability/yank disposition.
The release-security collector fetches one signed, versioned advisory snapshot
through a protected-base CI identity, verifies issuer/key/freshness and stores
its immutable digest outside candidate workspaces. It then generates
`NativeDependencyRiskDispositionSetV1` with exactly one row for every exact
package name/version/source/checksum in `Cargo.lock` and `Package.resolved`.
Every row includes advisory IDs and severity, yanked state and exactly one
disposition: `unaffected`, `affected_blocked`, or
`signed_time_bounded_exception`.

`unaffected` requires either no matching advisory/yank or a signed not-affected
range proof for the exact package bytes. Any yanked dependency or affected
advisory defaults to `affected_blocked`. A time-bounded exception is signed by
the release-security owner, binds package/checksum/advisory snapshot and
candidate, includes accountable owner, reason, compensating controls, issue
sequence and expiry no more than 30 days after issue, and cannot cover an
unknown package/checksum or revoked advisory key. Candidate, provider, build
script and ordinary Operator input cannot author, extend or select a
disposition. Expired, stale, missing, duplicate, unknown-issuer or unapproved
yanked rows block candidate registration, promotion and open.

The active `EvaluationTrustPolicyV1` pins accepted advisory publishers/keys,
maximum snapshot age and exception issuer; candidate manifest, native-build
policy/confinement receipt, CI gate and release evidence bind
`native_dependency_risk_disposition_set_sha256`. Fixtures add/remove an
advisory, yank/unyank one exact version, expire an exception at T-1/T/T+1,
change a package checksum, revoke the advisory key and make the source stale.
Only a complete current signed disposition set can pass; no network lookup at
runtime or permissive offline fallback exists.

Inventory does not confer execution authority. Every candidate build runs under
the release-owned, non-signing `release_build_executor` and one signed
`NativeBuildSandboxPolicyV1`. The executor receives immutable source and
toolchain descriptors plus a fresh empty output root. It has no code-signing,
notarization, Secure Enclave, Keychain, authority-store, production database,
provider credential, user-home or repository-secret entitlement. Network and
generic local IPC are denied. For each compiler, linker, Cargo `build.rs`, proc
macro, SwiftPM/Xcode plugin, Run Script phase, generator and linker script, the
policy admits only the inventoried executable/process descendants, declared
read roots, one step-specific write root, bounded environment-name/value-source
set and resource limits. An undeclared executable, shell interpolation target,
path, environment name, network endpoint, Mach service or output fails the
build; there is no unsandboxed retry.

The keyless executor and a kernel-backed monitor append one bounded,
content-addressed `NativeBuildObservationJournalV1` over every expected and
observed input, process, access class, denial probe, output digest and terminal
sequence. The executor cannot sign it or any receipt. The separately launched
`native_build_confinement_attestor` has read-only descriptors and observation
feeds, reobserves process/output identity, verifies journal completeness, and
alone signs `NativeBuildConfinementReceiptV1` with the custody-profile purpose
`native_build_confinement_attestation_v1`. It cannot execute a build input,
spawn a child, write an output, register a candidate or invoke another signing
purpose. Candidate registration requires that passing receipt for the exact
source/toolchain/native-inventory/build-policy/journal tuple before any
separately isolated signing/notarization helper may receive the measured
unsigned artifact. The signing helper never executes candidate build scripts
and cannot turn a missing confinement receipt into a signed candidate.

ABI probes use the same separation. A keyless `native_abi_probe_executor` runs
only inside one registered disposable fixture installation and writes
`NativeAbiProbeObservationJournalV1`; `native_abi_probe_attestor` independently
reobserves the fixture namespace, helper mapping, symbols, entitlements,
shipping exclusion and production non-mutation, then signs only
`NativeAbiProbeReceiptV1` under purpose `native_abi_probe_attestation_v1`.
Neither attestor may execute fixture/build inputs or write outputs, and neither
executor has a Keychain/signing entitlement. Purpose-key epochs, process audit
tokens, designated requirements and journal digests are bound by
`EvaluationTrustPolicyV1`. Replayed, cross-purpose, executor-signed,
attestor-executed, incomplete, reordered, concurrently changed or mismatched
journals fail before receipt insertion or candidate registration.

Retained malicious build fixtures place synthetic credentials in
denied files/environment/Keychain entries, expose a local and remote listener,
request an undeclared executable and attempt writes outside the step root; every
probe is denied, no synthetic secret appears in output, and no candidate or
confinement-pass receipt is emitted. Clean fixtures prove required generated
files remain reproducible under the same policy on every supported host.

The ownership table is complete:

| Boundary | Pinned dependency/API and features | Sole wrapper/unsafe owner | Required entitlement/ABI proof and fail-closed behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| structured Git | exact `gix` crate versions/checksums and explicit object/index/diff feature set; hooks, filters, alternates and command execution disabled | `db::trusted_git` safe facade; each project-owned `unsafe` block has stable inventory ID and named Rust owner | fixture repository parity plus object/index/path-byte/replace/graft denial; version or feature drift fails gate |
| SQLite | exact `sqlx`/`libsqlite3-sys` versions, bundled/system choice, compile options and required snapshot/backup/VFS APIs | `db::sqlite_abi` plus `control_plane_snapshot_attestor`; no raw handle crosses crate/XPC boundary | runtime `sqlite3_libversion`, compile-option, snapshot token, WAL/checkpoint race and immutable-backup ABI probes must match inventory |
| Security.framework/CryptoKit | `SecItemCopyMatching`, `SecItemUpdate`, separate Secure Enclave P-256 signing and key-agreement key creation, ECDSA sign/verify, ECDH key agreement, opaque key representation and access-control symbols from the pinned macOS SDK | narrow release-authority Security.framework/CryptoKit shim; unsafe pointer/CF ownership IDs and reviewer are listed | `SecureEnclave.isAvailable`, exact per-purpose custody profiles, raw64 low-`s` and ECDH/HKDF/AES-GCM vectors, cross-purpose sign/decrypt denial, independent rotation, code-signing/access-group entitlements, ThisDeviceOnly/non-export behavior and duplicate-item/read-update-read faults; missing/drifted symbol or software fallback is failed-serve |
| XPC/audit token | `xpc_connection_*`, typed message codecs, audit-token/designated-requirement inspection | sealed C/Rust/Swift XPC shim with one owner per unsafe callback/context | protocol version, peer audit token, Mach-service entitlement and copied/foreign endpoint denial |
| launchd/process | launchd plist/labels plus `posix_spawn`, process-group, signal, `proc_pidinfo`/birth/boot observation symbols | `provider_sandbox_launcher`, incident adapters and `runtime_owner_inspector`; no generic spawn facade | helper designated requirement/entitlements, exact argv/env/FD closure, PID-reuse and syscall-boundary fault probes |
| Seatbelt | sealed `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` identity and generated profile grammar for admitted macOS builds | `sandbox_policy` renderer and launcher only; no direct private sandbox FFI | versioned escape/allow probes on every supported OS; missing/deprecated behavior excludes host, never unsandboxed fallback |
| APFS snapshots | exact `fs_snapshot_*`/mount symbols and fixed registered-volume operation set from the pinned SDK | `workspace_snapshot_service` only | privileged helper entitlement/designated requirement, read-only snapshot/mount identity, writer-race and unsupported-filesystem denial |

No other module may call these FFI symbols or declare a matching entitlement.
The inventory names every project-owned unsafe block/file/line-stable ID,
invariant, reviewer and test; a source scan fails on an unowned `unsafe`, extern
symbol, XPC message family, launchd label, entitlement or executable build
input.

Runtime probes never use the production authority installation. Before a probe,
the release-owned fixture installer creates one signed
`NativeAbiProbeFixtureInstallationV1` with a random installation ID, temporary
authority and control-plane databases, a fixture-only Secure Enclave/key-
custody genesis, the fixed test-helper-only Keychain access group
`com.chainworks.release-authority.fixture` and random fixture service/account namespace,
`launchctl bootstrap` namespace and label prefix, Mach-service names, runtime
homes, repository/workspace and an explicit deny inventory containing every
production authority/database/Keychain/launchd/Mach/runtime path or identifier.
The probe process receives only fixture descriptors and labels. Pre/post
observations prove the production deny inventory was unchanged; any attempted
lookup or mutation is a hard failure and no production receipt is emitted.
Fixture cleanup is journaled and a leftover namespace blocks reuse rather than
being mistaken for a fresh installation.

The probe executable matrix is distinct from the shipped helper matrix. For
each production helper target, the build defines one
`NativeAbiFixtureHelperMappingV1` naming the common source/commit, protocol and
ABI manifest, production binary/designated requirement/entitlements, and a
separate fixture target, binary digest, fixture designated requirement and
fixture-only entitlements. Fixture targets are signed only by the CI/release
test identity, carry `com.chainworks.release-authority.fixture`, and are
excluded from every application bundle, package, archive and notarization
manifest. Production helpers carry only the production access group and their
code signatures are negatively tested for fixture-group access. Fixture
helpers carry no production group, service, Mach or launchd entitlement and
are negatively tested against the production deny inventory.

The release-owned mapper proves ABI/protocol parity from generated headers,
Rust/Swift layouts, XPC codecs, exported symbols, compiler flags and source
digests; entitlements and designated requirements are intentionally different
and compared against their declared side of the mapping. An unmapped helper,
source/ABI drift, fixture binary inside a shipping artifact, or either binary
accessing the opposite namespace fails the gate.

The build emits one signed `NativeAbiProbeReceiptV1` from the mapped fixture
helpers on the supported host. It binds the measured production-helper
identities, every `NativeAbiFixtureHelperMappingV1`, the disposable fixture
installation and covers symbol resolution, library/code identities, ABI sizes/
layouts, side-specific entitlements, positive/negative runtime probes,
shipping-artifact exclusion and the production-state non-mutation proof.
Cross-architecture fixtures cover every supported
target. Candidate/open admission rejects a missing, stale, wrong-host, reused-
fixture or partial receipt rather than assuming SDK compile success proves
runtime availability.

## Gates

Add canonical gates:

```text
./scripts/test-gate.sh agent-skill-compliance
./scripts/test-gate.sh agent-context
./scripts/test-gate.sh agent-evals
./scripts/test-gate.sh agent-native-boundaries
./scripts/test-gate.sh agent-quality
```

`agent-quality` aggregates the four deterministic gates and is required when a
change touches workflow definitions, catalog definitions, prompt assembly,
skill bundles, production agent bindings, eval assertions, release helpers,
native dependencies/features, entitlements or FFI wrappers.

The implementation adds an always-present `agent-quality` job to
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`; branch protection requires check name
`CI / agent-quality`. The job executes a selector binary and governed-path
policy loaded and digest-verified from the protected base revision, never from
the pull-request head or merge workspace. It receives only repository identity,
base/head OIDs and changed-path bytes from the trusted CI checkout. It emits
`agent_quality_ci_selection_v1` with repository/base/head/merge-base, protected
selector and path-policy digests, matched governed paths, decision, schema
version, issued time and CI run identity. Relevant changes execute
`./scripts/test-gate.sh agent-quality`; irrelevant changes emit an explicit
`not_applicable` receipt with empty matches, complete classification proof and
no gate/execution fields. Both decisions are signed as a GitHub artifact
attestation whose OIDC claims bind repository, protected workflow path/ref,
workflow digest, base/head OIDs, job and run attempt; the receipt is valid only
for that exact head and check run. Labels, commit messages, environment flags,
fork-controlled scripts and head-owned selector/policy files cannot select
`not_applicable`. That arm can pass the branch check but cannot be selected for
candidate/live/promotion/open evidence. For an unrelated-only exact HEAD, the
release-owned CI dispatcher must trigger the protected-base workflow; the
separate read-only collector must verify and sign the resulting
`release_candidate_forced` executed arm with a passing gate receipt before
candidate registration; no commit is intrinsically unable to become release
evidence merely because its PR path set was unrelated. Phase 0 registers the
gate aliases and exact constituent commands in `scripts/test-gate.sh list` and
`docs/reference/test-gates.md`; proposal-readiness before Phase 0 uses only the
existing rollout-contract linter. Nightly/Steward live-provider evals are separate
checks and cannot replace this deterministic PR gate.

Promotion/open also requires a retained signed `BranchProtectionReceiptV1`.
A release-owned read-only GitHub App collector, never the PR workflow token,
reads the repository/ruleset API only after the distinct write-only activation
controller finalizes its journal, and records repository ID, branch, ruleset ID
and revision/ETag, exact required check `CI / agent-quality`, bound head OID,
collector key/OIDC identity, observation time, durable-clock baseline/tick,
wall/monotonic correlation receipt and 15-minute expiry. The release trust
policy admits its signing key. Wrong repository/branch/head/check,
expired/unsigned receipt, unusable clock correlation or a ruleset change blocks
promotion. Workflow presence without this receipt is incomplete rollout
evidence. Open additionally requires the protected-base
`docs/reference/agent-context/rollout-contract.yaml`, whose signed
`AgentContextReleaseRolloutPolicyV1` has no disable or waive arm and sets a minimum continuous
healthy soak at least as long as the largest active rollout-signal window. One
same-generation `RolloutSoakReceiptV1` must cover every required sample and the
entire correlated interval. A process restart resumes only with the same
baseline and independently proven complete sample coverage; baseline rollover,
unverified restart gap, missing samples or generation change fails the old
revision and starts a successor interval.
